## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. At the table, read the boxed text aloud and glance at the bullets. The rules from Session 1's guide (Influence, Study, Search, Help, Hide, Grappled, Heroic Inspiration) still apply; tonight adds water, breath and cold.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-2) · [Scene 1: The Night Song](#scene-1-the-night-song) · [Scene 2: The Pilots' Hall](#scene-2-the-pilots-hall) · [Scene 3: The sandbank](#scene-3-the-sandbank) · [Scene 4: The hooded ferryman](#scene-4-the-hooded-ferryman-optional) · [Scene 5: Down to the bell](#scene-5-down-to-the-bell-optional) · [Scene 6: Back on the shore](#scene-6-back-on-the-shore) · [Running the fights](#running-the-fights-session-2) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-2) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-2) · [End of session](#end-of-session-2)

### Before you start (Session 2)

**Level:** four characters at level 3. No level-up tonight.

**First, check Ila.** Open Foresight and look at Ila Harrow. If the raid took her (Arrested), start tonight with [the Mere road cart](#if-ila-was-taken-the-mere-road-cart) at dawn, then pick up the rest. If she's free or hidden, start with the Night Song.

**What this session is about.** The dead of the Mute Mere sing every night, and the Old Shore sings back. Tonight the party learns why. Mother Sallow asks them to find the eastern-marsh ferry, missing a week. They find it grounded on a sandbank in the middle of the Mere, its ferryman dead and peaceful, with memory-eels circling. If they're brave, they dive to the drowned bell, where the Cantor of the Drowned Choir asks each of them one question: who are you grieving? This is the session about grief, water and honesty. It's the first time the danger is real.

**Your goals tonight:**
- The Night Song lands as eerie and sad, not just scary.
- The party finds the ferry and fights or avoids the eels.
- If they dive, the Cantor's question gets a real answer from at least one player.
- They pick up a second clue about Tam Harrow's death.
- End on: "Who was on the ferry?"

**Prepare:**
- **Tokens or minis:** the four characters; Mother Sallow; Ila; Brannagh Wick; a skiff (a long rectangle); the grounded ferry; the dead ferryman; six memory-eels; two Drowned Singers and two more eels for the belfry; the Cantor; the hooded Tidewarden. Optional: Brother Hadrik Voss and one extra Drowned Singer.
- **Maps:** your IsoForge kit (below) has the Memory Shore, the missing ferry and Ossa's belfry. For the sandbank, a rough oval 30 feet across with the ferry on one end and deep water all round. For the belfry, draw a stone tower top in the middle of the page and write "40 ft down" beside it.
- **Breath cards:** on an index card per character, write how many rounds they can hold their breath: (1 + Constitution modifier) × 10 rounds, minimum 5. A round is six seconds; ten rounds is a minute. Tick it off during a dive.
- **The Mere Memory table** (d6, in the book's Part 11.4) for anyone who stays up all night.
- **The hymn** from Session 1: *Call:* "Who walks the water?" *Answer:* "We remember you."
- **Ask the players, privately or aloud, before the dive:** "Is there someone your character grieves?" A one-word answer is fine. It's what the Cantor will ask.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **Holding your breath.** A character can hold their breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds). When they run out, they gain 1 level of Exhaustion at the end of each of their turns. As soon as they can breathe again, they lose all the Exhaustion they gained this way. At 6 levels of Exhaustion a character dies, so start warning loudly at 2.
- **Exhaustion.** Each level gives −2 to every d20 Test (attacks, checks, saves) and −5 feet of Speed.
- **Frigid Water.** The Mere is cold. A character can swim in it for a number of minutes equal to their Constitution score. After that, each extra minute they make a DC 10 Constitution save or gain 1 Exhaustion level. Short dives won't reach this; long ones will.
- **Swimming.** Without a Swim Speed, every foot of swimming costs an extra foot of movement. Diving 40 feet takes most characters two or three turns.
- **Fighting underwater.** Without a Swim Speed, melee attacks have Disadvantage unless they're made with a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear or trident. Ranged weapon attacks have Disadvantage, and miss automatically beyond normal range (crossbows, nets and thrown javelins or daggers are the exception to the Disadvantage). Spells work normally.
- **Frightened** (a condition). Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of the fear is in sight, and the character can't move closer to it willingly.
- **Grappled underwater.** Same as on land (Speed 0; action to escape), but the eels and Singers can drag a grappled character down with them.

### If Ila was taken: the Mere road cart

**Skip this unless Ila is Arrested.** At dawn, a covered Court cart leaves the Landing House for Hallowmere with Ila inside, a ferry-folk driver, a Hushman Sergeant and three Hushmen. Brannagh Wick sends a runner with its route and hour: the Mere road, second checkpoint, an hour past dawn.

> **SAY:** "The cart is grey canvas on a black frame. It rolls very slowly along the causeway, and its wheels make no sound at all. Through a gap in the canvas you see a ferry coat, much too big for the person wearing it."

- **Ila is never in danger on-screen.** She stays inside the closed cart, behind the driver, unharmed. Describe the canvas before anyone casts an area spell, and keep spells off the cart.
- **Three plans that work:** a false checkpoint that turns the cart onto a drowned causeway (Charisma (Deception) DC 15, and a ferry-folk pilot plays along); an ambush at the ford; or Brannagh's pilots refusing the ford crossing so the cart has to wait while the party talks or sneaks.
- **If it comes to a fight:** see [the Mere road cart fight](#the-mere-road-cart-if-ila-was-taken). The Sergeant yields the cart rather than die.
- **How it ends:** Ila climbs out of the cart, furious and shaking, and says, "I counted the fence posts. Two hundred and twelve." Then the Night Song tonight, as below.

### Scene 1: The Night Song

**Where and why.** The Mere Memory Shore at dusk, the evening after Session 1. The whole Old Shore comes out for the song. The party comes because Mother Sallow told them to, because Ila asked them to, or because the singing pulls everyone outside.

> **SAY:** "The water is perfectly still. Fog lies on it like a sheet. From somewhere beneath the surface, a woman begins to sing. It is not loud. It is grief in a voice you almost recognise. Every word is a name. You hear your own name, then the name of someone you lost, then a name you don't know, and then yours again. Along the shore of name-stones, the ferry-folk stand in a long line, lanterns low, and hum back."

**What's really going on.** The singers are the Drowned Choir: the Mere's dead, who can't rest because their bell, Ossa, has been silent for four centuries. They call out to the living to be remembered. The response hymn is a promise that they are. The Choir doesn't hunt people who grieve or sing. It hunts "the forgetful." Mother Sallow is descended from the Choir's leader, the Cantor, and doesn't say so.

**Mother Sallow.** *Voice, mannerism:* as in Session 1 (dry, short, pipe between her teeth). *Wants:* the party to sing, and to say a dead person's name out loud. *First words:* "Lanterns down. They don't like being looked at." *Lines:* "Sing it back. That's all they want. Somebody to answer." · "You don't have to mean it the first time. You will by the third." · "There. Hear that? They've stopped. An hour, maybe."

**Ila.** She stands beside whoever was kind to her in Session 1 and sings very quietly, counting the lanterns between verses. *Line:* "Dad always sang the answer too loud. Everyone laughed."

**What they can learn here:**
- **Singing the response quiets the song for an hour.** Free. Anyone who sings it sincerely succeeds: a Charisma (Performance) roll only decides how good it sounds, never whether it works.
- **The Choir doesn't attack the grieving or the singing.** Free, from Mother Sallow.
- **Something about Tam's last night,** if a character stays on the shore all night (below).

**Staying up all night:** anyone who stays on the shore until dawn makes a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, roll on the Mere Memory table. These are borrowed memories, not losses: the character remembers something that happened to someone else. **Clue option:** if the party is asking about Tam, make one failed save Tam's last night instead: grey gloves reaching over the side of a boat, a blank feeling where a route used to be, and a boat drifting with no cargo. Record it in the Memory ledger as kind "Mere."

**If they…**
- **…sing:** read "the singing stops, all at once, as if someone had laid a hand on it." Mark which characters sang with a dead person in mind. The Cantor will know.
- **…refuse to sing or mock it:** nothing attacks, but the ferry-folk turn their backs, and Mother Sallow says, "Then don't go on the water tonight." If they stole the Heart in Session 1 and haven't given it back, Sallow won't teach the hymn at all until they make amends: hand it back to Ila, and speak a dead person's name on the shore.
- **…try to stop the song with magic:** the spell Silence doesn't stop it. The Drowned hear grief, not sound.
- **…try to wade in toward the voice:** the water is black and cold and goes deep fast. Mother Sallow catches a sleeve: "Not at night. Not without the answer."

**Brother Hadrik Voss (optional complication).** Use him if your table likes arguing with allies. Halfway through the song, a grey-robed Faerûnian priest of Kelemvor walks down the shore swinging a smoking censer, a flask of holy water in his other hand.
- *Voice:* low, certain. Quotes the Doomguide.
- *Mannerism:* never lets the censer go out; relights it constantly.
- *Wants:* to bless the Mere and "lay the dead to rest," by force.
- *First words:* "The Lord of the Dead does not permit the dead to linger. I will give them peace."
- *Lines:* "These souls are owed judgment, not this endless keening." · "You would leave them singing in the cold forever?" · (if argued well) "...Judged. And remembered. Yes. The Doomguide says both."
- **Talking him down:** Influence, Charisma (Persuasion) DC 15. He's Indifferent. A Study check first, Intelligence (Religion) DC 12, about what Kelemvor actually teaches gives Advantage: Kelemvor's dead are owed judgment and remembrance, not erasure. Restraining him also works (the ferry-folk will thank you). Hold Person works too, but he's Hostile when it ends.
- **If he pours the holy water:** the Choir rises angry and one Drowned Singer climbs out of the shallows for him. Singing the response hymn stops it at once. Mother Sallow steps between Hadrik and the Singer and takes 5 damage if nobody covers her. The Old Shore blames "the Loud Quarter."

**How it ends.** The song fades, or stops for an hour, and the ferry-folk go home. Mother Sallow speaks to the party before she goes:

> **SAY:** "'The eastern ferry's been gone a week. Ferryman and all. It isn't like the Mere to keep a boat that long and give nothing back.' She knocks her pipe against a name-stone. 'Find it. I'll pay. And take a pilot. Brannagh won't refuse you if Ila asks.'"

### Scene 2: The Pilots' Hall

**Where and why.** The Pilots' Hall on the Quays, the next morning. Every boat that crosses the drowned town needs a pilot, and Brannagh Wick owns every pilot.

> **SAY:** "The Pilots' Hall is one long room hung with charts of streets nobody has walked in four hundred years. A short, wind-cracked woman with a coil of sounding-line over her shoulder is shouting tide-times at a ship's captain. 'She'll go out on the noon slack, lad, or she won't go at all.' She turns to you. 'And what do you want?'"

**What's really going on.** Brannagh trained Tam Harrow. The night he died, Tam took his boat out with no cargo and no ship to pilot, which no pilot does. She told the Court nothing. She believes he was going to the drowned belfry, and she's right.

**Pilot-Mistress Brannagh Wick** (about sixty, Scout).
- *Voice:* gruff; every ship is "she," every captain "lad."
- *Mannerism:* counts tides on her fingers out loud while she listens.
- *Wants in this scene:* to know the party won't get her boat or her pilots killed, and to keep Ila safe.
- *First words:* "And what do you want?"
- *Sample lines:* "The Mere's got two towns in it, lad. One you can see." · "Tam took her out with an empty hold. No pilot does that. No pilot." · "You bring my skiff back with everyone in it, or don't bring it back."

**What they can learn here:**
- **A skiff and a pilot are theirs for the asking** if Ila vouches for them or they helped the ferry-folk in Session 1 (filled the quota, defended the raid). Otherwise it's Influence, Charisma (Persuasion) DC 15, or 5 gp for a Quays skiff with no pilot.
- **Tam went out that night with no cargo,** and Brannagh thinks he was heading for the belfry. She tells them with the same conditions as the skiff; on a failed check she tells them anyway after the trip, if they bring her boat back. This is a source for how Tam died.
- **The sandbank is in the middle of the Mere,** over the drowned town's old square.

**If they…**
- **…go without a pilot:** the drowned rooftops just under the surface are a maze. A Wisdom (Survival) check, DC 12. On a failure they still get there, but the skiff scrapes a roof, ships water, and wakes the eels early: the eels get a free first round.
- **…want to swim or wade the whole way:** it's half a mile of cold water. Frigid Water applies. Talk them into a boat, or let them, and count minutes.
- **…ask Brannagh about the Court:** "The Court can't cross this water without my people. They know it. I know it. We're very polite to each other."

**How it ends.** They push off.

> **SAY:** "Under the skiff the drowned town slides by: a chimney, a weathervane, a street that slopes down into green dark. Something long and pale turns over beneath a roof and is gone. Ahead, the fog thins, and you see the eastern ferry, sitting crooked on a bar of yellow sand, with someone sitting very still in the stern."

### Scene 3: The sandbank

**Where and why.** A bar of sand about 30 feet across, in the middle of the Mere. The missing ferry is grounded on it.

> **SAY:** "The ferry is a flat barge with a single rail, run aground on the sand. In the stern sits the ferryman, an old man, face peaceful, eyes closed, both hands on a long oar. The oar is dripping, though it is bone dry around it. All around the sandbank, the water moves in slow pale rings."

**What's really going on.** The dead ferryman is the Tidewarden's old body. The Tidewarden is a bell-spirit of the Mere now, who ferries the dead, and he left this body behind when he took up Ossa's oar. Don't say any of that yet. The pale rings are memory-eels, which bite and steal small memories. They guard the drowned belfry nearby and treat the sandbank as theirs.

**What they can learn here:**
- **The ferryman died peacefully, not by violence.** A Search check, Wisdom (Medicine) DC 10, or free if anyone looks closely: no wounds, no water in his lungs. "As if he simply set himself down."
- **The oar drips with no water near it.** Free. A Study check, Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) DC 13: "This oar belongs to something, and that something isn't him anymore." Detect Magic shows a faint aura on the oar, none on the body.
- **The ferry's hold** has a few memory-pearls in a net bag (see Rewards).

**If they…**
- **…step off the boat onto the sand or into the shallows:** the eels attack. See [the memory-eels](#memory-eels-at-the-sandbank).
- **…stay in the skiff and try to slip past:** each character makes a Dexterity (Stealth) check, DC 15. If at least half succeed, the eels never notice them and they reach the ferry quietly. If not, the eels attack, but they ignore anyone sitting still in a boat for the first round.
- **…raise the dead ferryman's oar:** the eels flee at once. Anyone who thinks of it deserves Heroic Inspiration.
- **…want to take the body home:** good instinct. Brannagh's pilot helps load it. The ferry-folk keep a cold-house for the drowned. The Tidewarden will remember this kindness in Session 3.

**How it ends.** The eels flee or are beaten. If the party treated the body with respect, go to Scene 4. If someone asks "What's under the water here?", the pilot points down: "The bell." Go to Scene 5. Otherwise, row home and go to Scene 6.

### Scene 4: The hooded ferryman (optional)

**Where and why.** On the sandbank, after the eels, or at the Old Shore's dock that evening. A hooded figure appears beside the dead ferryman, or asks the party to carry him across the water.

> **SAY:** "There's someone standing in the ferry's stern who wasn't there a moment ago. Hooded, tall, holding the same long oar as the dead man, and the oar is dripping. His voice is like water over stones. 'You found him. Will you carry him home? I would, but I carry others now.'"

**What's really going on.** This is the Tidewarden. He never lies. He speaks in riddles. He wants the dead carried to rest, and the Heart returned to Ossa's bell.

**The Tidewarden** (Specter; he doesn't fight).
- *Voice:* low, slow, like water over stones.
- *Mannerism:* never looks straight at anyone; the oar drips steadily the whole time.
- *Wants in this scene:* the body treated kindly. Then, a promise about the Heart.
- *First words:* "You found him. Will you carry him home?"
- *Sample lines:* "I paid for my passage once. Everyone does." · "The bell is waiting for what was taken. So is everyone under it." · "Ask me one thing. I'll answer true. Then I'll ask one thing back."

**What they can learn here:** one true answer to one question, in a riddle. If they ask about Tam: "He came looking for a road to the bell, and someone took the road out of his head." If they ask who the dead man is: "He was me. I set him down when I took up the oar." In return he asks: "Will the Heart come home?" Any honest answer is fine.

**If they…** pay him in memory (he asks only a mote, a small thing): he will offer passage to the bell in an air pocket, now or in Session 3. Refuse, and he simply nods and is gone.

**How it ends.** He's gone between one drip and the next.

### Scene 5: Down to the bell (optional)

**Where and why.** Just off the sandbank, the top of Old Pellmoor's Ossa Belfry stands in the deep water about forty feet down. The party goes because they want to see the bell, the Tidewarden offered, or the Heart is humming toward it.

> **SAY:** "You go down through water so clear and still it feels like falling through glass. Below you a whole street opens out, doors and windows and a leaning spire, and in the middle of it a bell-tower rises like a finger pointing at the sky. Inside the open belfry hangs a great dark bell with no Heart in it. Around it, pale figures float upright with their eyes open, singing without breath. One of them rises to meet you: a woman in a soaked ferry coat, hair drifting, eyes too bright."

**What's really going on.** The woman is the Cantor: Ondra Sallow, a ferry-woman who drowned 260 years ago and leads the Drowned Choir. Mother Sallow is her descendant. The Cantor won't attack anyone who answers her truthfully. She attacks liars and anyone who defaces the bell. She wants to be remembered by name, and released.

**Breath.** Unless the Tidewarden gave them an air pocket, start counting breath. Getting down takes two or three turns, the conversation a few rounds, getting up two turns. That's tight but doable. Say each character's remaining rounds out loud every so often. If anyone runs out, give them a turn's warning before the first Exhaustion level, and remember they lose it all the moment they surface.

**The Cantor (Ondra Sallow)** (Ghost; she does not fight tonight unless the bell is attacked).
- *Voice:* she sings everything, in lines that sound like old hymns. Speak slowly, with a little tune.
- *Mannerism:* tilts her head as if listening to something very far away before each line.
- *Wants in this scene:* the truth. Who do you grieve? And, if they have it, the Heart.
- *First words:* "You have come down to the bell. Good. Tell me, who are you grieving? Do not lie to me. The dead can tell."
- *Sample lines:* "Say the name. Only the name. The water keeps the rest." · "A man came looking for a path to me. He never arrived." · "The Heart was taken from us. Ask the ferry-folk what they owe the dead."

**What they can learn here:**
- **Tam came to find a safe path to her and never arrived.** Free if anyone mentions Tam or Ila. This is another source on how Tam died; with Brannagh's or a Mere Memory, the Court's part is clear.
- **The Heart belongs in this bell.** Free.
- **A verse of Ossa's hymn,** if they answer truthfully: Advantage on the next saving throw against a Drowned Singer.
- **The full release verse,** four lines that let a spirit set down its song, if someone shares a sincere memory of a person who has died. The player can keep the details private and describe only the feeling. If your table is shy, she accepts someone grieving on Ila's behalf.

**If they…**
- **…answer truthfully:** she sings the name back. The water warms. She teaches the hymn verse.
- **…share a real memory of someone who died:** she teaches the release verse too. Give that player Heroic Inspiration.
- **…lie, or refuse her question:** her eyes go dark and the Choir moves. See [the Drowned Singers](#drowned-singers-at-the-belfry). She keeps singing and doesn't join the fight.
- **…swim up to the bell:** she raises a hand and asks their purpose. Returning the Heart earns safe access. Attacking or scraping the bell after that warning makes a Singer intervene.
- **…brought the Heart and want to ring the bell tonight:** let them; it's a wild and wonderful early choice. Before anyone fits the Heart, **say the Toll and wait for a yes**: "Ossa's Toll is a memory of someone who has died. The Ringer chooses it, and it's gone for good. If you say no, the bell doesn't ring and nothing is taken." Ila may not be the Ringer; she's fourteen and has just lost her father, so if she's here she stands beside an adult who rings it. If they say yes, use the bell-ringing text in Session 3's plan, record the Toll in the Memory ledger, and record "They bring the Heart down and ring Ossa tonight" in Foresight.
- **…use a druid's swimming Wild Shape:** no breath clock for the druid. The Cantor reads an animal shape as a lie unless it says its own name.

**How it ends.** They surface: with the verse, with a fight behind them, or with the bell rung. Row home. Go to Scene 6.

### Scene 6: Back on the shore

**Where and why.** The Old Shore, late afternoon. Mother Sallow is waiting on the dock with her ledger, because she promised to pay, and because something is wrong with the ledger.

> **SAY:** "Mother Sallow is sitting on an upturned crate at the end of the dock, a heavy ledger open across her knees. She doesn't look up. She runs one green-stained finger down the inside of the spine, where a page should be and isn't. 'Forty years I've kept this,' she says. 'Somebody's been in it.'"

**What's really going on.** The missing page lists the children the Court questioned over the last two years. Brother Eld, the village friar, took it. Ila's name is on it. That's Session 3. Tonight, just let them see the torn edge.

**What they can learn here:** a page is missing from the recent register; it was torn out carefully, by someone who knew where to look. Don't name Eld unless the players work it out; if they ask who could get at the ledger, Sallow says, "Me. Ila. And the chapel, when they borrow it for the Tithe."

**How it ends.** Mother Sallow pays them for the ferry and asks the question that ends the session.

### Running the fights (Session 2)

All of these are written for four level-3 characters. Foresight shows the difficulty for your actual party. Water makes everything harder than its numbers: breath is the real clock.

#### Memory-eels at the sandbank

*Six memory-eels. Each: AC 13, 13 HP, swim 30 ft.*
- **Setup:** the eels circle in the deep water 10 to 20 feet off the sand. Anyone wading, swimming or standing at the water's edge is a target. Anyone sitting still in a boat is ignored for the first round.
- **On their turn:** an eel swims in and **Bites** (+4 to hit, 1d8 + 2 piercing). If the bite deals damage, the target makes a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw; on a failure the player chooses one small memory their character loses until their next long rest (a breakfast, a song's second verse, a friend's eye colour). Write it in the Memory ledger as kind "Eel." Next turn, the same eel tries to **Coil**: a DC 12 Strength saving throw, or 3d4 bludgeoning damage and Grappled (escape DC 12), and it drags the character 10 feet under.
- **Describe hits:** "Something like a cold wet rope whips round your calf, and for a moment you can't remember what you had for breakfast." **Misses:** "A pale shape slides past your hand and is gone."
- **Retreat:** they flee when only two are left, or the moment someone raises the dead ferryman's oar.
- **Scale on the fly:** three players: four eels. Five players: eight. If the party is struggling, the eels lose interest in anyone who climbs back into the skiff.
- **Non-lethal outcomes:** a character who drops to 0 HP in the water floats up; the eels lose interest in anything that stops struggling. The pilot hauls them into the skiff. After the fight, let them take a short rest on the sand before any dive: don't chain this straight into the Singers.

#### Drowned Singers at the belfry

*Two Drowned Singers (each AC 12, 22 HP, swim 40 ft, never need to breathe) and two memory-eels. Only if they lie to the Cantor or attack the bell.*
- **Setup:** the Singers rise from the belfry, one on each side of the party. The eels stay near the surface and harry anyone left in the boat or treading water.
- **Round 1:** one Singer uses **Wail of Names**: everyone within 30 feet who can hear it makes a DC 11 Wisdom save, taking 2d4 psychic damage and becoming Frightened until the end of their next turn on a failure (half damage, no fear, on a success). It recharges on a 5 or 6 on a d6 at the start of its turn.
- **Each round:** the other Singer uses **Cold Grasp** (+4 to hit, 1d6 + 2 bludgeoning plus 1d6 cold) on the nearest diver. On a hit the diver is Grappled (escape DC 12), and the Singer pulls them 10 feet deeper. That costs them turns of breath; say so.
- **Describe hits:** "Fingers like wet stone close on your wrist, and the cold climbs to your elbow." **Misses:** "Its hand closes on the water where you were."
- **When it ends:** a character who sings the response hymn as an action stops the Singers attacking the whole group for an hour. Make sure the players remember they know it. The Singers also never pursue anyone above the surface: going up always works.
- **Scale on the fly:** three players: one Singer. Five players: a third Singer. Show the Singers rising a round before they arrive. If anyone hits 2 levels of Exhaustion from breath, have the Singers pause and watch: the dead don't want more company.
- **Non-lethal outcomes:** a diver who drops to 0 HP is released, and the Choir lifts them gently to the surface. They're Unconscious and need help, but they're breathing. The paralysis of an ordinary ghoul is removed from these Singers on purpose: a Paralyzed diver would drown.

#### The Mere road cart (if Ila was taken)

*A Hushman Sergeant (AC 15, 52 HP) and three Hushmen (AC 12, 32 HP).*
- **Setup:** two Hushmen walk beside the cart, one rides on the tailboard, the Sergeant rides up front beside the ferry-folk driver.
- **Each round:** the Hushmen keep the cart between themselves and the party, use **Arrest** (DC 12 Strength save or Grappled) on anyone who reaches the tailboard, and shout for the next checkpoint. The Sergeant attacks twice and uses **Command** to give a Hushman an extra attack with +1d4. They don't drive the cart on while it's under attack.
- **Retreat:** the Sergeant yields the cart when two Hushmen drop, or the moment the ferry-folk driver unhitches the horse.
- **Scale on the fly:** three players: drop one Hushman. Five players: add one.
- **Non-lethal outcomes:** a downed character is bound and left at the ford. Ila stays inside the cart the whole time, and is never hurt.

### Pacing (Session 2)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:15 | Recap, check Ila (the cart, if needed, adds 30 to 45 minutes) |
| 0:15 to 0:50 | Scene 1: the Night Song, and Hadrik if you use him |
| 0:50 to 1:20 | Scene 2: the Pilots' Hall, and the crossing |
| 1:20 to 2:10 | Scene 3: the sandbank and the eels (break after) |
| 2:10 to 3:10 | Scenes 4 and 5: the Tidewarden, the dive and the Cantor |
| 3:10 to 3:30 | Scene 6: the torn ledger and the closing question |

- **Running long:** skip Hadrik. Skip Scene 4; the Tidewarden appears in Session 3 instead. If they don't dive tonight, the dive happens in Session 3 when they return the Heart.
- **Running short:** add a night on the shore (the Mere Memory save); let them take the ferryman home to the cold-house; run Hadrik; have a ferry-folk widow ask them to speak her husband's name at the stones.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop when the eels flee and the fog lifts off the sandbank. Ask "Who was on the ferry?" anyway; it works just as well.

### If you get stuck (Session 2)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **The singing starts again.** Even by day, faint, from under the boat. Someone hears their own name.
2. **The Heart pulls.** If anyone carries it, it hums louder pointing one way: toward the belfry.
3. **Brannagh's pilot speaks up.** "My gran used to say the eels guard what the Mere's ashamed of." Pilots know things; use them to nudge.

**Names for Pellmoor** (cross one off when you use it):
- **Ferry-folk:** Wat Reedby, Agna Fenn, Dob Crane, Hanna Pike, Lise Ashcombe, Rowan Dabber, Maisie Sedge, Teo Rushford, Granny Weir, Bethan Lowe.
- **Pilots:** Sully Marsh, Hannet Bow, young Pim Rowe, Ida Sounding.
- **Hushmen:** Hushman Garrick Penn, Hushman Wilma Strand, Hushman Osric Fane, Hushman Bettony Ward.
- **Sailors:** Mags Haliburton (Baldurian cook), Darro Venisse (Tethyrian mate), Kesk Ironmantle (dwarf rigger).
- **Merchants:** Lantanese tinker Fibbet Quisk, Amnian spice factor Sadira Menoch, Corvanese reed-dye seller Old Tamsin.

### End of session 2

**The closing question:** "Who was on the ferry?" Then: "Before we wrap up, let's each say one thing we'll remember from tonight."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened** (press **The party did this** on each card): "They sing the response to the Night Song," "They row out to find the missing ferry," "They fight the memory-eels" or "They slip past the eels," "They dive to the drowned belfry," "They answer the Cantor truthfully" or "They lie to the Cantor," "They share a sincere memory of someone who has died," "They take the dead ferryman home," "They speak with the hooded ferryman," and any Hadrik or cart play.
- **World-state facts to check:** the Cantor's release verse (Learned, if anyone shared a sincere memory), the Drowned Choir (still Hunting unless Ossa rang), the Choir's clock (up if they lied to the Cantor or Hadrik poured), Ossa's Heart and Ossa's bell (only if they rang it), and Ila Harrow (Free, if they saved her from the cart).
- **Memory ledger:** eel losses as kind "Eel" (they come back after a long rest), Mere Memories as kind "Mere," and a Toll if Ossa rang.
- **Player wiki, afterwards:** press **Finish**, then **Send to wiki** on Brannagh Wick, The Night Song, The Cantor and The Ossa Belfry (send the Belfry and the Cantor only if they dove or were told of them).

**Rewards:**
- **Level:** none. They stay level 3.
- **Coin:** Mother Sallow pays 15 gp in mixed Faerûnian coin, everything in her tea tin, for finding the ferry. A party that refuses it earns her respect for good.
- **Treasure:** a net bag in the ferry's hold holds 1d4 + 1 memory-pearls: small glass spheres, each holding one preserved sensation (warm bread, rain on reed, a child's laugh). A Reckoner pays 10 gp each. Holding one and remembering it is free.
- **Knowledge:** the hymn verse (Advantage on the next save against a Drowned Singer) and the release verse, if earned.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** for raising the ferryman's oar, for a true answer to the Cantor, for talking Hadrik down with his own faith, for covering Mother Sallow.

### Places at a glance (Session 2)

- **The Mere Memory Shore** (Scene 1). *Light:* dusk going to dark. *Footing:* shingle, then black, cold water that goes deep fast. *Sound:* the song; the spell Silence doesn't stop it. *Exits:* the shore path back to the Old Shore. *Cover:* the crowd of ferry-folk.
- **The Mere road** (if Ila was taken). *Light:* an hour past dawn. *Footing:* a raised causeway, a drowned causeway beside it, and a ford. *Sound:* the cart's wheels make none. *Exits:* along the causeway, or into the marsh. *Cover:* reeds, the checkpoint hut and the cart itself (Ila is inside: keep area spells off it).
- **The Pilots' Hall** (Scene 2). *Light:* morning. *Footing:* one long room hung with charts of drowned streets. *Sound:* Brannagh shouting tide-times. *Exits:* the door to the Quays. *Cover:* chart tables.
- **The sandbank** (Scene 3). *Light:* open sky over the Mere. *Footing:* wet sand about 30 feet across, deep water all round. *Sound:* nothing, except the pale rings moving on the water. *Exits:* the skiff. *Cover:* the grounded ferry; anyone sitting still in a boat is ignored for the first round.
- **Ossa's belfry** (Scene 5). *Light:* dim, but the water is glass-clear. *Footing:* none: swimming, 40 feet down, a drowned street below. *Sound:* singing without breath. *Exits:* up; going up always works, and the Singers never follow anyone above the surface. *Cover:* the belfry's arches. Breath is the clock.

### Rumours on the Old Shore (Session 2, d6)

Five are true. The one marked *false* is what frightened people say.

1. The marsh ferry never came back. A pilot swears she saw it sitting on a sandbank in the middle of the Mere, and nobody will row out to it.
2. Whatever is singing at night, don't answer it unless you know the words.
3. A priest of Kelemvor off a Baldurian ship means to bless the Mere and lay the singers to rest.
4. Something near the sandbank bites, and afterwards you can't remember your own breakfast.
5. Brannagh Wick knows why Tam Harrow went out that night, but she won't say it to a Court face.
6. The Drowned Choir takes anyone who weeps on the shore. (*False:* it hunts the forgetful, never the grieving.)

sessions.summary: The Night Song, a missing ferry on a sandbank, memory-eels, and a question from the deep: who are you grieving?

plays.title: They search Brother Eld's desk
plays.why: Mother Sallow names him, and the page has to be somewhere.
plays.readAloud: The desk is very neat. Too neat. The drawer that sticks has been oiled.
plays.response: Once they have access, the page is found without a roll. If the three-day bargain with Mother Sallow held, she brings Eld's chapel key and says nothing. A good search also turns up the matching Court forms and a recent patrol entry recording Tam Harrow's interrogation. Failure only costs time and brings Eld in from the vestry, frightened.
plays.consequence: The party holds the missing page, with Ila's name on it.
plays.fallback: If they won't search, Eld brings them the page himself the next morning, unable to sleep.
plays.tells: Players ask when the chapel is empty, or how to get Eld out of it.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (Investigation) DC 14 finds it quickly, with the forms and the patrol entry. The essential clue is never lost to a failed check. Locate Object on 'the page' needs a sample; Detect Thoughts on Eld shows a man frozen in fear (see any-l3-truth-and-minds).
plays.later: The patrol entry is a source on Tam's death. S4: if they took the forms, Rook (S6) values them as evidence.
plays.keywords: eld, desk, search, chapel, page, ledger, find, investigate, steal, forms

plays.title: They ask who was on the ferry
plays.why: Session 2 ended on the question, so the players will ask it first.
plays.readAloud: Mother Sallow turns the ledger to the ferry roll and taps one line with her pipe. "Abel Tarn. Rowed the eastern ferry since before I was born. Funny thing. Nobody remembers him getting old."
plays.response: The ledger names the eastern ferryman as Old Abel Tarn. If the party met the hooded ferryman, they can put it together, and Sallow nods: 'Then he's rowing the dead now. Good. Somebody should.' The Tidewarden confirms it if asked. Tarn's body goes to the ferry-folk cold-house and is sung for that night.
plays.consequence: The party knows the dead ferryman was the Tidewarden's old body, and that the Mere's spirits were once Pellmoor's own people.
plays.fallback: If nobody asks, Mother Sallow mentions it while she shows them where the page was torn out.
plays.tells: Players ask Mother Sallow about the dead ferryman, or ask the Tidewarden who he was.
plays.rules: No check for the name. A Study check, Intelligence (Religion) DC 12, or the players guessing, connects him to the Tidewarden; if nobody does, the Tidewarden says it himself at the ferry-stair.
plays.keywords: who was on the ferry, ferryman, dead man, Abel Tarn, Tarn, ledger, ferry roll, tidewarden, body
plays.scene: Scene 1: Who was on the ferry

plays.title: They confront Eld privately and take the page
plays.why: A quiet confrontation protects the children and lets Eld save face.
plays.readAloud: "The page is in my desk, Mother. The Court asked me to keep it. I didn't read it, because I didn't want to. But I know what it says. I copied the names onto the Court's forms myself."
plays.response: Eld asks for absolution before anything else. He gives them the name of one child on the list whose family can still be warned, and then he leaves Pellmoor on the next ferry for the ash fields of Kell's Crossing, to pray among the dead fields.
plays.consequence: Eld is gone. One family is warned in time.
plays.tells: Players wait until Eld is alone.
plays.later: S4: Eld is not at the Assembly; use an unnamed Court chaplain. S9: he can be found at Kell's Crossing, in the ash, if the party goes there (s09-ring-calla).
plays.keywords: confront, eld, private, page, absolution, forgive, leave

plays.title: They expose Eld in front of the village
plays.why: The page names children. Some parties want justice in public.
plays.readAloud: Nobody shouts. That is the worst of it. The ferry-folk just look at him, one family at a time, until he can't stand it.
plays.response: The village turns on him. Eld flees to Hallowmere that night in shame and becomes a Court chaplain. Mother Sallow says nothing kind and nothing cruel.
plays.consequence: Eld is in Hallowmere, humiliated and useful to the Court.
plays.tells: Players gather the Old Shore, or read names aloud at the chapel door.
plays.later: S4: Eld is at the Assembly as a Court chaplain and will not meet their eyes. The Court learns what the party knows about the page.
plays.keywords: expose, public, accuse, shame, eld, village, crowd, justice

plays.title: They forgive Eld
plays.why: Eld is pliant, sorry, and offers help; mercy is a real option.
plays.readAloud: Eld cries like a man who has been holding it in for two years. When he stops, he asks what he can do, and he means it.
plays.response: Eld cries like a man who has been holding it in for two years. When he stops, he asks what he can do. The Court wants a chaplain at the Hallowmere masque and has written to him; he will go and be the party's inside ear. He still writes to the Court, and tells the party what he writes. His loyalty depends on how they protect him and the children. Foreshadow any renewed Court pressure before he wavers.
plays.consequence: The party has a source inside the Church, and Eld travels to Hallowmere.
plays.tells: A cleric or a kind character responds to his request for absolution.
plays.later: S4: Eld meets their eyes at the Assembly and slips them a note about Haldric's armory (s04-eld-at-assembly). S6: he can testify at the oath-duel if protected.
plays.keywords: forgive, absolve, mercy, eld, informant, redemption, spare

plays.title: They tell Ila the truth about her name on the list
plays.why: Ila recognises her own name and begins to cry; someone will speak to her.
plays.readAloud: Ila reads her own name twice. Then she says, very quietly, "That's why he was scared. Not of the water. Of them."
plays.response: Ila trusts people who tell her the truth about hard things. If they explain what the list means, she asks to decide the Heart's fate with them, and asks whether she can come. If they say "don't worry about it," she stops talking to that character.
plays.consequence: Ila's trust is earned or lost here.
plays.tells: A player turns to Ila instead of Eld.
plays.later: S3: she argues for returning the Heart to the Mere. Taking her along keeps her close and in danger (s03-take-ila-along); hiding her with the Pilots' Hall keeps her safe (s03-hide-ila). If the party does neither and the Heart goes to the Court, she is arrested (s03-ila-arrested).
plays.keywords: ila, comfort, truth, list, name, cry, tell her, father

plays.title: They tell Ila "don't worry about it"
plays.why: Protective players try to spare a child the hard truth, and Ila hates that more than anything.
plays.readAloud: Ila looks at you for a long moment. Then she turns to someone else and asks them instead.
plays.response: She stops talking to that character for the rest of the act: polite, flat, and finished. She asks someone else the same question, and trusts whoever tells her the truth. The character can win her back only by telling her something true and hard, unprompted.
plays.consequence: Ila is closed to that character, and turns to someone else.
plays.fallback: If nobody tells her, she reads the page herself and says, 'Four hundred and ten. That's when Dad started locking the door.'
plays.tells: A player says "Don't worry", "It's nothing", or hides the page from her.
plays.rules: No check. Influence does not repair this; only the truth does.
plays.later: S3: someone else can still tell her the truth (s03-comfort-ila).
plays.keywords: don't worry, it's nothing, protect her, hide the page, lie to Ila, spare her

plays.title: They work out how Tam Harrow died
plays.why: By now the party likely holds two of the four sources.
plays.readAloud: It isn't a mystery anymore. It's a ferry with no cargo, a patrol in grey gloves, and a man who couldn't remember the way home.
plays.response: Confirm it when any two sources agree: a Court patrol took Tam's memory of the route to the belfry and left him on the water; he fell in and drowned; the Choir kept his body, but did not kill him. Let Ila hear it from whoever she trusts most.
plays.consequence: The Court is responsible for Tam's death, and the party knows it.
plays.fallback: If they have only one source, Mother Sallow supplies the second from the ledger: Tam's name, with a Court mark beside it.
plays.tells: Players line up the patrol entry, the Cantor's words, Brannagh's story, or a Mere Memory.
plays.later: S6: Wren's confession (she gave the Court Tam's name) lands hard. Ila's anger shapes her choices for the rest of the campaign.
plays.keywords: tam, death, murder, how he died, clues, solve, patrol, route, memory taken

plays.title: They return the Heart to the Mere
plays.why: Ila, Mother Sallow and the Cantor all point this way.
plays.readAloud: The Tidewarden is waiting at the end of the old dock, oar dripping. He doesn't ask where you're going.
plays.response: The ferry-stair is safest, and the Choir guards it. The Tidewarden holds a pocket of breathable air around anyone who accepts peaceful passage; Mother Sallow's hymn earns that passage without any memory price. Diving magic or a sound alternative plan also works. Ila is fourteen: she may come to the stair, but she stays in the ferry with an adult and never goes down with the divers, so check session-zero Off-limits. At the belfry, the Cantor asks whether they mean to ring it.
plays.consequence: The Heart is home. The Choir is quieter while it stays there.
plays.fallback: If they hesitate at the water's edge, Ila holds out her hands for the bundle, and the Tidewarden's ferry waits for whoever carries it.
plays.tells: Players ask how to reach the drowned belfry safely.
plays.rules: If not using the Tidewarden: 2024 Suffocation and Frigid Water apply.
plays.later: Ringing is a separate choice with a Toll (next play). The Court still wants the Heart (S4).
plays.keywords: return, give back, mere, belfry, tidewarden, choir, cantor, put back

plays.title: They ring Ossa
plays.why: With the Heart at the bell, the question is only who pays.
plays.readAloud: The bell rings from under the water. It is deep and slow and it makes the whole Mere ripple. Every grey face on the shore lifts toward the sound. The Drowned fall silent, and one voice, very old and very clear, speaks a single name. Then the Mere is only water again, and the reeds bend in a breeze that smells of rain.
plays.response: Warn the Ringer and wait for a yes: 'Ossa will take a memory of the dead from you, and it will be heavy. You won't know which until it's paid.' Never say which: after the bell rings you choose it, from what the table knows of the character, and the player plays the loss (Part 2.7). Ila may volunteer; she is fourteen and has just lost her father, so offer the Toll to an adult instead and let her stand beside them. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. If they ring it, the Choir rests, and Mother Sallow remembers her husband Davin and the night of the Wrongweather. If anyone sings the Cantor's release verse afterward, Ondra speaks her own name and goes quiet.
plays.consequence: Ossa is rung. The dead of the Mere may rest.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer is unsure, the Cantor waits. A bell that waited four hundred years can wait a night.
plays.tells: A player asks what ringing would do, or what it costs.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (kind: Toll, bell: Ossa). Weight: Heavy (Ossa is the party's first or second bell). The deceased person need not be a loved one (v5 2.11). Ila may not be the Ringer.
plays.later: Concord: 1 of 6. S4: no Heart bargain at the Assembly. The Court withdraws collectors from the newly quiet Mere for a while (Court clock +1). S27: the Choir can sing at the summit if released.
plays.keywords: ring, ossa, toll, bell, ring the bell, memory of the dead, ringer

plays.title: They sing the Cantor's release verse after Ossa rings
plays.why: If they learned the verse in Session 2, this is the moment it was for.
plays.readAloud: The verse is short. When it ends, the Cantor sings her own name, Ondra Sallow, in a voice nobody has heard for two hundred and sixty years. Then she goes quiet, and so does everyone else under the water.
plays.response: The singer must sincerely commemorate a dead person. Ondra and the remaining Choir are released. Released spirits may return once, willingly, as allies; they are never compelled back.
plays.consequence: The Drowned Choir is released.
plays.fallback: If nobody learned the verse, Mother Sallow can rebuild it from the restored ledger (s03-sallow-rebuilds-verse); the Cantor will wait.
plays.tells: A player asks whether the Choir can be freed now.
plays.later: S22/S27: the Cantor may return once as an ally. S28: Mother Sallow sings the last verse with Ila.
plays.keywords: release, verse, sing, cantor, ondra, free the choir, choir, rest

plays.title: They carry the Heart to Hallowmere
plays.why: Some parties want allies (the Dawn Order, the Bellwrights) before deciding.
plays.readAloud: The bundle hums all the way to the edge of the Mere road, and then, as the reeds give way to grey hedges, it goes quiet, as if it knows where it's going.
plays.response: Act II begins early. Brannagh can ferry them across the Mere (three days to the capital instead of six) and knows a landing that skips the first checkpoint. Faerûnians need the Chancellor's invitation or a writ: the grey-sealed letter reaches them at the first checkpoint by the Court's own rider, and they can accept it there (s03-accept-invitation). Ila's place in this trip is s03-take-ila-along or s03-hide-ila.
plays.consequence: The party is on the road to Hallowmere with Ossa's Heart.
plays.tells: Players ask who in the capital opposes the Court.
plays.later: S4: the Gate Clerk already has their names (+2 to Persuasion DCs). Maudrin's bargain targets the Heart they carry. Concord: Ossa still needs a return to the Mere (the Tidewarden ferries the Ringer once they hold it again).
plays.keywords: hallowmere, capital, carry, take it, dawn order, bellwrights, travel, leave pellmoor, road
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: They keep the Heart in Pellmoor and defend the village
plays.why: A protective party won't let the Court take anything from the Old Shore.
plays.readAloud: Quill comes back with every Hushman the Landing House has, and a written deadline nailed to the chapel door. Behind him, forty foreign masts stand very still on the water and do nothing at all.
plays.response: Act II begins as a siege. Quill issues a deadline; villagers prepare shelter and an evacuation route; the party negotiates, resists a patrol, or leads an escape. The foreign ships stay neutral, but Brannagh can close the Mere to Court boats: no pilot, no crossing. Intercepted orders point to the Hallowmere vault.
plays.consequence: Pellmoor is under Court pressure and will be changed by it.
plays.fallback: If the siege drags, the Pilots' Hall offers to smuggle the Heart out by night.
plays.tells: Players ask about defences, the Landing House's strength, or who would fight.
plays.rules: Use the siege patrol (enc-s04-siege-patrol) scaled for four level-3 characters. Show retreat routes and the deadline before any fighting.
plays.later: S4: a short siege outline replaces the gate scene; the intercepted orders lead to Hallowmere. The Old Shore's trust is earned for the rest of the campaign. Faerûnian traders note which side the party took.
plays.keywords: keep, defend, protect, siege, stay, fight the court, village, pellmoor, barricade
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: They send the Heart to the Chancellor
plays.why: Greedy or desperate parties take the Court's reward.
plays.readAloud: The order comes back with the receipt, sealed in the same grey wax: the arrest of one Ila Harrow, listener, for questioning.
plays.response: Show the arrest order to the players before anyone acts on it. Give them a chance to warn, hide, or escort Ila (s03-take-ila-along, s03-hide-ila). Check session-zero Off-limits: Ila is arrested Off-screen, held in a room with a lamp and a bowl of soup, never harmed. If the party does nothing, the Hushmen come at dawn (s03-ila-arrested).
plays.consequence: The Court holds the Heart and wants Ila.
plays.tells: Players ask what the Court would pay, or want to end the danger quickly.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin is delighted and offers Ila's Tithe-exemption instead of a bargain (s04-exemption-releases-ila if she was taken, s04-exemption-for-ila if not). If Ila is taken, she is held in the Hall of Tithes (rescue alongside Tessa in S6). Concord: Ossa needs the Heart recovered (s04-ask-ossa-back).
plays.keywords: give, maudrin, court, chancellor, sell to the court, reward, surrender
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: They sell the Heart to Master Venn
plays.why: A Faerûnian buyer offers real gold and a way out of Corvane's problems.
plays.readAloud: Venn counts the gold onto the table himself, coin by coin, smiling. "The Gilded Heron sails in three days. Your relic will be admired in Athkatla by people who have never heard of a Toll. Isn't that a kindness?"
plays.response: Venn pays 600 gp (Influence, Persuasion, DC 15 raises it to 900; his buyer pays 5,000). The Heart goes aboard the Gilded Heron, which needs a pilot to leave the Mere and a day to cross the Seam. Ila learns within the hour. Brannagh Wick can delay the ship one day by refusing a pilot.
plays.consequence: The Heart is on a foreign ship. The clock is three days, maybe four (s03-delay-heron adds one).
plays.fallback: If the players regret it, Venn will sell it back for 1,200 gp or a heartkeep, and enjoy the profit.
plays.tells: Players ask what Venn would pay, or whether selling abroad keeps it from the Court.
plays.rules: Record the sale. The Heron leaves in 3 days; Brannagh can add 1; the Seam crossing takes 1 more.
plays.later: If it clears the Seam (s03-heron-sails): Ossa can't be rung and Concord is impossible until it is recovered. The safety valve is any-heron-wrecks. S4: the Court is furious with Venn, and with the party. S28: Ila never forgives it.
plays.keywords: sell, venn, merchant, gold, coster, gilded heron, ship, abroad, athkatla, profit, buyer
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: They board the Gilded Heron and take the Heart back
plays.why: If the Heart was sold, regret (or Ila) arrives quickly.
plays.readAloud: The Gilded Heron rides at anchor beyond the last pier, lamps lit, a drowned church spire just under her keel.
plays.response: Three ways: board her at night past two Coster guards and a mate; persuade Brannagh to deny her a pilot until Venn deals (s03-delay-heron); or buy it back (s03-buy-back-from-venn). Venn prefers money to trouble and folds once a guard drops or the Pilots' Hall turns against him. Invisibility, Misty Step and Pass without Trace make boarding easier but the Heron's lamps pick up a shimmer on the water; the mate has Passive Perception 14.
plays.consequence: The Heart is recovered, or it sails.
plays.fallback: If they fail, the Heron's first mate, a Baldurian who toasts the Gull's Wager, offers to 'lose' it overboard for 100 gp.
plays.tells: Players ask where the Heron is anchored, or who pilots her out.
plays.rules: Boarding: Dexterity (Stealth) DC 15 per character, or the encounter. Venn is Indifferent; he becomes Hostile only if humiliated in public.
plays.later: Recovered by force or theft: Venn holds a grudge and pays Quill to watch the party (S4 Court knows them). If they sail before it is done: s03-heron-sails.
plays.keywords: recover, steal back, board, ship, gilded heron, venn, buy back, pilot, retrieve
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: They accept the Chancellor's invitation
plays.why: The letter arrives whatever they chose, and it promises safety and answers.
plays.readAloud: "To those who carried the Heart of Ossa from Pellmoor: the Quiet Court extends its gratitude and its invitation. The Chancellor would be honoured by your presence at the Quiet Assembly in Hallowmere, in ten days. You will be safe. You will be remembered. Nothing you carry will be asked of you that you do not wish to give. M. Vesk, Quiet Chancellor, Warden of Silence."
plays.response: The grey seal makes the letter a writ of passage for everyone named in it, Stormborn included. Brannagh offers the Mere crossing. The party is still level 3; level 4 comes after the Hallowmere investigation in S6.
plays.consequence: The party is expected at the Quiet Assembly.
plays.tells: Players read the letter twice, or ask whether it's a trap.
plays.later: S4: the gate accepts the letter as a writ. Maudrin has read Quill's report and knows their faces.
plays.keywords: invitation, letter, assembly, accept, go, hallowmere, writ, chancellor

plays.title: They refuse the invitation
plays.why: A letter from the people who killed Tam is easy to burn.
plays.readAloud: The letter curls in the fire. The grey wax doesn't melt. It sits in the ashes, perfectly round, until someone picks it up.
plays.response: Don't force the trip. Captain Rook or Wren Caddock brings the investigation to them instead (a Dawn Order rider, or a Bellwright courier asking for help). The wax seal still works as a writ if they keep it.
plays.consequence: The Court takes note of the refusal.
plays.tells: Players call it a trap, or burn it.
plays.later: S4: start with Rook's or Wren's request instead of the Assembly; Maudrin's bargain comes later, by letter. The Court's clock ticks.
plays.keywords: refuse, burn, decline, ignore, trap, invitation, letter, no

plays.title: They burn the Chancellor's letter
plays.why: Some tables answer a polite threat with fire.
plays.readAloud: The paper catches and curls, but the grey seal only hisses in the flame. When the fire is out, it is still there in the ash, whole and cool. Mother Sallow says, "That's Court wax. It remembers."
plays.response: The paper burns; the seal does not. It still works as a writ if they keep it, and the Court will invite them again. Treat it as a refusal: Captain Rook or Wren Caddock brings the investigation to them instead, and Maudrin's bargain comes later, by letter.
plays.consequence: The party has refused the Court, loudly.
plays.fallback: If they want the seal gone, it sinks in the Mere and is on the doorstep at dawn.
plays.tells: A player holds the letter over a candle, tears it up, or throws it in the Mere.
plays.rules: No check. The seal resists fire and Thaumaturgy alike; Dispel Magic quiets its hum for a minute, no more.
plays.later: S4: start with Rook's or Wren's request instead of the Assembly (as s03-refuse-invitation).
plays.keywords: burn the letter, tear it up, destroy the invitation, throw it away, fire, seal

plays.title: They take Ila with them
plays.why: Ila asked whether she could come, and the party does not want her alone with Hushmen at the door.
plays.readAloud: 'I'll carry my own bag,' Ila says. 'And I'll tell you when the water's wrong. That's all I'm good for, so far.'
plays.response: Mother Sallow allows it only if an adult promises to bring her home. Ila is fourteen: she travels with the party and is never put in combat or described in harm; check session-zero Off-limits and give her a quiet place at every scene's edge. She keeps the Harrow house key and sings the response hymn at the Gate when asked.
plays.consequence: Ila is in the party's care, which makes her a lever for the Court.
plays.fallback: If the party hesitates, Sallow says 'She is safest with people who are looked for.'
plays.tells: A player says 'you're coming with us', or asks Mother Sallow's leave.
plays.rules: No check. Brannagh gives a pilot-letter for the Mere crossing.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin notices her at the masque and offers her exemption as a bargain. S6: Ila can reach the Hall of Tithes, which Wren's plan uses. S28: Ila grew up in the party's shadow.
plays.keywords: take ila, bring ila, travel, companion, child, escort ila

plays.title: They hide Ila at the Pilots' Hall
plays.why: The Court wants her; the Pilots' Hall is the safest roof in Pellmoor.
plays.readAloud: Brannagh looks at Ila over the sounding-line on her shoulder. 'Pilots' Hall has a loft nobody climbs. She'll have a hammock, a bell to ring if the gloves come, and a pilot on the stair.'
plays.response: Brannagh keeps Ila in the loft with a pilot on the stair, and the ferry-folk close ranks. Ila stays hidden until the party returns or the Court escalates. She argues, but accepts it if the party explains why; if they say 'don't worry', she stops speaking to that character.
plays.consequence: Ila is safe, and the Court's cart finds only an empty house.
plays.fallback: If nobody has a plan, Brannagh does it anyway.
plays.tells: A player asks Brannagh Wick where a child could sleep out of sight.
plays.rules: No check. The households that owe the party (s01-fill-the-quota) also offer a hiding place.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin's bargain is for the Heart, not Ila. S6: if the party told Maudrin where she was (s04-tell-where-ila), Hushmen go to the Pilots' Hall within two days. S28: Ila is hidden but angry.
plays.keywords: hide ila, pilots hall, safe house, protect ila, loft

plays.title: Hushmen come for Ila at dawn
plays.why: The Heart went to the Court and nobody sheltered her.
plays.readAloud: Grey wax on the Harrow door. Dorra Pell says it flatly: 'They came at first light. She went with her coat on and her head up.'
plays.response: Off-screen. Check session-zero Off-limits. Ila is taken by a Hushman Sergeant and two escorts and carried to Hallowmere, where she waits in the Hall of Tithes, a clean room with a bed. A courier from Brannagh's pilots can reach the cart before it leaves the Mere (s02-intercept-ila-cart applies on the road). Maudrin's offer will use her.
plays.consequence: Ila is under Court arrest.
plays.fallback: If the party reacts in time, Brannagh's pilots delay the cart one day.
plays.tells: A party that sold the Heart to Quill or the Chancellor leaves Ila in her father's house.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin offers Ila's release for a favour (s04-exemption-releases-ila). S6: rescue alongside Tessa (s06-rescue-tessa-with-ila).
plays.keywords: ila arrested, dawn, hushmen, taken, child arrested

plays.title: Quill returns with a second Hushman
plays.why: The lie held, or the party named Mother Sallow to him; either way Quill's report is out.
plays.readAloud: Quill stands in the chapel door with a second Hushman behind him. 'Good morning,' he says. 'I was reviewing my notes and found a gap in my notes, and I thought you'd want to help me fill it.'
plays.response: He asks the coat question again, and if Mother Sallow's name was given, he asks for her ledger. He is polite; the second Hushman is not. He wants a reason to search. Persuasion DC 16 on Quill buys a week. Hold Person or Suggestion on Quill works but the Landing House reads the hum as a confession.
plays.consequence: The Court's pressure rises one notch.
plays.fallback: If the party fights him, run s01-attack-quill.
plays.tells: The party has lied to Quill or named a villager to him in S1.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Quill (2024: 15 or his Intelligence of 10, whichever is higher). If bribed, he takes more gold and complains less.
plays.later: S4: the Gate Clerk raises Persuasion DCs by 2 if Quill is Suspicious (s04-refuse-courtesy-memory).
plays.keywords: quill returns, second hushman, search, ledger, mother sallow

plays.title: The three households warn the party
plays.why: The party filled the quota, so three Bellwright-sympathising households owe them.
plays.readAloud: A boy slips a folded net-tag under your door: a thread tied in three knots. Downstairs, the woman whose quota you filled says only, 'Not tonight. They're at the chapel.'
plays.response: The households warn the party when Hushmen move, offer a hiding place for Ila or the Heart, and later shelter villagers during a siege. They will not fight; they will lie. They do not ask for anything. Heroic Inspiration for a player who thanks them by name.
plays.consequence: The Old Shore has a back door.
plays.fallback: If nobody asks, the households send a child with a loaf.
plays.tells: Hushmen move in the village, or the party asks who can be trusted.
plays.rules: No check. A hiding place gives Advantage on Stealth checks to hide a person or bundle on the Old Shore.
plays.later: S4 (siege): they shelter villagers. S6: Wren already trusts the party.
plays.keywords: households, quota, warn, villagers owe, sympathisers

plays.title: They kill Brother Eld
plays.why: Eld wrote down the names of children for the Court.
plays.readAloud: Eld does not run. 'I knew it would be someone,' he says. 'I'd like to ask only that you tell Mother Sallow I tried to keep the page.'
plays.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill him?' A downed Eld can be bound. If he dies, the ferry-folk say nothing and the chapel stays shut. Say plainly that the only living witness to the Court's patrol entries is gone; the page and the forms still point at Quill and Hallowmere. No resurrection.
plays.consequence: Eld is dead. The Church notes it.
plays.fallback: If the player wavers, Eld offers the Heart's page and a name of a child to warn.
plays.tells: A player lifts a blade in the chapel, or waits for Eld on the Mere road.
plays.rules: Eld is a Priest Acolyte (CR 1/4) and can cast Silence once per day. A downed Eld can be knocked out instead of killed.
plays.later: S4: use an unnamed chaplain at the Assembly. S28: Mother Sallow knows who did it.
plays.keywords: kill eld, murder, chaplain, execute

plays.title: Brannagh denies the Heron a pilot
plays.why: The Heron needs a pilot to leave the Mere, and Brannagh runs the Pilots' Hall.
plays.readAloud: Brannagh counts the tide out loud and shakes her head. 'No pilot leaves this hall for the Heron today. She'll sit till Venn's patience runs out.'
plays.response: Brannagh can delay the ship one day by refusing a pilot; a second day costs the Pilots' Hall a favour and Venn a fine. The delay buys the party time to board or buy back the Heart. It also tells Venn exactly who is against him.
plays.consequence: The Heron's sailing is delayed by one day.
plays.fallback: If Brannagh refuses, a Baldurian mate offers to 'lose' the Heart overboard for 100 gp.
plays.tells: A player asks whether the Heron can be stopped without a fight.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on Brannagh (Friendly if Ila vouches). Each day of delay adds one to clock_ferry. At 6 the Hall suspends a crossing.
plays.later: S3: s03-heron-sails runs the clock out if the Heart is not recovered. Venn remembers.
plays.keywords: delay ship, pilot, pilots hall, brannagh, heron
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: The Gilded Heron sails with the Heart
plays.why: Three or four days pass and the Heart is still aboard.
plays.readAloud: The Heron slips her lines at the turn of the tide, a Pilots' Hall skiff ahead of her, and the last you see of her is a plum-coloured sail going into a wall of grey weather.
plays.response: Brannagh counts the days honestly. The Heron crosses the Seam in a day. The Heart is beyond Corvane. Ossa cannot be rung until it returns. Tell the table plainly what this closes (the Concord) and what stays open (the Second Dawn). Offer the safety valve if the table wants it: the Heron wrecks in the Wall and the Mere returns the Heart weeks later (any-heron-wrecks).
plays.consequence: Ossa's Heart is gone through the Seam.
plays.fallback: If the table is stunned, the Tidewarden says only: 'The Mere remembers what is taken from it.'
plays.tells: The party has not recovered the Heart by the end of the third or fourth day.
plays.rules: No check. Three days after the sale, four if Brannagh delayed once.
plays.later: S4: Maudrin hears of it from Quill's replacement (s04-tell-where). S28: Ila never forgives the sale. Any time: any-heron-wrecks, or any-ossa-written-off if the table moves on.
plays.keywords: heron sails, ship leaves, heart gone, seam, abroad
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: They buy the Heart back from Venn
plays.why: They sold it in haste, or Ila found out.
plays.readAloud: Venn spreads his ringed hands. 'Twelve hundred, friend, or a heartkeep. You see I am a reasonable man. I paid six, I lose nothing, and I was so looking forward to Athkatla.'
plays.response: Venn sells it back for 1,200 gp or a heartkeep and enjoys the profit. He remains Friendly; the party now owes him nothing and he thinks well of them. Persuasion DC 15 brings it to 900 gp. A heartkeep is a defining memory, chosen by the player.
plays.consequence: The Heart returns without a fight; Venn is a smiling creditor.
plays.fallback: If the party cannot pay, Brannagh offers to guarantee a loan.
plays.tells: A player asks what Venn wants for it, or counts out gold.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 for the discount.
plays.later: S4: the Court hears of the sale from Quill but Venn is not exposed.
plays.keywords: buy back, venn, pay, heartkeep, 1200 gp, heart
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: Mother Sallow rebuilds the release verse
plays.why: They missed the Cantor's verse, but Sallow's ledger can rebuild it.
plays.readAloud: Mother Sallow reads from the restored ledger in a low voice. 'It was a funeral verse, once. They sang it in my grandmother's time. I lost it with the rest.'
plays.response: Sallow reads the verse from the ledger and teaches it. It takes an hour. The verse is the same as the Cantor's: four lines and a sincere commemoration.
plays.consequence: The party knows the release verse.
plays.fallback: If the ledger is damaged, Ila hums the tune and Sallow supplies the words.
plays.tells: A player asks whether the Choir can be freed without the Cantor's help.
plays.rules: No check.
plays.later: S3: the verse is sung after Ossa rings (s03-sing-release).
plays.keywords: verse, ledger, rebuild, mother sallow, choir release

plays.title: Side dungeon: the Vennmark bond-house
plays.why: Venn's polite note makes him interesting, and his cellar is where Pellmoor's memories wait to be shipped. If they sold him the Heart, it's there too.
plays.readAloud: Every wall of Venn's counting-house is covered with clocks. Brass, walnut, enamel, a hundred faces, every hand moving, and not one of them makes a sound. Behind the counter, a door stands half open on a stair going down.
plays.response: Run it from The Vennmark bond-house in the wiki (every room keyed, with what to say, the traps and the treasure). Side dungeons in the wiki lists them all. Five rooms: the silent-clock counting-house, a stair with a speaking-tube and a cask trap, two hundred bottled memories (one of them Davin Sallow's), a cabinet of curiosities with a Mimic in it, and a strongroom with a needle lock. About 45 minutes. By day Venn shows them round and makes his offer; by night a watchman, his mastiff and two hired Toughs keep it. Venn never calls the Hushmen.
plays.consequence: They know what Pellmoor sells to the world, and who buys it. They may have the Heart back, and Mother Sallow may have her Davin.
plays.fallback: Only a possibility. If they never go, nothing in the story is lost.
plays.tells: They answer Venn's note, want the Heart back, follow Annet's tally book, or Mother Sallow asks about a bottle with her Davin's name on it.
plays.rules: Speaking-tube: Perception DC 12; DC 13 group Stealth to go down unheard. Cask: Perception DC 13; DC 13 Dexterity save or 2d6 Bludgeoning and Prone. Mimic: Investigation DC 15 to see it's alive. Strongroom needle: Investigation DC 15; DC 13 Constitution save or 2d10 Poison and Poisoned. Fight: a Mimic, two Toughs, a Guard and a Mastiff, between Low and Moderate for four level 3 characters. Puzzle (7.22): The one stopped clock and Venn's watch both say a quarter past nine: turning IX then III opens the strongroom with no roll and no needle, and a hidden drawer holds a Clockwork Amulet.
plays.later: Morning: Venn sends a note, "A pity. I would have paid." Session 4: if they took back a Heart he'd paid for, his Toughs watched the Old Shore until they left.
plays.keywords: dungeon, side dungeon, crawl, cellar, basement, hideout, traps, trap, treasure, hidden, loot, venn, bond-house, warehouse, memories, bottles, mimic, strongroom, heart, mother sallow, davin, puzzle, riddle
plays.scene: Scene 5: What to do with the Heart

plays.title: Treasure: Venn's strongroom
plays.why: Venn buys the best of everything and keeps it under a clock.
plays.readAloud: The iron door swings open on a room no bigger than a wardrobe. On the shelves: a purse of Amnian coin, two small bottles, a ledger, and a bag of plum velvet, embroidered with a clock, that's far too light for what's inside it.
plays.response: 150 gp, a Potion of Climbing, a Potion of Healing, the shipping book and Venn's Plum Bag. The Heart, if they sold it, in a velvet case. On the lowest rack outside: Davin Sallow's bottle (Investigation DC 12). Taken to Mother Sallow, she watches it once, alone; afterwards she trusts them completely, and each character who brought it gains Heroic Inspiration.
plays.consequence: They carry more, and Mother Sallow is theirs.
plays.tells: They open the strongroom, or Venn gives up its key.
plays.rules: **Venn's Plum Bag** (uncommon): a Bag of Holding. It holds up to 500 pounds, not exceeding 64 cubic feet, and always weighs 5 pounds. Retrieving an item from it is a Utilize action.
plays.later: See Side dungeons in the wiki for the rest.
plays.keywords: dungeon, side dungeon, crawl, cellar, basement, hideout, traps, trap, treasure, hidden, loot, bag of holding, plum bag, strongroom, potions, gold, davin sallow, reward
