## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. The only living witness to the Quiet Night tells them what happened, in his own words, and gives them the Frost Heart. They may free him, leave him, fight him or kill him. All four work. They reach level 6 when his story is settled.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-13) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-13) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-13) · [Scene 1: The confession](#scene-1-the-confession) · [Scene 2: The Key](#scene-2-the-key) · [Scene 3: Out of the glass](#scene-3-out-of-the-glass) · [Scene 4: The old man in the cloak](#scene-4-the-old-man-in-the-cloak) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-13) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-13) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-13) · [End of session](#end-of-session-13)

### Before you start (Session 13)

**Level:** four characters at level 5. They reach level 6 at the end, once the Sexton is resolved, however that goes.

**Check the world state first.** Five facts change tonight:
- **Is he Friendly?** If they gave him a patient hour, the confession starts with no roll. If he's Hostile, start with an apology (Influence DC 15).
- **Did someone agree with the sermon?** He speaks to that character first, and offers them the Heart.
- **Edda's diary:** if they have it, Scene 1 has its best version.
- **What did they tell him about the Court?** A lie has to be put right before he'll talk about the Key.
- **Isolde:** at Yara's camp, or a day out. She doesn't come into the chapel.

**What this session is about.** Imber Vesk ordered Edda Thorne to tune the bells into one long spring. She refused and wrote it down. He tuned them himself, with the Key, and the bells cracked. He has been sorry ever since. Tonight he says so to somebody. Then he asks for one thing: take me out of here, and let me finish my sermon somewhere it can be heard.

**Your goals tonight:**
- Read the confession slowly, and stop in the middle for them to ask things.
- Give the truth about the Key straight, if they tell him who holds it. This isn't a secret to protect; let them plan with it.
- However the scene goes, **the Frost Heart leaves with the party.** Every route ends that way.
- If they fight, he's a man in pain, and the fight stops the moment they stop.
- End on his warning: "Don't ring the Frost Spire without the Heart. The winter will come back all at once." Then ask: "Who will carry it up?"

**Prepare:**
- **Tokens or minis:** the four characters; the Glass Sexton; Imber (an old man, if you have one); two Stilled; Yara; Maren.
- **Maps:** the chapel from last session. Mark the pulpit, the aisle and the pews.
- **Props:**
  - *The warm cloak.* Put a real scarf on the table. Whoever picks it up gives Imber theirs.
  - *The confession,* printed large enough to read without looking down too much.
  - *A jug of cold water,* if your table likes that sort of thing. One sip each when the shell breaks.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **Freeing him:** Strength DC 15, or 20 Fire or Lightning damage aimed at the glass over the whole scene. Two or three Fire Bolts, one Burning Hands, or Produce Flame held close for a minute. Yara's saw does it in ten minutes with no roll. Thunder (Shatter, Thunderwave) breaks it and hurts him.
- **Once he's out,** he's an old man: Commoner, 4 hit points, unarmed. The cold counts for him too: Constitution DC 10 each hour, unless he has a cloak.
- **Spells:** Detect Thoughts works (a lullaby, and the name Cassia). Zone of Truth works and finds nothing hidden. Dispel Magic does nothing: a winter-moment isn't a spell. Counterspell does nothing to his Sermon or Icicle Volley.
- **The sermon in a fight:** Wisdom DC 15 or Charmed, with Speed 0, until the end of the character's next turn. Calm Emotions suppresses Charmed. Roll the save every time he uses it.
- **Shattering:** when his ice breaks, everyone within 15 feet makes a Dexterity save, DC 15, for 4d6 slashing (half on a success).
- **The Frost Heart** falls when his broken-form ends. Free to grab if you're next to it; otherwise Dexterity (Acrobatics) DC 12 from up to 10 feet.

### Key people tonight (Session 13)

| Who | What they are | Stat block | Where | Starts | Influence | Secret |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **The Glass Sexton (Imber Vesk)** | High Sexton of the Quiet Night | The Glass Sexton in the glass; Commoner when freed | The pulpit | Friendly, Indifferent or Hostile, from last session | DC 15 | The Key is the Seventh Bell's heart. His daughter Cassia carried it home. |
| **Yara Thenn** | Guide | Scout | The arch, with her saw | From before | DC 15 | She's drawn the chapel twice and never gone in. |
| **Maren Talla** | If she's awake | Commoner | The arch | Friendly | None needed | She remembers Imber as a kind man who forgave her for laughing in church. |
| **A Stilled in the pews** | One more if it comes to a fight | Stilled Person | The back row | Asleep | DC 15, as an action | Cracks awake in round 2 if there's a fight. |

**Places at a glance:**
- **The chapel:** as before. The candles are lower tonight.
- **The pulpit:** the glass has begun to drip.
- **Outside:** two hours to Yara's camp. The Spire stands over the trees, with a bell in it.

**Rumours:** none tonight. Everything they hear is from somebody who was there.

### Opening recap (Session 13)

> **SAY:** "Last time, you went into the chapel and a man in a pulpit made of glass asked you who rules the Court. *(Say what they told him.)* You led three carters out by the hand. *(If they did.)* He says he has one thing left to say. He's said it to the frost every night for four hundred years. He asked whether you'd listen. *(Say what they answered.)*"

- **If they said no:** "The candles are still burning. He's still there. He hasn't started again."
- **Then hand it over:** "Where are you sitting?" Let them choose a pew, the aisle, or the door.

### Scene 1: The confession

**Where and why.** The front of the chapel. They're listening.

> **SAY:** "He takes a breath. You didn't know he breathed. 'I shall not preach it,' he says. 'I shall only say it.'"

**What's really going on.** [He tells it plainly.](play:s13-listen-confession) He isn't bargaining. If they read Edda's diary to him, he'll cry.

> **SAY:** "'I ordered her to tune them into one long spring. Edda refused, and she wrote it down for me, so that I could never say I did not know. I tuned them anyway. The Key sang against the bells, and the bells cracked on the discord. I have been sorry for four hundred years.'"

**Read it in three pieces, and stop after each:**
1. *The order.* "There were seven bells, one for each part of the year. I wanted one. No winter. No harvest to fail. I thought: how can it be wrong, to want spring?" **Stop. Let them ask.**
2. *The warning.* "She came to my door at night. She said a bell that is asked to sing only one note goes mad. She said it twice, so that I would hear it. Then she wrote it down and gave me the page. I remember thinking how neat her hand was." **Stop.**
3. *The ringing.* "I put the Key to the first bell and it sang, beautifully, and the others leaned to listen. And then they all sang *against* it. Every bell in the world at once, and none of them the same. And then nothing. I thought I had gone deaf. I hadn't. That's what it was, you see. It was quiet." **Stop. Let it be quiet for a moment.**

**If they…**
- **[Read Edda's diary to him:](play:s13-read-diary-to-imber)** the glass fogs. "She told me," he says. "She wrote it down so I could not say I did not know." He asks for the last page again. Then the crown opens its hand, as it were: the Frost Heart comes out into the Ringer's hand without anyone touching it. No roll, and no need for the rest of the confession.
- **Ask what the Key is:** Scene 2. He won't, until they've told him who holds it.
- **Ask about Cassia:** his daughter. She took the Key home to the Vesks' reliquary the night he was disgraced. "She had my mother's laugh. You won't have heard it. I'd give you the Heart for an hour of it."
- **Get restless:** "Take the crown," he says. "I am too tired to wear it." Move to Scene 3.
- **Argue again:** the glass cracks. **"Do you wish me to go on?"** Then see the fights.
- **Tell him they don't forgive him:** he nods. "No. I shouldn't, in your place. I only wanted it heard."

**The gift.** When he's finished he asks one of them, the one he trusts, to lift the crown from his head. The glass lets go. The Frost Heart comes away in their hand: a bronze clapper, cold enough to burn, singing very softly.

**Bring it back.** In the pews, a Stilled woman who's been kneeling for four hundred years has turned her head towards him. Nobody saw it happen.

**How it ends.** They have the Frost Heart, and he asks them for one more thing: "Take me with you. I should like to finish it somewhere there's an answer."

### Scene 2: The Key

**Where and why.** At any point. The one question he most wants answered is who has it now.

> **SAY:** "He is silent so long you think the winter has taken him. Then: 'The Key passed to my daughter, Cassia, when I was disgraced. It stayed in the family's reliquary. Who holds it now? Tell me, and I will tell you what it is.'"

**What's really going on.** [The Key isn't a tool.](play:s13-ask-about-key) It's the clapper of the Seventh Bell. Maudrin uses it and doesn't fully understand what it was for.

**If they…**
- **Say Maudrin Vesk:** he keeps his word. "It is not a tool. It is the Seventh's heart. It sings the Dreamer to sleep. I struck the other bells with it, to make the calendar behave. Imagine using a cradle-song to hammer nails." Then he tells them where it's kept: a vault beneath the family chapel, now under the white palace; a lock, and a weighted line tied to the case, so that lifting it rings a bell somewhere else. (In Act IV, if they rob the palace, they find the line without a roll, and have advantage on the DC 16 lock.)
- **Ask who the Dreamer is:** "The one under the hill. I only ever saw its breath."
- **Refuse to tell him:** he says nothing more about it. "Then we'll each keep one thing."
- **Lied to him last session:** he asks again. This time the truth is enough.
- **Don't ask:** near the end, he asks them. "Who has the Key now? Someone must."

**Bring it back.** Ask the character who saw themselves in the glass: "A small dark key. Do you say anything?"

**How it ends.** They know, or they've chosen not to. If they know, *don't* soften it or say it's for later. Let them start planning.

### Scene 3: Out of the glass

**Where and why.** The pulpit. Skip it if he's already dead, or they've decided to leave him.

**If they…**
- **[Free him:](play:s13-free-sexton)** Strength DC 15, or 20 Fire or Lightning damage, or Yara's saw. Read:

> **SAY:** "The glass runs like wax. Inside it there is only an old man in wet ceremonial robes, thin as a rake, shaking so hard his teeth click. 'Oh,' he says. 'It is cold.'"

- If he hasn't handed over the Heart yet, he lifts the crown from his own head and gives it to them now.
- **[Use other spells:](play:s13-spells-on-sexton)** he knows what they're doing and enjoys watching it. "Ah. Tonework. I had almost forgotten the sound." Fire and lightning free him gently. Thunder breaks it and hurts him.
- **[Leave him frozen:](play:s13-leave-him-frozen)** he doesn't argue. The Heart still comes out of the crown when he asks it to. "Then tell me when it rings," he says. "I would like to know when the winter ends, even if I am the last to feel it." Remind them, once, that the Court is a day away. If they leave him, Isolde finds him first.
- **[Kill him:](play:s13-kill-imber)** ask once: "You mean to kill him?" He's unarmed and frail. If they do, he says "I know," and closes his eyes. The glass around the chapel goes dull. The Heart falls from the crown. Say plainly that the only living witness of the Quiet Night is gone. If they hesitate, he asks one thing: finish the sermon for me.

**Bring it back.** The candles, all of them, at once, begin to flicker.

**How it ends.** He's free, or he isn't. Either way the Heart is theirs and the chapel is quieter than it has ever been.

### Scene 4: The old man in the cloak

**Where and why.** The walk back, or the camp. Only if he's free.

> **SAY:** "'It is cold,' Imber says again, wonderingly, as if the word were new. 'I had forgotten it was a thing a person could feel.'"

**What's really going on.** [He needs looking after.](play:s13-escort-imber) A cloak, food, and a slow pace. He wants to see the Spire before anything else.

**Imber, out of the glass.** The long sentences have gone. He speaks in short ones now, and stops, surprised, when they end. *Lines:* "Is that soup? Is that what it smells like?" · "You have very kind hands. Were you a nurse?" · "Nobody asked me to stop. All those years. I'd have stopped." · "I'd like to see it ring. I won't ask to be forgiven. I'd just like to see it." · To Maren: "I know you. You laughed. During the long prayer."

**If they…**
- **Give him a cloak:** whoever gives up theirs makes the cold saves. He tries to give it back.
- **Sit with him:** he asks their names, and repeats each one carefully, and gets them all right afterwards.
- **Ask him to finish the sermon:** not yet. "When there's a bell to say it under."
- **Ask about the Court:** he's four hundred years out of date. But he knows the palace as it was: doors, passages, where the chapel stair comes out.
- **Yara** wants to know who's paying for the soup. She also gives him the good blanket.

**Bring it back.** Imber walks past a glass tree, stops, and puts his hand on it. "I'm sorry," he tells it. It isn't clear whether he means the tree.

**How it ends.** The Spire is above the trees. He stops and looks at it. Then: **"Don't ring the Frost Spire without the Heart. The winter will come back all at once."** Ask them: **"Who will carry it up?"**

### Running the fights (Session 13)

#### The Glass Sexton

*One Glass Sexton (Imber Vesk), and one Stilled who wakes in the pews in round 2.* **Only if they attack, or push him past "Do you wish me to go on?"**

- **Setup:** he's in the pulpit at the front and never leaves it in the first form. The party is in the pews. Mark three pews as cover.
- **First form (the ice): 95 hit points, AC 15.** Each round he uses two Icicle Volleys (+7 to hit, range 60 feet, 3d6 + 4 piercing plus 2d6 cold), or swaps one for the Sermon (Wisdom DC 15, or Charmed with Speed 0). He aims the Sermon at whoever's loudest and the ice at whoever hit him last. Fire or Lightning drops his AC by 2. Piercing and slashing do half. Anyone who hits him in melee is showered with shards: Dexterity DC 15 or 2d6.
- **Round 2:** the Stilled in the back row wakes and attacks behind the party. Influence DC 15 calms it.
- **The break:** when the ice runs out, it shatters (Dexterity DC 15, 4d6, half on a success, within 15 feet). Take a breath here and describe the old man inside. Any leftover damage is lost.
- **Second form (the man in broken glass): 45 hit points, AC 13, Speed 30.** Two claws (+6, 2d6 + 3 slashing and 2d4 cold), or Shattering Voice (4d10 thunder, Constitution DC 15, half on a success). He's weeping now.
- **When it ends:** at 0 the shell falls away and he's frail and alive. [The Frost Heart lands on the ice](play:s13-sexton-shell-breaks): free to take if you're next to it. He says: "Have we finished?" Only a deliberate act kills him.
- **The off switch:** at the end of any round in which nobody attacked him, he stops and asks, "Have we finished?" If they say yes, the fight is over, and he can still confess if asked kindly.
- **Leaving:** he doesn't follow.
- **Scale on the fly:** three characters, 70 hit points in the first form and no Stilled. If someone drops early, leave the Stilled asleep. At level 6, a second Stilled wakes in round 2.
- **Non-lethal outcomes:** a character who drops is left where they are. He calls for somebody to help them.

### Pacing (Session 13)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:10 | Recap; where are you sitting? |
| 0:10 to 1:10 | Scene 1: the confession |
| 1:10 to 1:45 | Scene 2: the Key |
| 1:45 to 2:30 | Scene 3: out of the glass (or the fight: allow an hour) |
| 2:30 to 3:20 | Scene 4: the old man in the cloak |
| 3:20 to 3:30 | The warning, and who carries it |

- **Where to break:** after "It was quiet."
- **Running long:** let Yara's saw free him while they talk about the Key.
- **Running short:** let Imber ask each character one question on the walk.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop when he lifts the crown.

### If you get stuck (Session 13)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **He asks one player something small.** "What do you eat for breakfast, now?"
2. **The glass drips.** One drop, on somebody's hand. It's warm.
3. **A candle turns towards whoever hasn't spoken.**

**If they can't decide what to do with him:** go round the table. "One sentence each: what does he deserve?" Then: "And what are you going to do?"

### End of session 13

**The closing question:** "Don't ring the Frost Spire without the Heart. The winter will come back all at once." Who will carry it up? Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** the confession, the Key, and how Imber's story went (freed, left, beaten, killed).
- **World-state facts to check:** the Frost Heart is with the party (set this on every route); Imber is frozen, freed or dead; do they know what the Key is, and does he know who holds it.
- **Level 6, now.** Give players a few minutes if they want to level up at the table.

**Rewards:**
- **The Frost Heart.** It goes with them, whatever they did.
- **The confession:** one of the three sources for the truth of the Key, with Edda's diary and Lysse's notes.
- **The Vesk reliquary:** where it is and how it's guarded, for Act IV.
- **Level:** level 6.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to whoever gave up a cloak, and to whoever asked him about Cassia.

plays.title: They climb the Frost Spire
plays.why: The bell is two hundred feet up a tower of ice, and most parties climb.
plays.readAloud: A spire of ice rises from the centre of the glass forest like a frozen fountain. Inside it the bell hangs motionless, locked in frost. Every breath you take freezes on the air. The bell is singing, so softly you hear it only in your teeth.
plays.response: About 200 feet of ice. Three DC 14 Strength (Athletics) checks get a climber to the top; a failure is a slip: the climber falls 20 feet (2d6 bludgeoning) and starts that check again. A rope team lets one climber Help another (advantage) on each check. If Yara is Friendly she shows the old Sexton's stair on the north face, which removes one check. Exhaustion from the cold applies its -2 per level to every check.
plays.consequence: They reach the bell.
plays.fallback: If the climbers keep slipping, let them find the old Sexton's stair cut into the ice on the north face: slower, one extra hour of cold, no checks.
plays.tells: Players ask about rope, pitons, or how high it is.
plays.rules: Athletics DC 14, three times. Fall: 20 feet, 2d6 bludgeoning. Help gives advantage. Exhaustion: −2 per level. Extreme Cold saves continue hourly.
plays.later: S15: a sketch of the Spire drawn at the top earns Yara's loyalty (s15-yara-map). S14: anyone who reaches the bell can be the Ringer.
plays.keywords: climb, spire, frost spire, athletics, rope, ice, fall, ascend, tower, top

plays.title: They fly, levitate or Spider Climb up the Spire
plays.why: At level 6, Fly, Spider Climb and Misty Step are on most casters' lists.
plays.readAloud: Your spell hums, and the Spire hums back, a half-note higher. At its foot, glass heads lift and turn toward the sound.
plays.response: It works. The Spire holds no silence-stones; Hieme is silent, not suppressing. Fly or Spider Climb skips the checks, Misty Step covers 30 feet at a time, and Levitate needs someone pulling a rope. The Glass-Wolves at the base hear the hum and come running, and the Stilled on the ice stairs turn their heads.
plays.consequence: A fast ascent, with the guards roused.
plays.fallback: If concentration breaks mid-air, the fall rules apply from that height; telegraph the wind before it happens (there is none).
plays.tells: A caster asks whether anything stops magic here.
plays.rules: Fly, Spider Climb, Levitate and Misty Step as written. Every spell hums; the Spire guards notice.
plays.later: S15: whoever flew can bring the Heart down quickly if Isolde arrives.
plays.keywords: fly, levitate, spider climb, misty step, magic, spell, flight, teleport, climb

plays.title: They fight the Spire's guards
plays.why: Glass-Wolves at the base and Stilled on the stairs stand between them and the bell.
plays.readAloud: The wolves at the base of the Spire were lying so still you took them for ice. Then all of them stand up at once.
plays.response: Glass-Wolves guard the base; Stilled watch from the ice stairs and move only when glass breaks or a climber passes within 5 feet. Run the Spire Guards. Each wolf shatters when it drops (shards: 1d6 slashing to creatures within 5 feet), and each shattering cracks the ice stairs a little more. The Stilled stop fighting the moment the bell rings.
plays.consequence: The way to the bell is open.
plays.fallback: If the fight drags, the bell's hum rises and the Stilled pause, listening, for a full round.
plays.tells: The party approaches the base openly.
plays.rules: A Stilled that hits a climber forces a DC 12 Strength saving throw or the climber slips and falls 20 feet (2d6 bludgeoning). Tell the climber before they pass one.
plays.later: S15: Stilled who fought here wake with the thaw and remember; spared or calmed ones count toward the Stilled's trust.
plays.keywords: fight, wolves, glass-wolves, stilled, guards, base, battle, combat, spire

plays.title: They sneak past the guards
plays.why: Parties that avoided the ambush in S11 will try the same here.
plays.readAloud: You pass so close to the nearest wolf that you can see the bubble of air frozen in its eye.
plays.response: A group DC 14 Dexterity (Stealth) check gets the party to the foot of the climb; Yara's map gives advantage and Pass without Trace gives +10. If they were never seen in S11, they also have surprise if it comes to blows. A distraction works too: a thrown glass-flower, a whistle, a Minor Illusion of a running deer draws the pack for two rounds.
plays.consequence: They begin the climb unseen.
plays.fallback: If one character fails, one wolf follows them alone, and the rest sleep on.
plays.tells: Players ask about cover, wind, or a distraction.
plays.rules: Group Stealth DC 14. Pass without Trace +10. Surprise if undetected in S11.
plays.later: S14: climbing still hums if they use magic; a mundane climb stays quiet.
plays.keywords: sneak, stealth, avoid, distraction, pass without trace, quiet, hide, slip past

plays.title: They ring Hieme
plays.why: They carried the Frost Heart up two hundred feet of ice for this.
plays.readAloud: The bell rings once. The sound is high and thin and clear, like a single thread of ice pulled across the sky. The frost on the Spire cracks. The glass trees hum. Everywhere in the forest, something begins to move. The winter is going. Not all at once, but slowly, like a tide turning back.
plays.response: Warn and wait for a yes: 'Hieme will take a memory from you, and it will be [weight].' You choose which after the thaw begins. If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. When it rings, the thaw begins and the Stilled wake over several weeks. If the Sexton is alive, he weeps, wherever he is, and the thaw reaches him last. A Silence spell around the bell only keeps those inside the sphere from hearing it; the ringing still works, because a bell's tone is more than sound (a silence-stone field would stop it, which is why Vaer was chained).
plays.consequence: Hieme is rung. Glassreach begins to thaw.
plays.fallback: If the Ringer hesitates, the bell's hum waits with them. A bell that waited four hundred years can wait an hour.
plays.tells: A player asks what it will cost.
plays.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Hieme: a Memory). Afterward, decide where the Frost Heart goes: left in the bell or carried on.
plays.later: Concord: one more of six. S15: Isolde arrives with Hushmen for the Frost Heart. S22: the thawed Stilled walk to the Tor if trust is earned. Act IV: the Court's patience ends; its clock moves.
plays.keywords: ring, hieme, bell, toll, memory, frost spire, thaw, winter bell, ringer

plays.title: They strike Hieme without the Frost Heart
plays.why: The party left the Sexton's crown behind, or lost the Heart to Isolde, and tries a hammer.
plays.readAloud: The Spire groans before you strike it. The frost on the bell thickens, and your breath freezes in the air and falls like hail.
plays.response: Telegraph it first: the bronze rings dead, the Spire groans, and Yara (or Imber) calls out that the bell has no Heart and striking it will freeze the Spire. If they swing anyway, the frost surges. For the next ten minutes, Extreme Cold saves come every minute at DC 15 (warm gear still means automatic success), and the Glass-Wolves at the base wake. Descending at once ends the effect: every minute spent climbing down is one save, no more. No Toll is asked, because nothing rang.
plays.consequence: Nothing rings, and the cold bites hard.
plays.fallback: If a player insists on trying again, the Spire itself cracks a warning down its full length.
plays.tells: A player raises a weapon or a mallet to the bell.
plays.rules: Accelerated Extreme Cold: DC 15 Constitution save each minute for up to 10 minutes; cloaks and Cold Resistance still succeed automatically. Descent ends it immediately.
plays.later: S13: the Frost Heart is still in the Sexton's crown (s13-listen-confession), or in Isolde's hands; they need it.
plays.keywords: hammer, strike, hit bell, no heart, without heart, force, improvise, weapon

plays.title: They leave the Frost Heart in the bell
plays.why: Carrying a Heart makes you a target; a bell with its Heart looks complete.
plays.readAloud: The Heart hangs in the bell where it belongs, still faintly singing. Frost is already forming on it again, softer than before.
plays.response: The resonance persists even if the Heart is later removed, so leaving it is safe for the Concord. It also means Isolde has to climb to take it, which she will not do herself.
plays.consequence: The Frost Heart stays at the Spire.
plays.fallback: If they change their minds, it comes down with one more Athletics check.
plays.tells: After ringing, a player asks whether they need to take it down.
plays.rules: A repeat ringing later needs the Heart and another Toll, and renews the effect without stacking it.
plays.later: S15: Isolde demands it; the party can say 'Go and get it', and her Hushmen spend a day failing the climb. Act IV: the Court may send climbers later; it never undoes Hieme's ringing.
plays.keywords: leave heart, keep in bell, frost heart, leave behind, safe, spire

plays.title: Nobody will pay Hieme's Toll
plays.why: After Vaer, Calla or Ossa, some characters have nothing left they want to give.
plays.readAloud: The bell keeps its one soft note in your teeth, patient as snow.
plays.response: Nobody pays, and that is a real choice: record it. Hieme can be rung later; the Heart goes with them or stays. Do not shame it.
plays.consequence: Hieme stays silent and Glassreach stays frozen, for now.
plays.fallback: If the table wants a way forward, remind them that any willing character may be the Ringer, and that the Toll is a memory, not a life.
plays.tells: A long silence when you warn of the Toll.
plays.rules: No Toll is taken when a ringing is declined.
plays.later: S22: the Concord needs Hieme; the Second Dawn stays open without it. S15: Isolde still comes for the Heart.
plays.keywords: refuse, won't pay, no toll, decline, don't ring, wait, later

plays.title: The Sexton's door: the dungeon inside the Spire
plays.why: Imber had the stair cut, and he never told anyone there were two of them. The second climbs inside the ice. It's the session's big dungeon and the main way up.
plays.readAloud: Behind the sleeping wolves, at the very foot of the north face, the ice is thinner. Under it, plain as a face under water, is a bronze door twice the height of a man, with the nine-bell sign of the Ninefold Church cast in its centre.
plays.response: This is the way up. Run the climb from The Frost Spire, area by area in the wiki, in place of Scene 2's three checks. Ten areas inside the ice: the door, a vestibule of frozen petitions over thin ice, the masons' gallery and its hoist, the echo stair, the lamp-room window onto the red-ribbon man, the choir loft, the icicle gallery, the frozen bell-rope, the Bell-Warden in the ringing room, and the last stair to the crown. The short way (1, 2, 5, 8, 9, 10) takes about 45 minutes; the long way about 1 hour 15. Break in the lamp-room. The window at 60 feet and a crack at 100 feet join the inner and outer stairs.
plays.consequence: They climb inside the Spire: no falls from the open face, more rooms, up to three fights, and Boots of the Winterlands.
plays.fallback: If they'd rather climb the open face, run Scene 2 as written. The lamp-room window at 60 feet still lets them into the dungeon halfway up.
plays.tells: They reach the foot of the Spire. The door is in plain sight on the north face, and Imber, Yara's map or Maren point them to it.

## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. A frozen bell at the top of two hundred feet of ice, a pack asleep at the bottom, and a price. It's the big night of Act III: the climb is the action, the ringing is the choice.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-14) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-14) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-14) · [Scene 1: The foot of the Spire](#scene-1-the-foot-of-the-spire) · [Scene 2: The climb](#scene-2-the-climb) · [Scene 3: The bell](#scene-3-the-bell) · [Scene 4: The thaw](#scene-4-the-thaw) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-14) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-14) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-14) · [End of session](#end-of-session-14)

### Before you start (Session 14)

**Level:** four characters at level 6. If anyone hasn't levelled up yet, do it first.

**Check the world state first.** Five facts change tonight:
- **Who carries the Frost Heart?** Ask now, so nobody argues about it at the top.
- **Is Imber with them?** He watches from the foot of the Spire, in somebody's cloak. If he's in the glass, he'll hear it from the chapel. If he's dead, finish his sermon for him, if they promised to.
- **How many bells have rung?** That sets the weight of the Toll: none or one is **heavy**, two or three is **grievous**, four or five is **ruinous**. Look up what that means for a memory in Part 2.7 before you start.
- **Did the wolves ever see them in Session 11?** If not, they can have surprise.
- **Exhaustion.** Write down each character's level. It's −2 for each level on every climbing check.

**What this session is about.** Hieme is the bell of winter. It stopped in the middle of a note, and everything in the forest stopped with it. If someone carries the Heart up and rings it, the winter ends, and the bell takes a memory from them, and they don't get to choose which. Nobody has to.

**Your goals tonight:**
- Make the climb feel high. Describe what they can see at sixty feet, a hundred and twenty, and the top.
- Give three honest ways up, and let any of them work: fight, sneak, or the old stair.
- **Before the ringing, say the warning in full and wait for a yes.** If it's a no, that's a real ending for the night, and you don't argue.
- Read the ringing slowly. Then stop talking for a few seconds.
- End on the question: **"What did the Frost Spire cost the thaw?"**

**Prepare:**
- **Tokens or minis:** the four characters; seven Glass-Wolves; six Stilled; Yara; Imber.
- **Maps:** draw the Spire from the side, as a tall triangle with a line every twenty feet and the stair on the north face. Mark where the six Stilled stand on it. It's all you need.
- **The memory.** Think about what you'd take from each character who might ring: one clear thing they've talked about at the table. Keep it kind, and make it matter. You say it after the thaw begins. Don't take the thing a player has asked you not to touch.
- **Props:** a wine glass and a wet finger. One note, quietly, when they ring it.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **The climb:** three Strength (Athletics) checks, DC 14. A failure is a slip: fall 20 feet, 2d6 bludgeoning, and try that same check again. Someone roped to the climber can Help, for advantage.
- **The old Sexton's stair** is on the north face. If Yara is Friendly she shows them where it starts, and it takes away one check. Anyone who's stuck can use all of it: an extra hour of cold, no checks.
- **Exhaustion:** each level is −2 to every D20 Test and 5 feet off your Speed.
- **Extreme Cold:** each hour, Constitution DC 10 or one level of Exhaustion. A warm cloak succeeds.
- **Falling:** 1d6 for every 10 feet, and you land Prone. Feather Fall stops it.
- **Magic works here.** Fly and Spider Climb skip the checks. Misty Step is 30 feet. Levitate needs a friend with a rope. But every spell hums, and the pack hears it.
- **Silence** hides the sound only from those inside it. It doesn't stop the bell from ringing.
- **Glass-Wolves** burst when they drop: Dexterity DC 12 or 1d6, everyone within 5 feet. Vulnerable to Thunder.

### Key people tonight (Session 14)

| Who | What they are | Stat block | Where | Starts | Influence | Secret |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Yara Thenn** | Guide, and the only map-maker here | Scout | The foot of the Spire | From before | DC 15 | She's tried the climb three times. She got to the first Stilled each time, and stopped. |
| **Imber Vesk** | If he's free | Commoner | The foot of the Spire, sitting on a pack | Friendly | None needed | He had the stair cut. He's never told anyone there were two of them. |
| **Maren Talla** | If she's awake | Commoner | With Imber, or at camp | Friendly | None needed | She knows two of the people on the stair by name. |
| **The Stilled on the stair** | Six people who were climbing to beg the bell to stop | Stilled Person | On the ice stairs | Asleep | DC 15, as an action | Their ribbons have names. The one at the top is a bell-ringer. |
| **The pack** | Seven Glass-Wolves | Glass-Wolf | Lying at the base like fallen ice | Hunting by sound | No | They follow whoever fell. |

**Places at a glance:**
- **The foot:** broken columns of ice, seven shapes lying among them. Good cover.
- **The lower stair (0 to 60 feet):** three Stilled stand on it. Wolves can reach this far.
- **The high stair (60 to 140 feet):** three more. Wolves can't.
- **The open face (140 to 200 feet):** wind should be here. There isn't any.
- **The crown:** a room with no walls, a frozen bell, and the whole forest below it.

**Rumours:** none. They're here.

### Opening recap (Session 14)

> **SAY:** "Last time, a man who broke the world told you he was sorry, and gave you the bell's Heart. *(Say what they did about him.)* He asked you not to ring the Spire without it. You've carried it since yesterday, and it's so cold that nobody has been able to hold it for long. Look up. That's the Spire."

- **Then hand it over:** "Who's carrying the Heart today, and what have you wrapped it in?"
- **If Isolde's lot is close:** Yara points south-east. Smoke, one thin line of it. "That's a day off. They don't light fires unless they want you to see."

### Scene 1: The foot of the Spire

**Where and why.** The middle of the glass forest. They see the whole climb before they start.

> **SAY:** "A spire of ice rises from the centre of the glass forest like a frozen fountain. Inside it the bell hangs motionless, locked in frost. Every breath you take freezes on the air. The bell is singing, so softly you hear it only in your teeth."

**What's really going on.** Seven Glass-Wolves are lying in the ice at the foot. They look like ice until they don't. Up the stair stand six people who were climbing to ask the bell to stop.

**Yara.** *Lines:* "Two ways up. There's the one that kills you and the one that takes longer." · "I got to that fellow there. Red ribbon. I turned round." · "I'll rope the first pair. I won't go up. Somebody has to know where you were." · If she's Friendly: "North face. There's a stair under the frost. He had it cut." (She nods at Imber.)

**Imber,** if he's here. He sits on a pack and looks up. *Lines:* "I was younger than any of you when I climbed it." · "You needn't ring it for me." · "It will ask you for something. It asked me, once, and I'd already given it."

**If they…**
- **Look at the base properly:** Perception DC 15, or ask Yara. Seven long shapes, and one of them is breathing.
- **[Sneak past:](play:s14-sneak-guards)** group Dexterity (Stealth) DC 14. Yara's map gives advantage; Pass without Trace gives +10. Read:

> **SAY:** "You pass so close to the nearest wolf that you can see the bubble of air frozen in its eye."

- **If one character fails,** one wolf follows them, alone. The rest sleep.
- **[Distract them:](play:s14-sneak-guards)** a thrown glass-flower, a whistle, a Minor Illusion of a running deer. The pack goes after it for two rounds.
- **[Fight them:](play:s14-fight-guards)** see the fights.
- **Use the cold:** nobody has told the wolves that fire is a different thing. A bonfire lit well away brings them all to the wrong place.

**Bring it back.** The bell hums, once, a half-note higher, and every wolf's ear turns towards it.

**How it ends.** They're on the ice, with somebody's foot on the first step.

### Scene 2: The climb

**Where and why.** Two hundred feet of ice. Three checks. Each one is a place they stop.

**What's really going on.** [It's hard, and it isn't a puzzle.](play:s14-climb) The ice stair is broken in two places and stops short of the top; each gap is one of the three checks. They go as a rope team, or one by one. Ask each time: who's roped to whom, and who's Helping? Say the fall before they risk it.

> **SAY (the first third):** "At sixty feet you pass the first of them: a man with his hand on the rail, looking up. Somebody has tied a red ribbon round his wrist. The wood has vanished under you, and from here it looks like a lake."

- **The Stilled on the stair:** they don't move unless glass breaks nearby, or someone passes within 5 feet. If one wakes, it lashes out at whatever's nearest. A hit means a Strength save, DC 12, or the climber falls 20 feet. Say so before they squeeze past one.
- **Talk to it:** an action, Influence DC 15. Read its ribbon aloud for advantage. A calmed one sits down on the step, holds the rail, and doesn't let go of the next climber.

> **SAY (the second third):** "At a hundred and twenty feet the stair stops. Above it there's only the face of the ice, and the bell, humming in your back teeth. You can see Yara's fire. You can see a smudge of smoke to the south. You can see all of it, the whole forest, like something under a glass dome on a shelf."

> **SAY (the top):** "The last ten feet are a lip of ice as wide as a bed. You pull yourself over it, and there's the bell. It's as tall as a person, bronze under a skin of frost, and it's not swinging. There's a hook inside it where a clapper ought to be."

**If they…**
- **[Fly or use magic:](play:s14-magic-climb)** it works. Read the box and let them have it. The wolves run for the base and the Stilled turn their heads.
- **Fall:** 2d6, Prone, 20 feet down. Roped to someone? They're caught at the end of the rope: no damage, but the other climber makes a Strength save, DC 12, or is pulled off with them.
- **Keep slipping:** somebody finds the stair on the north face. An hour of cold. They arrive.
- **Stop to draw it:** at the top, or on the way. One minute and no roll. Yara will want it ([Session 15](play:s15-yara-map)).
- **Get the Heart out to look:** it's singing. The bell answers it.
- **Leave someone below:** they'll be the one to see the smoke move, and they'll hear it first.

**Bring it back.** The frost on the nearest pane has a face-sized clear spot in it. Somebody's breath has been on the other side. Four hundred years of it.

**How it ends.** At least one of them is standing under the bell with the Heart.

### Scene 3: The bell

**Where and why.** The crown, the bell, and the person who'll ring it. There is no hurry in this scene.

> **SAY:** "Nobody's put a hand on it since the night it stopped. The rope's still there, stiff as a rod. The hook is empty. The Heart is humming in your hands, and you can feel it leaning."

**What's really going on.** The one with the Heart can ring. They can't do it without the Heart, and they can't do it without agreeing to pay.

**Say it out loud, to the player who'll do it, and then wait.**

> **SAY:** "Hieme will take a memory from you, and it will be *(heavy / grievous / ruinous)*. I'll choose which memory after the winter breaks. You won't get it back, and no spell will. Do you ring it?"

**If they…**
- **Ask what the weight means:** tell them straight, from Part 2.7. *Heavy:* one defining memory, gone for good. You rewrite what it held up. *Grievous:* one person who matters to you, gone from memory. You know of them. You don't know them. *Ruinous:* a whole year of your life, gone, with everyone you met in it.
- **Ask which memory:** "I don't know yet. I'll tell you after." That's the bell's rule, not yours.
- **Say no:** [the bell doesn't ring.](play:s14-refuse-to-ring) "The bell keeps its one soft note in your teeth, patient as snow." Nothing is taken. Somebody else can ring. Nobody at all is a real choice; record it and don't shame it. Go to the end of the session.
- **Say yes:** [they ring it.](play:s14-ring-hieme) Make them describe the swing. Go to Scene 4.
- **Hesitate:** give them all the time they need. Ask the others one question each, quietly: what would you tell them? Then look back.
- **[Strike it without the Heart:](play:s14-strike-without-heart)** stop them first. Yara's voice from below, or Imber's: "It has no Heart! It'll freeze!" If they swing anyway, the frost surges. Constitution DC 15 every minute for up to ten minutes (cloaks still succeed), the wolves wake, and climbing down ends it. No Toll, because nothing rang.
- **Try to have the whole party pay it:** one Ringer. It doesn't split.
- **Try to have Imber do it:** he can't climb it. He'd ask.

**Bring it back.** The Heart pulls, very gently, towards the hook.

**How it ends.** It rings, or it doesn't.

### Scene 4: The thaw

**Where and why.** The top, and then the whole forest. Read it slowly. Then be quiet for a moment.

> **SAY:** "The bell rings once. The sound is high and thin and clear, like a single thread of ice pulled across the sky. The frost on the Spire cracks. The glass trees hum. Everywhere in the forest, something begins to move. The winter is going. Not all at once, but slowly, like a tide turning back."

**What's really going on.** The Toll lands after this. Let them have the thaw first.

**Then the Toll.** Ask the Ringer to close their eyes, if they like. Then tell them, plainly and kindly, what's gone. Say it as something missing, not as something stolen.

> **SAY (an example, for heavy):** "You're thinking about *(say who)*, because you often do when something is beautiful. And there's a gap. You know you had a mother. You know she had a kitchen. You can't see it."

- Ask them to write down the belief, bond or fear that went with it, and what they'll say instead.
- **If they want a private moment:** stop the game for a few minutes. It's a hard thing.

**If they…**
- **Look down:** the Stilled on the stair are moving, very slowly. They stop fighting the moment it rings.
- **Look for Imber:** he's weeping. He isn't hiding it. "It's the right note," he says. "It's the right note. I never heard it, you know, not properly. I was standing too close."
- **[Leave the Heart in the bell:](play:s14-leave-heart)** it hangs where it belongs and it's still ringing, very faintly. Safe. The ringing can't be undone. But Isolde will have to climb for it.
- **Take it down with them:** lighter than it was. Warm, almost.
- **Draw it, now:** the thaw changes the shape of everything. Yara hasn't seen this before either.

**Yara,** at the bottom, when they come down: she's looking at a drop of water on her glove. *Lines:* "That's wet." · "Nobody's going to buy ice from me." · "...Good."

**Bring it back.** Water. One drop, then another, then so many drops it sounds like rain, and it's been so long that nobody can remember the word.

**How it ends.** They sleep by the fire, with the forest dripping around them. Ask: **"What did the Frost Spire cost the thaw?"** Start with the Ringer. Let them answer in their own words, or not at all.

### Running the fights (Session 14)

#### The Spire guards

*Seven Glass-Wolves at the base and six Stilled on the stair. Half the Stilled are asleep until the first wolf shatters.*

- **Setup:** the wolves lie in a ring at the foot. The Stilled stand on the stair at 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 and 120 feet. The characters may be anywhere on the face.
- **What the wolves do:** they drag people off the first rope: bite, knock Prone, and pull. They can't reach past sixty feet. When three have shattered, the rest break off and go, fast.
- **What the Stilled do:** nothing, until glass breaks near them or someone passes within 5 feet. Then they hit whoever is closest (two claws) and try to shove them off: a hit means a Strength save, DC 12, or the climber falls 20 feet, 2d6.
- **The rhythm:** every wolf that bursts cracks the stair. The first one wakes three Stilled. Say the sound, then look up: "One of them has turned its head."
- **Show the way out early.** In round 1, a Stilled on the stair looks at a climber and you describe the fear. Talking works, as an action, at DC 15.
- **If it drags:** in round 4 the bell hums louder and the Stilled stop to listen for one round.
- **When it ends:** when three wolves have shattered, when everyone's above sixty feet, or the instant the bell rings. The Stilled stop at once.
- **Scale on the fly:** level 5, leave out two Stilled and one wolf. Three characters, five wolves and three Stilled. The climb and the falls will do the damage: add nobody.
- **Non-lethal outcomes:** someone who drops on the stair is caught by the rope. Someone who drops at the base is dragged a little way off and left, and Yara has a bandage.

### Pacing (Session 14)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:15 | Recap; who carries it, wrapped in what |
| 0:15 to 1:10 | Scene 1: the foot of the Spire (fight, or the sneaking) |
| 1:10 to 2:15 | Scene 2: the climb |
| 2:15 to 2:50 | Scene 3: the bell |
| 2:50 to 3:30 | Scene 4: the thaw, the Toll, the question |

- **Where to break:** at the top of the stair, before anyone steps under the bell.
- **Running long:** let the stair cover all three checks, and skip the wolves once they're over sixty feet.
- **Running short:** start Session 15's first scene at sunrise.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop with somebody's hand on the rope. Ask "Do you ring it?" and don't take an answer.

### If you get stuck (Session 14)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **A wolf gets up and stretches,** without waking. Then it lies down again.
2. **The bell hums and the Heart hums back.** Whoever's nearest feels it in their teeth.
3. **Yara points at the smoke.** It's closer.

**If nobody will pay:** it's all right. Ask, once: "Has everybody who wants to say something said it?" Then go to camp. Hieme can be rung another day. Isolde will still come for the Heart.

**If someone argues about the weight:** show them Part 2.7. It isn't a punishment, and it isn't a vote.

### End of session 14

**The closing question:** "What did the Frost Spire cost the thaw?"

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** the climb, the guards, the ringing (or the refusal), and where the Heart ended up.
- **World-state facts to check:** Hieme is rung; the Heart is with the party or in the bell; Stilled trust, if any of them were calmed or hurt.
- **The Toll:** in the Memory ledger as a Toll, with the weight and exactly what you said. The player's new belief, bond or fear goes next to it.
- **A sketch:** who drew it, or that nobody did. Yara will ask.

**Rewards:**
- **Hieme:** one more of the six for the Concord.
- **Glassreach:** beginning to thaw. The Stilled will wake over the coming weeks.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to the Ringer, and to whoever stayed below and kept the rope.

plays.title: They help the waking Stilled
plays.why: Hundreds of people are stepping out of a four-hundred-year winter with nothing, and the party caused it.
plays.readAloud: The forest drips. Everywhere, glass is turning back into bark and leaf, and people are stepping out of their own winters with their arms still raised, asking each other's names.
plays.response: The Stilled wake over several weeks, confused, angry or grateful, and need food, shelter and a way out. A party member who organises it (Yara's camp as a hall, Wyn and Maren Talla as guides, Kell's Crossing bread if Calla rang) earns the Stilled's trust. Ask each player one thing their character does for one waking stranger. The Stilled child asks for her mother; somebody has to tell her.

plays.fallback: If the party is in a hurry, Yara takes charge and asks only for coin and one promise: come back.

plays.title: They promise the Brightwater's crew passage home
plays.why: A dozen Sword Coast sailors from 1082 DR wake up and ask the way to the sea.
plays.readAloud: “The Brightwater was moored at a river mouth, west of here, under a sky full of weather.” The bosun looks at the clear, still air. “Where did the weather go?”
plays.response: Corran Vell and eleven of the Brightwater's crew want to go home through the Seam; nobody has told them about the Stormwall. Getting them to Pellmoor means Brannagh Wick's pilots and a captain willing to carry them. Venn's agents in Pellmoor would pay well to exhibit them in Athkatla, and a letter from the Landing says so to their faces; the party can refuse for them.

plays.fallback: If nobody takes them on, they set off south on their own, and Isolde's Hushmen arrest them at Kell's Crossing as Charter-breakers.

plays.rules: Influence DC 15 on a Baldurian factor or the Corvane Venture to find them berths; Venn will ask for nothing and want everything.

plays.response: She smiles and leaves; no fight. On her way out she looks, once, at whatever they care about most here (Yara, the Stilled child, Imber) so they know she noticed.

## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. The winter is over and everyone it took is waking up hungry. Then the Court arrives, very politely, for what the party carries. It ends with a choice of road that decides the whole of Act IV. It's mostly people, and one short show of force.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-15) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-15) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-15) · [Scene 1: The thaw](#scene-1-the-thaw) · [Scene 2: The request](#scene-2-the-request) · [Scene 3: What a lovely thaw](#scene-3-what-a-lovely-thaw) · [Scene 4: The map and the road](#scene-4-the-map-and-the-road) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-15) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-15) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-15) · [End of session](#end-of-session-15)

### Before you start (Session 15)

**Level:** four characters at level 6. They reach level 7 at the end, once Glassreach is settled.

**Check the world state first.** Six facts change tonight:
- **Did Hieme ring?** If nobody rang it, there's no thaw: the Stilled who are awake are the only ones, Scene 1 is a few people by one fire, and Isolde still comes.
- **Isolde:** following them, turned informant, captured (then Tristan Vesk comes instead), or retreated to the Court or never sent (then skip Scene 3 and give its time to Scenes 1 and 2).
- **Imber:** frozen, freed, dead, or taken. If he's free, Isolde's scene changes. If he's frozen in the chapel, she finds him.
- **The Hearts they carry.** Make a list. Isolde asks for Hieme's, and for Calla's if they have it.
- **Do the Stilled trust them?** No bond, wary, or earned. That picks which plays appear.
- **Which Stormborn ally do they have?** None, the Harpers, or Sister Aurelie's Dawn Mission. If none, tonight can give them a crew.

**What this session is about.** They've changed something very big, and now there are consequences: ninety-odd hungry strangers from four hundred years ago, a bosun who wants to go home, and a woman in grey lace with a small army of gloves. Nobody has to be beaten. Then they choose which of the two last bells to go for first.

**Your goals tonight:**
- Give each player one Stilled to help. Ask: "What does your character do for one person who's just woken up?"
- Let Isolde be frightened of them, and make her polite about it.
- Say the two roads fairly. Both will be visited: the one they leave gets shorter later.
- End on the question: **"Brassfall or Vael Tor: which bell next?"** Then stop. They'll plan on their own time.

**Prepare:**
- **Tokens or minis:** the four characters; Isolde (or Tristan); one Sergeant and four Hushmen; Yara; Maren; Imber; Vell.
- **Maps:** Yara's camp among thawing trees: one fire, a long table, a track to the south.
- **Props:** something wet. A bowl of melting ice in the middle of the table that you don't mention.
- **The sketch,** if one of them drew it. If not, be ready to ask someone to describe the top of the Spire.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **Influence** is the action for changing somebody's mind. Roll the skill you're using against the DC. Friendly people are easier to ask and hostile ones won't listen without a reason.
- **Winning back the Stilled:** Influence DC 17, with advantage if Maren or a Stilled they saved speaks for them. A sincere apology or a night on guard counts as a reason. If it fails, try again after a night of real work.
- **Grappled:** Speed 0, and Disadvantage on attacks against anyone but the grappler. A Hushman's Arrest is a Strength save, DC 12. Escape takes an action: Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics), DC 12.
- **Isolde's Cunning Action:** Dash, Disengage or Hide as a Bonus Action. That's how she leaves.
- **A creature at 0 HP** can be knocked out instead of killed, when a melee attack brings it there. Captured, not dead.
- **Heroic Inspiration** for a memory or a Gift given freely to a waking Stilled.
- **Cold:** it's thawing. No more saves by the fire. If they go out at night, Constitution DC 10 without a cloak.

**Places at a glance:**
- **Yara's camp:** one fire when they left, nine now. A long table made of doors.
- **The track south:** mud already.
- **The Spire:** a column of running water with a bell in it.

**Rumours (d6)** from people who've just woken:
1. "There's a bell in the sky." (True.)
2. "A man is telling everyone he's sorry." (True, if Imber's free.)
3. "They've got a soup with no taste. It's the best thing I've ever had." (True: it's the soup.)
4. "The river's talking." (True: it's the thaw.)
5. "The soldiers are coming to put us back." (False, but ask Maren what she's afraid of.)
6. "Is it still the same king?" (There isn't one.)

### Opening recap (Session 15)

> **SAY:** "Last time, you climbed the Frost Spire, and one of you heard Hieme ring. *(If it rang: say who, and what it cost.)* You slept to the sound of dripping. *(If it didn't: 'You came down, and it's still winter.')* You wake up and the first thing you hear is somebody crying, and then somebody laughing, and then a lot of people asking each other's names."

- **Then hand it over:** "What's the first thing your character does for a stranger this morning?" One answer each, quickly. That's Scene 1.

### Scene 1: The thaw

**Where and why.** Yara's camp, and the trees around it. Skip it if Hieme wasn't rung; instead, do the fire with whoever's awake.

> **SAY:** "The forest drips. Everywhere, glass is turning back into bark and leaf, and people are stepping out of their own winters with their arms still raised, asking each other's names."

**What's really going on.** There are ninety-odd people who haven't eaten since 1082. Yara has a kitchen and no plan, which is a first. [Helping them is the whole scene.](play:s15-help-stilled)

**Go round the table. Ask each player: "One person. What do they need, and what do you do?"** Take whatever they say, let it work, and give Heroic Inspiration for anything that costs them.

**Who they might meet:** a tall woman who can't stop apologising; a boy with a fishing rod; two brothers who want to know who won; a baker; a nun of the Ninefold (Brother Ewin's friend Sister Corrow); Joss Arrand with his bucket, if he was calmed in Session 11.

**If they…**
- **[Organise it:](play:s15-help-stilled)** Yara's camp as a hall, Wyn and Maren as guides, Kell's Crossing bread if Calla rang. It's the biggest thing a group can do here. It earns their trust.
- **Are in a hurry:** Yara takes charge. "Coin and one promise. Come back."
- **The child asks for her mother.** Let the table decide who tells her, and what. Don't rush. Her mother isn't among the Stilled. Her name was on a ribbon that Maren's family never found.
- **[The Stilled remember them badly:](play:s15-win-back-the-stilled)** if trust is wary, a woman steps out of the winter: "You. You woke my husband with fire." Read it, and let them answer. Influence DC 17, with advantage if Maren or a Stilled they saved vouches.
- **Vell and his crew:** twelve of them are awake and standing in a row, in order, the way they stood for muster.

> **SAY:** "'The *Brightwater* was moored at a river mouth, west of here, under a sky full of weather.' The bosun looks at the clear, still air. 'Where did the weather go?'"

- **[Promise them passage:](play:s15-brightwater-crew)** it'll take Brannagh Wick's pilots and a captain who'll carry them. Influence DC 15 on a Baldurian factor or the Corvane Venture. Venn will ask for nothing and want everything. If they show Vell's badge, it counts as his word; the crew follow whoever holds it. Let the player who's holding it say what they promise.
- **If somebody offers Venn's agents:** they'd pay well to show the crew in Athkatla. Vell gets to hear that. He says no. "We're not a fair."
- **Won't take them on:** they set out south alone, and Isolde's Hushmen arrest them at Kell's Crossing. Say so.

**Bring it back.** Someone who was calmed in Session 11 comes and puts a ribbon in a player's hand. It's theirs, with their own name on it.

**How it ends.** Everyone has a fire, a name and a bowl. And somebody says, "There are horses on the track."

### Scene 2: The request

**Where and why.** The long table, that afternoon. Only if enough of the Stilled are awake (Waypoint offers this card once the thaw's well along). Otherwise fold it into Scene 1.

> **SAY:** "The woman who steps forward is Maren Talla, thin and upright, with the dust of four centuries in her hair. 'We have a request,' she says. 'And a debt we would like to repay.'"

**What's really going on.** [The Stilled have a voice.](play:s15-stilled-emissary) They want food, shelter and somewhere to go. They'll walk to the Tor when the time comes, if trust is earned, and carry the Sexton's story. If trust is wary they want amends first. Influence DC 15 then; none if it's earned.

**Maren.** *Lines:* "I've been told. I should like to hear it from you. What year is it?" · "We don't want to be a wonder. We want to be neighbours." · "We'll walk. Slowly. Tell us which road." · "He asked me to forgive him. I said I'd think about it. I've had practice thinking."

**If they…**
- **Ask the year for her:** she listens to the number, nods, and counts it on her fingers.
- **Promise them somewhere:** record it in the bargain log. Kell's Crossing, Yara's camp, the Hall: anything they can do.
- **Ask them to fight:** they'll think about it. If trust is earned, they'd stand in front of somebody. They won't carry a blade.
- **Say no:** they thank them and ask for a map.

**Bring it back.** Maren gets up, looks at the Spire dripping, and sits down again in the first chair she's chosen for herself.

**How it ends.** The horses.

### Scene 3: What a lovely thaw

**Where and why.** The south track, at the edge of the camp. Yara's at their back, and Maren's. Isolde comes with a Sergeant and four Hushmen.

> **SAY:** "She's on foot, which she never is, with her skirt pinned up out of the mud and a Sergeant two paces behind. She looks at the fires, the table, the people. Then she looks at you, and smiles, the one that reaches her eyes."

Then, unless she's their informant or Tristan came instead, she says the plan's speech:

> **SAY (Isolde):** "What a lovely thaw. I'm told you have something of ours. The Frost Heart, let us say. Give it to us, and the Court will forget your little interference. Refuse, and the Court will remember it very precisely."

**What's really going on.** She's alone in the north, she doesn't want a fight, and she's frightened of what these people did. She'll leave if they refuse, and remember everything.

**Isolde.** Silk over mail, two sugars in a travelling cup, kind when nobody's looking. *Lines:* "You've made such a mess. It's charming." · "I'm not here to be clever, darling. I'm here because it's *cold*." · "Put it in my hands, and it stops being your problem. I'd love it if it stopped being your problem." · If they mention her son: "Leave my son out of this, or I'll put you in it."

**If they…**
- **[Refuse:](play:s15-refuse-isolde)** she smiles and leaves. On the way out she looks once at whatever they love most here, so they see her notice. Insight DC 15: relief.
- **[Give it to her:](play:s15-give-heart)** she takes it in both hands, away from her body. If they carry Calla's Heart she asks for that too, sweetly, and the Hushmen step closer. Hieme has already rung, so the thaw goes on. Record her promise in the Bargain Log, word for word, and write down what it doesn't cover.

> **SAY:** "She takes the Heart in both hands and holds it away from her body, as if it might drip. 'There. Wasn't that easy?'"

- **If it's hanging in the bell:** "Go and get it, then." She looks at the Spire. She isn't going up it. Her Hushmen spend a day finding that out.
- **[Attack her:](play:s15-attack-isolde)** see the fights. She's already moving.
- **[Capture her:](play:s15-capture-isolde)** a successful grapple, or 0 HP before her second turn. "Oh, you wonderful, wonderful people," she says, with her eyes on the road. Her Hushmen surrender. Treated kindly, she'll talk about her son, the Ironhorn sales and what the Court is planning.
- **She's their informant:** she makes the speech in front of her own people, word for word. [Then, while they water the horses,](play:s15-isolde-informant) without moving her lips: "I need a story. Give me one I can sell." They "lose" the Heart in the thaw, and she reports it. Deception DC 12 to stage it. She tells them what she knows: the Chancellor marches on the Tor the moment two more bells ring.
- **[She recognises Imber:](play:s15-isolde-wants-imber)** she stops in the middle of a word.

> **SAY:** "Isolde stops smiling. She looks at the old man in the borrowed cloak, at the shape of his nose, at the ring on his finger. 'Oh,' she says softly. 'Oh, Maudrin will hate this.'"

- **What she offers:** take him to Hallowmere, for his safety. She means Maudrin's. Influence DC 15 makes her forget she saw him; she wants something for it. If they say nothing, Imber introduces himself by his full title.
- **[She takes him:](play:s15-isolde-takes-imber)** only if they let her, or lose. If he was frozen, her people carry him out in his block with a lamp under it.
- **Tristan comes instead:** [his own offer](play:s15-tristan-envoy), less charming and more honest. "Tristan Vesk. The Chancellor's cousin, and, I'm afraid, the one who writes her letters." He wants Isolde back; her release is a bargaining chip. He mentions, to see their faces, that the Court has a second Chancellor waiting.
- **Haven't got it:** lie (Deception DC 15), or say who has.

**Bring it back.** The fourth Hushman, the one who heard the bell, has stopped listening to anybody. Ask them what they hear.

**How it ends.** Isolde is gone, or taken, or on their side. The Hushmen are wet to the knee.

### Scene 4: The map and the road

**Where and why.** Evening. Yara's table, one lamp, and the road.

> **SAY:** "Yara clears a space with her forearm and unrolls the sketch. She weights its corners with cups. 'Nobody has ever drawn that,' she says, and for once she does not name a price."

**What's really going on.** [The sketch.](play:s15-yara-map) If nobody drew one, she asks them to describe it and writes it herself. It earns her loyalty: a guide, stores and a lower price. Heroic Inspiration for a drawing given freely.

**Then the road.** Tell them both, the same way, and don't lean.

> **SAY (Brassfall):** "East, past the last glass trees, the sky flickers over a line of bronze-veined mountains, though there are no clouds at all."

> **SAY (Vael Tor):** "South and east, the plain rises to a single hill ringed with grey stones. Even from here, if you close your eyes, you can hear something breathing in its sleep."

**What they know, so you can say it straight:**
- **[Brassfall](play:s15-road-brassfall):** six days around the Ironhorn foothills. The bell is Thrane, storms; its Heart is in Kessa's Heart-Hall. Ringing it brings the storms back, and sailors say it'd loosen the Stormwall.
- **[Vael Tor](play:s15-road-vael-tor):** about a week, by Kell's Crossing. The bell is Mirel, dreams. If they have its Heart, they can ring it as soon as they get there; if not, the Librarian's courier is waiting at the Hall.
- **Both bells are needed** for the Concord. The one they don't choose now becomes a shorter visit later (Sessions 20 and 21).
- **Yara:** "Brassfall pays better."
- **Imber,** if he's alive: "The Tor. It is where it ends. I would like to see it before."

**Bring it back.** Yara unrolls another sheet, empty. "That's for whichever one you draw next."

**How it ends.** Ask: **"Brassfall or Vael Tor: which bell next?"** If they can't agree, they don't have to tonight. Let them say what they'd want to know first.

### Running the fights (Session 15)

#### Isolde's escort

*Lady Isolde (Court Agent), one Hushman Sergeant and four Hushmen. A show of force. The party is meant to win, or she's meant to leave.*

- **Setup:** at the edge of camp, in mud. Isolde at the front and the Hushmen in a loose half-circle.
- **What happens:** she talks first. She fights only if attacked: one round of poisoned daggers, then Cunning Action to Disengage and Dash for the trees. The Hushmen grapple whoever's closest to her and fall back by twos.
- **She has silence-stone gloves.** Her attacks make no sound. They don't stop spells.
- **Who to worry about:** nobody. Hushmen want arrests. If one drops a character, it ties their hands and waits.
- **When it ends:** she's out of sight among the trees. Her people surrender if the Sergeant goes down, or if she's taken. Nobody chases anybody south.
- **If they fought out of Hallowmere in Session 9,** add two Hushmen.
- **If they raid her camp by night,** add two more Sergeants.
- **If it's Tristan,** a smaller escort and no Cunning Action. He leaves with a promise.
- **Scale on the fly:** three characters, the Sergeant and two Hushmen.
- **Non-lethal outcomes:** it's a fight in front of ninety witnesses, and she knows it. She'll call off her own people the moment it looks ugly.

### Pacing (Session 15)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:10 | Recap; the first thing you do for a stranger |
| 0:10 to 1:10 | Scene 1: the thaw |
| 1:10 to 1:30 | Scene 2: the request |
| 1:30 to 2:25 | Scene 3: what a lovely thaw (allow 45 minutes more for a fight) |
| 2:25 to 3:20 | Scene 4: the map and the road |
| 3:20 to 3:30 | The question |

- **Where to break:** when somebody says "There are horses on the track."
- **Running long:** fold the request into the thaw. Never cut the road.
- **Running short:** let each player say one thing to a person they've helped, on the way out.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop when Isolde leaves. Ask the road question by message, between sessions.

### If you get stuck (Session 15)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **Somebody asks them their name** and gets it wrong on purpose, politely.
2. **The child comes out from under the table** and asks to be held.
3. **A Hushman drops their gloves in the mud.** They've got no idea what they're for now.

**If they can't choose the road:** ask each of them to name one person they want to see again before the end, and where that person is.

**Names for the waking** (cross one off when you use it): Sister Corrow, the baker Hen Tull, the boy Finny with the fishing rod, the tall woman Iva Roke, Mr. Aske the schoolmaster, two brothers, Ren and Hal Dorne.

### End of session 15

**The closing question:** "Brassfall or Vael Tor: which bell next?" Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** the thaw, the crew, Isolde (or Tristan), Imber, the road.
- **World-state facts to check:** Stilled trust, Stormborn friends, the Frost Heart (party, bell or Court), Isolde, Imber, the Court Clock, the Act IV route.
- **Bargain log:** anything Isolde or Tristan promised, in their own words, and anything the party promised the Stilled.
- **Set the Act IV route** in World state, if they chose one. It picks which of the next sessions appear.

**Rewards:**
- **Level:** level 7, now that Glassreach is resolved.
- **The thaw's people:** the Stilled, if trust is earned, walk to the Tor in Act V.
- **The Brightwater's crew,** if promised passage: a Faerûnian ally for Act IV.
- **Yara,** for good, if they gave her the sketch.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to whoever gave the most to a stranger, and to whoever drew the Spire.

## Table card

plays.readAloud: The mountains are veined with bronze. Old lightning-shafts drop into the earth like the throats of bells. The sky flickers above you, though there are no clouds.
plays.response: Branch A runs in full (16A–19A); Vael Tor is compressed later into Sessions 20–21. Both bells matter for the Concord.
plays.consequence: The party is on Branch A.

plays.title: They carry Old Garrow's lamp
plays.why: A gruff, funny ghost asks a plain favor (H-20).
plays.readAloud: "Right, lads and lasses, you look like you can carry a lamp. My girl's in the Ironhorn foothills, near the camp, with a red horse-skull on her tent. Yenna's her name. Tell her I'm sorry about the collapse. And don't drop it. It's the only thing down here that hums on purpose."
plays.response: The lamp holds the storm-stone that tethers Garrow. Carrying it lets his ghost rest near his daughter. In exchange he leads them safely through the Old Works, past the unstable shaft and, if they ask, past the Storm-stone Golems. Tell the table plainly that the lamp holds a stone, and stones attract the Thane (H-20).
plays.consequence: A safe path through the mine, and a reason to meet Yenna.
plays.tells: Players accept the lamp or ask about Yenna.
plays.rules: The lamp is a storm-stone: metal near it sparks. Old Garrow uses the 2024 Specter (CR 1) but rarely fights.
plays.later: S17A: Yenna takes the lamp, or Kessa demands the storm-stone for his Heart-Hall (see the lamp plays there). S28: Garrow's laugh is heard once more if the lamp reached Yenna.
plays.keywords: garrow, lamp, ghost, yenna, carry, favor, old works, h-20

plays.title: They refuse Garrow's request
plays.why: Some parties won't carry a ghost's tether into an armed camp.
plays.readAloud: Garrow's lamp dims. "Suit yourselves. Mind the third shaft, then. It's cracked. I'd know."
plays.response: He withdraws, disappointed, but warns them which shaft is unstable. Declining never triggers the collapse; only entering the visibly cracked passage risks it.
plays.consequence: No guide through the mine, and no lamp for the golems to recognise.
plays.tells: Players decline or ignore him.
plays.rules: Entering the cracked shaft: DC 13 Dexterity save, 3d6 Bludgeoning on a failure, half on a success.
plays.later: S17A: Yenna meets them without her father's message and is cooler; the party earns her trust by other means. S16A: the golems do not stand aside for them, so the vault is a fight or a skipped room.
plays.keywords: refuse, garrow, no, decline, lamp, ghost

plays.title: They loot the storm-stone vault
plays.why: A room of glittering storm-stones is irresistible, and guarded.
plays.readAloud: A treasure room of storm-stones, pale blue and humming. Every metal thing you carry sings back at them.
plays.response: Picking one up safely takes care; a fumbled stone discharges. Each stone lifted wakes one more Storm-stone Golem (up to three). Storm-stones are illegal to export and smuggled anyway; Mirabar dwarves in Pellmoor pay well, and the Court arrests sellers.
plays.consequence: Storm-stones in hand and golems to deal with, or a clean retreat.
plays.fallback: If the golems are too much, back out of the room: they do not leave the vault. With Garrow's lamp in hand they stand aside (next play). Without the lamp, a Bloodied golem's shard can be prised out.
plays.tells: Players ask what storm-stones are worth, or pick one up.
plays.rules: Pick up a stone: DC 13 Dexterity check; failure 3d8 Lightning. Encounter: the golems. Prising a golem's shard out (Utilize action, DC 15 Strength (Athletics), once it is Bloodied) deactivates that golem. Wooden weapons do not trigger their Storm-Stone Heart.
plays.later: Anytime: a stone sold in Pellmoor is any-sell-storm-stone (Landing clock). S17A: Kessa wants stones for his Heart-Hall and notices who carries them.
plays.keywords: storm-stone, vault, treasure, golem, loot, lightning, mine

plays.title: They notice the storm-stones hum toward the sea
plays.why: A v6 clue: the dead lightning wants to go where Thrane's storms went.
plays.readAloud: Every storm-stone in the vault hums a little louder when you turn it west, toward the sea, the way a compass needle hums toward north.
plays.response: A Stormborn character recognises the sound: the same thunder they sailed through in the Stormwall. Let them guess. Garrow says the stones "always leaned west, since before my time." Corin, later, says the storms "went to the rim and wait."
plays.consequence: The party suspects ringing Thrane will affect the Stormwall.
plays.tells: A Stormborn sailor or an Arcana-trained character studies the stones.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) DC 15, or automatic for a character who crossed the Seam.
plays.later: S19A or S21: ringing Thrane loosens the Stormwall. S28: new fleets crowd Pellmoor and the Landing Charter strains (s28-landing-fleets).
plays.keywords: stormwall, storm-stone, west, sea, thunder, clue, seam, sailor

plays.title: They examine the lamp before agreeing
plays.why: Careful players inspect a ghost's gift.
plays.readAloud: The blue flame does not flicker when you breathe on it. At its heart, pale and humming, sits a stone no bigger than a thumb.
plays.response: A Study action (Intelligence (Arcana) DC 15) shows a storm-stone inside, its dead lightning tied to Garrow. It sparks near metal. Detect Magic shows a tether of abjuration and necromancy. Dispel Magic on it frees Garrow's ghost at once, and he gives no help in the Old Works.
plays.consequence: The party knows what it is agreeing to carry.
plays.tells: A player asks what is in the lamp or tries to identify it.
plays.rules: Study, Intelligence (Arcana) DC 15. Dispel Magic ends the tether.
plays.later: S17A: Kessa wants exactly this stone.
plays.keywords: lamp, arcana, identify, detect magic, storm-stone

plays.title: The golems stand aside for the lamp
plays.why: Garrow's lamp is the golems' kin-stone.
plays.readAloud: The great bronze shapes turn their heads toward the blue flame, and then, one by one, they step back from the door.
plays.response: With the lamp, the golems attack no one who lifts a stone carefully (the DC 13 Dexterity check still applies); they attack only if the lamp is set down or a stone is thrown. Garrow chuckles. A stone is still a stone: selling one is a crime in Pellmoor.
plays.consequence: The vault is open without a fight.
plays.tells: The party carries the lamp into the vault.
plays.rules: Lifting a stone: DC 13 Dexterity check, 3d8 Lightning on a failure.
plays.later: Anytime: selling a stone is any-sell-storm-stone.

plays.title: They find a lightning tree on the Brass Road
plays.why: The steppe is storm country. Lightning that has nowhere to go ends up in trees and carts and people, and the Ironhorn know what it's worth.
plays.readAloud: A lone oak stands on the hillside, split down the middle by lightning, years ago. It's still crackling. Blue light crawls up and down the wound, and every hair on your arms stands up when you come near.
plays.response: The Brass Road and the steppe, entry 1. A storm-stone has grown in the heart of the tree. Cutting it out takes a DC 14 Strength check with an axe or a pick, and each attempt hurts. If they'd rather meet people, run entry 2, the bronze carts, with a storm coming. Or roll a d12 on The Brass Road and the steppe.

plays.rules: Each attempt, the cutter makes a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw: 2d10 Lightning damage, half on a success. Gloves of anything but metal give Advantage. The storm-stone is worth 100 gp in Brassfall or to the Ironhorn, or Tavi Ondrel the storm-smith binds it into a Javelin of Lightning (uncommon) for 100 gp and the stone (Shops of the Brass Road).
