## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. It's a lullaby, then a fight to get off the hill. A bell that gives instead of taking, hundreds of people turning over in their sleep, and the first hope anyone's felt in months. Let them have it before the grey riders come.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-19b) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-19b) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-19b) · [Scene 1: The Heart and the bed](#scene-1-the-heart-and-the-bed) · [Scene 2: Ringing Mirel](#scene-2-ringing-mirel) · [Scene 3: The first good morning](#scene-3-the-first-good-morning) · [Scene 4: Dry gloves](#scene-4-dry-gloves) · [Scene 5: Off the hill](#scene-5-off-the-hill) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-19b) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-19b) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-19b) · [End of session](#end-of-session-19b)

### Before you start (Session 19B)

**Level:** four characters at level 7.

**Check the world state first.** Five facts change tonight:
- **Mirel's Heart:** do they have it? If it's still with the courier, the first scene is [the bargain](play:s16b-courier-bargain), again.
- **Mirel:** if she rang already, in 16B, go straight to Scene 3.
- **How many bells have they already rung?** That sets the Toll's weight: none or one, **Heavy**; two or three, **Grievous**; four or five, **Ruinous.**
- **The Cult:** ceased or feeding? It decides who's crying, and where the party can run to.
- **Corin:** an ally? He can put the Toll off an hour.

**What this session is about.** Hope has a price, and it's a strange one: to make the fear stop for everyone else, somebody has to take a new one home.

**Your goals tonight:**
- Give the warning, honestly, before anybody lifts a hand.
- Make the ringing beautiful. Read it quietly.
- Give everyone a good half hour. Then the riders.
- End on the question: **"What did it feel like to hope?"** Then stop.

**Prepare:**
- **Tokens or minis:** the four characters; three Wardens; three Sergeants; six Hushmen.
- **Maps:** the Hall, with its rows; the hillside outside, with the ring of stones and the Cult's little circle on one side.
- **A lullaby,** any one, hummed or played very softly. Stop it when you read the ringing.
- **The Toll Deck,** and the fear cards you made for Session 16B. **Don't use one of those for the Toll. The bell gives a *new* fear.**

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **The Fear Toll (the bell gives one):** when the Ringer's in sight of the thing, at the start of each turn they make a Wisdom save, DC 13, or they're Frightened until that turn ends. **Heavy:** for a year. **Grievous:** for good. **Ruinous:** for good, and it's something they can't avoid, like the dark, or sleep.
- **It's a feeling.** It never decides what the character does. Magic can't end it early; Calm Emotions helps for a minute, and Heroes' Feast for a day.
- **Use only fears the player agreed to** at session zero.
- **Frightened:** Disadvantage on checks and attacks while they can see it, and they can't choose to move closer.
- **Warden's Stone:** while it's out, nobody can cast a spell within 10 feet of the Warden. **It's a thing:** AC 12, 10 HP. Or knock it off its chain: a Utilize action and Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), DC 15.
- **Arrest:** Strength save, DC 12, or they're Grappled and can't cast anything with a Verbal part.

### Key people tonight (Session 19B)

| Who | What they are | Stat block | Where | Starts | Influence | Secret |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Warden Thale** | Commands the patrol | Hushman Warden | The south road | Courteous | DC 16, and only to let the sleepers alone | His sister's in bed sixty. He hasn't told his men. |
| **Sergeant Ivo Quade** | His second | Hushman Sergeant | At his shoulder | By the book | DC 15 | He's started humming at night. He thinks nobody's heard. |
| **Mother Lumen** | Leader of the Hush Cult | Hush Cult Leader | The Hall, or the circle | Weeping | None needed | She hasn't dreamed for eleven years. She will tonight. |
| **Brother Lull** | Tucks them in | Hush Cultist | The rows, with a lamp | Beside himself | None needed | He's got a list of every name, and where they came from. |
| **Wat and Pip Furrow** | Waiting at bed two hundred and twelve | Hush Cultist; Pip has no stats | The far rows | Hopeful | None needed | Pip's brought her shoes. |
| **Page two hundred and six** | The courier, if it's still here | Commoner | By the central bed | Patient | It trades | It'd like to hear the bell before it goes back. |

**Places at a glance:**
- **The central bed:** empty, and always has been. The bell hangs over it. To ring Mirel, you stand on the bed.
- **The rows:** hundreds of sleepers, climbing away into the grey.
- **The hillside:** stones, long grass, the south road, the Cult's circle to the west.

**Rumours (d6)** among the Cult this morning:
1. "It doesn't take. Mirel *gives*." (True.)
2. "The last one who rang her was afraid of birds till he died." (True.)
3. "Grey coats on the south road. A dozen." (True.)
4. "If she rings, they'll all wake up." (False. They'll dream, and it'll be a good one.)
5. "There was never anyone in that bed." (True. It was made for the Ringer, to lie down after.)
6. "The stair's gone quiet." (True.)

### Opening recap (Session 19B)

> **SAY:** "You've been as far as step *(nineteen / twenty / a hundred)*. Something spoke to each of you in your own voice. It asked you *(read out one or two)*. Now you're back in the Hall, in the grey light, with *(a warm bronze Heart the size of a loaf / a man with a hammer / a child holding a pair of shoes)*. Hundreds of people are asleep all round you. And over the empty bed there's a bell, the colour of old honey, leaning toward you."

- **Then hand it over:** "What's the best night's sleep your character ever had?" One answer each. Don't rush. It's the shape of what's coming.

### Scene 1: The Heart and the bed

**Where and why.** The Hall. Settle who's doing it, and say the price.

> **SAY:** "The bed under the bell is made up, with one corner turned down. It's the only empty one that's got dust on it. Standing on it, you could just reach."

**What's really going on.** Mirel wants her Heart. She's the gentlest of the seven, and the only one whose Toll comes toward you.

**If they…**
- **Haven't got the Heart:** the courier's here. [A dream you've never told anyone,](play:s16b-courier-bargain) or a Gift. It'd very much like to hear it, so it'll take the dream *after*, if they give their word.
- **Robbed the courier:** it isn't here. Its book is, face down.
- **Have Corin as an ally:** he's walking up and down, whispering. "Once. Let her ring *out*. Don't damp it. And lie down, after. That's what it's for."
- **[Ask Corin to put the Toll off:](play:s19b-corin-defers-toll)** he can, for an hour.

> **SAY:** "Corin lays a hand on your shoulder. 'An hour,' he says. 'Ring first. Be afraid after.'"

- **Ask what'll happen to the sleepers:** nobody knows. Lull's got a lamp in each hand.
- **Look for trouble:** Wisdom (Perception) DC 13, from the door: dust on the south road, a long way off. An hour, perhaps. Is there time? Yes.

**Bring it back.** The bell moves an inch toward whoever's holding the Heart. Then an inch toward somebody who isn't.

**How it ends.** Someone steps up on to the bed, with their boots off.

### Scene 2: Ringing Mirel

**Where and why.** The bed. This is the Toll. Straight, and then soft.

**Say the warning first, out loud, to everyone:**

> **SAY:** "Mirel will give you a fear, and it will be *(Heavy / Grievous / Ruinous)*."

**Then explain it, out of character:**
- **It's a new fear.** You choose it, after it rings.
- **Heavy:** a year. **Grievous:** for good. **Ruinous:** for good, and of something they can't avoid.
- What it does: near the thing, a Wisdom save, DC 13, at the start of each turn, or Frightened until that turn ends.
- **It's never anything that player ruled out.** Anyone can ring in anyone's place. Anyone can say no.

**If they…**
- **[Ring her:](play:s19b-ring-mirel)** stop the music. Read it as if there were a baby asleep in the next room:

> **SAY:** "The bell sings like a lullaby sung by someone who loves you. Every sleeper on the Tor sighs and turns over. The Sleepless dissolve into mist. For a moment the air feels like the first morning of spring, and you feel, impossibly, hopeful."

- **Go round, first:** "What does your character hope for, right now? You hadn't for a while." One line each. **Then give the Toll.**
- **Choosing the fear:** pick something small, particular, and a bit odd, that'll turn up now and then: birds indoors; the sound of a latch; being thanked; deep water; a chair facing a wall. Say how it feels arriving: "You're lying on the bed. You look up, and you notice there's a gap under the door, and you can't stop noticing it." Record it: kind Fear, bell Mirel.
- **[Say no, all of them:](play:s19b-refuse)** that's allowed. She's silent, the Sleepless still walk, and she can be rung another time. The Forecast shows what it means.

> **SAY:** "The bell hangs above the central bed, its Heart in your hand, and you lower your arm."

**Bring it back.** Hundreds of people turn over. Say it again, later, whenever it's quiet: "They've all turned over."

**How it ends.** The Ringer lies down, for a minute. It's what the bed's for.

### Scene 3: The first good morning

**Where and why.** All over the hill. This is the reward. Half an hour. Protect it.

> **SAY:** "They haven't woken. But it's a different sort of sleeping. Somebody's smiling. Somebody's snoring, and the old man next to them, who hasn't moved in ninety years, puts a pillow over his head. The light in the glass roof's gone gold. And under the hill, very low, the lullaby's changed key. It sounds sad, and then it sounds grateful."

**Pick two or three, and let the players choose:**
- **Lumen.** [She's on her knees by the bell.](play:s19b-cult-after-mirel) The whole Cult's stopped humming. If they'd not been convinced, they're convinceable now, without a roll.

> **SAY:** "The Leader is on her knees. 'It sounded like someone loved it. We had forgotten.'"

- **Wat and Pip.** Bed two hundred and twelve. She's dreaming, and she's laughing at it. Pip puts her shoes on the floor beside the bed, side by side, for when. [They can have a minute with her now,](play:s16b-wake-a-sleeper) and it's easier: no check.
- **Brother Lull.** He's got his list. Every name, every village. He asks the party to carry copies. "So someone *comes*." Letters home for hundreds of people: it's a good thing to have in Act V.
- **Page two hundred and six.** It shuts its book, and it's crying ink. "That is what we were *for*," says the Librarian.
- **The stones.** The little lights are going up, one at a time, like sparks off a fire.
- **Lie down in the grass.** Anyone who sleeps now dreams, and it's theirs. (Not if the Hush has their dreams. Then somebody sits with them.) It counts as a Short Rest.

**Go round the table:** "What does your character do with half an hour of hope?" Ask the Ringer last. If their fear turns up, play it gently.

**Bring it back.** They've all turned over.

**How it ends.** Pip, from the door: "There's *soldiers*. They're walking funny. They're not making any noise."

### Scene 4: Dry gloves

**Where and why.** The hillside, south. The Court heard.

> **SAY:** "Grey riders come out of the marsh at a walk. Their gloves are dry."

**What's really going on.** [They've come to investigate, and to arrest whoever rang.](play:s19b-hushmen-arrive) Warden Thale's a decent man with an order. His sister's been in bed sixty for nineteen years.

**Warden Thale.** Quiet, tidy, tired; takes his helmet off to talk. *Lines:* "Which of you rang it? No. Don't tell me yet. Once you've told me I've got to do something." · "I'll have the Heart, and I'll have the Ringer. I'd like to do it in that order, with nobody lying down." · If they're kind about the sleepers: "Is there… do you know who's in sixty?"

**If they…**
- **Take him to bed sixty:** he goes, with two men. She's smiling. He stands there for as long as you like. **He still has an order.** But he'll give them until sunset before he remembers it, if they ask. Influence, Persuasion DC 16, or no roll if Lull shows him her socks.
- **Lie about who rang:** Deception against his Insight, at Disadvantage: the Ringer's got honey-coloured light in their hair, and it won't brush out.
- **Give up the Heart:** he'll take it, and he'll look away while the Ringer leaves. Write it down.
- **Give up the Ringer:** it's a real choice. It's a jail, not a grave; you've got a rescue for next session.
- **Hide among the sleepers:** lovely. Six of them search the rows, very quietly, on tiptoe, because it's a room full of people asleep. A group Stealth check, DC 13, under the covers.
- **Run west, into the Cult's circle:** they won't follow. It's the one place the Court has never set foot. If the Cult's an ally, they link hands.
- **Stand:** he puts his helmet on. "I'm sorry about this." Run the fight. **Outside.** He won't fight in the Hall, and neither should they.

**Bring it back.** One of the Hushmen's crying, and hasn't noticed.

**How it ends.** The Court's driven off; or it's got what it came for; or the party's gone.

### Scene 5: Off the hill

**Where and why.** Wherever they are when it's over. Short. Look at the road.

> **SAY:** "From the edge of the stones you can see the whole plain. It's evening. There are lights a long way off, villages, and they've got the look of places where people are sitting up talking. Whatever you did, they felt it there too. Behind you somebody's closing the doors of the Hall, very quietly, with a shoe."

**What's really going on.** The Court now knows exactly who they are. The second bell's across the plain, at Brassfall, and it's coming faster (Sessions 20 and 21).

**If they…**
- **Ask what's next:** east. [A thane with black hands,](play:s20-brassfall-second) and a bell in a hole in the ground.
- **Want to leave somebody here:** Lull'll have them. There's a bed, if they're tired. (There's always a bed.)
- **[Ask the Cult to stand with them:](play:s22-ally-cult)** if they've ceased, yes. Lumen's asleep. Nod says it for her. "I'd like to. I'd forgotten that I could like to."
- **Listen at the stair:** "Thank you," it says, in nobody's voice. Then, "Be quiet now."

**Bring it back.** They've all turned over.

**How it ends.** Ask: **"What did it feel like to hope?"** The Ringer last.

### Running the fights (Session 19B)

#### Court Hushmen on the hill

*Three Wardens (AC 16, 82 HP), three Sergeants (AC 15, 52 HP), six Hushmen (AC 12, 32 HP). Run it outside.*

- **Setup:** the hillside, with the ring of stones for cover. The patrol comes up from the south in three little groups: a Warden, a Sergeant and two Hushmen each. The Cult's circle is 80 feet west.
- **What happens:** one group goes for the Ringer, and one for the Heart. The third stands between the party and the circle. Sergeants call on people to surrender. Wardens open their cases when somebody starts casting: **say the light's going flat first,** and give the caster a turn.
- **A Warden's turn:** two blows (+5, 12 damage, pushed 10 feet), or two crossbow shots (+4, 13).
- **A Sergeant's turn:** two light blows or shots (+4; about 5 each, and 3 Necrotic with the glove), or one and a signal: an ally attacks with a d4 extra.
- **A Hushman's turn:** a glove (+5, 5 and 2 Necrotic; Advantage beside a friend), or an arrest (Strength DC 12 or Grappled; escape DC 12).
- **Who to worry about:** the Ringer. If they're Grappled and carried 60 feet down the hill, they've been taken. Say so out loud each round.
- **The stones are the fight for a caster.** AC 12, 10 HP, or a hand on the chain.
- **When it ends:** the commanding Warden falls; or the party's inside the Cult's circle; or they've got the Ringer or the Heart, and they go.
- **Scale on the fly:** one Sergeant instead of three for a lighter fight. Two Wardens for a lighter one still.
- **Non-lethal:** all of it. They arrest. Anyone who drops wakes up tied, and still has their boots.

### Pacing (Session 19B)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:10 | Recap; the best sleep you ever had |
| 0:10 to 0:30 | Scene 1: the Heart and the bed |
| 0:30 to 1:00 | Scene 2: ringing Mirel |
| 1:00 to 1:40 | Scene 3: the first good morning |
| 1:40 to 2:50 | Scene 4: dry gloves, and the fight |
| 2:50 to 3:10 | Scene 5: off the hill |
| 3:10 to 3:20 | The question |

- **Where to break:** when Pip says "soldiers."
- **Running long:** let Thale go to bed sixty, and give them until sunset. No fight.
- **Running short:** write three of Lull's letters home. Who are they to?
- **If you need to stop early:** stop on the first good morning, and let the riders be next week's opening. It's a kind way to end a hard stretch.

### If you get stuck (Session 19B)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **A sleeper says a name,** clearly, and it's one of theirs.
2. **The bell hums by itself,** one bar, and everyone finishes it.
3. **The Ringer's new fear** turns up, small, in the corner of the room.

**If nobody wants to pay the Toll:** don't push. She can be rung later. The Sleepless will still walk until she is, and that's the only thing that's lost.

**If the fear you picked lands badly:** stop, and change it, out loud. "It wasn't that. It was this."

**Names for Hushmen and sleepers** (cross one off when you use it): Hushman Ferrin, Hushman Cray, Corporal Wend, Bess in sixty, Grandfather Moll, the twins Ede and Ewan, Master Wick the dyer.

### End of session 19B

**The closing question:** "What did it feel like to hope?" Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** the ringing (or the refusal), the Cult, the riders.
- **World-state facts to check:** Mirel (rung), Mirel's Heart, the Cult, the Court and Hush Clocks. No new Sleepless on the Tor.
- **Toll log:** the fear, and its weight.
- **Lull's list:** who's carrying it, and any letters they promised to deliver.
- **Who was arrested,** if anyone was.

**Rewards:**
- **A bell, rung.** The Concord's one step closer.
- **A safe hill.** Nobody rolls to sleep on the Tor again.
- **Level 8.** Session 20's fights are written for it, so tonight's a good time.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to the Ringer, and to whoever sat with them.

## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. It's the other half of the story, told fast: the place they didn't go first. One arrival, one bargain, one Heart. Everything here was a whole session on the other road, so pick the best scene of each and let the rest happen on the way.*

### Before you start (Session 20)

**Level:** four characters at level 8.

**Check the world state first.** Five facts decide the night:
- **Act IV road:** if they went to **Brassfall first (A)**, tonight's **Vael Tor**. If they went to **Vael Tor first (B)**, tonight's **Brassfall**. Cross out the half of each scene you don't need. That's most of your preparation.
- **The Heart they're here for:** Thrane's (Brassfall) or Mirel's (the Tor). If they've already got it, Scene 3 is a conversation instead of a bargain.
- **The lamp** (Brassfall only): nobody's, carried, or already with Yenna.
- **Corin:** if he's still **unmet**, he finds them tonight, in Scene 4. If he's an ally or refused, skip him.
- **Mirel** (the Tor only): if she's rung, nothing walks at night.

**What this session is about.** They've done this once. They know what a Heart costs now. What'll they pay when they can see the bill coming?

**Your goals tonight:**
- Get them across the plain, and show them what the first ringing changed.
- Run one real bargain, with a real cost, and let them choose it.
- Have them leave with the Heart, or with a clear reason why not.
- End on the question: **"What did the second Heart cost you?"** Then stop.

**Prepare:**
- **The other road's guide.** For Brassfall, skim Sessions 16A and 17A. For the Tor, skim 16B. Put a bookmark in the one scene you liked best, and run that one properly.
- **Tokens or minis:** the four characters. **Brassfall:** two Champions, five Riders, five Warhorses. **The Tor:** four Sleepless.
- **Maps:** the Heart-Hall and the fires round it; or the hillside and the ring of stones.
- **For Brassfall:** something metal you can put down as a stake. **For the Tor:** a notebook with no words in it.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **Influence:** they say what they want; you decide if the person's Willing, Hesitant or Unwilling. Only Hesitant needs a roll.
- **Help:** anyone proficient can give a friend Advantage on one check.
- **An oath is a rule at this table.** If Kessa's loan is sworn, write the exact words down. It's checked next session.
- **A traded dream's gone.** The player makes it up, says it once, and the character doesn't have it any more.
- **Sleeping on Vael Tor (if Mirel's unrung):** everyone who sleeps makes a Wisdom save, DC 13. A failure is a nightmare; failing by 5 or more brings one Sleepless (one a night at most). Whoever stays on watch doesn't roll.
- **Passing unseen through a camp:** Stealth, DC 15 each. One careful plan is worth Advantage.

### Key people tonight (Session 20)

| Who | What they are | Stat block | Where | Starts | Influence | Secret |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Old Garrow** | Foreman's ghost (Brassfall) | Specter, but he rarely fights | The mouth of the Old Works | Gruff; friendly to anyone who works | None needed | He thinks the Ironhorn raid was his fault. |
| **Yenna Garrow** | His daughter, a clan rider | Ironhorn Rider | The red horse-skull | Wary | DC 15; none with the lamp | She's always known he's down there. |
| **Kessa Ironhorn** | Thane of the Ironhorn | Kessa Ironhorn | The Heart-Hall | Loud, fair | DC 15 | Dying of the Heart's lightning. The Key won't cure him. |
| **The courier** | The Librarian's hands (the Tor) | Commoner | The central bed | Patient | It trades | "Page two hundred and six." It'd like to be put back. |
| **Mother Lumen** | Leader of the Hush Cult (the Tor) | Hush Cult Leader | The circle of humming | Kind | Not tonight | Her rest takes every dream you've got. |
| **Corin Aldeth** | A Bellwright, if he's unmet | Corin Aldeth | Wherever they camp | Hopeful | DC 15 | "The whole name" is the Ringer's own. He's guessed. |

**Places at a glance:**
- **Brassfall:** a red town under veined mountains. The Old Works below, the clan camp above, the Heart-Hall in the middle of it with forty fires round it.
- **Vael Tor:** one grey hill, a ring of stones, a glass-roofed Hall with hundreds asleep in it, and a stair round the back.

**Rumours (d6)** on the road between:
1. "A bell rang. My aunt slept through the night, or it stormed, or it's finished with *something*." (True; say which.)
2. "Grey coats are asking for four travellers. They've got drawings. They're not good drawings." (True.)
3. "There's a fellow with a hammer asking too. He says please." (True if Corin's unmet.)
4. "The Thane's taken to wearing gloves at supper." (True.)
5. "There's a library that walks. It's got as far as the hill." (True.)
6. "Maudrin Vesk is dead." (False. She's packing.)

### Opening recap (Session 20)

> **SAY:** "Six bells hang in the Ninefold Shore, and you've stood under *(number)* of them. The last one was *(Thrane's, in the Lightning Shafts / Mirel's, in the Sleeping Hall)*. You paid *(the Toll, in one line)*, or you walked away. The Court's grey riders came for you afterwards, and they know your faces now. There's one more bell on this side of the sea. It's three days across the plain, and it's getting dark earlier."

- **Then hand it over:** "What's the one thing your character's doing differently, this time?" One line each. Hold them to it.

### Scene 1: Across the plain

**Where and why.** Three days on the road. Fifteen minutes. It's here so the players can see what they did.

> **SAY:** "You can tell where the bell reached. There's a line across the country, as if somebody'd drawn it. On one side of it people look the way they've always looked. On the other side they keep stopping, in the middle of things, with their heads up."

**Show them one thing the first ringing changed,** from your notes:
- **Thrane rang:** it's raining, properly, for the first time in a hundred years. Children have been let out in it. Somebody's mending a lightning rod and swearing happily.
- **Mirel rang:** people have slept. They're sitting on walls in the sun telling each other what they dreamed. Somebody asks the party, shyly, if they'd like to hear one.
- **Neither rang:** it's quiet, and there's less of everything than there should be.

**If they…**
- **Hurry:** they arrive a day ahead of the Court's news. Give them Advantage on the first Influence check tonight.
- **Stop and help somebody:** they arrive at dusk, with one more friend. Any name from the list.
- **Look behind:** Wisdom (Perception) DC 14. Two grey riders on the skyline, not closing. **They've been seen.** That's the start of Session 21, not tonight.
- **Want a fight:** there isn't one here. Say so kindly and move on.

**Bring it back.** Somebody on the road recognises the Ringer, and gives them an apple, and won't take money.

**How it ends.** The road goes up. Read the arrival, below.

### Scene 2: The other gate

**Where and why.** The place itself. One arrival, and the first person they meet.

#### If tonight's Brassfall

> **SAY:** "The mountains are veined with bronze, and the sky flickers without clouds. At the mouth of the Old Works, a blue lamp is waiting."

**What's really going on.** [They've come to Brassfall second.](play:s20-brassfall-second) Garrow's been holding that lamp up since he died. He only wants one thing, and it's on the way.

- **Old Garrow.** Gruff, impatient, funny. He calls everyone lads and lasses. *Lines:* "Lads and lasses! You took your time. Did you come the long way round, by the sea?" · "It's not heavy. It's only a lamp. It only wants carrying to somebody." · "Tell her I'm sorry about the collapse. Tell her I'm proud. In that order, and don't drop it."
- **[Run the lamp and Yenna in one scene.](play:s20-lamp-delivered-quick)** He asks, they say yes, and it's dusk at the red horse-skull:

> **SAY:** "Garrow's lamp is waiting at the mouth of the works, and over the next hill a red horse-skull."

- Let the player who carried it say the words. Yenna hangs it up inside, comes out, and offers one thing: a horse, a bow, or a word to her clan.
- **[Refuse him:](play:s16a-refuse-lamp)** he nods. He's been refused before. Yenna's still here, and she's hurt, not angry.

#### If tonight's Vael Tor

> **SAY:** "The hill rises alone above the plain. From the summit, a sound like someone breathing in their sleep drifts down toward you."

**What's really going on.** [They've come to the Tor second.](play:s20-vael-tor-second) The Hall's doors are never locked. Who'd leave?

- **Brother Lull,** if you like a guide: round, whispering, always folding something. *Lines:* "Oh, *shoes*, please. Thank you." · "You can talk. They like it. Just don't sing."
- **Let them walk the rows.** Ask each player for one sleeper they notice. One of them's somebody the party's heard of. [They can try to wake one:](play:s16b-wake-a-sleeper) it's a minute of somebody looking up at them, and then it's over.
- **If Mirel's already rung,** they've all turned over, and some of them are smiling.

**Bring it back.** Brassfall: the lamp leans toward whoever just told a lie. The Tor: everyone in one row breathes out together.

**How it ends.** Brassfall: "He'll see you now. He's decided to like you." The Tor: somebody's standing by the empty bed, with a book.

### Scene 3: One bargain

**Where and why.** This is the session. Give it an hour, and make the price real.

#### If tonight's Brassfall: the thane

**Kessa Ironhorn.** Laughs with his whole chest; tucks his gloved hands in his belt. Skip the contest unless they ask for it. He's heard about them.

> **SAY (Kessa, in private):** "I'm dying, rider. Ring it, and return it after."

**What's really going on.** The Heart's been eating his hands. He believes the Key can cure him, because Isolde sold him a memory that said so. It can't. He can't ring Thrane himself, because the Shafts mark whoever rings, and he wouldn't live through the first stroke.

**If they…**
- **[Take the loan:](play:s20-accept-kessa-quick)** say the oath aloud. It comes back to the Heart-Hall. Ask each player whether they're swearing it. Write it in the Bargain log.
- **[Take it by night:](play:s20-take-thrane-quick)** one plan, one night. If Yenna's a friend she does the carrying, and all they need is a distraction. Otherwise Stealth, DC 15 each.

> **SAY:** "Drums at midnight. A rider yawns, sees nothing, looks away."

  He'll know by morning. Tell them that before they go in.
- **[Duel him for it:](play:s17a-duel-kessa)** "Finally." He fights fair and stops at Bloodied.
- **Try to take it openly:** see the fights. He'll stop it for a fair wager or a yielded blade.
- **Tell him the Key won't cure him:** he goes quiet, and then he asks who else knows. He still wants it rung.
- **Offer him something else:** what have they got that he'd believe? A Gift from Isolde's vial, or a way to heal the mark, or a promise about Maudrin. Let a good offer work.

#### If tonight's Vael Tor: the book

> **SAY:** "A figure in archivist's grey stands by the central bed, holding a bone-bound book that has no words. 'A dream you have never told, and the Heart is yours.'"

**What's really going on.** [It's the same offer it always makes.](play:s20-courier-bargain-quick) It wants to be read, and to read. It doesn't hurry.

**If they…**
- **Trade a dream:** the player makes it up and says it, once. Then it's gone. Put it in the ledger as a Trade.
- **Trade a Gift instead:** it'll take one.
- **[Say no to all of it:](play:s16b-refuse-courier)** it closes the book, and stays. Mirel won't ring, and that's allowed.
- **[Take it:](play:s16b-take-from-courier)** it opens its hand. Say first that the Librarian will shut every door it has.
- **Ask it things:** one true memory, one true answer. It knows where Maudrin is. ("Packing a small bag. She has taken the Key out of its case to look at it, twice.")

**Bring it back.** Brassfall: he misses the cup with his hand, and waits to see who'll notice. The Tor: the book turns a page, and the page has tonight on it.

**How it ends.** They've got it, or they haven't, and somebody's a little poorer. **Say the cost out loud:** "So that's what it cost."

### Scene 4: The night before

**Where and why.** A fire. This is either Corin's scene, or a quiet one. Don't run both.

#### If Corin's unmet

He comes into the firelight with his hands where they can see them.

> **SAY (Corin):** "Ah, you have been to the mountains. Good."

*(At the Tor, "to the hill".)* Thin, in a scorched apron, with his head on one side and a tuning hammer through his belt. He hums until he's upset.

**What's really going on.** He's been a day behind them for a week. He's got Edda Thorne's Notes, which his family has kept for three generations, and they describe a way to finish the song: six bells rung, the Key *seated* in the Seventh and never struck. It asks the Ringer for "the whole name". He thinks that means theirs. He'll say so without being asked.

- **[Say yes:](play:s20-corin-accept-here)** he hands over the Notes, all of them, and doesn't know what to do with his arms.
- **[Say no:](play:s20-corin-refuse-here)** he's disappointed, not angry. In the morning there's a bronze hound sitting a hundred feet off. It rings a little when it scratches.
- **[Argue with him:](play:s18a-argue-with-corin)** he'd love that. He's had nobody to argue with.
- **Say "ask us again":** that's fair. Leave the fact as unmet. He'll come to the Tor.

#### If he isn't

- **Brassfall:** the clan's dancing, and somebody has to dance. Or Yenna comes and sits by the fire and doesn't say anything for a while, and then tells one story about her father.
- **The Tor, if Mirel's unrung:** they've got to decide where to sleep. [On the hill,](play:s16b-rest-on-tor) with the saves; or in [the Cult's circle,](play:s17b-accept-rest) at the Cult's price; or down on the road, cold and safe. If something walks, see the fights.
- **The Tor, if she's rung:** everyone dreams. Go round: one image each.

**Bring it back.** One ember in the fire is exactly the colour of the Heart. It takes a long time to go out.

**How it ends.** Whoever's on last watch hears the bell hum. Once. It's heard them.

### Scene 5: The bell you haven't met

**Where and why.** Morning. Five minutes, walking toward it. **Don't ring it tonight.**

> **SAY:** "You don't have to look for the way. The Heart's pulling, like a child that's seen somebody it knows. And then you're over the last rise, and there it is, hanging in its own quiet, and it's leaning toward you. It's been waiting longer than there've been maps."

**If they…**
- **Rush at it:** Brassfall's bell is down the Lightning Shafts; the Tor's is over the empty bed. Either way, stop at the threshold. "You can ring it. You'll have to say who." That's next week.
- **Settle who:** let them start that talk, and leave it unfinished if they can't agree.
- **Look back:** Wisdom (Perception) DC 13. Dust. A dozen grey coats, and they've stopped being careful.
- **Have no Heart:** they stand in front of a bell they can't ring. "It's all right," it seems to say. "I'm used to it." They can still get it. Ask them how.

**Bring it back.** The apple from Scene 1. Is there any left?

**How it ends.** Ask: **"What did the second Heart cost you?"** Go round. If nobody paid anything, ask what it cost somebody else.

### Running the fights (Session 20)

You may not need either. They're here if somebody reaches for a weapon.

#### Kessa's guard at the Heart-Hall

*Two Ironhorn Champions (CR 5), five Ironhorn Riders (CR 3), five Warhorses. Only if the party tries to take the Heart by force.*

- **Setup:** a big tent with four ways out, forty feet across. The Riders are outside, mounted. The Champions are on the threshold, side by side.
- **What happens:** each Champion picks one person, out loud, and fights only that person. Riders go round and block the ways out, and catch whoever runs. Nobody attacks a person who's put their weapon down.
- **What they fight for:** the Heart. They don't chase anyone who hasn't got it.
- **Who to worry about:** whoever's outside when the horses arrive. A charge is the biggest hit here.
- **When it ends:** Kessa walks out and shouts. He'll stop it for a fair wager, or a blade laid down, any time after the first round.
- **Scale on the fly:** drop one Champion for a lighter fight. Keep the second for round two for a harder one.
- **Non-lethal:** all of it. They're guests who've been rude.

#### The Sleepless of the Tor

*Four Sleepless (CR 5; AC 13, 67 HP). Only if Mirel's unrung and somebody's save went badly.*

- **Setup:** night, on the hill, between the stones. They come up through the ground mist, one at a time, wearing the sleeper's fear.
- **What happens:** they go for whoever made them, one at a time. They talk while they do it. Let the player answer back.
- **Who to worry about:** that player. Ask before you start: "All right with this?" If not, use a faceless child.
- **When it ends:** at dawn; if Mirel rings; or the moment they're inside the Cult's circle. Say all three aloud in round one, as a thing Lull shouts from the Hall.
- **Scale on the fly:** three for a lighter fight, five for a harder one.
- **Non-lethal:** they can be walked away from. They stop at the stones, and at the light.

### Pacing (Session 20)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:10 | Recap; what they're doing differently |
| 0:10 to 0:25 | Scene 1: across the plain |
| 0:25 to 1:00 | Scene 2: the other gate |
| 1:00 to 2:00 | Scene 3: one bargain |
| 2:00 to 2:40 | Scene 4: Corin, or the fire, or the night |
| 2:40 to 2:55 | Scene 5: the bell |
| 2:55 to 3:05 | The question |

- **Where to break:** after they've agreed the price, before they've paid it.
- **Running long:** cut Scene 1 to its read-aloud, and give Garrow's lamp one line each way.
- **Running short:** run the [steppe contest](play:s17a-contest) at Brassfall, or the watch on the Tor.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop with the Heart in somebody's hands. Corin can come in the morning.

### If you get stuck (Session 20)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **The person they're bargaining with gets tired,** and says the true thing instead.
2. **The Heart hums the note of a bell they've already rung.** Everyone in earshot looks up.
3. **A grey rider turns up alone,** lost, thirsty, and very young, and asks the way.

**If they remember every beat from the other road and want to skip to the end:** let them. One sentence of summary, and straight to the bargain.

**If nobody will pay:** that's an answer. The bell isn't rung, and the finale's harder. Say so, plainly, and let them keep it.

**Names for riders, sleepers and travellers** (cross one off when you use it): Brill, Perrin, Gatt, Corwen, Tansy, Marl, old Anse.

### End of session 20

**The closing question:** "What did the second Heart cost you?" Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** the arrival, the lamp or the Hall, the bargain, Corin.
- **World-state facts to check:** Thrane's or Mirel's Heart, the lamp, the oath to Kessa, Corin, the Notes, the Ironhorn, Bellwright and Court Clocks.
- **The Bargain log:** the oath, in its exact words; or the dream, as a Trade.
- **Who's been seen,** and by whom.

**Rewards:**
- **The second Heart,** or a reason.
- **A friend on this side of the plain:** Yenna, or Lull, or page two hundred and six.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to whoever paid.

## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. It's the last bell on this side of the sea, and the first time the Court comes with everything it has on the road. The ringing's the middle of the night, not the end. After it, somebody brings news: Maudrin Vesk has stopped waiting.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-21) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-21) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-21) · [Scene 1: The threshold](#scene-1-the-threshold) · [Scene 2: The second ringing](#scene-2-the-second-ringing) · [Scene 3: What it gave back](#scene-3-what-it-gave-back) · [Scene 4: A long grey line](#scene-4-a-long-grey-line) · [Scene 5: Maudrin is coming](#scene-5-maudrin-is-coming) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-21) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-21) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-21) · [End of session](#end-of-session-21)

### Before you start (Session 21)

**Level:** four characters at level 8.

**Check the world state first.** Six facts decide the night:
- **Act IV road:** **A** rings **Mirel** tonight, on Vael Tor. **B** rings **Thrane** tonight, in the Lightning Shafts.
- **The Heart:** have they got it? No Heart, no ringing. Go to the refusal in Scene 2, or run the bargain again.
- **How many bells are already rung?** None or one, **Heavy**; two or three, **Grievous**; four or five, **Ruinous.** Waypoint shows it on the play.
- **Kessa** (road B): living, or dead? And the **oath:** sworn, or not? (Road A: was it kept or broken in 19A? It matters in Session 22.)
- **The Cult** (road A): ceased, or feeding?
- **Corin:** an ally? He's here, and he can put a Toll off an hour.

**What this session is about.** They've come to the end of what they can do without her. Every bell they ring from here, Maudrin Vesk hears.

**Your goals tonight:**
- Give the warning at its new weight. It's worse than last time. Say so.
- Let the bell be wonderful, and then give them half an hour of it.
- Hold or lose the road against a real Court patrol.
- End on the question: **"Maudrin is coming. Where will you meet her?"** Then stop.

**Prepare:**
- **Tokens or minis:** the four characters; four Wardens; two Sergeants; two Knights; eight Hushmen.
- **Maps:** the bell's place (the ledge, or the bed); a road with a ridge above it.
- **Road B:** a bowl of rice to pour for rain. **Road A:** a lullaby.
- **The Toll Deck,** and each player's off-limits list in front of you.
- **The Forecast page,** open. If they refuse tonight, you'll show it to them.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **The Sense Toll (Thrane takes one):** *Heavy*, one sense dulled for a year, with Disadvantage on every check that relies on it. *Grievous*, dulled for good. *Ruinous*, gone for a year (sight means Blinded, hearing Deafened), then dulled for good. Sight and hearing only if that player agreed at session zero.
- **The Fear Toll (Mirel gives one):** in sight of it, a Wisdom save, DC 13, at the start of each turn, or Frightened until that turn ends. *Heavy*, a year. *Grievous*, for good. *Ruinous*, for good, and it's something they can't avoid.
- **Lightning-Marked** (Thrane): once before the next dawn, when the Ringer takes Lightning damage, they can use their Reaction to deal 1d6 Lightning to someone within 10 feet.
- **Blinded:** can't see; Disadvantage on attacks, Advantage against them. **Deafened:** can't hear; fails any check that needs hearing. **Frightened:** Disadvantage while they can see it, and can't choose to move closer.
- **Warden's Stone:** no spells within 10 feet while it's out. AC 12, 10 HP, or Sleight of Hand, DC 15.
- **Nothing undoes a Toll.** Not Greater Restoration, not Wish. If somebody asks, say so before they ring, not after.

**Places at a glance:**
- **The Lightning Shafts (road B):** a hole in a mountain, a ledge halfway down, a bell with blue sparks crawling on it.
- **The Sleeping Hall (road A):** hundreds of beds, one empty, and a honey-coloured bell over it.
- **The road out:** one track along a valley. A ridge on the north side. Nowhere to turn a cart.

**Rumours (d6)** in the last camp:
1. "They've stopped the mail to Hallowmere. Both ways." (True.)
2. "She's leaving the city. She's never left the city." (True. It's happening today.)
3. "There's a patrol on the valley road with *knights* in it." (True.)
4. "The Key's made of glass." (False.)
5. "The last Ringer who did two in a season went deaf and laughed about it." (True, and the laugh wasn't a good one.)
6. "If you don't ring it they'll leave you alone." (False. She's been frightened already.)

### Opening recap (Session 21)

> **SAY:** "You crossed the plain. You bargained for a Heart, and it cost you *(the oath / a dream / a Gift / a night's work you're not proud of)*. And then you came over the last rise and stood in front of *(Thrane / Mirel)*, and the bell leaned toward you. The dust on the road behind you is closer than it was. You've been saying, all the way here, that you'd decide who in the morning. It's morning."

- **Then hand it over:** "What's the last thing your character did before they went in?" One line each.

### Scene 1: The threshold

**Where and why.** The way in. Short. Settle who, and say what it costs now.

> **SAY (Thrane):** "The ladder goes down into blue light. Every nail in it is humming. Halfway down there's a ledge, and on the ledge a bell as tall as a horse, with sparks crawling over it like ants."

> **SAY (Mirel):** "Hundreds of people are asleep. The bed in the middle's made up, with one corner turned down. The bell over it is the colour of old honey, and it's so quiet in here you can hear it being patient."

**What's really going on.** It's the same as last time, and it's worse. Every bell that's rung makes the next one heavier. The bells aren't cruel; there's simply less of the world left for them to lean on.

**If they…**
- **Can't agree who:** ask each player, "If nobody else would, would you?" Then ask whoever said yes fastest to wait, and whoever said it slowest to speak.
- **Want Corin's help:** an hour's delay, never less. He says so. "It's a kindness, that's all. It isn't a discount."
- **Haven't got the Heart:** they stand there. It can still be got. Offer them one more try at the [quick loan](play:s20-accept-kessa-quick) or the [quick trade](play:s20-courier-bargain-quick), with the Court an hour nearer.
- **Want to know what's on the road:** an hour away. Enough to ring. Not enough to rest.
- **Ask what Maudrin knows:** she felt the last one. She'll feel this.

**Bring it back.** The bell's a little closer than it was when they came in. It hasn't moved.

**How it ends.** Someone has their hand on the Heart.

### Scene 2: The second ringing

**Where and why.** The bell. Straight, slow, and with the music off.

**Say the warning out loud, to the whole table:**

> **SAY (Thrane):** "Ringing Thrane will take a sense from you, and it will be *(heavy / grievous / ruinous)*. You won't know exactly what until it's paid, and it can never be undone or bought back. Do you ring?"

> **SAY (Mirel):** "Ringing Mirel will give you a fear, and it will be *(heavy / grievous / ruinous)*. You won't know exactly what until it's paid, and it can never be undone or bought back. Do you ring?"

**Then, out of character,** read them the one line for that weight from the rules above. Yes or no, nothing in between. Anyone can ring for anyone. Anyone can say no and not say why.

**If they…**
- **[Ring Thrane:](play:s21-ring-thrane-second)** ask the Ringer to hit the table with a flat hand. Pour the rice.

> **SAY:** "The bell cracks like a whip. For the first time in four centuries a real storm rolls over the mountains."

  Then be quiet, and give the Toll. Choose a sense that character's enjoyed *at this table*. Start with the small true thing: "You can smell rain. Everyone's always told you about it. It smells of nothing."
- **[Ring Thrane with Kessa dead:](play:s21-ring-thrane-second-kessa-dead)** the same storm. Nobody cheers. Yenna stands in it with her hands open.

> **SAY:** "The bell cracks like a whip, and a real storm rolls over the mountains."

- **[Ring Mirel:](play:s21-ring-mirel-second)** almost whisper it:

> **SAY:** "The bell sings like a lullaby sung by someone who loves you, and the Sleepless dissolve into mist."

  Then go round: "What does your character hope for, right now?" **Then** the Toll. Something small and particular, and a bit odd, that'll turn up again.
- **[Refuse, all of them:](play:s21-refuse-second)** it's a real ending to the scene. Read this and leave a gap after it.

> **SAY:** "The second bell waits, silent, as you turn away from it."

  Open the Forecast and show them what it closes: the Concord needs all six. The Second Dawn stays open. They can come back for this bell in Session 22, and it'll cost them days. Maudrin still moves.
- **Drop before it's struck:** the ringing's cancelled, and nothing's owed. After the strike, it's owed.

**Record it at once:** the kind, the bell, the weight, and the player's own one line.

**Bring it back.** The Ringer's first bell answers, very far off. They're the only one who hears it.

**How it ends.** They come up, or out, into whatever they've made.

### Scene 3: What it gave back

**Where and why.** Outside. The reward. Twenty minutes, and nobody's allowed to interrupt it.

> **SAY (Thrane rang):** "It's raining on people who've only read about it. A whole camp's standing in it with their mouths open. An old man's got his boots off and he's stamping in a puddle, scowling, as if it might get away."

> **SAY (Mirel rang):** "They've all turned over. Somebody's snoring, and somebody's laughing in their sleep, and a little old woman in the third row says, very clearly, 'Oh, *there* you are.'"

> **SAY (neither):** "Nothing happens. It's an ordinary afternoon. You can hear a lark. You'd forgotten there were ordinary afternoons."

**Pick one or two:**
- **Road B, Kessa living:** he picks up a cup, with two fingers, easily. It's a season's ease and not a cure, and he knows it. "I'll wait at the Hall, rider. Don't be long." Then settle the oath, here or on the way:
  - **[Give the Heart back:](play:s21-return-heart)** the oath's **Kept.** They'll ride at the Strike.

> **SAY:** "Kessa hangs the Heart back on its skull. 'You kept your word.'"

  - **[Keep it:](play:s21-keep-heart)** the oath's **Broken.** He doesn't chase them.

> **SAY:** "Kessa watches you ride out with his Heart and says nothing."

  - **Never swore:** it's a thing between honest people. Ask what's fair.
- **Road B, Kessa dead:** Yenna asks for it. Nobody's oath binds them. "I'd like one thing of his to be where he left it."
- **Road A:** Lumen's on her knees. [The whole Cult's stopped humming.](play:s19b-cult-after-mirel) If they weren't convinced, they are now. Brother Lull's going along the rows with a list of names, and where they came from.
- **Road A, and they swore to Kessa months ago:** somebody rides in from the Ironhorn with one bronze bead. It's the same news: "He says, is it kept?" They know whether it is.

**Go round:** "What does your character do with twenty minutes of this?" The Ringer last.

**Bring it back.** The Toll, gently. The thing they can't smell; the thing in the corner of the room.

**How it ends.** Birds go up, all at once, along the ridge.

### Scene 4: A long grey line

**Where and why.** The valley road. The big fight of Act IV, if they want it.

> **SAY:** "Grey riders appear on the ridge, a long line, gloves like mirrors."

**What's really going on.** [It's the biggest patrol they've seen.](play:s21-court-patrol-arrives) It was sent to hold the road, and it was sent two days before Maudrin decided to come herself. They want the Ringer and the Heart. They'd rather not kill anybody. Commander Rushe has been told not to come back without one of the two.

**Commander Rushe.** Fifty, spare, exact; a scar through one eyebrow. Reads from a paper and hates it. *Lines:* "By order of the Court of Hush: the bell, the Ringer, or the Heart. I'm to ask for all three. I'd settle for the one." · "I've a list of your names. They've spelt yours wrong." · "I'd take a surrender. I'd take it at any point. Please remember that I said so."

**If they…**
- **Talk:** Influence, Persuasion DC 17, once. A success doesn't send Rushe home. It buys the thing they asked for: ten minutes, or the wounded left alone, or the Hall untouched.
- **Give up the Heart:** they'll go. Write it down. [It can be won back at the Strike:](play:s23-recover-thrane) tell them so. (Mirel's is [the same](play:s23-recover-mirel).)
- **Give up the Ringer:** it's a jail, not a grave, and there's a rescue.
- **Use a friend:** the Ironhorn (oath kept, or Yenna alone), or the Cult's circle, or the Bellwrights with Corin, can break the line. **An ally takes an objective, never a kill:** Yenna's riders drive off the Knights' horses; the Cult links hands across the road; Corin's hounds open every lead case in the rear rank.
- **Run:** there's one track. Horses are faster. They lose the tail of the party unless somebody holds the narrow place. Who?
- **Hide:** group Stealth, DC 14, in a valley in broad daylight. With rain, or with mist, Advantage.
- **Fight:** see below. Surrender's offered before, and once in each round.

**Bring it back.** Rushe, between sentences, wipes rain off the list with a thumb. (If it's not raining, dust.)

**How it ends.** Three Wardens down, or a Heart handed over, or the party gone. Rushe looks at the paper, and folds it up very small.

### Scene 5: Maudrin is coming

**Where and why.** The far end of the valley, at dusk. The whole of Act IV's been leading here.

> **SAY:** "There's a rider on the road, coming the other way, on a horse that's nearly finished. They don't slow down for you. They just fall off it, more or less, at your feet, and start talking."

**Sela Pask.** Young, filthy, hoarse. Talks in bits, with her hands on her knees. *Lines:* "Hallowmere. I've come from… give me a minute. She's packing." · "She's leaving the city. Vesk. *Herself.* Within the day." · "I've watched that gate four years. She's never once come out of it."

**What's really going on.** The ringing frightened her. She hasn't been frightened since she was a child, and she doesn't know what to do with it except work. She's going to Vael Tor, with the Key, to seal the stairs before anyone can reach the Seventh. **She leaves within a day,** unless something they did earlier changed that.

**What Sela knows, if they ask:**
- **How many?** A column. Carts. She counted forty before someone looked up.
- **Who's with her?** The Dawn Order, if Rook lost the duel. Only the grey, if Rook won.
- **Why now?** "Because of *you*. Everyone in the city heard it. The windows hummed."
- **Where?** "The south road. It only goes to one place."
- **What was she carrying?** "One small trunk. And a case, about this long, and she wouldn't let anybody else touch it."
- **If Maudrin's dead already:** it's Tristan packing, with a ledger under one arm. The rest's the same.

**If they…**
- **Want to go for her now:** Session 22 starts at dusk. This is dusk.
- **Want to rest:** they can have a Long Rest. She's four days from the Tor.
- **Ask for help:** who've they been kind to? Start the list. It's next week's session.
- **Give Sela a horse:** she's theirs for life. Where does she ride?
- **Despair:** Sela looks at them, puzzled. "She's never come *out* before. You did that."

**Bring it back.** Somewhere, a long way south, the bell they've just rung is still going. Very faintly. Nobody's touched it.

**How it ends.** Ask: **"Maudrin is coming. Where will you meet her?"** Let them talk. Write down every place they name.

### Running the fights (Session 21)

#### The Court patrol

*Four Wardens (AC 16, 82 HP), two Sergeants (AC 15, 52 HP), two Dawn Order Knights (AC 18, 52 HP), eight Hushmen (AC 12, 32 HP). It's a big fight for level 8: talk first, run it outside, and use the friends they've made.*

- **Setup:** a valley road, 20 feet wide, with a ridge 30 feet up on one side and a stream on the other. The Wardens are on the road in a line. The Knights are mounted, behind them. (If Rook won the duel, they're the last two who followed Haldric. Leave them out if you'd rather.) The Hushmen are along the ridge.
- **What happens:** the Wardens hold the road and open their cases, staggered, so the light goes flat in patches. Round 2, the Knights charge through the middle. Round 3, the Hushmen come down off the ridge in two fours, at whoever's carrying the Heart.
- **A Warden's turn:** two blows (+5, 12 damage, and pushed 10 feet), or two crossbow shots (+4, 13).
- **A Sergeant's turn:** two light blows or shots (+4; about 5 each, and 3 Necrotic with the glove), or one and a signal: an ally attacks with a d4 extra.
- **A Knight's turn:** two swords (+5, 10 and 4 Radiant each). They won't strike anyone who's down. They won't strike a child, or a bell.
- **A Hushman's turn:** a glove (+5, 5 and 2 Necrotic; Advantage beside a friend), or an arrest (Strength DC 12 or Grappled; escape DC 12).
- **Who to worry about:** the Ringer. If they're Grappled and carried 60 feet, they've been taken. Say how far every round.
- **The easy wins:** break a stone (AC 12, 10 HP). Spook the horses. Block the road with a cart. Put the Heart somewhere nobody expects.
- **When it ends:** three Wardens down; or they've got a Heart, and they go; or the party's away.
- **Scale on the fly:** take out a Warden and both Knights for a lighter fight. Keep four Hushmen on the ridge until round four if it's going badly.
- **Non-lethal:** all of it. They arrest. Anyone who drops wakes up tied, and not far away.

### Pacing (Session 21)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:10 | Recap; the last thing before they went in |
| 0:10 to 0:25 | Scene 1: the threshold |
| 0:25 to 0:55 | Scene 2: the second ringing |
| 0:55 to 1:20 | Scene 3: what it gave back, and the oath |
| 1:20 to 2:35 | Scene 4: a long grey line |
| 2:35 to 3:00 | Scene 5: Maudrin is coming |
| 3:00 to 3:10 | The question |

- **Where to break:** when the birds go up along the ridge.
- **Running long:** let a friend break the line. One good description, and Rushe folds the paper up.
- **Running short:** spend longer in Scene 3, and let them answer the bronze bead.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop on the ridge, with the grey line on it. Open next time with Rushe reading.

### If you get stuck (Session 21)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **The bell rings once more by itself,** and everyone, on both sides, stops and looks up.
2. **One of the grey riders takes their gloves off,** and puts them down on the road.
3. **Sela arrives early,** through the middle of everything, shouting the news to both sides.

**If the Toll lands badly:** stop, change it, out loud. "It wasn't that. It was this."

**If they refuse and then regret it:** they can come back, in [Session 22](play:s22-detour-for-a-missed-bell). It'll cost days, and the Court will use them.

**Names for riders, scouts and grey coats** (cross one off when you use it): Hushman Selwyn, Hushman Gale, Corporal Dunne, old Bryn the drover, Veda, Corm.

### End of session 21

**The closing question:** "Maudrin is coming. Where will you meet her?" Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** the ringing (or the refusal), the oath, the patrol.
- **World-state facts to check:** Thrane or Mirel (rung), its Heart, the oath to Kessa (kept or broken), the Stormwall, the Cult, the Court, Ironhorn and Landing Clocks.
- **Toll log:** the kind, the bell, the weight.
- **Where they said they'd meet her.** You'll want it.

**Rewards:**
- **A bell, rung.** Read out how many they've got.
- **Level 9.** Session 22's fights are written for it.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to the Ringer, and to whoever offered first.

plays.title: They read Edda Thorne's account of the Quiet Night
plays.why: The diary, the Notes or the Librarian finally tell what the Key is.
plays.readAloud: "He wants to tune the seven into one long spring. I told him the seventh is not a bell. It is the lullaby. The Key is not a tuning tool. It is the heart that sings Oum to sleep, and he has taken it to make the calendar behave. If he strikes the Seventh with it, the dream will wake or it will crack. I told him so. He did not hear me."
plays.response: Piece it together with them: the Seventh keeps Oum asleep; the Key is its only Heart; Imber struck the Key against the bells and the discord cracked the lullaby; Maudrin has known since she took the Key. The sources: Corin's Notes (with the Quiet Night leaf), the diary, or the Librarian, who reads the page aloud for one true memory (not if the party robbed the courier). One line in the Notes says Thrane's weather "will go to the rim and wait": a sharp player may connect it to the Stormwall.
plays.consequence: The party knows what every ending costs and why.
plays.fallback: If they miss every source, the Librarian's courier finds them with the page, unless they robbed it; then Corin or Wren brings a copy.
plays.tells: Players open the diary or the Notes, or ask the Librarian.
plays.rules: Study action, Intelligence (History or Arcana) DC 13 to connect the line about Thrane's weather to the Stormwall; no roll needed for the main truth.
plays.later: S22: Telling Isolde (s22-tell-isolde) and Haldric (s24-haldric-truth) the truth can turn them. S24 to S27: the four endings are now informed choices.
plays.keywords: diary, notes, edda, truth, key, quiet night, read, librarian, lullaby, oum

plays.title: Word comes that Maudrin has marched
plays.why: She leaves Hallowmere within a day of the second ringing.
plays.readAloud: The scout is out of breath and still won't sit down. "She's left the city. Hushmen, Dawn Order knights, wagons. She's wearing it on a chain around her neck. A grey case."
plays.response: Maudrin carries the Key in a silence-stone case on a chain and marches on Vael Tor with Hushmen and Dawn Order knights (only Haldric's knights if Rook won the duel; Rook's knights stay with Rook). The palace vault is empty: the Key goes with her. The Strike is a day or two away because the Hush frays faster with every bell: she must bring the Key near the Seventh to hold it steady (s22-why-maudrin-marches).
plays.consequence: The race to the Tor begins; the Key is on her chain.
plays.tells: The second Act IV bell has rung.
plays.later: S23: the Strike at the foot of the Tor. The palace vault is empty; going back to Hallowmere for the Key finds only Ansel and the Tithe-Ledger.
plays.keywords: maudrin, march, army, leaves hallowmere, scout, news, key on a chain

plays.title: The Key leaves the palace vault
plays.why: Only when Maudrin was marked as marching but the Key was never recorded as leaving.
plays.readAloud: The palace vault stands open and empty. Ansel Quay is dusting the shelf where the case used to sit.
plays.response: Update the world state: the Key is on Maudrin's chain from now on. The palace route is closed; the chain route opens.
plays.consequence: The Key travels with Maudrin.
plays.tells: Maudrin has marched and the Key still shows the palace.
plays.later: S23: the chain route (any-steal-key-chain) and the summit (S24).

plays.title: They call in their allies
plays.why: Everything the party did in Acts I–IV pays off here.
plays.readAloud: Word goes out along every road you have travelled, and some of the people you helped start walking toward the Tor.
plays.response: Ask each player which ally they want to bring and which they trust, then run one ally play per company that agrees: each is +1 on the allies clock and takes an objective (hold the ridge, cut the retreat, break the line), not a creature count. The clock stops at 6. Ally logistics: Hallowmere to the Tor is about four days; Pellmoor is six; the Choir cannot leave the Mere, so its hymn arrives by a Mere-glass vial (Mother Sallow's message); the Stilled walk slowly and arrive at dusk.
plays.consequence: The party knows exactly who stands with it.
plays.tells: Players list who owes them.
plays.rules: Ally actions: Rook's knights take one Hushman off the line; Yenna's riders cut the retreat; the Cantor's hymn gives Advantage on saves against Frightened; the Stilled stand as living walls; the Blanks break the line by numbers; the Stormborn's ship guns or Harper sabotage remove one Warden.
plays.later: S23 and S24: each ally's objective changes the encounter; at 3 allies the party picks which flank to hold; at 6 the Court cannot hold the Tor road and Maudrin must come in person.

plays.title: They tell Kessa the Key can't cure him
plays.why: Kessa believes the Key will heal his lightning-sickness (H-21), and he deserves the truth.
plays.readAloud: Kessa laughs, and then stops laughing, and looks at his blackened hands for a long time. "Well. Then I'd better die somewhere with weather."
plays.response: He takes it hard and honestly. If Thrane has rung, he asks to die in the open air during a storm. He keeps his alliance if the party has kept its word. The decision is his and the table's; he is not predestined to die.
plays.consequence: Kessa fights for the party, or for a good death, not for a cure.
plays.tells: Kessa is alive and asks about the Key.
plays.later: S28: Kessa's last storm if the table wants it (s28-kessa-storm).

plays.title: Corin offers to pay the Great Toll himself
plays.why: Corin's whole family has tried to finish this song for three generations, and the Notes now name the price.
plays.readAloud: “If the price is a name, then let it be mine. My grandmother died one breath into this song. Let me finish it.”
plays.response: Corin, who misread the "whole name" for years, now understands the Great Toll and offers to be the Ringer himself. He is wrong to want it for the family's sake, not evil. Let the party argue; his offer does not remove their consent for anyone else. He can defer a Toll for an hour, never cancel it.
plays.consequence: A willing Ringer is on the table that is not a PC.
plays.tells: Corin is allied and reads the Notes with the party.
plays.later: S26: if the party refuses him, he may still try to reach the bell (s26-corin-cracks-the-lullaby). S27: the Concord with Corin as the Seventh's voice (s27-corin-voice).

plays.title: They ambush Maudrin's column on the road
plays.why: Proactive parties strike first, on ground they choose.
plays.readAloud: From the ridge you can see the column coming: grey horses, grey gloves, and one rider in dove-grey at the centre.
plays.response: Ansel knows the routes Maudrin's Hushmen take from the palace to the Tor (if he's dead, his route-book does). A good ambush gives the party Surprise and a chosen battlefield; the vanguard (not Maudrin) is hit first. Run the Strike's lead column there instead, then Maudrin arrives at the Tor.
plays.consequence: The Strike happens on the party's terms.
plays.fallback: If they'd rather hurt the column without meeting it, get ahead of it to the Quiet Quarry (s22-quiet-quarry).
plays.tells: Players ask Ansel Quay or a scout for her route.
plays.rules: Surprise (2024): surprised creatures have Disadvantage on their Initiative rolls. Group Stealth: DC 14 against the column's Passive Perception.
plays.later: S23 as normal, with terrain and surprise in the party's favour: Maudrin's remaining column is smaller, and she will not underestimate them again.
plays.keywords: ambush, road, column, attack first, ansel, route, surprise

plays.title: The Quiet Quarry: spoil the Wardens' stones
plays.why: Every silence-stone the Court carries is cut from one hill on the Tor road, and the column stops there for fresh ones. It's the session's big dungeon, and the Court's weak point.
plays.readAloud: Ansel's finger runs up the map and stops on a hill north of the ridge. "The quarry. The column always stops there. The Wardens' stones go dull on the road, you see, so they take on fresh ones. There's a goat-path. I used to count the carts."
plays.response: Run it from The Quiet Quarry, area by area in the wiki, in place of the ambush. Nine areas: the rim, the cutters' terraces and their foreman, the overseers' house and the quarry guard, the bucket-crane, the dead galleries where no spell works, the pump-room and its sluice, Old Patient and the fresh stones on the cutting floor, the hidden Mother Seam, and the spoil chute down to the road. The short way (1, 4, 7, 9) takes about 45 minutes; the long way about 1 hour 15 to 1 hour 30. Break in the pump-room. They arrive by noon; the column arrives at dusk.
plays.consequence: If they spoil or steal the fresh stones, the Wardens march to the Strike on dull ones: their Emanations reach only 5 feet. Up to three fights, and an Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location.
plays.fallback: If they'd rather fight on open ground, the ambush on the road is still there (s22-ambush).
plays.tells: They ask Ansel (or his route-book) where the column stops, or want to hurt the Court before the Strike without fighting the whole vanguard.
plays.rules: Ansel's goat-path: no roll (his route-book, if he's dead). The ambush or the quarry, not both: the column can't be hit in two places on one day. Raw silence-stone: no spells and no sound beyond 10 feet in the dead galleries. Soaked silence-stone goes dull for a month.
plays.later: S23: the Wardens' stones reach only 5 feet if the stock was spoiled or stolen.
plays.keywords: dungeon, side dungeon, crawl, cellar, basement, hideout, traps, trap, treasure, hidden, loot, quiet quarry, quarry, silence-stone, warden's stones, wardens, goat-path, ansel, column, sabotage, spoil, stones

plays.title: Dagny Thurl and the silent cutters
plays.why: The cutters are Blanks, sent where nothing they hear matters. Their foreman isn't, and she hates where her stone goes.
plays.readAloud: The foreman wipes her hands on her smock and looks you over. Then, slowly, she makes a sign, palm down and then a closed fist, and points at the grey giant sitting on the floor below.
plays.response: Dagny is Friendly if they're kind to her cutters, Influence DC 15 otherwise. She tells them the guard's shifts, the chalk marks in the dead galleries and the sluice in the pump-room, and, once Friendly, the Mother Seam. She teaches them the sign for "rest", which Old Patient obeys. If the Blanks are the party's allies, some cutters know their faces; they won't fight, but they'll raise dust to cover the bucket-crane (Advantage on the group Stealth check).
plays.consequence: A guide through the quarry, the golem's word, and the cutters' cover.
plays.fallback: If nobody talks to her, the sign can still be worked out by watching the cutters (Insight DC 15).
plays.tells: They take the cutters' stair down the terraces (area 2), or someone signs back.
plays.rules: Influence DC 15 (Indifferent). The sign: palm down, then a closed fist. Talk with the cutters is by sign: no check to be understood, and no lying either.
plays.later: S23: if they ask her, Dagny watches the Strike from the road, to see what her stone does.
plays.keywords: cutters, blanks, foreman, dagny, dagny thurl, sign, hand-sign, rest, quarry, quiet quarry, ally

plays.title: The Xorns in the dead galleries
plays.why: Two Xorns found a hill full of stone nobody else can work, and silver in every Hushman's purse.
plays.readAloud: In perfect silence the gallery wall bulges, and a squat, three-armed thing pushes its way out of the stone. Its wide mouth opens. Then it leans close to your belt pouch, and sniffs.
plays.response: They're hungry, not cruel. 25 gp in silver, or a gem, for each, and they sink back into the stone and leave the party alone; Friendly, they point out the deadfall. Draw steel on them, or refuse, and they take what they smell: The Xorns in the Combat tab. Nobody can cast a spell in the galleries, on either side.
plays.consequence: A toll paid, or a fight in the deaf dark.
plays.fallback: If the fight goes badly for them, the Xorns sink into the wall with whatever they grabbed.
plays.tells: They take the long way through the dead galleries (area 5).
plays.rules: Raw silence-stone: no spells, no sound beyond 10 feet. The deadfall: Perception DC 15 spots the chalk warning; DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, 4d10 Bludgeoning damage, half on a success.
plays.keywords: xorn, xorns, dead galleries, galleries, silence-stone, toll, silver, gems, deadfall, trap, quiet quarry

plays.title: Old Patient and the Wardens guard the fresh stones
plays.why: The first cutters carved a golem to haul their blocks. The Court kept it, and taught it to guard them.
plays.readAloud: The grey giant by the lead cases lifts its head, slowly, like an old man who has heard his name. Dust runs off its shoulders. The two Wardens beside it reach for their mauls.
plays.response: If a character makes the cutters' "rest" sign (palm down, then a closed fist), Old Patient sits back down and stays down. The Wardens fight anyway: Old Patient in the Combat tab, without the golem. Otherwise both: Old Patient walks at whoever is nearest the cases. Flooding the floor from the pump-room mid-fight soaks the stock, and any Warden knocked Prone in the water soaks his own stone.
plays.consequence: The stock is theirs to spoil or steal: twelve Warden's Stones. Flood them, soak them at the cutters' troughs (a minute each), smash them (AC 12, 10 HP each) or carry them off (20 pounds a case).
plays.tells: They reach the cutting floor (area 7), by the bucket-crane or the galleries.
plays.rules: Old Patient is a Stone Golem; the Wardens use the Hushman Warden, each with a Warden's Stone (a 10-foot Emanation where spells can't be cast). A Moderate encounter for four level 9 characters; much less if the golem sits down.
plays.later: S23: if the stock is spoiled or stolen, the Wardens' stones reach only 5 feet at the Strike.
plays.keywords: old patient, golem, stone golem, wardens, warden's stones, cutting floor, boss, quarry, quiet quarry, stones, sabotage

plays.title: They open the sluice and flood the cutting floor
plays.why: Silence-stone only drinks sound while it's dry, and the quarry's old drainage cistern sits right above the floor.
plays.readAloud: The wheel groans, then gives. Somewhere below, a sound like a held breath let go, and a grey wave runs out across the cutting floor between the blocks.
plays.response: The floor floods knee-deep in 2 rounds: Difficult Terrain for everyone, and every silence-stone in the water goes dull for a month. That spoils the fresh stock in its open cases, and any Warden knocked Prone in it soaks his own stone. The guard hears the water: if nobody has dealt with them, they come in 5 rounds.
plays.consequence: The Court's fresh stones are spoiled, and the cutters lose a week's work (Dagny doesn't mind).
plays.tells: They reach the pump-room (area 6), or Dagny tells them about the wheel.
plays.rules: Turning the wheel: a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check, or two people and ten minutes. Soaked silence-stone is just stone for a month.
plays.later: S23: the Wardens' stones reach only 5 feet.
plays.keywords: sluice, flood, water, pump-room, wheel, wet, dull, silence-stone, sabotage, quiet quarry

plays.title: Treasure: the Mother Seam
plays.why: The quarry-master who ran this hill before the Court came hid from them for a year, in the one place no spell could find him.
plays.readAloud: Behind the slab, a little chamber of black, glassy stone, so pure it hurts your ears. A stool, a candle stub, and a tin box with a dead man's initials scratched in the lid.
plays.response: An Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location, three garnets (100 gp each) and two Potions of Greater Healing.
plays.consequence: One character the Court can't scry, all the way to the Tor.
plays.tells: Dagny tells them, or they search the cutting floor's back wall (Investigation DC 16).
plays.rules: **Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location** (uncommon, requires attunement): while you wear it, you can't be targeted by Divination spells or perceived through magical scrying sensors unless you allow it. **Potion of Greater Healing** (uncommon): regain 4d4 + 4 Hit Points.
plays.later: Next treasure: the Court's trunks in Session 23. See Treasure in the wiki.
plays.keywords: dungeon, side dungeon, crawl, cellar, basement, hideout, traps, trap, treasure, hidden, loot, amulet, amulet of proof against detection and location, garnets, gems, potion of greater healing, mother seam, reward, quiet quarry

plays.title: Why Maudrin leaves Hallowmere now
plays.why: Players ask why she waited thirty-eight years and goes now.
plays.readAloud: “She has had it thirty-eight years,” Ansel says, quietly. “She never took it out of the vault. Why would she take it out now?”
plays.response: The truth, for the DM: the Court's silence-stones and gloves are tuned to the Key's hum, and a sealed Key would go quiet and end them. She kept it close to the Seventh's tune and far from any recess. Each bell rung shifts the world's key, so the Key's hum from the palace no longer holds the lullaby; she must carry it to the Tor to keep it steady. She wants the unrung Hearts (rung Hearts are worthless to her), the Key, and the Ringer, to Tithe, so no one can pay the Great Toll or strike. She will seal the stairs, not the Key.
plays.consequence: The table has a reason for her march.
plays.tells: A player asks Isolde, Ansel, a prisoner, or casts Detect Thoughts.
plays.rules: Insight DC 15 (Isolde or Ansel); Detect Thoughts on Maudrin: "keep it as it is."
plays.later: S24: she negotiates a seal. S26: her last offer.
plays.keywords: maudrin, why, motive, key, silence stones, march

plays.consequence: The Court marches.
plays.tells: The party took the Key from the palace vault.
