### If you get stuck (Session 24)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **Maudrin asks for the time.** She hasn't heard a bell in so long that she's forgotten how to guess.
2. **A Hushman takes a glove off,** in the line, where everyone can see.
3. **The lullaby misses a note.** Everybody on the hill feels their stomach drop.

**If the talk goes round in circles:** "I'll ask you once more," says Maudrin, "and then I'm going to go downstairs."

**If they take the Final Offer and one player doesn't want to:** it isn't taken. It needs all of them. Say so kindly.

**Names for Hushmen and knights** (cross one off when you use it): Alder, Dorrit, Ser Roland, Lyle, Zeb, Gilly, Sergeant Vint.

**The closing question:** "Who goes down the stairs?" Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

- **Plays that happened:** the talk, the offer, Haldric, the fight, and how it ended.
- **World-state facts to check:** Maudrin (and her Hit Points), the Key, Haldric, Corin, the Notes, the resistance, Tristan.
- **Who's going down, and who isn't.**
- **Level 11** for everyone.

**Rewards:**

## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. It's a hundred steps and not much else, and it's the one people talk about afterwards. Go slowly. The memories they give up are the best writing anyone will do all campaign, and it won't be you that does it.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-25) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-25) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-25) · [Scene 1: The top step](#scene-1-the-top-step) · [Scene 2: Twenty](#scene-2-twenty) · [Scene 3: Forty-one](#scene-3-forty-one) · [Scene 4: The landing](#scene-4-the-landing) · [Scene 5: The last step](#scene-5-the-last-step) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-25) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-25) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-25) · [End of session](#end-of-session-25)

### Before you start (Session 25)

**Level:** four characters at level 11.

**Check the world state first.**
- **Where's Maudrin?** Gone down with the Key: her sealers are on the landing. Coming as a witness: she's beside them. Captured, dead or exiled: nobody's sealed anything.
- **The Key.** If the party's got it, they can show it on the landing and the sealers stand aside.
- **Mirel.** Unrung: Sleepless on the stairs. Rung: it's quiet, and the Hush sings.
- **The Memory ledger.** Has anyone walked part of this stair before (Session 18B)? **They pay only what's left.** If they made their save then, it stands.
- **The Hush Cult.** If it's ceased, somebody will hum for them.
- **Who said they'd go down,** last time. And **who isn't at the table.** An absent player's character never pays. They wait above.

**What this session is about.** What you'd give up, and what you'd keep. There's no right number.

**Your goals tonight:**
- Say the price again, all of it, at the first step.
- Ask for each memory out loud or on paper. The player picks. Nobody hurries them.
- Let friends say no. It's a good thing when they do.
- Get whoever's going to the bottom, whole or lighter.
- End on the question: **"What did the stairs take from you?"** Then stop.

**Prepare:**
- **A strip of paper numbered 1 to 100** down the middle of the table. Move a token along it.
- **Index cards and one pen each.** A card for every memory. They keep it, or they give it to you face down. Ask which.
- **The Memory ledger,** open.
- **The casting-pit.** Know where it is. Somebody will want it.
- **Tokens or minis,** only if you need them: six Wardens, four Sergeants, three Knights and twelve Hushmen; or seven Sleepless.
- **The lullaby.** Hum it at steps 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100. Each time, get one note further.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **[The price of the stairs:](play:any-stairs-price)** the first nineteen steps are free. After that, **one memory for every full twenty.** The first time somebody reaches step 20, they make **one Wisdom save, DC 13.** On a failure their total for the whole campaign stops at **five;** on a success, at **two.** It happens once in a lifetime. Coming back up is free.
- **What a memory is:** something that happened to the character. Never a class feature, a spell, a skill, or anything the player knows. Nobody loses control of their character.
- **It isn't a Toll.** No ending gives it back.
- **The dead pay nothing,** and nor do children, because children don't go.
- **Climbing:** Strength (Athletics). Falling's 1d6 Bludgeoning for every 10 feet, and you land Prone.
- **Teleport and Dimension Door** work only if they've seen the chamber (Scrying, a dream, or standing in it). Otherwise they can't picture it, and nothing happens.

> **SAY:** "You went up the Tor in three bends, and by the third you were walking in step. Maudrin Vesk asked you what you'd have done. *(What you said. - **Then hand it over:** "What's a memory your character would never give up? Don't tell me why." Write it on a card. **Nobody's going to ask for that one.** Say so.

### Scene 1: The top step

**Where and why.** Daylight, just. Who's coming, who isn't, and what it costs.

> **SAY:** "The stairs are warm, as if someone had just stood on them."

**Read the price again, all of it:**

> **SAY:** "Nineteen steps, free. Then one memory for every twenty. At the twentieth there's one save, and only one, ever. If it goes against you, you'll lose five, all told. If it goes your way, two. You choose them. They don't come back, not with any ending. You can turn round on any step. Coming up costs nothing."

**What's really going on.** It isn't a punishment. The Seventh's what keeps the Dreamer asleep, and it's made of what people give it. The stairs are where it's fed.

**Then the friends.** [Let each one answer for themselves.](play:s25-allies-refuse) Go round, quickly.

> **SAY (Ilam):** "Ilam Bray looks down the stairs for a long moment, then at Jonah. 'I've only just got him back,' he says. 'I can't lose him again.'"

- **Ilam:** no.
- **Rook:** "We'll hold the top. That's an order I can give."
- **Corin:** yes. He won't say why he's shaking.
- **Kessa:** "I've a wife's laugh and a horse's name, and I'm keeping both. Shout, and I'll hear."
- **Yenna:** yes, if her father's lamp can stay with Sela.
- **The Stilled:** they can't bend their knees.
- **Sela:** "I could. If you want." Let a player answer her.

**If they…**
- **[Turn back:](play:s25-turn-back)** they can. No penalty.

> **SAY:** "The first step is warm, as if someone had just stood on it."

- **[Find the other way:](play:s25-foundry-chute)** Corin or the Notes know. So does anyone who's looked under the north stone.

> **SAY:** "At the top of the Tor, under the ring of stones, the old casting-pit drops straight down into the dark. Warm air rises out of it, smelling of bronze."

  Three climbs, Athletics DC 15. A slip's a fall, usually 20 feet: 2d6. **It never stops them.** It costs no memories and you mustn't add another price. Flying counts too. They can split up: some by the stairs, some by the pit. They all get there.
- **[Try to teleport:](play:s25-teleport-to-the-shrine)** if they've seen it.

> **SAY:** "One blink and the cold of the shrine is on your face."

- **Want to send a child, or be told it's fine:** no, and no.
- **Want to make somebody else pay for them:** it doesn't work like that. It knows whose foot it is.
- **Have all chosen the pit:** lovely. Run Scenes 2 and 3 as voices through the wall, skip the landing, and spend the time on Scene 5.

**Bring it back.** Someone asks what the card said. (The memory they'd never give up.) They don't have to answer.

**How it ends.** The first foot goes down.

### Scene 2: Twenty

**Where and why.** [The stair.](play:s25-descend) Move the token. Let the first nineteen go by in a minute.

> **SAY:** "The stairs go on for a long time. Each step has a memory carved into it, worn smooth by the feet of those who came to listen. Some are your memories. Some are strangers'. You hear a child laughing, a bell tolling, a man telling a joke to someone who isn't there."

**Ask, going round:** "You hear one voice you know. Who is it?"

**At step twenty, stop.** Everyone who's walking, and hasn't before, makes the save: **Wisdom, DC 13.** Tell each of them their number: two, or five.

**Then the first memory.** Here's how. Do it the same way every time.
1. Hum the lullaby. One more note than last time.
2. "It's asking. What do you give it?"
3. They say it, or write it. **Small's fine.** "The smell of my father's coat." "Which foot I put first on the ice."
4. Say it back, and then: "It's gone. You know you had something. You don't know what it was."
5. Write **Stairs** in the ledger, with the step.

**What's really going on.** It wants things with love on them. It doesn't mind how big. Somebody who gives it something they're ashamed of will find it takes that just as gladly. Let them. It's allowed to be a relief.

**If they…**
- **Can't think of one:** give them three words to pick from. *A door, a song, a winter.*
- **Want to keep it private:** face down. They can choose to share one at the end.
- **Give it something cruel that was done to them:** it's theirs. Ask if they're sure, once.
- **Try to give it nothing:** then they can't go any further down. The step's just a step. Nobody's cross.
- **Lie:** it takes the thing the lie was covering.
- **Fly, ten feet above the steps:** that's a real way round it. It costs nothing.

**Bring it back.** Whatever they gave their first bell, whoever's a Ringer. Somebody's voice on the stairs has it. Only for a second.

**How it ends.** They go on. Step forty's the same again, for everyone. **Anyone on two is finished now,** and can say so.

### Scene 3: Forty-one

**Where and why.** One step past forty. It's where they look at what's under their feet.

> **SAY:** "On the forty-first step is the face of a woman you have never met, laughing at a joke."

**What's really going on.** [Some of these weren't given here.](play:s25-read-the-steps) They were Tithed or sold, and they've come to rest. Study, Intelligence (Investigation), DC 13: whose. **This is Jonah's mother.** It's the face he can't remember. (If they met Mara Bray on the steps in Hallowmere with an empty frame in her lap, it's her, laughing. If she's home already, it's still her.)

**If they…**
- **Work out who she is:** they can't take her away. They can look as hard as they like, and tell him. One of them can draw. It matters in the epilogue.
- **Look for their own:** whatever they've paid this stair is carved on the step that took it. They can look at it, like a stranger's picture on a wall. Nothing comes back.
- **Look for the Blanks' names:** there are four hundred on the wall, very small. Someone's been copying them out, by hand, in pencil. It's Maudrin's writing.
- **Have Maudrin with them:** she stops on forty-one. "That one was me," she says. "I signed for it." She waits to be shouted at.
- **Want to smash it:** it's only stone. Smashing it doesn't send it home. Say so first.

**Bring it back.** The joke. The man on step nineteen who was telling one. *She's who he's telling it to.* Give them the punchline now, if you can think of one. Keep it bad.

**How it ends.** A light below, and somebody's breath.

### Scene 4: The landing

**Where and why.** Step fifty: a round room, a ledge, a hole in the middle. Which of these is it?

**The Court's sealers: if Maudrin went down.** [They're on the landing.](play:s25-sealers-on-the-stairs)

> **SAY:** "The stairs end in a wall of grey gloves and silence-stone."

**Sergeant Minna Saul.** Late forties. She keeps touching her ring. *Lines:* "We're to ask you to go back. That's all it is. We're to *ask.*" · "I've lost three on this stair. One of them was his name. I've got the ring, look. It's got an M in it." · "Please don't make me do this part."

- **[Show the Key](play:s25-sealers-on-the-stairs)** (if the party's got it), or Maudrin in custody: they stand aside, and hold a lamp for them.
- **Talk:** Persuasion DC 15 gets one of them past to argue with Maudrin, or gets the twelve Hushmen to sit down. Give her her husband's name (it's in the Ledger; or Ansel knows: it's **Emmot**) and no roll. She weeps, and opens the line.
- **Push through:** see the fights. They won't follow below the landing.

**The Sleepless: if Mirel never rang.** [On every step.](play:s25-sleepless-on-the-stairs)

> **SAY:** "On every step stands someone's fear, patient as a statue."

- **Walk between them:** group Stealth, DC 14, or a slow walk with your eyes shut and one hand on the wall. Let them do it. One person hears their own fear say something sensible.
- **The Cult hums:** if it's ceased, the Leader and two others come down as far as here and hum. They fold up like washing.
- **Fight:** see below.

**Neither: if it's quiet.** The Hush is here, and nothing else is.

> **SAY (the Hush, in each person's own voice):** "Are you coming to hear it, or are you coming to stop it?"

Let each of them answer. It isn't a test. "That's all right," it says, to anything.

**What's really going on.** The people on this landing are all scared of the same thing, and it isn't the party.

**If they…**
- **Came by the pit:** they come out on the far side of the landing, behind everyone, and may walk past.
- **Knock someone into the hole:** it's forty feet to the next turn of the stairs. 4d6. They're all right. They've got a step to pay for, and they know it.

**Bring it back.** One of the Hushmen's the one who took his glove off on the second bend. He's put it back on, and it's inside out.

**How it ends.** Down. Sixty, eighty, a hundred. **Hum it each time.** Anyone who failed the save goes on paying: one at each.

### Scene 5: The last step

**Where and why.** [The bottom.](play:s25-reach-the-bottom) They've arrived. Don't start the next bit.

> **SAY:** "The last step is wider than the others, and at the bottom a bell the size of a house hangs in the dark."

**Let it be big.** Ask: "How far away do you stop?"

**What's really going on.** It's Ysh, the Seventh. It isn't ringing; it's *humming.* It's been humming to one thing for four hundred years, and every few minutes it drops a note. When it does, everyone's stomach goes, and far underneath, something turns over.

**Then take stock.** Let them sit on the last step. Everybody looks at their cards. If they want to, each one reads out **one.** If they came by the pit, they're sitting next to people who didn't. Let that conversation happen.

**If they…**
- **Ask what they've forgotten:** they can't know. Their friends can. "You used to whistle." It's a good few minutes.
- **Want to look at the bell:** there's a notch in it the shape of the Key. The metal's blank. There's writing cut in the rock underneath it, in a small plain hand. *For whoever can't sleep.*
- **Want to ring it now:** next time. It takes what it takes, and everyone should've slept on it.
- **Hear somebody else breathing:** if Maudrin's down here, she's on the far side of the bell. She hasn't lit a lamp. She says, "Take your time."
- **Want a rest:** a short one. Nobody can sleep here. Everyone's being sung to.

**Bring it back.** The card from the opening. The one they'd never give up. Tell each of them: it's still there. Have them hold it for a second.

**How it ends.** Ask: **"What did the stairs take from you?"** Round the table. Nobody has to. Then stop.

### Running the fights (Session 25)

**Ten feet wide, no rail, a drop in the middle.** That's the fight. Only two people can stand side by side. Pushing matters more than damage.

#### The Court's sealers

*Six Wardens (AC 16, 82 HP), four Sergeants (AC 15, 52 HP), three Knights (AC 18, 52 HP), twelve Hushmen (AC 12, 32 HP). They only need to say no.*

- **Setup:** Knights in front, shoulder to shoulder. Wardens behind, with their stones out: nobody's casting within ten feet. Hushmen round the ledge.
- **What happens:** they hold. They don't come forward. They don't chase anyone below the landing. They'll arrest anybody who's fallen over.
- **A Warden's turn:** two mauls (+5, 12, pushed 10 feet), or two bolts (+4, 13). Stone: AC 12, HP 10, or Sleight of Hand DC 15.
- **A Knight's turn:** two swords (+5, 10 and 4 Radiant each).
- **A Sergeant's turn:** two blows (+4; about 5, and 3 Necrotic), or one and a signal (a d4 for an ally).
- **A Hushman's turn:** a glove (+5, 5 and 2 Necrotic), or an arrest (Strength DC 12 or Grappled; DC 12 to get out).
- **Use a few at a time.** Two Knights and two Wardens can reach. The rest are waiting. Don't roll for people who can't get there.
- **When it ends:** three of the front rank down; the Key's shown; Maudrin's a captive; or someone gives Minna her husband's name.
- **Scale on the fly:** leave out two Wardens. Or count every three Hushmen as a wall you can climb over.
- **Non-lethal:** suggest it. They're very scared.

#### The Sleepless on the stairs

*Seven Sleepless (AC 13, HP 67). Only if Mirel never rang. Resist weapon damage. Can't be Charmed, Frightened, knocked over or knocked out.*

- **Setup:** one on each step from fifty to fifty-six. They don't move until somebody's next to them.
- **What happens:** each takes the shape of one person's fear. Ask the player. It doesn't have to be large.
- **A Sleepless's turn:** a gaze (30 feet, Wisdom DC 13; 10 Psychic and Frightened for a round), and a touch (+6, 16 Psychic, and that much off their maximum until a long rest).
- **Who to worry about:** anyone who's Frightened and can't go *down.* They're stuck. Somebody has to come back for them.
- **When it ends:** the Cult hums; it's dawn outside; or they're past the last one.
- **Scale on the fly:** five of them. Four, if two people went by the pit.
- **Non-lethal:** they aren't alive. Someone might thank theirs, and it goes.

### Pacing (Session 25)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:10 | Recap; the card they'd never give up |
| 0:10 to 0:35 | Scene 1: the top step |
| 0:35 to 1:10 | Scene 2: twenty, and forty |
| 1:10 to 1:30 | Scene 3: forty-one |
| 1:30 to 2:20 | Scene 4: the landing |
| 2:20 to 3:00 | Sixty, eighty, a hundred; Scene 5: the last step |
| 3:00 to 3:15 | The question |

- **Where to break:** straight after the first memory's written down.
- **Running long:** no fight. Show the Key, say the name, or walk past with eyes shut.
- **Running short:** more voices. Each player makes one up for somebody else's character to hear.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop on the landing. Nobody likes it, but it's a place.

### If you get stuck (Session 25)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **The song drops a note.** Everyone grabs the wall.
2. **A step has the party on it.** Last month. Round a fire, laughing.
3. **Somebody behind them on the stairs** is counting under their breath. There's no one there.

**If it's too much for somebody:** the pit, always. It's not a lesser way down. Or a break, and a biscuit.

**If it's turning into a competition:** it's private cards from here, face down. No reading out.

**If nobody pays anything:** they all flew, or they all climbed. That's a clever party. Let them have it.

**Names for Hushmen and voices on the steps** (cross one off when you use it): Pru, Kester, Isaac, Mabel, Wilf, Sergeant Minna Saul, Swithin.

### End of session 25

**The closing question:** "What did the stairs take from you?" Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember." (It lands differently tonight.)

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** who walked, who climbed, who turned round; the landing; Jonah's mother.
- **The Memory ledger:** every loss, marked **Stairs,** with the step, and each person's cap.
- **World-state facts to check:** the Hush Shrine (reached), Maudrin, the Key, the Cult.
- **Friends who paid.** They'll carry it in the epilogue.
- **Friends who stayed,** and where they're standing.

**Rewards:**
- **The bottom of the stairs.**
- **A face for Jonah,** if somebody read the step.
- **A clear way out:** the casting-pit. They'll want it.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to everyone who wrote something on a card.

plays.title: They stop Maudrin striking Ysh
plays.why: If she holds the Key at the bell, the whole world hangs on one action.
plays.readAloud: Maudrin stands beside the bell with the Key raised. "Let me seal it, and the world continues. Take another step, and I will choose what follows." Her hand is shaking.
plays.response: Ask what the characters do before she acts; if combat begins, roll initiative and use the Keeper with her Wardens. Striking needs her action while adjacent to Ysh with the Key out of its case. Grappling, disarming, bargaining and blocking her route can all prevent it. She prefers to seal the stairs and hold the Key. Only a completed strike opens the Unbound; killing her afterward can't undo the sound.
plays.consequence: She strikes, seals, surrenders, or loses the Key.
plays.fallback: If the table freezes, have her hesitate one heartbeat and say a name: Cassia's, or her grandmother Ilse's.
plays.tells: Maudrin raises the Key; players shout, move, or reach for a spell.
plays.rules: Initiative; her strike is her action on her turn. Grapple (2024 Unarmed Strike option) or disarm (DC 17). Counterspell can't stop it: the strike is not a spell. Plane Shift, Banishment and Hold Monster: she has Legendary Resistance and Magic Resistance; see any-geas-dominate-hold.
plays.later: She strikes (s26-maudrin-strikes), seals (s26-maudrin-leaves-with-key), yields (s26-grapple-the-key) or dies (s26-kill-maudrin-at-bell).
plays.keywords: strike, stop her, maudrin, bell, ysh, grapple, disarm, prevent, block

plays.title: Maudrin strikes the Seventh
plays.why: If no one stops her action, she chooses what follows.
plays.readAloud: The Hush cracks. The lullaby falls silent, and the world goes quiet in a way you have never heard before: not the silence of the bells, but the silence of a held breath about to be released.
plays.response: She pays all six Tolls (Memory, Year, Sense, Name, Fear, Gift), each at Ruinous weight, and the Hush cracks. Oum opens an eye. The players, not Maudrin and not the DM, choose Remake or Unmake through their conversation with Oum (S27).
plays.consequence: Ysh is struck. Oum wakes.
plays.tells: She is adjacent to Ysh with the Key uncased on her turn.
plays.later: S27: the Unbound (s27-oum-answers, s27-oum-remake, s27-oum-unmake). Dreams return (s27-dreams-return).
plays.keywords: strike, maudrin strikes, bell rings, oum wakes, unbound

plays.title: The party stands at the bell with the Key
plays.why: Everything ends here, and the party decides.
plays.readAloud: The bell is vast and blank, its surface like the face of a sleeping god. You stand before it with the Key in your hands. The lullaby is still there, very faint, asking you to be quiet. Your choice is the only one left in the world.
plays.response: The figure from the Session 11 winter-moment stands at the bell's foot: the character, older, holding the Key, smiling. Ask that player what they feel; don't explain. Then disclose every option and its price before anyone acts (the Forecast tab lists which are open): Concord, Unbound, Second Dawn. Take a table break before an irreversible choice. Maudrin, weeping behind them, offers no resistance.
plays.consequence: The campaign's ending is chosen.
plays.fallback: If the table can't agree, they may postpone: leave with the Key, unsealed, and keep adventuring.
plays.tells: The party holds the Key at the bottom of the stairs.
plays.rules: Concord: seat the Key without striking, a willing Ringer accepts the Great Toll (ask in private). Unbound: strike, the striker pays all six Tolls at Ruinous weight. Second Dawn: one uninterrupted minute to seal the Key in its recess, no Toll.
plays.later: S27 resolves the chosen path. S28 epilogues follow the ring ledger.
plays.keywords: choice, key, bell, ysh, ending, decide, seventh, final choice

plays.title: They take the Key from Maudrin at the bell
plays.why: A grapple or a disarm ends the race before it starts.
plays.readAloud: The Key comes away from her glove with a sound like a drawn breath. She does not reach for it.
plays.response: She strikes with her action while adjacent to Ysh with the Key uncased; interrupt her before then. Grappling her, knocking the Key from her hand (DC 17 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) as a Utilize action), bargaining or blocking her route all work. On success the party holds the Key and Maudrin stops fighting.

## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. One room, one bell, and a choice. There's a fight in it, or there isn't. Either way, the important hour is the one where four people sit round your table and talk, so get there before anyone's tired.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-26) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-26) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-26) · [Scene 1: The bell in the dark](#scene-1-the-bell-in-the-dark) · [Scene 2: Her hand is shaking](#scene-2-her-hand-is-shaking) · [Scene 3: Footsteps](#scene-3-footsteps) · [Scene 4: What's on the table](#scene-4-whats-on-the-table) · [Scene 5: What will you ring](#scene-5-what-will-you-ring) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-26) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-26) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-26) · [End of session](#end-of-session-26)

### Before you start (Session 26)

**Level:** four characters at level 11.

**Check the world state first.**
- **Who's got the Key?** This is the whole night. **Maudrin:** run Scenes 1, 2, 4 and 5. **The party:** Scene 2 is a page long. **The Court, sealed away:** they're not here; run [the rescue chapter](play:s27-rescue-chapter) instead.
- **Maudrin.** At the bell, beside them as a witness, captured, dead or exiled? And how hurt: if she was below half at the Strike or on the Tor, she starts on **85 HP.**
- **Ser Haldric.** Still hers, turned, or gone? That picks the fight.
- **Corin.** Ally: he's beside them. **Refused or an enemy: he's coming** (Scene 3). Unmet or dead: skip it.
- **The six bells.** Open the Forecast (Foresight) and read which endings are open, **with their prices.** Write them on a card in plain words.
- **The Session 11 note.** Which player saw themselves in the glass, and the words they said. Have them in front of you.
- **Oum** (asleep) and **Ysh** (unstruck). Check nobody's changed them.

**What this session is about.** Whether you can do a thing that can't be undone, and who gets to decide.

**Your goals tonight:**
- Let them look at it before anybody speaks.
- Give Maudrin her case, properly, before a single die.
- Put every open ending on the table with its price. Nobody should be surprised by a cost.
- **Take a real break** before they choose.
- End on the question: **"What will you ring, and what will it cost you?"** Then stop.

**Prepare:**
- **If the Concord's open: talk to the likely Ringer's player in private, days before.** Say what [the Great Toll](play:s27-concord) is: their name, forgotten by everyone, and the character retires as the Seventh's voice. They can say no now, or tonight, or with a hand on the bell. Refusing costs nothing.
- **The endings card,** one line each.
- **Tokens or minis:** one Keeper; five Wardens; four Sergeants; eight Hushmen; Haldric; Corin; two Heart-Hounds.
- **A big dark cloth or a bowl** for the bell. Put it in the middle of the table. Nothing goes on it.
- **The Memory ledger.**
- **The lullaby.** All of it, tonight. Stop on the second-to-last note.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **[Her strike](play:s26-stop-the-strike) is her action, on her turn,** standing next to the bell with the Key out of its case. That's all it takes. Tell them so.
- **What stops it:** Grappling her, getting the Key out of her hand, standing between her and the bell, or an offer she'll take.
- **Grapple:** an Unarmed Strike. She makes a Strength or Dexterity save (her choice) against 8 + your Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus. While she's Grappled, she can't strike the bell.
- **Knock the Key from her hand:** a Utilize action, **Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand), DC 17.**
- **Counterspell does nothing** to the strike. It isn't a spell.
- **[Control spells](play:any-geas-dominate-hold):** Geas and Dominate fail while she holds the Key. Hold Monster and Banishment allow a save, and she's got Legendary Resistance.
- **[Teleport](play:any-teleport-and-gates):** works in and out, now they've seen the room. Not within ten feet of a silence-stone.
- **The six Tolls at Ruinous,** for whoever strikes: a **Memory** (a whole year, and everyone met in it), a **Year** (twenty years older, 5 feet less Speed), a **Sense** (gone a year, then dulled for good; sight or hearing only if that player agreed at session zero), a **Name** (everyone in one town forgets them), a **Fear** (something they can't avoid, for good), a **Gift** (a skill or tool proficiency, given away).

### Key people tonight (Session 26)

| Who | What they are | Stat block | Where | Starts | Influence | Secret |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Maudrin Vesk** | The Quiet Chancellor, and the last one holding it up | Maudrin Vesk, Keeper of the Seventh | By the bell | Frightened | DC 20 | She hasn't decided. She came down to find out. |
| **The Hush** | The lullaby | — | In the bell | Tired | It can't be persuaded | It'd like to stop. It's afraid of what happens when it does. |
| **The one in the glass** | One of them, older | — | At the foot of the bell | Waiting | No | None. It's a question. |
| **Ser Haldric Mose** | If he's still hers | Ser Haldric Mose | In front of her | Sure of himself | DC 15 | Nobody's told him why she keeps him close. |
| **Corin Aldeth** | Coming, or beside them | Corin Aldeth | The stairs | Certain | DC 15, or the truth | He knows what it costs. He's never thought of it as *his.* |
| **Sergeant Godric** | Her door-ward | Hushman Sergeant | The last step | Wishing he was elsewhere | DC 13 | Has been humming along and hasn't noticed. |
| **Tolliver** | A young Hushman | Hushman | Behind the bell | In tears | None needed | Can read. Has read what's cut in the floor. |

**Places at a glance:**
- **The chamber:** sixty feet across, round, bare rock. Your voice comes back late.
- **Ysh:** a bell as big as a house, hung from the root of the hill, and quite blank. Its lip's as high as your chest. It's never been struck.
- **The notch:** under the lip, the shape of the Key. Seat it there.
- **The recess:** in the rock at the bell's foot. Seal it there.
- **The last step** on one side, **the casting-pit** on the other.

**Rumours (d6)** (what people have told them about this room, all the way along):
1. "Wenna Aldeth rang it once." (False. She rang a handbell, up on the hill, and it killed her.)
2. "Nobody built it. It was here." (False. Somebody did. There's a pit.)
3. "If you put your hand on it, you hear your mother." (True. Everyone does.)
4. "She goes down there to talk to it." (Maudrin. False. She'd never been past the top step, until now.)
5. "There isn't a seventh bell." (Every schoolbook in Hallowmere.)
6. "You'll know what to do." (Nobody who said this had been.)

### Opening recap (Session 26)

> **SAY:** "A hundred steps. Some of you walked them, and some of you didn't, and you've each got less than you came with or you know someone who has. *(Who paid? Who turned back?)* You've been sitting on the last one. In front of you there's a bell the size of a house, and it's humming, very quietly, the way you'd hum with a child asleep on your shoulder. One of you stands up."

- **Then hand it over:** "Who stands up?" That player leads the first scene.

### Scene 1: The bell in the dark

**Where and why.** They walk across the floor. Nobody's told them not to.

> **SAY:** "It doesn't get any bigger as you walk. It was already as big as it was. The floor's worn smooth in a ring around it, about as wide as a person pacing. Inside the ring there's writing cut in the rock, in a small plain hand. It only says one thing, over and over. *For whoever can't sleep.*"

**Ask each of them:** "Do you touch it?" Anyone who does hears their own mother, or whoever was nearest to one, humming. Same tune. It always was.

**What's really going on.** Somebody cast this, in the pit overhead, for something frightening they had to look after. Nobody knows who. Nobody was hiding it, either. They only wanted it left alone.

**[The one in the glass](play:s26-winter-figure-empty-hands).** On the far side of the bell somebody's standing. It's the player with the Session 11 note.

*If Maudrin's got the Key:*

> **SAY:** "At the foot of the bell stands one of you, older, with open hands and no Key, waiting."

*If the party's got the Key,* keep the figure for Scene 4.

Say to that player, "What do you feel?" Then read them, word for word, what they said in Session 11. **Don't explain any of it.** Nobody else has to see it.

**If they…**
- **Talk to the figure:** it knows everything they know. It says what they'd say. Let the player answer their own questions.
- **Touch it:** warm, this time.
- **Attack it:** there's nobody there.
- **[Cast Dream or speak to the Hush](play:any-dream-and-sending):** one question for one true memory, told out loud. Nothing's lost. *"Yes. I'm tired. Does it matter?"*
- **Look at the ring on the floor:** hundreds of people's shoes, a very long time ago. Round and round, the way you walk with a baby.

**Bring it back.** The tune. Whoever first heard it in Session 1, off the bronze in their hands: tell them it's the same three notes, and then the rest.

**How it ends.** *Maudrin's here:* a small sound, like a case being unlatched. *She isn't:* nothing. It's only them. Go to Scene 4.

### Scene 2: Her hand is shaking

**Where and why.** *If she's got the Key.* She's been here an hour. She hasn't done it.

> **SAY:** "Maudrin stands beside the bell with the Key raised. 'Let me seal it, and the world continues. Take another step, and I will choose what follows.' Her hand is shaking."

**[Ask each of them what they do](play:s26-stop-the-strike) before she does anything.** Go round the table. Nobody rolls Initiative until somebody makes you.

**What's really going on.** If the Key's sealed in the rock, its hum stops, and so does every silence-stone the Court's got. So she won't seal *it.* She'll seal **the stairs,** and carry the Key close to the tune for the rest of her life, and then give it to someone. She's had four hundred years of other people doing it to prove it works. And she's seen the party ring bells, and the sky didn't fall.

**Maudrin Vesk.** Dove-grey, one glove off. *Uses your name. Doesn't raise her voice, even now.* **Wants** somebody else to be right.

*Lines:*
- "I've stood at the top every midwinter since I was twenty. I'd never come down. I used to think it was talking to me."
- "I'll lock the stairs. Not this. If this goes quiet, everyone who's ever trusted me is standing out there with nothing between them and the dark."
- "Tell me what happens. Not what you hope. *What happens.*"
- "I don't want to. I want you to hear me say that. I don't *want* to."
- *(To whoever's been kindest to her:)* "You'd make a good one of me, you know. I'm sorry."

**If they…**
- **[Talk](play:s26-parley-at-the-bell):** Persuasion, **DC 20.** Read: "'I will seal it,' she says, 'and no one will wake it. Don't make me choose what comes after.'" Make her case for her, honestly. Give **Advantage** for a promise that covers the Court's people, for Cassia's name, for her grandmother Ilse's, or for the one question she asked on the Tor, answered. She'll take **a sealed stair and a witness:** one of theirs, with her, for good. She'll also take somebody she trusts holding the Key.
- **Fail the roll:** she's sorry. She lifts it higher. They've still got a round.
- **[Take the Key](play:s26-grapple-the-key):** grab her, or knock it out of her hand (DC 17). Read: "The Key comes away from her glove with a sound like a drawn breath. She does not reach for it." **She stops.** So does everybody. The fight's over.
- **Stand between her and the bell:** she has to move them. She can't bring herself to for a turn.
- **Say nothing, and nobody moves:** she hesitates one heartbeat, and says a name. **Cassia.** Or **Ilse.** Then she looks at them as if they'd said it.
- **[Walk away](play:s26-walk-away):** "Maudrin watches you go up the stairs. 'Thank you,' she says. She means it." Ask outright: **are you finished fighting this?** Only if everyone says yes is it over. If it's a plan, it's a plan.
- **[Help her seal it](play:s26-help-seal),** having all agreed to stop: "You stand with her at the bell while the Hushmen close the stairs behind you." Same question. Ask it twice.
- **[Let her take the Key away](play:s26-maudrin-leaves-with-key):** "The Key goes back in its case. 'Not today,' she says to the bell." They can follow her, or go up and plan.
- **[Kill her](play:s26-kill-maudrin-at-bell):** "The Key falls out of her hand and rings once on the stone." Only on stone. Her Hushmen put their maces down. If she'd already struck, it changes nothing.
- **[She strikes](play:s26-maudrin-strikes):** read it slowly, below. She pays all six, at Ruinous. And **the players,** not her and not you, will answer what's woken. Go to the end of the session.

> **SAY (only if it's struck):** "The Hush cracks. The lullaby falls silent, and the world goes quiet in a way you have never heard before: not the silence of the bells, but the silence of a held breath about to be released."

**If the party's got the Key and she's here:** she's a step behind them. She's got nothing left, and she's weeping. She won't stop them. If somebody goes back and stands beside her, that's the scene.

**If she isn't here:** skip it. Say her name once, if it's right: "There's a place to stand here, worn smooth, and nobody in it."

**Bring it back.** What they told her on the Tor when she asked, "What would you have done?" She remembers it exactly. She repeats it back to whoever said it.

**How it ends.** They hold the Key, or they don't. Everyone's breathing hard. If Corin's coming, it's now.

### Scene 3: Footsteps

**Where and why.** *Only if Corin was refused, or he's an enemy.* He's had the Notes for months and he's never had the Key. **If he's an ally,** skip this; he's sitting on the floor with his palm on the bronze and his eyes shut.

> **SAY:** "Footsteps behind you, running, and a hammer ringing against the wall."

**What's really going on.** He believes there's a chord that puts everything right. He's correct. It needs six bells. **If all six aren't rung and he seats the Key, it cracks.** And it was Corin who worked out what "the whole name" means. *Yours,* he said. He's never once said it about himself.

**Corin Aldeth.** Scorched apron, a hammer, no coat. *Humming, half a note out from the bell.* **Wants** to finish what Wenna started.

*Lines:*
- "It's all right. I know how it goes. Let me just… I know how it goes."
- "Three generations. Three. And you want to *talk* about it?"
- "Wenna got as far as the top of the hill. Look. Look how far I've got."

**If they…**
- **[Get in his way](play:s26-corin-races-to-the-bell):** he tries to take the Key off whoever's holding it. He'll hit a person to do it and be appalled.
- **Tell him what it costs:** the whole name. **His.** Nobody would ever know an Aldeth had been here. He stops dead. "Nobody'd… not even that it was *us?*" He sits down.
- **Show him it isn't whole:** strike or hum the rung bells' notes; there's a gap. Performance, or Intelligence (Arcana), **DC 15,** or no roll if somebody in the party's a Ringer who's rung one. He hears it. He's a craftsman.
- **Offer him a part:** if all six are rung, he might be the one. Not tonight; next session. Mark it.
- **[Let him get there](play:s26-corin-cracks-the-lullaby),** with the Key, before six are rung: "He does not strike it. He seats the Key as the Notes describe, and the chord is not whole, and the bell cracks." It's struck. Oum wakes. Go to the end.

**Bring it back.** In Session 18 each of them said their whole name out loud, and he listened to it like a bell. He says one of them now, all of it, and gets it right.

**How it ends.** He's stopped, or it's too late.

### Scene 4: What's on the table

**Where and why.** [They're standing at the bell with the Key.](play:s26-the-choice) Nothing's chasing them. **This is the scene.**

> **SAY:** "The bell is vast and blank, its surface like the face of a sleeping god. You stand before it with the Key in your hands. The lullaby is still there, very faint, asking you to be quiet. Your choice is the only one left in the world."

**The one in the glass,** if they've got the Key: older, the Key in both hands, smiling. "What do you feel?" Read them their Session 11 words. Say nothing else.

**Then put your notes down and say it plainly.** Out of character is fine. One line each, only the ones that are open:

- **The Concord** *(all six bells rung):* "You seat the Key in the bell, and you don't strike it. Everything you've rung sounds at once, and the song's whole. **Somebody becomes part of it.** They give up their name. Nobody who's ever known them will remember them. It has to be somebody who wants to, and they can say no at any moment and lose nothing."
- **The Hush Unbound** *(always open, until it's sealed):* "You strike it. **Whoever strikes pays all six kinds of Toll, at the heaviest there is.** The one who's sleeping wakes up and asks you something, and you'll have to answer."
- **The Second Dawn:** "You lock the Key in the rock, unstruck. It takes one of you a minute, undisturbed, and **it costs nothing.** What you rang stays rung. What you didn't doesn't come back." Read them the ring ledger, bell by bell. *With none rung, say so: it's a stalemate, and nothing's mended.*
- **Wait:** "You can go back up with the Key and think about it. [It'll still be here.](play:s27-postpone) It's a bit louder every day, that's all."

**Giving up isn't on the list.** Don't offer it. If somebody says, "What if we just stopped?", answer truthfully: the Court keeps the Key, and the collectors go back to their rounds.

**What's really going on.** There isn't a right one. If they ask you what you'd do, say: "I don't have to live there."

**If they…**
- **Ask for the exact price:** tell them the kinds and the weight, never the particular thing. (Nobody knows which year.)
- **Want to know what it'd do for somebody they love:** say. This is the moment to be generous with facts.
- **Ask Maudrin,** if she's here: she's honest. "I'd seal the stairs. You know that. But I've never once seen what happens if you don't."
- **Ask Corin:** he's shaking. He tells them the Concord's true.
- **Ask the Hush:** "Whatever you do, do it gently."
- **Argue:** good. Let it run. Keep anyone from being shouted down. "I'd like to hear from" is a useful sentence.
- **Can't agree:** they wait. Say it kindly, and mean it.
- **Someone starts to do it on their own:** stop. Say, "That's everyone's. Is everyone all right with it?" It only happens if they are.

**Bring it back.** Ask each of them what they wrote at session zero about what they'd lost. One line. Then: "Would you get it back?" Tell them the truth, from the ledger.

**How it ends.** **Take a break. Fifteen minutes, away from the table.** Put the kettle on. When they sit down again, go to Scene 5.

### Scene 5: What will you ring

**Where and why.** Back at the bell. Lights down, if you can.

> **SAY:** "Nobody's moved. It's still humming. It's got to the end of the verse, and it's stopped on the note before the last one, the way it does. It's waiting to see."

**Ask once round the table:** "What does your character want to happen? Not the group. You." No answering back. Then: **"And who's holding the Key?"**

**What's really going on.** You're not resolving it tonight. You're making sure they know what they've chosen. The rite, the strike, the minute: that's all next time. *(If there's an hour left and everybody's wide awake, go straight on to Session 27. It's allowed.)*

**If they…**
- **Have chosen:** say it back in one sentence. "So: you'll seat it, and it's *(name)*'s voice." Or "So: you'll strike it, and it's *(name)*'s hand." Get a nod from each of them.
- **Have a Ringer who wants to think:** of course. Ask that player again, privately, before next time.
- **Have [lost someone tonight](play:s26-help-ringer-falls):** "Your friend is on the stone, and Maudrin's hand has stopped." Everybody's does. Let them reach. [Revivify](play:any-pc-dies) has a minute. The dead pay nothing.
- **Were too late:** it's been struck. It isn't a failure. Somebody enormous is opening an eye, and they're the first thing it'll see.

**Bring it back.** Whoever struck the first bell of the campaign: remind them what they said when they picked up the hammer.

**How it ends.** The last note. Don't hum it. Ask: **"What will you ring, and what will it cost you?"** Let each of them answer. Then stop.

### Running the fights (Session 26)

**Nobody has to fight tonight.** If they do, it's four characters at level 11 against something built to stop them, for about four rounds, and **it ends the second the Key leaves her hand.** Say that at the top, so nobody feels they have to grind through a room of people.

**A fair clock for the strike.** She's by the bell already, so be open about it.
- **Her first turn:** she steps back against the bell, and the Key's out. Say: "She could do it now. She doesn't."
- **Her second turn:** she says the name. Her hand comes up.
- **From her third turn,** if nobody's holding her, standing between, or talking her down: she strikes.
- **She prefers not to.** Any real offer buys a turn.

#### The bell, with Ser Haldric

*One Keeper of the Seventh (AC 17, 170 HP; 85 if she came here hurt), five Wardens (AC 16, 82 HP), three Sergeants (AC 15, 52 HP), six Hushmen (AC 12, 32 HP), Ser Haldric (AC 18, 55 HP). Lighter: two fewer Wardens.*

- **Setup:** she's against the bell. Wardens in a half-ring ten feet out from her. Haldric in front. Sergeants at the last step and the pit. Hushmen anywhere; they'd rather be nowhere.
- **What happens:** Wardens block and shove. Haldric calls somebody out by name and fights only them. Sergeants keep the doors. Nobody chases anyone who backs off.
- **The Keeper's turn:** four Hush Bolts (+9, 23 psychic, 150 feet), or a spell: Silence or Hold Person (twice a day each, DC 17), Wall of Force, Dimension Door or Modify Memory (once each). She uses Wall of Force early, between her and whoever's fastest. She keeps Dimension Door to get back to the bell.
- **Off her turn:** Counterspell and Shield (three times a day each). Three Legendary Actions a round: a Hush Bolt, thirty feet of silent movement, or the Toll of Quiet (Wisdom DC 17, 18 psychic and Deafened).
- **Her gloves:** spell attacks made within ten feet of her have Disadvantage. She's got Magic Resistance and three Legendary Resistances.
- **A Warden's turn:** two mauls (+5, 12, pushed ten feet), or two bolts (+4, 13). The stone: no spells within ten feet; AC 12, HP 10, or Sleight of Hand DC 15 to pull it.
- **Who to worry about:** a wizard inside two stones. Tell them where the stones are, every round.
- **Allies who came down:** each named one takes a Sergeant or two Hushmen off the board. Don't roll it.
- **When it ends:** the Key leaves her hand; she takes an offer; she's at 0; or she strikes. Any of those, and everyone stops. She never leaves this room in a fight.
- **Scale on the fly:** easier, the Hushmen are sitting down by round two. Harder, she's on full HP and starts with Wall of Force up.
- **Non-lethal:** 0 HP with a melee hit is Unconscious and Stable, if they say so. They'll say so for her.

#### The bell, without Haldric

*One Keeper, five Wardens, four Sergeants (AC 15, 52 HP), eight Hushmen. Lighter: two fewer Wardens.*

- **Setup and turns:** as above. One Sergeant stands where Haldric would have, and looks embarrassed about it.
- **If Haldric's come with the party:** she stops talking in the middle of a word when she sees him. She loses her first turn. He says whatever he's come to say. **Wait for it.**
- **When it ends:** as above.

#### The bell, and Corin

*One Keeper, four Wardens, two Sergeants, Corin Aldeth (AC 14, 81 HP), two Heart-Hounds (AC 15, 58 HP). Lighter: no hounds.*

- **Setup:** Corin comes off the last step on round one, sixty feet from the bell, with a hound either side.
- **What happens:** it's a race. He's after the Key; she's after time. The Wardens can't tell who to stop.
- **Corin's turn:** three Ringing Strikes (+6, 16 thunder). Counterspell (Constitution save, DC 14). He goes for hands.
- **A Heart-Hound's turn:** two bites (+5, 7). They sit if he says sit.
- **When it ends:** for him, when someone tells him the cost is his own name. For her, when the Key's gone. **If he gets it to the notch with six unrung, it cracks.**
- **Non-lethal:** nobody in the room wants him dead. Not even her.

### Pacing (Session 26)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:10 | Recap; who stands up |
| 0:10 to 0:35 | Scene 1: the bell; the one in the glass |
| 0:35 to 1:10 | Scene 2: her hand is shaking |
| 1:10 to 1:45 | A fight, or Scene 3, or neither |
| 1:45 to 2:20 | Scene 4: everything on the table |
| 2:20 to 2:35 | **The break** |
| 2:35 to 3:05 | Scene 5: what will you ring |
| 3:05 to 3:15 | The question |

- **Where to break:** after Scene 4, always, before anyone decides anything.
- **Running long:** cut the fight at round three; somebody gets a hand on the Key.
- **Running short:** go on into Session 27. There's nothing in the way.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop on Maudrin's shaking hand. It's a very good place.

### If you get stuck (Session 26)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **The song stops for one breath.** Everyone in the room turns round. It starts again.
2. **Tolliver reads the writing out loud,** because nobody's told him not to.
3. **Maudrin asks one of them to hold her glove.**

**If they attack her the moment they see her:** fine. She talks through the first round anyway.

**If a fight's going badly:** she doesn't want anyone dead on this floor. She stops the Wardens herself. "That's *enough.*"

**If they've got a cleverer plan than any of this:** check it against two things. Is the Key struck or unstruck? Does anybody pay who didn't choose to? Then let it work.

**If someone's really upset:** stop, kettle, come back. It'll wait. It's good at it.

**Names for the Court's people down here** (cross one off when you use it): Sergeant Godric, Tolliver, Bettany, Rusk, Jocelyn.

### End of session 26

**The closing question:** "What will you ring, and what will it cost you?" Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** the standoff and how it ended; Corin; the choice; the figure in the glass.
- **World-state facts to check:** the Tuning Key, Ysh, the Hush Shrine, Maudrin, Ser Haldric, Corin, resistance.
- **What each player felt** when the figure looked at them. Put it next to the Session 11 note.
- **What they've chosen,** in one sentence, and who's holding the Key.
- **The Ringer,** if there's one, and that they've been asked in private.

**Rewards:**
- **The Key,** if they've got it.
- **The choice.** Nobody's had it for four hundred years.
- **The bargain,** if they made one: a seal and a witness, in her own words.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to whoever changed their mind out loud.

## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. You'll only run one of the endings below, and you already know which. Read that one twice and skim the rest. Nothing tonight is difficult; it's only big. Go at half your normal speed, and leave silences alone.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-27) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-27) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-27) · [Scene 1: Once more round](#scene-1-once-more-round) · [Scene 2: The Concord](#scene-2-the-concord) · [Scene 3: The Second Dawn](#scene-3-the-second-dawn) · [Scene 4: The Hush Unbound](#scene-4-the-hush-unbound) · [Scene 5: The first morning](#scene-5-the-first-morning) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-27) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-27) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-27) · [End of session](#end-of-session-27)

### Before you start (Session 27)

**Level:** four characters at level 11.

**Check the world state first.**
- **Ysh.** Unstruck, or struck last time? **Struck:** go from the recap straight to Scene 4, at Oum's question.
- **The Key.** With the party: they choose. With Maudrin or the Court: is the group's resistance **ended,** or not? Ended: the Empty Choir (Scene 5). Not ended: the rescue chapter (Scene 5).
- **The six bells.** Read the ring ledger out to yourself, in order, with who rang each one. **Every ending uses it, and nothing unearned comes back.**
- **The Ringer.** Who, and have you spoken to that player alone? If it might be **Corin** (ally) or **Maudrin** (here or captured), that's decided by the table.
- **Mirel.** Unrung: the Sleepless gather if somebody seals the Key.
- **Dreams.** Lost in Session 17B? They come back tonight, in every ending but one.
- **The release verse.** Did they learn it in Session 2, and does somebody remember the words?
- **The Cult.** If they've ceased or been turned, their hum ends the Sleepless.

**What this session is about.** What you keep, when you can't keep everything.

**Your goals tonight:**
- Ask once more, privately if it's the Concord. A no costs nothing at all.
- Let whoever's hand it is do it themselves, out loud, in their own time.
- For the Unbound: **Unmake only if every single player says yes.** Anything less is Remake.
- Read out what's restored, bell by bell, with the name of whoever rang it.
- End on the question: **"What will survive?"** Then stop.

**Prepare:**
- **The ring ledger and the Memory ledger,** copied out by hand. You'll read from paper.
- **Blank cards, and a pen each.**
- **For the Concord:** something to seat. A key into a bowl. Let them do it with their own hand.
- **For the Unbound:** six cards headed Memory, Year, Sense, Name, Fear, Gift.
- **For the Second Dawn:** ten counters and, if Mirel's unrung, seven Sleepless.
- **The verse,** from Session 2.
- **The lullaby,** all of it. You'll hum the last note tonight.

**Rules you'll use tonight, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **[The Concord](play:s27-concord):** six bells rung, the Key in hand, Ysh unstruck, one willing voice. No ordinary Toll. The **Great Toll** is the voice's whole name.
- **[The Second Dawn](play:s27-second-dawn):** one uninterrupted minute at the recess. In a fight, that's **one action a round for ten rounds, by one character.** Nobody's in a fight? Then it's a minute. Let it be one.
- **[The Unbound](play:s27-unbound):** one action. Whoever strikes pays all six kinds at **Ruinous.** Warn them of the kinds and the weight, never the exact losses.
- **[Refusing](play:s27-refuse-a-toll-mid-rite):** before the strike, it cancels everything, and nothing's lost. After it, the Toll's owed.
- **[If the Ringer dies](play:s27-ringer-dies-at-rite)** before it's done: nothing transfers, no Toll. Revivify has a minute. Somebody else may step in. The dead don't pay.
- **[Wish](play:any-wish)** can't pay a Toll, ring a bell, strike Ysh, or undo what comes next.

### Key people tonight (Session 27)

| Who | What they are | Stat block | Where | Starts | Influence | Secret |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Oum** | The one who's dreaming | — | Everywhere, if it's woken | Curious | It can't be fooled | It likes them. It's always liked them. |
| **The Hush** | The lullaby | — | In the bell | Ready | It can't be persuaded | It doesn't mind who sings it. |
| **The Ringer** | One of them, or someone who's offered | — | At the notch | However they are | None needed | Ask the player. |
| **Maudrin Vesk** | If she's alive and here | Maudrin Vesk, Keeper of the Seventh | By the wall | Finished fighting | DC 20 | Would do it, if anyone thought she deserved to. |
| **Corin Aldeth** | If he's an ally | Corin Aldeth | By the notch | Calm | None needed | Came to terms with it on the stairs. |
| **Ondra, the Cantor** | Far off, under the Mere | — | Not here | Singing | The verse | Has been holding the place in the music for somebody. |

**Places at a glance:**
- **The notch:** under the bell's lip. For the Concord.
- **The recess:** in the rock below. For the Second Dawn.
- **The flat of the bell:** for the other thing.
- **The last step** and **the pit:** both open. Nobody's keeping them here.

**Rumours (d6)** (what each of them once believed about the end):
1. "If you ring all seven, the world starts over." (Half true.)
2. "The gods come back." (Nobody's ever met one. They've met bells.)
3. "Everybody dies." (Not unless everybody at this table says so.)
4. "It's all somebody's dream." (True. It doesn't make it less.)
5. "They'll put up a statue." (Not in the Concord. That's the point.)
6. "You'll wake up at home." (Nobody's ever tested it.)

### Opening recap (Session 27)

> **SAY:** "Last time, you stood in front of a bell, and you told each other what you wanted. *(Say what they chose, in one sentence, and whose hand it is.)* Nobody's moved since. It's still on the note before the last one. Somebody upstairs is sitting on a step with a lamp, waiting to find out what sort of morning it's going to be."

*If it was struck last time, read instead:* "Last time, somebody struck the bell that's never been struck. The Hush cracked. You've been standing in that silence ever since. And it's just been broken."

- **Then hand it over:** "What's the last ordinary thing you think of?"

### Scene 1: Once more round

**Where and why.** At the bell. *(Skip it if it's been struck.)* They've slept on it, really slept on it, in their own beds. People change their minds.

> **SAY:** "Nobody says anything for a moment. The Key's in your hand. It's gone warm, the way a cup does. All you've got to do is decide to have decided."

**Ask each of them:** "Is it still the same answer?" It's all right if it isn't.

**Then, for the Concord, take the Ringer's player out of the room.** Really do. Two minutes in the kitchen.
- "It's their name. Nobody who's ever known them will know them. You retire them: they're the voice in the bell, for as long as there's a bell. They won't be in pain. They won't be alone; it's a song for company."
- "You can say no now, and it costs nothing. You can say no with your hand on the Key. Nobody'll be told you were asked, if you don't want."
- If yes: **"What are your last words?"** Let them write them down.

**What's really going on.** This is the only scene all campaign that's about the players. Treat it that way.

**If they…**
- **[Say no](play:s27-refuse-toll):** "The bell waits. It has waited four hundred years; it can wait for you to be sure." Go back in and say, "There's no voice for the Concord yet." Nothing else. No Toll, no price, no reason.
- **Want someone else to do it:** ask. Anyone willing, in the party. Then Corin, if he's an ally. Then Maudrin, but only if she's the one who says it.
- **All offer at once:** oh, that's a lovely thing. Give them five minutes. They pick.
- **Have changed the plan:** say the new one back in a sentence. Check the prices. Get a nod from everyone.
- **[Want to wait](play:s27-postpone):** they leave with the Key. It's a bit louder every day. No clocks, no punishment. Finish on Scene 5's question and play something else next week.
- **Want to say goodbye first:** yes. One person each, whoever's down here, or by Sending. Two lines.

**Bring it back.** The spare word. Something this table's been saying since Session 1 that isn't in any book. Use it in the next sentence you read.

**How it ends.** Somebody takes a breath. Go to **one** of the next three scenes.

### Scene 2: The Concord

**Where and why.** *All six bells rung; the Key with the party; somebody's said yes.* Under the lip, at the notch.

**Let them seat it.** With their own hand, on the table. Don't speak until it's in. Then, slowly:

> **SAY:** "You hear the six bells, each in its own voice: the dawn bell's clean light, the memory-bell's deep sorrow, the frost-bell's thin ice, the harvest's warm round sound, the storm's crack, the dream's soft lullaby. Together they form a chord that has not existed for four centuries. The chord rises and wraps around the Hush."

**After each bell's name, look at whoever rang it,** and have them say one word: what it took. Then ask the Ringer, in front of everyone, quite gently: **"Do you give it?"**

*If they say yes, and only then:* they say their last words.

> **SAY:** "The Dreamer hears it, sighs, and begins to dream more gently."

**Hum the last note.** Finally.

**What's really going on.** There's a new voice in the song. It's theirs. Everyone in the room's looking at a person they've never seen before, who's smiling at them, and then there's nobody there. They don't know why they're crying.

**Then, round the table,** everyone but the Ringer's player: **"Somebody once…"** and finish it. A thing that character did. No name. "Somebody once carried me up a hundred stairs." "Somebody once lied to a tax collector about a herring." Nobody in the world knows who. Let it go round twice.

**If they…**
- **Say no with a hand on the Key:** it comes out of the notch as easily as it went in. The chord fades. Nobody's lost a thing. Back to Scene 1.
- **[Let Corin do it](play:s27-corin-voice):** "'Three generations,' Corin says. 'It's an old song.' He touches the Key." Ask the table, not the dice. He pays it himself. Nobody in the party retires. Nobody remembers who brought the hammer.
- **[Let Maudrin do it](play:s27-maudrin-voice):** only if she offers, freely, and they agree. "'I kept it as it was,' she says. 'Let me keep it as it should be.'" The Court's got no head, and nobody can quite say who it used to be.
- **Want to write the name down first:** let them. The ink's there. It just doesn't say anything.
- **Ask if the Ringer can hear them:** "Yes." Say that one straight away.

**Bring it back.** The first thing that character ever said at your table. If you've got it written down, hand it to their player, folded.

**How it ends.** It's quiet, and it's a good quiet. Go to Scene 5.

### Scene 3: The Second Dawn

**Where and why.** *Any number of bells; the Key with the party, unstruck.* At the recess. One person kneeling.

**Count it.** Ten breaths, or ten rounds. Put a counter down for each. On each one, name a bell, or a place, or a person, from the ring ledger. After it:

> **SAY:** "You seal the Key into the Hush, unstruck, and the lullaby steadies. Above ground, the bells you rang are still ringing in the world. They are not enough to save everything, but they are enough to begin."

**Then read what's theirs,** only the ones that rang, with the name of who rang it:
- **Ossa:** the dead rest.
- **Vaer:** the sun comes up over Hallowmere, and it'll come up tomorrow.
- **Calla:** the ash fields bear, and next year too.
- **Hieme:** the thaw goes on.
- **Thrane:** the storms are out on the steppe where they belong.
- **Mirel:** the Sleepless are quiet.

**And then the ones that didn't.** Say them too. Say it plainly, in the same voice: "There's no dawn in Hallowmere." They chose with their eyes open.

**What's really going on.** Nobody's won. Nobody's paid, either. It's the ending where everyone walks out.

**If they…**
- **Haven't rung a single one:** tell them **before** the first counter. It's a stalemate. The song holds, and nothing's mended. If they still want it, it's theirs.
- **Are interrupted, with Mirel unrung:** [the Sleepless gather](#running-the-fights-session-27). Protect the minute.
- **Are interrupted by what's left of the Court:** one action a round, ten rounds. Nobody's heart's in it.
- **Stop halfway:** nothing's lost. Begin again.
- **Have Maudrin with them:** her gloves go quiet. She takes the other one off. She flexes her hand as if it's just been given back to her.

**Bring it back.** The bells' first keeper: whoever rang Ossa, on Ossa's counter, says what they forgot. Or that they can't.

**How it ends.** **Hum the last note.** It's quiet. It's a bit thin. It'll do. Go to Scene 5.

### Scene 4: The Hush Unbound

**Where and why.** *Somebody's striking it, or somebody did.* If it's a player, warn them once more, all six kinds, at Ruinous. "Do you?" Then let them bang the table.

> **SAY:** "The Hush cracks. Oum opens an eye, and the dream begins to unravel."

**The six Tolls.** Six cards, in front of whoever struck. One at a time, they turn one over and you settle it together: the **Memory** (which year?), the **Year** (twenty; show me), the **Sense,** the **Name** (which town?), the **Fear,** the **Gift** (who gets it?). Write each in the Memory ledger. If it was Maudrin, do it in six sentences. She doesn't make a sound.

**Then the light changes.** Read this very gently. It isn't a monster.

> **SAY (Oum):** "Who is ringing my lullaby? I have been dreaming a very long time. Is the dream finished? Is it time to wake?"

**[Pause.](play:s27-oum-answers) Out of character, all together.** Explain both:
- **Remake:** Oum dreams it again, from the parts it loved best. Some of what's here will be gone. **Each of you names one thing that won't be.**
- **Unmake:** the dream's over. It's kind, and it's the end. You'd have one last night, with everyone you love, and then the light. **It only happens if every one of you wants it.** If anybody isn't sure, it's Remake, and nobody has to say who.

**Vote on paper, folded, so nobody can be leaned on.** You read them alone.

**Oum.** Enormous, and interested, like a child at a window. *Asks direct questions. Never, ever lies.* **Wants** to know how it goes.

*Lines, when they talk:*
- "You're very small. I made you, didn't I? Or you made me a song."
- "Which part hurt?"
- "Was it good? I couldn't always see. I was asleep."
- "The one with the hammer is frightened. I don't want anyone to be."
- *("Are we real?")* "You're the realest thing I ever thought of."
- *("What happens if you wake?")* "Then it's morning, and you were a very good dream."
- *("Can you bring somebody back?")* "I can dream them. I don't know if that's what you mean. Is it?"
- *("Were you angry?")* "No. Did someone tell you I was angry?"

**What's really going on.** Nobody's ever asked it anything before. All anybody's done for four hundred years is sing louder.

**If they…**
- **Ask it to go back to sleep:** "I could. Not the same way. It wouldn't be the same dream." That's Remake.
- **Fight it:** there's nothing to hit. It watches them with great attention. "Is that a game?"
- **Let Maudrin argue,** if she's here: she gets one minute, honestly made: she wants the world exactly as it was. Oum listens. "But you weren't happy," it says. She doesn't decide. Nor do you.
- **[Choose Remake](play:s27-oum-remake):** "The bells ring once more, and each of you names something that will not be lost." Go round. One each, out loud. Say each one back, and add one detail that's better than it was.
- **[Choose Unmake, all of them](play:s27-oum-unmake):** "The light is soft, and everyone you loved is standing in it." Stop there. The last night is Session 28, and it's all goodbyes.

**Bring it back.** The drawing, the song, the story: whatever one of them told or sang to a sleeper along the way. Oum knows it. "I liked that one."

**How it ends.** The bells, or the light. **Hum the last note,** and let Oum join in.

### Scene 5: The first morning

**Where and why.** All endings. Up the stairs or up the pit. Coming up is free.

*The Concord, the Second Dawn or a Remake:*

> **SAY:** "Sela Pask's on the top step with a lamp, where you left her. She looks at your faces. She doesn't ask. She blows the lamp out, because, look. You don't need it."

**[Sing the verse](play:s27-release-choir),** if they've got it and Ossa's rung. They only have to mean it, for one dead person, by name.

> **SAY:** "Far away, under a lake so still it holds the sky, a woman sings her own name, and stops singing."

*(If they never learned it, Mother Sallow can rebuild it from the ledger. It can wait for Session 28.)*

**[That night, if they'd lost their dreams](play:s27-dreams-return):**

> **SAY:** "That night, for the first time in weeks, you dream."

Ask each player: **"What of?"** Ten words. This is often the best minute of the campaign.

**The other three ways it can go:**
- **[The Empty Choir](play:s27-empty-choir),** only because they all said they'd finished fighting. "The Hush falls quiet again, not because you saved it, but because the Hushmen have sealed the stairs. The places you changed still bear your mark. Elsewhere, the collectors return to their rounds." Then say what they changed that's still changed: the thaw, the storms, the quiet Sleepless. Dreams stay lost. Dawns and harvests run out when they run out. Ask if they're sure. A crew, the Choir or the Stilled would still come for them.
- **[The rescue chapter](play:s27-rescue-chapter),** if the Court's got the Key and they're still fighting. "The Court's sealed stairs are a vault of grey stone. Somewhere inside is the Key." Make it a whole session: [one way in](play:any-key-back-from-court) (Ansel's schedule, the Stilled's tunnel, the Choir by water, a Stormborn crew over the top), **one** thing that goes wrong, and one person on the Court's side who lets them past. When it works, the Key's theirs, and you're back at Session 26, Scene 4.
- **They waited:** breakfast. Somebody makes it. The hill's humming.

**What's really going on.** It's a morning. They'd forgotten what those are like.

**If they…**
- **Ask what happens to somebody they love:** next time. They'll see them. Promise it.
- **Want to know if it was right:** nobody's going to tell them. Ilam says, "Well. It's done," and hands them some bread.
- **Can't remember who they're missing** (the Concord): that's a feeling. Let them have it. There's one more cup on the table than there are people.
- **Go looking for Maudrin:** she's sitting on the hill with her bare hands in the grass.

**Bring it back.** The lamps. Yenna's, the camp's, the ones they've left burning in every window since Session 1. Down the hill somebody's going along putting them out, one by one, because it's light.

**How it ends.** Ask: **"What will survive?"** One answer each. Then stop.

### Running the fights (Session 27)

**There's one, and only if they're sealing the Key and Mirel never rang.** It's a minute long. They don't have to win it. They have to not stop.

#### The sealing minute

*Seven Sleepless (AC 13, 67 HP). Lighter: five. Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing and Psychic damage.*

- **Setup:** one character's on their knees at the recess with the Key, using their action every round. The rest are round them. The Sleepless come up through the floor, thirty feet out.
- **What happens:** they're made of what the **sealer's** afraid of. Ask that player for three things, and use them. They go for the sealer, every turn, unless somebody's in the way.
- **A Sleepless's turn:** a gaze (30 feet, Wisdom DC 13, 10 psychic and Frightened), or a touch (+6, 16 psychic, and their Hit Point maximum drops).
- **The count:** put a counter down at the end of each of the sealer's turns. **If they skip a round or drop to 0, it starts again,** with them or with somebody else.
- **Being Frightened doesn't stop it.** They can seal with their eyes shut.
- **What helps:** standing in the gaze's way; bright light; saying out loud what one's made of (an action, no roll: that one hesitates for a turn); **humming.** If somebody from the Cult's here, or a player hums it all the way through at the table, the lot of them stop and listen, and fade.
- **Who to worry about:** whoever's got the fewest Hit Points next to the sealer. Maximum Hit Points come back after a Long Rest; say so.
- **When it ends:** ten counters. They go out like candles.
- **Scale on the fly:** easier, the count carries on when someone else takes over. Harder, two of them were never afraid of anything until now.
- **Non-lethal:** the Sleepless don't kill a sealer. They sit down on top of them and keep them company. It's worse.

#### What's left of the Court

*Only if a fight's still on from last time. Use what's standing; no new arrivals.*

- **What happens:** they can see somebody sealing it. Half of them have stopped to watch. A Sergeant says, "Let them."
- **When it ends:** by the fifth counter, whatever happens.

### Pacing (Session 27)

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:10 | Recap; the last ordinary thing |
| 0:10 to 0:40 | Scene 1: once more round; a word in the kitchen |
| 0:40 to 1:40 | Scene 2, 3 **or** 4 |
| 1:40 to 1:55 | A break. A long one. |
| 1:55 to 2:40 | Scene 5: the first morning; the verse; dreams |
| 2:40 to 2:55 | The question |

- **Where to break:** straight after the last note. Nobody'll want to talk for a bit anyway.
- **Running long:** let it. Skip the verse; it's in Session 28.
- **Running short:** start Session 28 tonight, with the ferry-dock.
- **If you need to stop early:** stop on the last note. It's the end of something.

### If you get stuck (Session 27)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **Somebody's allowed to laugh.** Have Corin, or Ilam, or Sela sneeze at the wrong moment.
2. **The bell hums one person's name.** Just to see.
3. **Ask, "What's your character's hand doing?"** It always works.

**If they want a fifth ending:** check three things. Is the Key struck, sealed, seated, or theirs? Did anyone pay who didn't choose to? Is it more than they rang for? If it passes, let them have it.

**If somebody's crying:** that's fine. Ask if they want to stop. Usually they don't.

**If somebody wants Unmake and others don't:** it's Remake. They get to name the thing that survives first.

**If the Ringer's player regrets it next week:** in the story, a Toll doesn't come back. At your table, people matter more than rules. Talk to them, and fix it together.

**Names, if you need one** (cross one off when you use it): Juniper, Sorley, Brock, Yarrow.

### End of session 27

**The closing question:** "What will survive?" Then: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** the ending; Oum's answer; the verse; dreams.
- **World-state facts to check:** Ysh (concord, sealed or struck), the Tuning Key, Oum, resistance, the Stormwall, the release verse, the Drowned Choir, dreams, Corin, Maudrin.
- **The Memory ledger:** all six Tolls, if it was struck. The Great Toll, if it was given.
- **What each player said would survive,** in their own words. You'll need it next time.
- **Their dreams.** All of them.

**Rewards:**
- **The world,** more or less.
- **A name nobody knows,** and a feeling.
- **Dreams.**
- **Heroic Inspiration:** to the table. They can spend it on anything, at any time, in any game.

## Table card

**Session 27 · The Four Paths** · four characters, level 11 · end on **"What will survive?"** · first, check Ysh, the Key, resistance, the ring ledger, the Ringer (asked in private), Mirel, dreams, the verse

| Who | Voice and habit | Wants | First words |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Oum** | Huge, curious, never lies | To know how it goes | "Who is ringing my lullaby?" |
| **The Hush** | Your own voice | Somebody to sing it | "Ready when you are." |
| **Corin** | Not humming, for once | To be let | "Three generations. It's an old song." |
| **Maudrin** | Bare hands | To be useful | "Let me keep it as it should be." |
| **Sela** | Hoarse; top step; a lamp | To see their faces | *(Blows it out.)* |

**Ask again first.** A no costs nothing, at any moment before it's done.

**Concord** (six rung, Key with party, unstruck): seat it; read the chord; each ringer says what it took; "Do you give it?"; last words; "…begins to dream more gently." Then round the table: **"Somebody once…"** Corin (ally) or Maudrin (offers freely) can be the voice instead.

**Second Dawn:** ten counts at the recess, **an action a round by one character;** skip one and it restarts. Read back only what was rung (Ossa dead rest, Vaer dawns, Calla harvests, Hieme thaw, Thrane storms, Mirel quiet), then what wasn't. None rung: stalemate, say so first. *Mirel unrung:* **seven Sleepless** (AC 13, 67 HP, gaze Wisdom DC 13, touch +6 16); humming ends it.

**Unbound:** warn; strike; six cards at Ruinous; Oum's question; **pause.** Folded votes. **Unmake only if all agree;** otherwise **Remake,** one thing each. Oum never lies.

**Empty Choir:** only if they all chose to stop. **Court has the Key, still fighting:** the rescue chapter. **Wait:** no penalty.

**Afterwards:** the verse (Ossa rung); **"That night… you dream." "What of?"**
**Break** after the last note.

plays.title: They return to Pellmoor
plays.why: The story began on a dock with a girl and a humming bundle.
plays.readAloud: The Mere is so still the ships look painted on it, as always. On the oldest dock, a young woman in a ferry coat that finally fits her is counting the masts.
plays.response: Two NPC scenes and a closing question. Ila (if not Tithed; the ila flag tells you) keeps the ledger and may become the ferry-folk's Ringer; Mother Sallow reads Davin's name aloud at last if Ossa rang; Brother Eld confesses, leaves, or is gone (check the eld flag). Ansel retires to the coast; Tobias Quill is Tithed by his own office, or is a friend. Then the Landing: Brannagh, Sela, Venn. Close on: "Who keeps the ledger now?"
plays.consequence: Act I's threads close.
plays.tells: Players ask what became of Ila and Mother Sallow.
plays.keywords: pellmoor, return, ila, mother sallow, epilogue, ledger, home

plays.title: They see the Stormwall open
plays.why: If Thrane rang and the ending stabilised it, Corvane is no longer hidden.
plays.readAloud: From the Pellmouth you can see it: where the wall of storm stood for four hundred years there is only weather now, grey and ordinary, and beyond it a sail, and another, and another.
plays.response: Over a few years the Stormwall thins to ordinary sea. The Landing Charter can't hold; ships go wherever they like. Ask each player what their character makes of a Corvane joined to the world: a Stormborn going home, a Bellfolk seeing the sea for the first time, a Lander staying for good.
plays.consequence: Corvane joins the Forgotten Realms in earnest.
plays.tells: Players ask what happens to the ships and the trade now.
plays.later: A hook for a next campaign: the Realms come to Corvane, and not all of them are friendly.
plays.keywords: stormwall, open, sea, ships, faerun, world, future, trade

plays.title: They decide who rules the Ninefold Shore
plays.why: With Maudrin gone or beaten, the Court, the Dawn Order and the Ironhorn all move.
plays.readAloud: Hallowmere’s terraces are full of people looking up, waiting to be told who speaks for them now.
plays.response: Rook (if she won the duel and lives) leads a restored Dawn Order; Tristan Vesk wants the Chancellor's chair; Kessa, if alive, wants the Tithe-taxes ended on the steppe. The party's allies and promises decide who gets the party's backing. Close on: "Who will rule the Ninefold Shore?" If the party backs a claimant, run s28-chair-seated (Claim clock full) or s28-chair-contested instead.
plays.consequence: The Ninefold Shore has new rulers, chosen with the party’s weight behind someone.
plays.tells: Players ask what happens in Hallowmere.
plays.keywords: rule, court, chancellor, tristan, rook, kessa, hallowmere, future, government
