### Epilogue round (Session 30)

After the epilogue for the chosen path, and before the closing question, go round the table once. Long-running tables end this way: each player gets their character's last scene, and laughter and tears come quickly one after the other. Let both happen.

1. **Ask each player in turn:** "Where is your character a year from now? What are they doing the first time they hear a bell?" Let them say as much or as little as they like, and don't correct anything.
2. **Give each one image back.** Look at their roster notes from session zero (what they lost) and their lines in the Memory ledger. Narrate one small thing the world returns or remembers for them: a face, a song, a name read aloud.
3. **Read the Tolls aloud.** One line for each Toll paid in the campaign, in the order they were paid, in the players' own words from the Memory ledger. Then pause.
4. **Then the closing question:** "What will you ring next?"

**In Waypoint:** the [Memory ledger](go:memory-ledger) (Campaign → Party & preferences) lists every Toll in order, and the roster keeps the session-zero answers.

## Running this session (new DM guide)

*Read this once the day before. One evening, two or three: your choice. There's nothing to beat any more. You're going to visit people. Pick the ones your table loves, give each a scene, and ask a question at the end. That's all an epilogue is.*

**Contents:** [Before you start](#before-you-start-session-28) · [Key people](#key-people-tonight-session-28) · [Opening recap](#opening-recap-session-28) · [Scene 1: The grey vault](#scene-1-the-grey-vault) · [Scene 2: The oldest dock](#scene-2-the-oldest-dock) · [Scene 3: The empty chair](#scene-3-the-empty-chair) · [Scene 4: A sail, and another](#scene-4-a-sail-and-another) · [Scene 5: The last round](#scene-5-the-last-round) · [Fights](#running-the-fights-session-28) · [Pacing](#pacing-session-28) · [If you get stuck](#if-you-get-stuck-session-28) · [End of session](#end-of-session-28)

### Before you start (Session 28)

**Level:** four characters at level 11. Nobody'll check.

**First, which ending was it?** It changes what you run.
- **The Concord or the Second Dawn:** all five scenes, as they're written.
- **A Remake:** Scenes 1 to 4 in a world that's a little different, then [the rebuilt one](play:s28-remake-rebuild) in Scene 5. Whatever each player named is there, whole, in every scene.
- **An Unmake:** skip to Scene 5. [The last night](play:s28-last-night) is all there is. Nothing happens years later.
- **The Empty Choir:** Scene 2, in whispers, then [the Court rules on](play:s28-court-rules) in Scene 5.
- **They waited, or the Key's with the Court and they're still fighting:** you're not here yet.

**Then check the world state for each person, before you say a word about them:** Ila, Eld, Quill, Ansel, Rook, Haldric, Maudrin, Kessa, the lamp, Corin, Ilam and Jonah, Wren and Tessa, the jars, Pellmoor, the Stormwall, the Choir and the verse.

**How to split it:**
- **One evening:** Scene 2, Scene 3, Scene 5.
- **Two:** Scenes 1 and 2; then 3 and 5.
- **Three (28, 29 and 30):** Scenes 1 and 2; then 3 and 4; then 5, by itself, with food.

**What this session is about.** Everyone they ever helped is still alive somewhere, having a Tuesday.

**Your goals:**
- Two people each session, and a closing question.
- Say what's true. Nothing unearned gets mended, and nothing earned gets forgotten.
- Give every player the last word about their own character.
- End the last one on the question: **"What will you ring next?"** Then stop.

**Prepare:**
- **The roster notes** from session zero: what each character had lost.
- **The Memory ledger.** Every Toll, every step.
- **What they said would survive.**
- **A list of eight names,** the people your table likes best. Cross them off as you visit.
- **A candle, or a lamp.** You're going to blow it out.
- **If somebody became the bell's voice:** something for that player to do. They play everybody else. Hand them Ila, or Bet, or Kessa. And now and then, they hum.

**Rules you'll use, in plain words (D&D 2024):**
- **Nobody rolls to see whether.** If you want dice, roll to see **how well.**
- **[Jars](play:s28-return-jars):** owners who open their own get their memories back, whole. Nobody can open one for somebody else.
- **Tolls don't come back.** Nor do the stairs. Not from jars, not by Wish, not in any ending.
- **[A smashed jar](play:s28-jars-destroyed)** is gone; only a Remake could have mended it.
- **The Great Toll:** nobody remembers the name. Not one person. Don't let somebody half-remember it to be nice. It's the whole point.
- **Heroic Inspiration:** anybody who's got one, spend it now. They may add one true thing to the world.

### Opening recap (Session 28)

> **SAY:** "It's quiet. You'd forgotten how much noise being frightened makes. The morning after, you slept till noon. The morning after that, somebody asked what you wanted for breakfast, and you all looked at each other, because nobody'd asked you that in a year. *(What did you say would survive? One line each.)* And then, because there was nothing left to run from, you went to see some people."

- **Then hand it over:** "What do you have for breakfast?" It's a real question. Let it take five minutes.

*Start of Session 29:* "Back a bit, to the first autumn. Nobody's in charge of anything yet." *Start of Session 30:* "No recap. You know what happened."

### Scene 1: The grey vault

**Where and why.** Session 28, a few weeks after. *(Not in an Unmake or the Empty Choir.)* Under Hallowmere. There's a queue out of the door and up the hill.

> **SAY:** "Bet Ostrow opens a small labelled jar in the grey vault, and smells bread, and finally knows why she has cried at that smell for seventy years."

*If the jars were destroyed, read instead:* "A grey vault of broken glass." Someone's swept a path through it. Bet's come anyway. She's brought rolls.

**What's really going on.** [The Tithe's being undone, one jar at a time](play:s28-return-jars), by people who are very bad at queueing. There's no magic. There's Lysse, at a desk, with a list.

**Lysse Carrow.** Ink to the elbow. *Interrupts herself.* **Wants** it all written down in the right order this time.

*Lines:*
- "Name? No, the one you had before. Oh, I'm sorry. Take your time. I'm so sorry. *Next.*"
- "I found mine filed under nine other people. I've been nine other people. It's very tiring."
- "What do I call you, in the book? You get to choose. Nobody else has had to ask."

**Give each player one jar to hand over.** You say who's in front of them; they say what they say. Pick from:
- **Jonah Bray,** in the queue by himself with [a wooden bird.](play:s28-ilam-jonah) Ilam's outside, because he didn't want to hope in front of him. If Mara was found, she's holding the jar, and it's for both of them. Jonah looks at her face. "Oh," he says. "*That's* who that is."
- **A Hushman** who doesn't know whether he's allowed. It's his wife's name.
- **Tessa Caddock,** if she's free, with her mother a step behind. Wren's sewn the sleeve back on, and isn't sure about the rest of it. Tessa takes her hand or doesn't. **Ask the table what they think she does.**
- **Tobias Quill,** if he was Tithed by his own office. Pale, polite, no idea who they are. "Forgive me. Have we met? I've a form, if so." His jar's right there. **They can give it to him.** Or not. Nobody'd know.
- **An empty shelf,** with a label in the Coster's hand: *shipped.* That's for another day.

**If they…**
- **Look for their own Tolls:** there's no jar. There never was one. Lysse is the only person who says it properly: "I can't find it. I looked twice. I'm going to leave a page."
- **Ask about [those who paid the stairs](play:s28-stairs-payers):** Ilam says nothing about a morning he cannot remember. Each ally who went down says one thing that's gone soft at the edges. Let the players answer.
- **Meet Yara Thenn:** selling tools for opening jars. She's got a glass-flower on the counter, not for sale. If somebody's kind, she opens it, and the whole room hears Teo laugh, once. Then it's a flower.
- **Want to open one that isn't theirs:** it won't.

**Bring it back.** The bread. Every bit of it, since Session 4.

**How it ends.** Bet's got the bell now, a small one. She's nine years old, and it's a baking morning. She rings it, and everybody in the queue looks up.

### Scene 2: The oldest dock

**Where and why.** Session 28. Three or four years on. Say so.

> **SAY:** "The Mere is so still the ships look painted on it, as always. On the oldest dock, a young woman in a ferry coat that finally fits her is counting the masts."

**Stop. Let one of them speak first.** She doesn't turn round. She says, "Are you here for the Heart, or for the bell?"

**What's really going on.** [It's Ila.](play:s28-ledger) She's the ferry-folk's Ringer, or near enough, and she's keeping the ledger. *If she was Tithed:* she's here, and she's counting, and doesn't know why she likes it; if they brought her jar, she's got it in her pocket. It's hers to open. *If she travelled with them:* she's been home a week, and she's bossy about it.

**Ila Harrow.** Seventeen or so. *Blunt, flat. Counts when she's nervous; she's not nervous.* **Wants** to show them something.

*Lines:*
- "You got old. I'm allowed to say that. I've been keeping track."
- "I've got a page for everybody. There's one for people who aren't anybody any more, as well. I don't know who it's for. I just thought there ought to be one."
- "Don't cry on it, it's ink."

**Mother Sallow,** dry as ever, on an upturned boat, with her pipe unlit. If Ossa rang, she reads a name out of the ledger, aloud, over the water. "Davin Sallow. Net-maker. He was tall." *She can see his face.* Then, if the verse was never sung, she sings the last line of it, with Ila, and far out something stops being sad.

**If they…**
- **[Brought Nessa,](play:s28-ila-nessa)** or told her, or Calla rang and word got about: "A woman at the ferry-dock stops, mid-step." Say nothing. Let Ila count something. She gets to four.
- **Ask for Brother Eld:** *still here:* he's on the chapel steps with the missing page, and today he reads it out, to everybody, with his own name at the bottom. *Forgiven:* he runs the school. *Fled or gone:* there's a letter, and it's only the list. *Dead:* Sallow's put him in the book. "He's a name like anyone."
- **Ask for Ansel:** he's bought a house on the coast. It's damp, and he's thrilled. He's copied the whole ledger from memory, "for insurance."
- **Ask for Quill:** he helps at the Landing House, badly, if he was a friend.
- **Go to the Memory Shore:** Session 1's stone, with one of their names on it. The date's still six years off. Sallow's scratched it out. "It remembers what hasn't happened yet," she says. "It can be *told.*"
- **Look for the Tidewarden:** he's bringing the last of them in. He ships his oar. It's stopped dripping.
- **Came here in the Empty Choir:** it's the same dock, at night, with the door shut. She's keeping the ledger under the floor. She says, "I'm not stopping." Neither's anyone.

**Bring it back.** Her first question. And then what they answered, in Session 1, word for word if you've got it.

**How it ends.** She closes the book and holds it out, in case somebody'd like to carry it for a bit. Ask: **"Who keeps the ledger now?"**

### Scene 3: The empty chair

**Where and why.** Session 29. The first autumn. Hallowmere, the top terrace. Nobody's sitting in it.

> **SAY:** "Hallowmere's terraces are full of people looking up, waiting to be told who speaks for them now."

**What's really going on.** [Somebody's got to.](play:s28-who-rules) Three people have a claim, one of them wants it, and everyone's looking at the party, because it's easier. **They don't have to choose. They do have to say something.**

**Who's here:**
- **[Captain Rook](play:s28-haldric-rook),** if she's alive. If she won the duel, half the city'd follow her. *Clipped. "We" for "I," till tonight.* "We'd want… no. *I'd* want it looked after. I don't want to be looked at." If she lost, she's on the edge of the crowd in somebody else's coat.
- **[Tristan Vesk](play:s28-tristan-chair),** if Maudrin's gone. "Tristan Vesk sits in the chair a little too carefully." He stands straight back up again. *Soft. Writes it down.* "I'm not her. I know you'd rather I was worse. I'd do the drains."
- **Thane Kessa,** if he's alive, with rain on him. *Big. "Rider."* "End the Tithe-tax on my grass and you can put a goat in it."
- **The Blanks,** if they were freed, right at the front. Nobody's asked them. If a player does, it goes very quiet, and one says, "Could it be a *bench?*"

**Maudrin.**
- **[Captured](play:s28-maudrin-trial):** "She sits in the Dawn Order's hall in plain grey." No gloves. The party speaks last. Trial, exile, or her own office's Tithe: say all three out loud and let the table choose. She'll answer anything. She doesn't ask for anything.
- **[Exiled](play:s28-maudrin-exile):** "A ship at the Pellmouth." She carries her own bag. She stops next to whoever answered her on the Tor, and says their name.
- **Dead:** Haldric's got the letters. He reads one out. It's about watching a small boy learn to fence, from across a hall.
- **The bell's voice:** nobody can remember who sat there. There's a dove-grey glove on the arm of the chair. It seems a shame to move it.

**If they…**
- **Back somebody:** it's them. Ask what the party wants in return. They get it.
- **Want it themselves:** somebody puts a cushion on it. Good luck.
- **Want nobody:** then it's the bench. It's a mess, and it works on alternate weekdays.
- **Ask for Haldric:** *turned:* at the back, plain cloak, next to Rook. *Disgraced:* outside, holding horses, and being quite good at it. He knows, or he's just found out. He asks one of them, "What's one supposed to *call* her?"
- **Ask for Isolde:** auctioning the Court's secrets from a balcony, "darling," or in a very comfortable cell.
- **Ask for Kessa's [last storm](play:s28-kessa-storm):** if the table wants it. "He rides out into the rain." His clans go with him as far as the ridge. Give it a minute's quiet. Roll the thunder yourself, on the table.
- **Ask for Yenna:** [the lamp](play:s28-yenna-lamp) hangs on a pole outside her tent, and she laughs, and it's *his* laugh. Everybody who met the old man down the Old Works knows it.

**Bring it back.** A promise. Somewhere in your notes there's one they made, and forgot. Somebody on the terrace hasn't. It's being kept, right now, without them.

**How it ends.** Ask: **"Who will rule the Ninefold Shore?"**

### Scene 4: A sail, and another

**Where and why.** Session 29, or the start of 30. *Only if Thrane rang, and it isn't an Unmake.* The Pellmouth, some years on.

> **SAY:** "From the Pellmouth you can see it: where the wall of storm stood for four hundred years there is only weather now, grey and ordinary, and beyond it a sail, and another, and another."

**What's really going on.** [The Stormwall's thinning.](play:s28-new-world) [The fleets are coming](play:s28-landing-fleets): three in a month. The Charter can't hold. Corvane's just a place, now, on a map, next to other places. Some of them are lovely.

**Brannagh Wick,** counting. *"Lad."* "Thirty-one. Thirty-two. I'm going to need a bigger string."

**Ask each player:** "What does your character make of it?" A Stormborn going home. Somebody who's never seen a wave. A Lander who's decided to stay.

**If they…**
- **Go and look:** it's just the sea. That's extraordinary.
- **Meet Master Venn:** he's got nothing left to sell; people have stopped. He's taken up clocks. His own's ticking. "Friend! Listen!"
- **Go to [Corin's workshop](play:s28-corin-epilogue),** on the way: "The workshop is quiet." He's asleep in a chair. Peal's on his feet. Or there's nobody, and all the bells on the wall ring a bit when you come in, and nobody knows who hung them.
- **Meet Imber:** he's preaching to six people and a dog in a wood that's dripping. He gets to the end. "That's all," he says, astonished. "That's the end of it."
- **Find the Librarian:** it's open on a step, in the sun. **It reads out their names.** Each of them, whole. (It leaves a space, the length of a name, if somebody became the voice.) Then it closes, and it's a book.
- **Didn't ring Thrane:** the wall's still there. Kessa, or whoever rides after him, will see to it. Skip the scene.

**Bring it back.** The boat they came in on.

**How it ends.** A ship's hailing the Pellmouth, in a language nobody here's ever heard. Somebody should answer.

### Scene 5: The last round

**Where and why.** Session 30. Find your ending:

**The Concord, or the Second Dawn.** They're all in one room, or at one fire. Ask them where. Then [the Epilogue round](#epilogue-round-session-30), just above this guide: it's four steps, and it does the work.

**A Remake.**

> **SAY:** "A city of grey stone grows gold at the edges."

[One scene each](play:s28-remake-rebuild), built round what they named. Start every one with the thing, right there, in somebody's hand. Then the Epilogue round.

**An Unmake.**

> **SAY:** "The light is soft on the water, and everyone you loved is standing in it."

[One goodbye each.](play:s28-last-night) Who to? Play the other person, very simply. Don't be clever. No years later. **The last line belongs to the table:** ask them to write it together, and have the quietest person read it. Skip the Epilogue round; read the Tolls aloud, then stop.

**The Empty Choir.**

> **SAY:** "Dawn never fully comes to Hallowmere."

[Then say what's still changed,](play:s28-court-rules) all of it, slowly. Somebody's keeping a ledger under a floor. Ask: "Where are you hiding?" Then the Epilogue round, quietly.

**If somebody became the voice:** in the Epilogue round their player goes last. Everyone else says what they're doing the first time they hear a bell, a year on. Then that player hums. It's their turn.

**Read the Tolls aloud,** in order, in their words. It's in the ledger. Pause after each. Don't hurry because it's long. It's supposed to be long.

**What's really going on.** You've been sitting round a table with these people for a year. That's the thing that survived.

**If they…**
- **Can't think what to say:** "What's in your character's pockets?" That'll do it.
- **Make a joke:** wonderful. Leave it in.
- **Want to talk as themselves:** yes. That's what the end of this one's for.

**Bring it back.** The very first dice roll of the campaign. Who made it? What for?

**How it ends.** Light the lamp. Hum the lullaby once through, and leave the last note for them. Ask: **"What will you ring next?"** Let everyone answer. Blow it out. Then stop.

### Running the fights (Session 28)

**There aren't any.** Nobody's left who wants one.

#### If somebody starts one anyway

*Use a Knight (AC 18, 52 HP) or a Hushman (AC 12, 32 HP), and only until somebody sits down.*

- **Setup:** a drunk, a duel for old times' sake, a bar.
- **What happens:** one round. Everybody's level 11. It's over, and someone's buying.
- **When it ends:** when the first person laughs.
- **Non-lethal:** all of it.

### Pacing (Session 28)

*Each of the three evenings goes the same way.*

| Time | What's happening |
|---|---|
| 0:00 to 0:15 | A recap, and breakfast |
| 0:15 to 1:05 | The first person, and whoever else they want to see |
| 1:05 to 1:20 | A break, and cake |
| 1:20 to 2:10 | The second person |
| 2:10 to 2:30 | Loose ends: one line each, as fast as you like |
| 2:30 to 2:45 | The closing question |

- **Where to break:** between the two people, while everybody's still smiling.
- **Running long:** "And what happened to…?" Answer in a sentence. People love a sentence.
- **Running short:** ask who they haven't seen. There's always somebody.
- **If you need to stop early:** ask the closing question anyway. It always works.

### If you get stuck (Session 28)

**Three quick moves:**
1. **Somebody comes in with a plate.** Who is it?
2. **A bell rings, somewhere, for no reason.** Everybody looks up, and it's all right.
3. **Ask a player, "Who'd be annoyed if we didn't visit them?"**

**If they ask for someone dead:** there's a stone, or a song, or a child with the same nose.

**If it gets too sad:** Venn's clock. Garrow's laugh. The goat.

**If two of them remember it differently:** they're both right. Write down both.

**If they want to keep playing:** there's a ship hailing the Pellmouth. There are jars across the sea. Say, "Not tonight," and grin.

**Names, for anyone new** (cross one off when you use it): Dillon, Fenwick, Hewett, Lettice, Pascoe, Ursel.

### End of session 28

**The closing questions:** Session 28, "Who keeps the ledger now?" Session 29, "Who will rule the Ninefold Shore?" Session 30, "What will you ring next?" Then, the very last time: "Let's each say one thing we'll remember."

**Record in Waypoint:**
- **Plays that happened:** every visit.
- **World-state facts to check:** the Tithe jars, Chancellor Maudrin Vesk, Thane Oru Kessa, the Stormwall, Pellmoor Landing, the Drowned Choir.
- **Who's in the chair,** or on the bench.
- **Each character's last scene,** in their player's own words. Then mark the last session played.

**Rewards:**
- **A page each,** in Ila's book.
- **Breakfast.**
- **The next one.** Whoever wants to run it, hand them this screen.

## Table card

**Sessions 28 to 30 · Aftermath** · four characters, level 11 · end on **"Who keeps the ledger now?"**, **"Who will rule the Ninefold Shore?"**, **"What will you ring next?"** · first, check which ending it was, then each person's state

| Who | Voice and habit | Wants | First words |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ila** | Blunt, flat; counts things | To show them a page | "Are you here for the Heart, or for the bell?" |
| **Sallow** | Dry, short; unlit pipe | To say a name | "Davin Sallow. Net-maker. He was tall." |
| **Lysse** | Interrupts herself; ink | It written down right | "Name? No, the one you had before." |
| **Rook** | Clipped; says "I" | Not to be looked at | "We'd want… no. *I'd* want." |
| **Tristan** | Soft; writes things down | The chair, politely | "I'd do the drains." |
| **Kessa** (he) | Big laugh; "rider" | The tax gone, and rain | "You can put a goat in it." |

**Which ending?** *Concord, Second Dawn:* everything. *Remake:* everything, plus what they named. *Unmake:* only the last night; one goodbye each; nothing later. *Empty Choir:* the dock at night, then the Court rules on.

**Split:** one evening, Scenes 2, 3, 5. Two: 1 and 2; 3 and 5. Three: 1 and 2; 3 and 4; 5.

**True things:** owners open their own jars. Tolls and stairs never come back. Smashed jars are gone. **Nobody remembers the voice's name.** Dawn, bread, thaw, storms, sleep, the dead: only where they rang.

**Vault:** a jar each (Jonah, Tessa, a Hushman, Quill). **Dock** (three or four years on): Ila; Sallow; Eld's page; Nessa if Calla rang; the stone. **Chair** (the first autumn): Rook, Tristan, Kessa, the Blanks; Maudrin's trial. **Sails:** only if Thrane rang.

**Last round:** the Epilogue round; Tolls aloud, in order; the voice's player goes last, and hums. Light the lamp, leave them the last note, ask, blow it out.

**Break** between the two people.

page.title: CORVANE IN THE REALMS (v6 canon)
page.aliases: Forgotten Realms, Faerun, Faerûn, Sword Coast, Trackless Sea, Stormborn, Loudfolk, revision 6
page.body:
*Revision 6 canon. Where this page and v5 disagree, this page wins. The Canon Sheet (3.3) still governs every date and family line it lists.*

**Where Corvane is.** Corvane is a continent called **Hesk**, far out in the Trackless Sea beyond the last Sword Coast charts, part of the Forgotten Realms. A permanent band of storm circles it at sea, thirty to sixty miles deep: Faerûnian sailors call it **the Stormwall**, Corvanese who know of it call it **Thrane's Hem**. For four centuries no ship crossed it. Sword Coast sailors kept a legend of "the Ringing Land" west of the world; Candlekeep holds one water-stained portolan labelled *the Belled Coast*.

**DM truth: what the Stormwall is.** When Thrane fell silent on the Quiet Night, its storms did not end. They lost their shepherd and were pushed outward to the edge of the bells' resonance, where Ysh's lullaby stops. That is why no storm has crossed Brassfall in four hundred years: every storm Corvane should have had is in the Wall. Nobody knows this. Corin Aldeth suspects it; Edda Thorne's Notes imply it in one line ("Thrane's weather will go to the rim and wait").

**Before the Silence.** A few Faerûnian ships reached Corvane before the Quiet Night. Some of the Stilled in Glassreach are those sailors, frozen in 2 SS in Sword Coast clothes four centuries out of fashion.

**The Wrongweather (382 SS / 1462 DR).** The Ironhorn raid broke Old Garrow's sealed shafts. The dead lightning that poured out called to the storms at the rim, and for one night a storm tore up the river Pell onto the Mute Mere, the first weather the Mere had seen in 380 years. Davin Sallow drowned in it. When it passed it left a calm channel through the Wall: **the Seam**. At dawn the battered Baldur's Gate cog *Gull's Wager* drifted onto the Mere.

**Thirty years of contact.** Ilse Vesk's **Landing Charter** (384 SS) made Pellmoor the only lawful landing. Foreigners trade freely there but need a Court **writ of passage** to travel inland. Traffic has grown from one ship a year to forty or sixty a season. In come gold and silver, steel, paper, books, spices, wine, lenses and Lantanese clockwork (the Landing House removes every chime). Out go bottled memories (the richest export by far), glass-flowers, memory-pearls, reed-dye, bone-bound books and Ironhorn horses. Storm-stones and bronze are banned exports and smuggled anyway.

**Who is here.** The Vennmark Coster of Athkatla (Master Orsolo Venn), the Waterdhavian Corvane Venture, Baldurian factors, Lantanese gnome tinkers, Mirabar dwarves who want bronze, two quiet Harper agents, and Zhentarim memory smugglers. Lathander's Dawn Mission, a Kelemvorite shrine-tent and Chauntea's faithful; the Ninefold Church calls them "the loud gods."

**People and words.** Corvanese call Faerûnians **Stormborn** (polite) or **Loudfolk** (rude); Faerûnians call Corvanese **Bellfolk** or **the Quiet**; settled Faerûnians are **Landers**. Corvanese are mostly human, with halfling ferry-families, dwarven mining clans in Brassfall and very few elves. Dragonborn, tieflings, orcs, goliaths, gnomes and aasimar arrived with the ships, and Corvanese stare. Corvanese speak **Hesk**; Common is Pellmoor's second tongue.

**Magic.** Spells work by the 2024 rules. In Corvane every spell hums faintly as it is cast: that hum is Tonework, and it is how the Weave sounds here. Silence-stones suppress spells under the house rule in 2.6.

**Calendar.** 412 SS = 1492 DR.

page.title: THE STORMWALL AND THE SEAM
page.aliases: Stormwall, Thrane's Hem, the Seam, Pellmouth, river Pell, Wrongweather
page.body:
- **Read-aloud:**
> **SAY:** "Ahead, the sea stands up. A wall of black cloud and white water runs from one horizon to the other, lit from inside by lightning that never stops. And in it, like a door left open, a lane of grey calm a mile wide."
- **What it is:** a permanent band of storm thirty to sixty miles deep that circles Corvane at sea. DM truth: Thrane's lost storms, waiting at the rim of the bells' resonance.
- **The Seam:** the one calm channel through it, opened by the Wrongweather of 382 SS, in line with the mouth of the river Pell. A mile or two wide; it drifts with the seasons. Crossing takes about a day with a pilot who knows its moods.
- **The river Pell:** about forty miles from the Pellmouth inland to the Mute Mere. Two days by river.
- **Dangers:** drifting off the Seam. Ships that do are rarely seen again; pilots who come back describe a warm grey light at the storm's heart (see 11.7, the Edge of the Dream).
- **If Thrane rings:** the storms come home to Brassfall. For a season the Seam widens into a broad road and new fleets arrive within a month. If an ending stabilises Thrane (the Concord, or the Second Dawn with Thrane rung), the Stormwall thins to ordinary sea weather over a few years and Corvane joins the world.
- **Voyage:** about six weeks from Baldur's Gate or Waterdeep. Sailing season is spring (Ches) to early autumn (Eleint).

page.title: MEMORY AS MONEY
page.aliases: memory currency, keep, keeps, mote, motes, heartkeep, knowing, reckoner, gilding, exchange rate, coin, gold
page.body:
Corvane traded memories long before the ships came. The Court's Tithe made it a habit and the Reckoners made it a currency. Gold arrived thirty years ago and is winning, slowly.

**How it works**
1. **Drawing.** A memory can be drawn out of a person only with their consent, by a Court-licensed **Reckoner** with a tuning fork and a small stoppered vial of Mere-glass. It takes about a minute and feels like forgetting a word on the tip of your tongue, then not minding. Drawing without a licence is *leeching*, a crime.
2. **Keeps.** A drawn, sealed memory is a **keep**: a vial of faintly luminous mist that hums one low note when held. Reckoners grade it by **weight** (how much feeling it holds) and stamp the wax. The content stays private unless someone opens it.
3. **Keeps circulate sealed,** passed hand to hand like banknotes. Their value rests on two facts: someone will always pay to witness one, and its owner can always redeem it.
4. **Opening.** If the original owner opens a keep, the memory returns whole. Anyone else *witnesses* it, as a guest in someone else's day, without acquiring the owner's identity. Each stranger's witnessing fades it; after three it is a grey, spent vial.
5. **What cannot be drawn:** skills, spells, languages, proficiencies, anything a character can do. "You can sell the day you learned to swim, but never the swimming." Nobody can sell someone else's memory.
6. **Blanks** are people who sold or Tithed so many heavy memories that they no longer recognise their own families.

| Weight | What it holds | Worth at Pellmoor | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Mote** | A passing memory: last Ossday's supper, a stranger's coat | about 1 sp | Grey wax. Small change. |
| **Keep** | A memory with feeling: a good afternoon, a small win | about 1 gp (floats daily) | Plain wax. The everyday coin. |
| **Heartkeep** | A defining memory: a parent's face, a wedding day | 25 to 100 gp or more | Red wax. The Tithe prefers them. |
| **Knowing** | Knowledge: a route, a recipe, a password, a face | by usefulness | Blue wax. The seller loses the knowledge. |

**Gold, and why the Court hates it.** Old Corvanese coin was iron "ticks" and Court scrip; bronze is bell-metal. Gold cannot be Tithed, cannot fade, cannot be Reckoned. At Pellmoor nearly every stall takes either. **Court taxes on Corvanese subjects must be paid in memory; foreigners pay the landing due in gold.** Paying a local's Tithe in gold is **gilding**: illegal and common. A keep fetches about 1 gp 2 sp at Pellmoor and about 8 sp in Hallowmere. The Hallowmere gate's courtesy memory is a registration, not a fee, and the clerk refuses gold.

**Table rules (2024)**
- A character may pay in memory wherever coin is accepted in Corvane. The player chooses the memory and writes one line in the [Memory ledger](go:memory-ledger) (Campaign → Party & preferences). The DM never chooses it.
- A Reckoner buys memories at the posted rate less a 10 percent fee.
- Motes and keeps have no mechanical effect. When a character sells a heartkeep, the player rewrites one thing the memory held up (a belief, a bond, a fear). It never removes player knowledge or control of the character.
- The DM may award **Heroic Inspiration** when a character gives a memory freely to someone who needs it.
- Once, a character who witnesses a Knowing keep has Advantage on one ability check that knowledge plainly helps.
- Keep the kinds apart: a **Toll** can never be bought back; a **Tithe** can be redeemed from its jar; a **trade** is a keep; **Mere Memories** are borrowed; **eel bites** return after a long rest; **stairs** losses follow the stairs' rule.

page.title: THE LANDING (Foreign traders at Pellmoor)
page.aliases: Vennmark Coster, Corvane Venture, Harpers, Zhentarim, Landers, foreign traders, merchants
page.body:
- **Wants:** Profit, above all from bottled memories. An end to the Landing Charter's limits (or, for the Coster, an exclusive export licence). Safe passage through the Seam.
- **Fears:** The Court closing the Seam to them. A rival house winning the Court's favour. The Wall moving.
- **Methods:** Gold, credit, gifts to officials, hiring ferry-folk pilots, and buying memories in bulk.
- **Ideal:** *Prosperity.*
- **Members:** the Vennmark Coster of Athkatla (Master Orsolo Venn; the largest memory exporter), the Waterdhavian Corvane Venture (cautious, respectable), Baldurian factors, Lantanese tinkers, Mirabar dwarves after bronze. In the shadows: two Harper agents who distrust the Tithe, and a Zhentarim smuggling ring on Strangers' Row.
- **Secret:** The Coster buys "surplus" Tithed memories from the Court and ships them to Faerûn. The Tithe-Ledger has an EXPORT — VENNMARK column. Some Blanks' memories are in Athkatla.
- **How They React:** Warmly to customers, coldly to anyone who costs them money. They will not fight the Court, and they will not fight for it.
- **Clock move (at 6):** the Coster wins an export licence, a new fleet arrives, or a Zhentarim memory-smuggling ring is exposed.

page.title: 26. PILOT-MISTRESS BRANNAGH WICK
page.body:
- **Role:** Runs the Pilots' Hall on the Quays. Every ship that crosses the drowned town does it with one of her pilots. Tam Harrow was one of them.
- **Look:** Ferry-folk, about 60. Short, wind-cracked hands, a coil of sounding-line always over one shoulder.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A short, weather-beaten woman of about sixty stands at the far end of the Pilots' Hall with a coil of sounding-line over one shoulder. She's counting under her breath, and she doesn't stop when you come in."
- **Voice:** Gruff. Counts tides out loud. Calls every ship "she" and every captain "lad."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "...four, five, slack on six. Right. Who's asking, and what ship are they off?"
  - *Asked about Tam Harrow:* "Tam was the best pilot I had. Knew every drowned street under this harbour by its old name. Don't tell me he drowned on a flat-calm night, lad."
  - *Asked about piloting:* "Every ship out of this Mere goes with one of mine, or she goes onto the rooftops. Nobody leaves without my say."
  - *If the players are stuck (and Ila trusts them):* "Tam took his boat out the night he died. No cargo, no ship to pilot. I told the Landing House nothing. He was headed for the old belfry, out where it's deep. Ask the girl if he ever said why."
  - *Asked about Venn's ship:* "The Heron? Pretty hull. She sails when I say. I can find a reason to keep her a day, if you give me a reason."
  - *If they break their word:* "You broke your word on my water. Don't ask me for a pilot again."
- **Wants:** The Hall kept independent of the Court and the trading houses. Ila safe.
- **Secret:** Tam took his boat out the night he died with no cargo and no ship to pilot, which no pilot does. She told the Landing House nothing. She thinks he was going to the Ossa Belfry, and she is right.
- **2024 stat block:** Scout (CR 1/2).
- **How She Reacts:** Trusts people who keep their word on the water. Will refuse a pilot to any ship she has a reason to stop, and every ship needs one to leave the Mere.

page.title: 27. RECKONER SELA MAUNT
page.body:
- **Role:** Court-licensed memory assayer at the Reckoning House on the Tally. The person who explains memory money to newcomers.
- **Look:** Corvanese, 40s. Grey apron, three tuning forks in a breast pocket, reading lenses bought from a Lantanese tinker.
- **First look (read aloud):** "Behind a counter scored with fine notches, a tired woman in a gray apron peers through a jeweller's lens at a small sealed jar. Three tuning forks stick up from her breast pocket. She taps one on the counter, listens, and writes something down."
- **Voice:** Precise, kind, slightly tired. Taps a fork against the counter when she thinks.
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "Weighing or selling? Either way, set it on the counter and don't shake it."
  - *Explaining memory money:* "A mote's a passing thing. A keep's a proper memory, sealed. A heartkeep's the kind you'd cry to lose: red wax, priced by appraisal, love."
  - *Asked about paying a Tithe in gold:* "Some folk try to pay the Court in gold. The Court doesn't care for it. I don't know anything about it, and neither do you."
  - *Shown a forged keep:* "Hear that? Rings flat. Somebody sealed a dream in there and called it a memory."
  - *If they show her the Heart:* "Put that away. Now. Don't let anyone on the Tally see it, and especially not the man two stalls down."
  - *If the players are stuck:* "Questions about the Old Shore, ask Brannagh at the Pilots' Hall. She knows every family on the water."
  - *If they are kind to her:* "If you ever sold something you want back, come round the back. We don't talk about the back."
- **Wants:** Honest weights and a quiet life.
- **Secret:** She keeps a "Lost Shelf" of heartkeeps sold in grief and quietly lets the sellers buy them back at cost, which the Court forbids.
- **2024 stat block:** Commoner (CR 0).
- **How She Reacts:** Helps anyone who is kind to her: she can read a keep's weight, tell a forged keep from a true one, and explain gilding without saying the word. She will not appraise a bell's Heart: "That's not a memory, love. That's a bell."

page.title: 28. MASTER ORSOLO VENN
page.aliases: Venn, Orsolo, Gilded Heron, merchant, Amnian
page.body:
- **Role:** Factor of the Vennmark Coster of Athkatla, the largest memory exporter in Pellmoor. A human-sized antagonist of the memory trade.
- **Look:** Amnian, 50s. Plum velvet in a grey country, rings on every finger, a silent Lantanese pocket-clock he consults constantly.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A man in plum velvet, absurd in this gray country, rises to greet you with both hands out. There's a ring on every finger, and he checks a silent brass pocket-clock before he has finished smiling."
- **Voice:** Warm, fluent Hesk with an Amnian lilt. Calls everyone "friend" and means "customer."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "Friends! Welcome, welcome. You're fresh off a ship, I can tell. Let me be the first to help you spend your money."
  - *If he hears of the Heart:* "A humming relic? Friend, I have a buyer who would weep. Name your price. Then double it, because I like you."
  - *Making his offer:* "Six hundred gold, today, and no questions. The Heron sails in three days. After that, my offer sails too."
  - *If refused:* "Of course, of course. Think it over. I'll write down that you said no. I write everything down."
  - *If it turns violent or public:* "Friends, friends. Business is business. Let's not make it a scene."
  - *Asked about the Court:* "The Court and I understand each other. The Landing House stamps what I ship. Officer Quill is a great friend of trade."
- **Wants:** An exclusive export licence from the Court. Curiosities from the Ringing Land for his buyers in Athkatla.
- **Secret:** He pays Tobias Quill to look away from certain cargoes. A buyer in Athkatla offers 5,000 gp for "a true bell-relic of the Ringing Land." The Coster buys Tithed memories from the Court for export, and its ledgers prove it.
- **The Gilded Heron:** the Coster's carrack, anchored beyond the last pier. Two Coster guards (Tough) on watch; a Baldurian crew who won't fight for the Coster.
- **2024 stat block:** Noble (CR 1/8), with two Toughs (CR 1/2) as guards.
- **How He Reacts:** Generous, then persistent. Prefers money to trouble and folds when a deal turns violent or public. Holds grudges in ledgers, not in alleys.

page.title: 29. SISTER AURELIE DAWNMANTLE
page.aliases: Aurelie, Dawnmantle, Lathander, Morninglord, Dawn Mission
page.body:
- **Role:** Morninglord priestess of Lathander who runs the Dawn Mission on Strangers' Row. Optional ally for clerics, paladins and anyone hurt.
- **Look:** Waterdhavian, 30s. Rose-and-gold vestments faded by the Corvanese light.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A young woman in faded rose-and-gold vestments sweeps the step of a small mission house hung with painted sun-discs. She looks up at you with real, unguarded delight, as though visitors are the best thing that could happen to her today."
- **Voice:** Bright and earnest. Says "when the sun comes back" as if it were a date in a diary.
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "Welcome to the Dawn Mission! Are you hurt? Hungry? Lost? We do all three."
  - *Asked about Hallowmere:* "When the sun comes back to Hallowmere, I mean to be standing in the square to see it."
  - *Asked about her writ:* "Four times I've asked the Court for a writ to Hallowmere. Four times, 'not this season.' I'm starting to think they mean every season."
  - *Asked to heal:* "A small donation, or a true story about a sunrise. Honestly, I'd rather have the story."
  - *If they mention Vaer's bell:* "A bell that brings back the dawn? Tell me everything. Tell me twice. I'm coming with you."
  - *If the players are stuck:* "Nobody travels inland without a writ, unless the Court itself names you in one. If anyone from the Court ever writes to you, look closely at the seal."
- **Wants:** A writ of passage to Hallowmere, to bring Lathander's dawn to a city that has none.
- **Secret:** The Court has refused her writ four times. She is close to trying without one, which would get her arrested.
- **2024 stat block:** Priest (CR 2).
- **How She Reacts:** If the party tells her about Vaer's bell, she becomes a devoted ally, and a liability, in Act II. Heals for a donation, or for a true story about a sunrise.

page.title: 30. BROTHER HADRIK VOSS
page.body:
- **Role:** Kelemvorite priest with a shrine-tent on Strangers' Row. Believes the restless dead of the Mere are an abomination to be laid to rest.
- **Look:** Grey robes, a skeletal-hand pendant, a censer he never lets go out.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A man in gray robes sits cross-legged outside a canvas shrine, a censer smoking steadily beside him. A pendant shaped like a skeletal hand hangs at his chest. He is watching the Mere, not you."
- **Voice:** Low and certain. Quotes the Doomguide.
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "The dead of this water do not rest. Have you come to help me, or to argue?"
  - *Asked about the Drowned Choir:* "'Every soul is owed its judgment.' These ones refuse theirs. I will give it to them."
  - *Asked about his plan:* "On the night they sing, I bless the water. The singing stops, and they go where they belong."
  - *If argued with from his own faith:* "The Doomguide does say the dead are owed remembrance. You're telling me that's what they're asking for."
  - *If asked about his brother:* "My brother went into the sea and never came out. No grave. No judgment. Don't talk to me about the restless dead."
  - *If talked down:* "Then I'll sit with them instead. Kelemvor can wait one night."
- **Wants:** To lay the Drowned Choir to rest, by force if need be.
- **Secret:** His own brother drowned at sea and was never found. The Mere's unrestful dead feel like an accusation.
- **2024 stat block:** Priest (CR 2).
- **How He Reacts:** Can be argued down from his own dogma: Kelemvor's dead are owed judgment and remembrance, not erasure (DC 15 Persuasion; a DC 12 Religion Study first grants Advantage). If he blesses the Mere during the Night Song, the Choir rises angry.

page.title: PELLMOOR LANDING: THE QUAYS, THE TALLY AND STRANGERS' ROW
page.aliases: Landing House, Reckoning House, Pilots' Hall, Strangers' Row, Loud Quarter, Brass Lantern, Quays, Tally
page.body:
**The Landing House (Quays).** Court customs. A grey stone hall with a silence-stone lintel. Writs of passage, the 5 gp landing due, cargo seals, and the chime-removal bench where every imported clock is silenced. Six Hushmen and Tobias Quill's office.
> **SAY:** "The clerk stamps your papers without reading them. 'Landing due, five gold. Pellmoor and the Mere road only. Anywhere else needs a writ from Hallowmere. They take about a season. Next.'"

**The Pilots' Hall (Quays).** A long reed-roofed shed built over the water, its floor a map of Old Pellmoor's drowned streets in painted planks. Brannagh Wick's pilots wait on benches for ships.
> **SAY:** "The floor creaks under you, and you realise it's painted: streets, alleys and a market square in faded blue, each with its old name lettered beside it. Old Pellmoor, the town under the harbour. On the benches along the wall, a dozen pilots in salt-stiff coats look up, decide you're not a ship, and look away again."

**The Reckoning House (the Tally).** A narrow shop with a slate by the door and a counter scored by tuning forks. Sela Maunt weighs keeps under a Lantanese lens. Behind a curtain: the Lost Shelf.
> **SAY:** "The slate by the door reads, in careful chalk: 1 KEEP = 1 GP 2 SP. MOTES AT 1 SP. HEARTKEEPS BY APPRAISAL. Underneath, smaller: NO GOLD FOR TITHES."

**Strangers' Row, the Loud Quarter.** Foreign inns, counting-houses, the Dawn Mission, a dwarven smithy, a gnomish clockmaker selling silent clocks, Brother Hadrik's shrine-tent, and music at all hours.
> **SAY:** "Strangers' Row hits you all at once: a fiddle and a lute playing two different songs, a smith's hammer clanging, the smell of frying onions and temple incense, shop signs in Common, Dwarvish and scripts you don't know. After the gray hush of the rest of Corvane, it is almost too loud to bear."

**The Brass Lantern.** The Faerûnian inn. Loud, warm, overpriced, and the only place in Corvane that serves Waterdhavian ale. The *Gull's Wager*'s old first mate drinks in the corner.
> **SAY:** "The Brass Lantern is warm, crowded and loud: brass lamps, wet cloaks steaming by the fire, and someone singing a Waterdeep drinking song badly. The board over the bar lists prices in gold and, in smaller letters underneath, in motes. In the far corner an old sailor drinks alone with his back to the wall."

page.title: 2024 RULES NOTES (v6)
page.aliases: 2024, 5.5e, rules, Heroic Inspiration, Influence, Extreme Cold, Suffocation, Exhaustion, encounter budget
page.body:
- **Heroic Inspiration** replaces v5's "Inspiration."
- **Influence** (action): social plays use it. The DC is 15 or the creature's Intelligence score, whichever is higher; its attitude (Friendly, Indifferent, Hostile) decides whether a check is needed at all.
- **Study** (Intelligence) and **Search** (Wisdom) actions: clue scenes use them. Essential clues are never lost to a failed roll.
- **Extreme Cold** (Glassreach): end of each hour, DC 10 Constitution save or 1 Exhaustion level. Cold Resistance or Immunity succeeds automatically; so does a warm cloak or cold-weather gear (house rule kept from v5).
- **Exhaustion:** each level gives −2 to d20 Tests and −5 feet of Speed; a long rest removes 1 level; level 6 is death.
- **Suffocation:** hold breath for 1 + Constitution modifier minutes (minimum 30 seconds); out of breath, 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each turn, all removed when breathing again.
- **Frigid Water:** minutes equal to the Constitution score, then a DC 10 Constitution save each minute or 1 Exhaustion level.
- **Conditions** use the 2024 definitions. A Sense Toll at Ruinous weight uses Blinded or Deafened (Part 2.7).
- **Encounters:** Waypoint's Foresight computes difficulty from your roster with the 2024 XP budget per character (Low, Moderate, High). Corvane creatures have full 2024 stat blocks built on 2024 Monster Manual creatures; open them from any encounter.
- **Spells that touch memory** (Modify Memory, Greater Restoration, Remove Curse, Speak with Dead, Zone of Truth and others) have rulings in Foresight's anytime plays. Search "If they…" for the spell's name.

page.title: WHAT CHANGED IN REVISION 6
page.body:
**World.** Corvane is part of the Forgotten Realms, hidden behind the Stormwall until the Wrongweather opened the Seam in 382 SS (1462 DR). Pellmoor is now Pellmoor Landing, a port of about 4,000. Memory is a working currency alongside gold (MEMORY AS MONEY). New NPCs 26–30. New faction: THE LANDING.

**Act I.** New Session 1 opening (arrival at the port). Quill works from the Landing House and is short because Pellmoor pays in gold; H-03 can be solved by giving memories on the villagers' behalf. New Session 3 option: sell the Heart to Master Venn (the *Gilded Heron* sails in three days). Optional complication: Brother Hadrik Voss blesses the Mere. Brannagh Wick is a fourth source on Tam's death; any two still establish the Court's responsibility.

**Act II.** Stormborn need a writ at the Hallowmere gate; the Chancellor's invitation counts. Optional reveal: the Tithe-Ledger's EXPORT — VENNMARK column.

**Act III.** Some Stilled are Faerûnian sailors from before the Silence. Glassreach uses 2024 Extreme Cold.

**Act IV.** Ringing Thrane loosens the Stormwall for a season. New Session 22 ally if earned: the Stormborn.

**Endings.** A stabilised Thrane thins the Stormwall for good; in the Empty Choir the Court keeps the Seam.

**Part 9.** Situation 17 now has ships home; Situation 18 has a sailor's dragon story; the Edge of the Dream lies inside the Stormwall.

**Rules.** 2024 throughout (2024 RULES NOTES). Full stat blocks and calculated encounter difficulty live in Foresight.

page.title: VAER, THE BELL OF DAWN
page.body:
**Vaer is the bell of dawn, law and beginnings.** It hangs in Vaer's Belfry in Hallowmere, a prison and watchtower, in chains of silence-stone above the Dawn Order's barracks.
- **While it is silent:** the Long Dusk. The dawn never fully comes to Hallowmere.
- **Its Heart:** Vaer's Heart, in the Dawn Order armory. Ser Haldric Mose holds it.
- **The Toll:** a memory of a beginning. Heavy if no bell or one bell has rung before it, Grievous after two or three, Ruinous after four or five. Name the kind and the weight, never the memory, and wait for a yes.
- **When it can ring:** Session 9.
- **What ringing does:** one whole day of real sun, then a real dawn every morning for a year. The Court issues a Silence Warrant for the Ringer; the Dawn Order enforces it only if Captain Rook lost the oath-duel in Session 6.

page.title: OSSA, THE BELL OF MEMORY
page.body:
**Ossa is the bell of memory, ancestors and rest.** It hangs in the Ossa Belfry in Old Pellmoor, the drowned town under the Mute Mere.
- **While it is silent:** the dead cannot rest. The Drowned Choir sings grief in Ondra Sallow's voice and hunts the Mere.
- **Its Heart:** Ossa's Heart. Tam Harrow stole it in 392 SS and hid it in an oilskin in the reeds; Ila Harrow has it in Act I.
- **The Toll:** a memory of someone who has died. Heavy if no bell or one bell has rung before it, Grievous after two or three, Ruinous after four or five. Name the kind and the weight, never the memory, and wait for a yes.
- **When it can ring:** Session 2 (if they bring the Heart down that night), Session 3, or on a Pellmoor detour in Session 9.
- **What ringing does:** the dead of the Mere are free to rest, and the Choir falls silent and stops hunting. Only the verse releases the Cantor: she sings her own name, then goes quiet. Mother Sallow remembers her husband.

page.title: HIEME, THE BELL OF WINTER
page.body:
**Hieme is the bell of winter and endurance.** It hangs in the Frost Spire in Glassreach.
- **While it is silent:** winter is frozen in place. Glassreach froze in a single night in 2 SS, and the Stilled stand in it still.
- **Its Heart:** the Frost Heart, set in the Glass Sexton's crown. He can give it in Session 13.
- **The Toll:** a memory, any memory. Heavy if no bell or one bell has rung before it, Grievous after two or three, Ruinous after four or five. Name the kind and the weight, never the memory, and wait for a yes. If nobody will pay, it does not ring.
- **When it can ring:** Session 14.
- **What ringing does:** a thaw. The Stilled wake over several weeks (Session 15). If the Sexton is alive, he weeps. The Court sends Lady Isolde Drave to recover the bell.

page.title: CALLA, THE BELL OF HARVEST
page.body:
**Calla is the bell of harvest, grace and generosity.** It hangs in the Old Granary at Kell's Crossing.
- **While it is silent:** crops fail. Bet Ostrow rang it once, at nine, in 340 SS, and was Tithed for it.
- **Its Heart:** Calla's Heart, in the Tithe-Ledger Room of the Court's vault, on a shelf marked "Harvest, Withheld". Maudrin Vesk controls it.
- **The Toll:** a gift, given to someone in need, and never returned. Heavy if no bell or one bell has rung before it, Grievous after two or three, Ruinous after four or five. Name the kind and the weight, never the memory, and wait for a yes.
- **When it can ring:** Session 9, at Kell's Crossing.
- **What ringing does:** one harvest season. The ash fields bloom and there is bread for everyone. Court Tithe-men raid the Crossing for the rest of the season, and collectors try to take the Ringer.

page.title: THRANE, THE BELL OF STORMS
page.body:
**Thrane is the bell of storm, courage and war.** It hangs in the Lightning Shafts at Brassfall.
- **While it is silent:** no storm has crossed the mountains since the Quiet Night. The storms went out to sea instead, and became the Stormwall.
- **Its Heart:** Thrane's Heart, in the Heart-Hall of the Ironhorn camp. Thane Oru Kessa holds it, and its dead lightning is killing her.
- **The Toll:** a sense. Heavy if no bell or one bell has rung before it, Grievous after two or three, Ruinous after four or five. Name the kind and the weight, never the memory, and wait for a yes.
- **When it can ring:** Session 19A, or as the second bell in Session 21.
- **What ringing does:** storms return, storm-stones blaze and metal hums. The Stormwall loosens. Kessa's sickness eases and the Ironhorn celebrate. The Court sends a strike force, and Maudrin moves.

page.title: MIREL, THE BELL OF DREAMS
page.body:
**Mirel is the bell of dreams and hope.** It hangs in the Sleeping Hall at Vael Tor.
- **While it is silent:** nightmares walk. The Sleepless come out of Vael Tor in the shape of a sleeper's worst fear.
- **Its Heart:** Mirel's Heart, in the Sealed Stacks of the Bone Archive. The Librarian of the Sealed Book keeps it.
- **The Toll:** a fear, which the bell gives the Ringer. Heavy if no bell or one bell has rung before it, Grievous after two or three, Ruinous after four or five. Name the kind and the weight, never the memory, and wait for a yes.
- **When it can ring:** Session 16B (as soon as they reach it), Session 19B, or as the second bell in Session 21.
- **What ringing does:** the Sleepless dissolve and the sleepers dream gently. The Hush's lullaby changes key. Hushmen come to the Tor.

page.title: YSH, THE SEVENTH BELL
page.body:
**Ysh is the bell of sleep, peace and rest, and it is silent on purpose.** It hangs in the Hush Shrine, deep under Vael Tor. Its silence holds Oum, the Dreamer, asleep.
- **Its Heart:** the Tuning Key. Maudrin Vesk keeps it in her palace vault in Hallowmere until she leaves the city (Session 22), then carries it in a silence-stone case.
- **The Toll, if it is struck:** all six kinds at once, each Ruinous.
- **Never struck:** in the Concord the Key is seated in the Seventh and never struck, and the Ringer pays the Great Toll instead.
- **Struck:** the Hush opens and Oum begins to wake (Hush Unbound: Remake or Unmake).
- **Where it is decided:** Sessions 26 and 27.

page.title: THE RINGER
page.body:
**The Ringer is whoever rings a bell, and the one who pays its Toll.**
- **Who may ring:** any willing adult who is there. Children never ring; Ila may stand beside the Ringer. A character whose player is absent never pays a Toll, and the dead pay nothing.
- **Before it rings:** say the kind of Toll and its weight, never the exact memory, and wait for a yes. If nobody says yes, the bell does not ring and nothing is taken.
- **The weight:** Heavy if no bell or one bell has rung before, Grievous after two or three, Ruinous after four or five. Ysh takes all six kinds at once, each Ruinous.
- **After it rings:** you choose what was taken, within the kind, and it goes on the Toll tracker.
- **Afterwards:** once Vaer rings, the Court issues a Silence Warrant for the Ringer.

page.title: THE CONCORD
page.body:
**The Concord is the ending in which the world is mended.** It is the first of the four paths.
- **What it needs:** all six bells rung (Vaer, Ossa, Hieme, Calla, Thrane and Mirel), Ysh still unstruck, and the Tuning Key in the party's hands.
- **The rite:** a willing Ringer seats the Key in the Seventh, never striking it, and pays the Great Toll, giving up their whole name. Session 27 runs it.
- **What it makes:** a restored world, not a perfect one.
- **How the party learns of it:** Edda Thorne's diary gives the first hint (Session 5). Corin Aldeth shows them Edda Thorne's Notes, which describe it in full (Session 18A).
- **The other paths:** Hush Unbound (Ysh is struck: Remake or Unmake), the Empty Choir (the Court secures the Key and the Long Dusk goes on) and the Second Dawn (the party seals the Key away unstruck, and the world is partly restored).

page.title: THE TITHE OF MEMORY
page.aliases: Tithe, Tithes, Tithe of Memory, Tithe Clock
page.body:
**The Tithe of Memory is the Quiet Court's tax in memories.** Since 1 SS, people have given up memories in exchange for protection and tax relief. It pays for the silence-stones and the Court's grip on Tonework.
- **Where:** memories are taken and recorded at the Hall of Tithes. The master ledger is in the Tithe-Ledger Room.
- **What it does to people:** those who give too much become Blanks.
- **The Tithe Clock:** each night the party spends inside a Court-controlled city adds one tick, from 0. At 6, the Hushmen sweep the city with a checkpoint on every road. At 12, the Court puts silence-stones in every street. The clock resets after a week away from Court cities; checkpoints and stones already placed stay.

page.title: BLANKS
page.body:
**A Blank is someone who has given away so many memories that they no longer know their own family.** They are common in Hallowmere.
- Jonah Bray's mother, Mara Bray, is a Blank: she was Tithed of him.
- In Session 7, hundreds of them surround the Hall of Tithes, asking who they were.

page.title: THE QUIET NIGHT
page.body:
**The Quiet Night is the night of 0 SS, when all seven bells fell silent in one breath.** Years are counted from it: SS is years since, BS years before.
- **What happened:** High Sexton Imber Vesk took the Tuning Key from the Bellwright Tower's reliquary and tuned the bells into one long, gentle spring, against Edda Thorne's warning. The Key sang against the bells, and the Choir went silent. Brassfall's storms stopped the same night.
- **What people believe:** that the bells caused it. The Ninefold Church became the Quiet Court on that belief. Within the Court's leaders, only Maudrin Vesk knows that the Key did it.
- **The Key afterwards:** it passed to Imber's daughter, Cassia Vesk, and stayed in the Vesk reliquary until Maudrin took it in 374 SS.
- **Where the truth comes out:** Edda Thorne's diary (Session 5), the Glass Sexton's story (Session 13) and the truth of the Key (Session 22).

page.title: THE SILENCE WARRANT
page.body:
**A Silence Warrant is a Court order that lets any Hushman arrest the Ringer on sight in a Court city.** The Court issues it after Vaer rings (Session 9).
- The Dawn Order enforces it only if Captain Rook lost the oath-duel (Session 6).
- While it stands, a bluff about the Ringer is 2 harder.

page.title: THE TUNING KEY
page.body:
**The Tuning Key is the Heart of Ysh, the Seventh Bell, and the most important object in the campaign.**
- **Its history:** Imber Vesk used it on the Quiet Night. It passed to his daughter, Cassia Vesk, and stayed in the Vesk reliquary until Maudrin Vesk took it in 374 SS, at twenty.
- **Where it is:** Maudrin's palace vault in Hallowmere until she leaves the city (Session 22). After that she carries it in a silence-stone case.
- **What it decides:** seated in Ysh and never struck, it makes the Concord. Struck, it opens the Hush. Sealed away unstruck, it gives the Second Dawn. Kept by the Court, it means the Empty Choir.

page.title: OUM, THE DREAMER
page.body:
**Oum, the Dreamer, is the god dreaming the world.** Nobody has ever seen Oum.
- The seven bells were cast to keep the dream steady. Ysh keeps Oum asleep; the other six keep the world in shape while the dream lasts.
- Some believe Oum is dying. Others believe Oum is waking.
- If Ysh is struck, the Hush opens and Oum begins to wake.

page.title: SILENCE-STONE
page.body:
**Silence-stone is a grey stone that drinks sound.** The Court uses it to hold down Tonework.
- Hushmen wear silence-stone gloves. Vaer hangs in chains of it. Maudrin carries the Tuning Key in a silence-stone case once she leaves Hallowmere.
- At 12 on the Tithe Clock, the Court puts silence-stones in every street of the city.

page.title: THE LONG DUSK
page.body:
**The Long Dusk is the grey, endless twilight over Hallowmere since 1 SS.** The dawn has not come since Vaer fell silent.
- Ringing Vaer brings one day of real sun, then a real dawn every morning for a year.
- If the Court secures the Tuning Key (the Empty Choir), the Long Dusk goes on.

page.title: THE BRASS ROAD
page.body:
**The Brass Road is the old trade road from Brassfall to the steppe,** partly collapsed since the Long Unraveling: bronze carts, ruts, and a sky that flickers with no clouds in it.
- Session 16A opens on it. Corin Aldeth's workshop is under a tavern on it (Session 18A), and the Court's strike force comes up it (Session 19A).
- Thane Oru Kessa took Thrane's Heart from it, and the Heart has been eating her hands since.

page.title: THE HALL OF TITHES
page.body:
**The Hall of Tithes is where Hallowmere's memories are taken and recorded.**
- Court pensions are paid there (Session 4). Hushmen don't chase past it.
- **The clerks' dormitory** (Session 6): one corridor, three doors, a stair-head with an alarm bell, and a kitchen at the bottom. Tessa Caddock is held there.
- **Session 7:** hundreds of Blanks surround it, asking who they were, and Sergeant Orla Gaunt's Hushmen form a line on its steps.

page.title: 31. MAREN TALLA
page.body:
- **Role:** A weaver of Glassreach, Stilled on the first night of the freeze, in 2 SS. Wyn Talla's family has kept vigil over her for four hundred years. She asks first after her brother, Pell.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A woman of about thirty in a shawl stands in the glass, half turned, one hand held out behind her as if somebody small was meant to take it. Around the worn bench at her feet lie a hundred years of candle stubs."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Once she is woken:* "I've been told. I should like to hear it from you. What year is it?"
  - *About the other Stilled:* "We don't want to be a wonder. We want to be neighbours."
  - *Asked what they will do:* "We'll walk. Slowly. Tell us which road."
  - *About the Sexton:* "He asked me to forgive him. I said I'd think about it. I've had practice thinking."
- **Stat block:** Stilled Person while the glass holds her; Commoner once woken.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 11:** A weaver; frozen on the first night, in 2 SS. **Where:** Her glass, three trees past the clearing. **Starts:** Indifferent, confused. **Influence:** DC 15, or say her name. **Secret:** She heard the Sexton before he froze. He can't bear to be argued with. **Voice:** Soft, touches everything. **Wants:** To know about Pell. **First words:** "Did Pell get home?"
- **Session 12:** Woken in Session 11. **Where:** The chapel door; she won't come in. **Starts:** Friendly, if they woke her. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** She was in these pews on the first night. He sang. **Voice:** Soft; won't come in. **Wants:** Them not to argue. **First words:** "Don't."
- **Session 13:** If she's awake. **Where:** The arch. **Starts:** Friendly. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** She remembers Imber as a kind man who forgave her for laughing in church. **Voice:** Soft; laughs in church. **Wants:** Him not to be alone. **First words:** "You look cold."
- **Session 14:** If she's awake. **Where:** With Imber, or at camp. **Starts:** Friendly. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** She knows two of the people on the stair by name. **Voice:** Knows two of them by name. **Wants:** Him not to be alone. **First words:** "That's Tilda. She's afraid of heights."
- **Session 15:** Speaks for the Stilled. **Where:** The long table. **Starts:** Friendly, or wary. **Influence:** None if trusted; DC 15 if wary. **Secret:** She hasn't been told what Glassreach means for her family's names. **Voice:** Upright, dust in the hair. **Wants:** To be neighbours. **First words:** "We have a request."

page.title: 32. WYN TALLA
page.body:
- **Role:** An old trapper at the edge of Glassreach, beside Yara Thenn's camp, and the last of her family to keep the vigil over Maren Talla. She paid Edrin Moss to carry the glass letter.
- **First look (read aloud):** "An old woman by the fire, with a trapper's hands, a weaver's patience and a basket of candles at her feet. She has been watching you since you arrived, and she doesn't pretend otherwise."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "You came. I told her you'd come. I tell her everything."
  - *About the vigil:* "My mother sat with her, and hers. I haven't got a daughter. So it's me, and then it's nobody."
  - *About the glass:* "Don't use a hammer. Whatever you do. Please."
  - *If the players are stuck:* "My family has sat with her four hundred years. The voice in the chapel is the first thing that ever answered us."
- **Stat block:** Commoner.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 10:** An old trapper; keeper of a vigil. **Where:** Yara's fire. **Starts:** Friendly to anyone who asks about Maren. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** She paid for the letter. A voice in the glass told her what to write, and signed itself I.V. **Voice:** Slow, plain, pours a second cup. **Wants:** Maren, gently. **First words:** "You came."
- **Session 11:** Keeper of the vigil. **Where:** Beside the glass, all night. **Starts:** Friendly. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** She's afraid that Maren will be angry with her for taking so long. **Voice:** Plain, talks about the weather. **Wants:** Maren, not cross. **First words:** "This is the sister."

page.title: 33. EDRIN MOSS
page.body:
- **Role:** A Glassreach trapper who can't read. Wyn Talla paid him to carry the glass letter (Session 8). He will guide them to the forest, but never past the first tree.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A weather-beaten trapper, out of breath, holds a letter sealed in blue wax well away from himself, as if it might bite. He looks at the fire before he looks at you."
- **Things to say:**
  - *About the letter:* "Don't ask me to read it. I don't read."
  - *Asked who sent him:* "An old woman paid me. She talks to the glass."
  - *Worried:* "There were grey coats on the road behind me. Is that bad?"
  - *If the players are stuck:* "Her hut's by Yara's camp, at the edge of the glass. I'll take you to the first tree. Not one step past it."
- **Stat block:** Scout.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 8:** A Glassreach trapper; the courier. **Where:** The inn steps, breathless. **Starts:** Indifferent; Friendly if paid or warmed up. **Influence:** DC 15. **Secret:** Wyn Talla paid him: an old woman at the forest's edge, beside Yara's camp, whose family has watched the glass for four hundred years. A voice in the glass told her what to write. **Voice:** Out of breath; can't read. **Wants:** His money; a fire. **First words:** "A woman paid me."
- **Session 10:** The courier from Session 8. **Where:** Yara's fire, if they protected him. **Starts:** Friendly. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** He won't go past the first tree. He never has.

page.title: 34. CORRAN VELL
page.body:
- **Role:** Bosun of the Brightwater, a ship out of Zazesspur caught in the freeze of 2 SS with thirty-one aboard. He thinks it is 1082 DR.
- **First look (read aloud):** "Among the Stilled at the edge of the clearing stands a man in a sea-coat cut four hundred years out of fashion, with a brass badge on his breast: a ship under three stars. When the glass lets him go, the first thing he does is look at the sky."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "What year is it? Is it still ten hundred and eighty-two?"
  - *About the ship:* "The Brightwater was moored at a river mouth, west of here, under a sky full of weather. Where did the weather go?"
  - *About the crew:* "There were thirty-one of us. I counted. A bosun always counts."
  - *Asked why they came:* "We only came ashore for water."
  - *About home:* "Who won? There was a war on, at home. There's always a war on."
- **Stat block:** Stilled Person until calmed; Commoner once thawed.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 10:** A sailor of the Brightwater, from Zazesspur. **Where:** The edge of the clearing. **Starts:** Hostile from shock for a moment, then Indifferent. **Influence:** DC 15, in Common. **Secret:** He thinks it's 1082 DR. His crew are in these trees. **Voice:** Old sea-words, checks the sky. **Wants:** His crew home. **First words:** "What year is it?"
- **Session 11:** Bosun of the Brightwater. **Where:** Depends on last session. **Starts:** Depends. **Influence:** DC 15, in Common. **Secret:** He'll give his sailor's word and keep it.
- **Session 15:** Bosun of the Brightwater. **Where:** By the water barrels. **Starts:** From before. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** Twelve of his thirty-one are awake. **Voice:** Old sea-words; counts in a row. **Wants:** Passage for twelve. **First words:** "Where did the weather go?"

page.title: 35. TESSA CADDOCK, THE HOSTAGE
page.body:
- **Role:** Wren Caddock's daughter, held in the clerks' dormitory of the Hall of Tithes to keep her mother working for the Court (Session 6). If your table has not agreed to children in danger, make her Wren's grown sister.
- **First look (read aloud):** "On the end of a narrow cot in the clerks' dormitory sits Wren's daughter, knees drawn up, watching the door. She has her mother's face exactly. (At a table that keeps children out of danger, she is Wren's grown sister, with the same face.)"
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "Are you from Mam? Don't lie. Everyone here lies, nicely."
  - *Asked why she is here:* "They keep me so Mam keeps working. She knows it. I know it. We don't say it."
  - *On the way out:* "Don't let go of my hand till we're outside. Not even on the stairs."
  - *Afterwards:* "Is Mam all right? Is she in trouble now, because of me?"
- **Stat block:** Commoner.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 6:** Wren's daughter, held as leverage. **Where:** The clerks' dormitory. **Starts:** Frightened. **Influence:** None. **Secret:** She knows her mother's face. That's why they keep her.

page.title: 36. MABRY COLE
page.aliases: Sergeant Mabry Cole, Sergeant Cole, Sgt Mabry Cole
page.body:
- **Role:** The Hushman sergeant on Hallowmere's gate (Session 4). He reads writs well. In Session 9 he holds the north gate against the Ringer, and he may remember them.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A Hushman sergeant in grey stands by the gate-house door with his arms folded, one hand in a glove of silence-stone. He looks bored, and he misses nothing: who's nervous, who's armed, whose writ is new."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "Hands where I can see them."
  - *At the counter:* "Writ."
  - *If they refuse the courtesy memory:* "Refusing is your right. So is a night in the Belfry."
  - *At the north gate, Session 9:* "I remember you. You were polite at my gate. Don't make me sorry."
- **Stat block:** Hushman Sergeant.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 4:** The gate's Hushman sergeant. **Where:** The Gate Office door. **Starts:** Indifferent; Suspicious (+2 to his DCs) if Quill reported them. **Influence:** DC 15 (Intelligence 14). **Secret:** He reads writs well: Investigation DC 17 to catch a forgery. **Voice:** Clipped; raps his stone glove. **Wants:** No trouble. **First words:** "Hands where I can see them."
- **Session 9:** The north gate's Sergeant. **Where:** The gate. **Starts:** Hostile to the Warrant. **Influence:** DC 15. **Secret:** He may remember them from Session 4.

page.title: 37. ORLA GAUNT
page.aliases: Sergeant Orla Gaunt, Sgt Orla Gaunt
page.body:
- **Role:** The Hushman sergeant who commands the line at the Hall of Tithes in Session 7. She doesn't want a massacre.
- **First look (read aloud):** "Behind the Hushman line on the steps of the Hall of Tithes stands a sergeant with a whistle on a cord and a hand crossbow held low. She is watching the crowd, not you, and counting: her people, their sticks, the ways out."
- **Things to say:**
  - *To the crowd:* "Clear the steps."
  - *To Ilam Bray:* "Bray! Back in line!"
  - *If the party talks to her:* "I've got orders, and I've got a square full of frightened people with sticks. Give me a reason to go home."
  - *If the crowd sits down:* "Nobody dies on these steps today. Not on my record."
- **Stat block:** Hushman Sergeant.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 7:** Commands the line. **Where:** Behind the line, with a hand crossbow. **Starts:** Hostile to anyone who interferes. **Influence:** DC 15. **Secret:** She withdraws when half her line is down or the crowd sits down. She doesn't want a massacre on her record. **Voice:** Whistle; hand crossbow. **Wants:** A clean sweep. **First words:** "Clear the steps."

page.title: 38. MOTHER LUMEN
page.body:
- **Role:** Leader of the Hush Cult in the Sleeping Hall at Vael Tor. She is dying slowly, and she feeds the Hush her own dreams first.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A woman of sixty, thin as a rake, in a grey robe, comes to meet you with both hands out to take one of yours. Her voice goes down at the end of everything she says, like being tucked in."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "There. There you are."
  - *To anyone tired:* "You needn't decide anything. You can just sit."
  - *About the Cult:* "We don't take. We're given."
  - *About the price:* "I'll tell you exactly what it costs before you say yes. I wouldn't do that to you."
- **Stat block:** Hush Cult Leader.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 17B:** Leader of the Hush Cult. **Where:** The circle. **Starts:** Warm. **Influence:** DC 16; Advantage with evidence. **Secret:** She's dying, slowly. She feeds the Hush her own dreams first. **Voice:** Falling, like being tucked in; holds hands. **Wants:** It to stay asleep. **First words:** "There. There you are."
- **Session 18B:** Leader of the Hush Cult. **Where:** The top step. **Starts:** Depends on yesterday. **Influence:** DC 14 to pass. **Secret:** She's been to the bottom. It cost her five. She can't remember her mother's house. **Voice:** Falling, gentle. **Wants:** You not to lose five. **First words:** "I had a mother. I must have had."
- **Session 19B:** Leader of the Hush Cult. **Where:** The Hall, or the circle. **Starts:** Weeping. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** She hasn't dreamed for eleven years. She will tonight. **Voice:** Weeping, gentle. **Wants:** To dream. **First words:** "It sounded like someone loved it."
- **Session 20:** Leader of the Hush Cult (the Tor). **Where:** The circle of humming. **Starts:** Kind. **Influence:** Not tonight. **Secret:** Her rest takes every dream you've got.
- **Session 21:** (road A) The Cult's Leader. **Where:** The Hall. **Starts:** Depends on the Cult. **Influence:** DC 14. **Secret:** Hasn't dreamed for eleven years. **Voice:** Weeping, gentle. **Wants:** To dream. **First words:** "It sounded like someone loved it."

page.title: 39. BROTHER LULL
page.body:
- **Role:** A Hush Cultist who looks after the sleepers in the Sleeping Hall. He has never given a dream: he says he is too busy, and he is frightened to.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A round little man in a grey robe goes along the rows of beds whispering, always folding something: a blanket, a sock, a hand put back under the covers."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "Oh, shoes, please. Thank you."
  - *About a sleeper:* "That's Master Wick. He was a dyer. He's been here since my grandfather."
  - *About the sleepers:* "They're not unhappy. I'd have known."
  - *If they bring socks for bed forty-one:* "Forty-one. Aunt Posy. Nobody's ever... Oh, thank you."
- **Stat block:** Hush Cultist.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 16B:** **Voice:** Whispers; folding. **Wants:** You to take your shoes off. **First words:** "Oh, *shoes*, please."
- **Session 17B:** Looks after the Sleeping Hall. **Where:** In and out with blankets. **Starts:** Friendly. **Influence:** DC 13. **Secret:** He's never given a dream. He says he's too busy. He's frightened to. **Voice:** Whispers; folding. **Wants:** Not to have to give one. **First words:** "Oh, you'll want a blanket."
- **Session 19B:** Tucks them in. **Where:** The rows, with a lamp. **Starts:** Beside himself. **Influence:** None needed. **Secret:** He's got a list of every name, and where they came from. **Voice:** Whispers; a list. **Wants:** Someone to come for them. **First words:** "So someone *comes*."

page.title: 40. SISTER NOD
page.body:
- **Role:** A Hush Cultist of twenty who gave up dreaming last winter, and has forgotten what she used to want.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A young woman, pale and exact, tucks a blanket into an empty bed with perfect corners, then looks up at whichever of you is most tired."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "I don't dream. It's very restful."
  - *To the most tired one:* "You look so tired."
  - *Asked what she gave:* "I don't mind. Really. I don't mind."
- **Stat block:** Hush Cultist.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
- **Session 16B:** **Voice:** Pale, exact. **Wants:** Not to be asked. **First words:** "I don't dream. It's very restful."
- **Session 17B:** Twenty; gave up dreaming last winter. **Where:** By the arch. **Starts:** Exact, flat. **Influence:** DC 13. **Secret:** She's forgotten what it was she used to want. **Voice:** Exact, flat. **Wants:** Not to be asked what she wanted. **First words:** "I think I was going somewhere."

page.title: 41. WAT FURROW
page.body:
- **Role:** Came up to Vael Tor in the autumn with his son, Pip, to take his wife home from bed two hundred and twelve of the Sleeping Hall, and stayed.
- **First look (read aloud):** "A big, slow man in a farmer's coat is chopping wood beside the Hall, very carefully, as if he has all the time in the world. Every so often he stops and looks at the door."
- **Things to say:**
  - *Greeting:* "I was going to take her home. I expect I still am."
  - *About his wife:* "Bed two hundred and twelve. I sat down for a minute."
  - *If they try to take Pip away:* "He'll sleep in a bit. He always does in the end."
  - *If they offer to bring his wife out:* "You'd do that? Then I'm coming. I'll carry her. I'm good at carrying."
- **Stat block:** Hush Cultist.

**Session by session** *(from the guides' people tables)*
