- **What's going on:** they aren't Hushmen. They're bandits in stolen coats, led by "Sergeant" Rusk, and a peddler they robbed this morning is tied up in the hut.
- **What to do:** Insight DC 13, or anyone who has met a real Hushman: the buttons are bone, not pewter, and the spears are fish-gigs. Pay, bluff (Deception DC 13 to claim to be Court yourself), or fight: *The chain across the road* in the Combat tab. Called out as fakes in front of the peddler, two of the four throw their coats down and run.
- **Reward:** 30 gp and a sack of other people's things in the hut. **A real Hushman's coat** (they took it off a drunk): wearing it gives Advantage on Deception to pass as a Hushman at a distance. **The peddler** is Gammer Tansy. Freed, she gives each of them one oddity from her pack for nothing (see Random magic and wonders), and she remembers them for the rest of the campaign.

### 4. Lights in the fog
> **SAY:** "Fog comes off the Mere at dusk, thick as wool. Out in it, low on the water, two lights blink, twice and then once. On the shore below the road, somebody answers with a shuttered lantern."
- **What's going on:** a Coster night boat landing bottled memories in a cove, out of sight of the harbor and its clerks. Four boatmen (Commoners) and a tally-man, Dace's cousin Lorn (Spy), who has a crossbow and no interest in a fight.
- **What to do:** watch (DC 13 group Stealth check), follow the cart inland, or walk down and ask. Lorn will pay 20 gp to be forgotten. Pressed (Intimidation DC 14), he'll say where the cart's going: the Vennmark bond-house, or Hallowmere's Tithe-house.
- **Reward:** the bribe, or six crates of fine Amnian wine (10 gp a bottle, twelve bottles a crate) if they take the cargo, or a story to tell Sela Maunt, who'll owe them a favor.

### 5. The weeping milestone
> **SAY:** "The milestone says HALLOWMERE 31 in letters worn nearly flat. Salt water is running down its face, though it hasn't rained all day, and the stone is warm when you touch it."
- **What's going on:** a woman named Ottilie paid a memory to the Tithe forty years ago, and the Tithe-man was lazy: he put it into the nearest stone. Whoever touches it sees a few seconds of her last walk along this road with her sister.
- **What to do:** Arcana or Religion DC 13 knows what it is. A *Dispel Magic*, a hammer and a DC 15 Strength check, or a heartfelt request (the stone only wants to be listened to) lets the memory go. The sister, Maud, is alive and very old, in the next village.
- **Reward:** told about it, Maud weeps and gives them her sister's ring (a silver ring worth 25 gp) and the best meal they'll have in Act I. The character who freed the memory gains Heroic Inspiration.

### 6. A wayshrine
> **SAY:** "At the fork stands a little stone shrine no higher than your waist. It's shaped like a bell, with a niche in its side, a dish in the niche and moss on everything. There's something in the dish."
- Roll on Wayshrines in Random magic and wonders.

### 7. Gammer Tansy
> **SAY:** "A mule comes round the bend under a load three times its size: pots, lanterns, birdcages, a mirror, a rocking horse. Walking beside it is a tiny old woman with a clay pipe. 'Buying or selling?' she says. 'I'm both.'"
- See Gammer Tansy in Random magic and wonders.

### 8. A ferry-folk burning
> **SAY:** "Out on the grey water a little boat is burning, slow and steady. On the shore twenty people stand in a line, singing a song with no words. An old woman sees you and walks up the bank to the road."
- **What's going on:** a ferryman's funeral. His family tithed their memories of him to pay their debts, and none of them can remember his face. They need strangers to say his name, Jory Fenn, three times over the water, so somebody living has.
- **What to do:** say it. Someone who sings with them (Performance DC 10) makes it a good one. Insight DC 12: the old woman, his mother, can't remember him either, and is pretending.
- **Reward:** the ferry-folk carve them an oar-token; shown on the Old Shore, any ferry-folk boat takes them anywhere on the Mere for nothing. His mother gives them his knife (a silver-chased dagger worth 25 gp) because "it should go with somebody who knew his name".

### 9. The wreckers' lantern
> **SAY:** "On the cliff path above the road, a lantern is swinging from a pole at the very edge, where no lantern should be. Out at sea, a ship's lights are turning toward it."
- **What's going on:** wreckers want the ship on the rocks by midnight. Three of them (Bandits) and their boss, Nan Scarrow (Bandit Captain), wait in a gully below.
- **What to do:** put the lantern out and light a warning fire on the headland (a DC 12 Survival check to light it fast in the wind), or drive the wreckers off. They come up to stop it: three Bandits and a Bandit Captain, a little under Low for four level 3 characters. They run if Nan drops.
- **Reward:** the ship, the *Saffron Gull* out of Amn, puts in at Pellmoor next day. Her captain pays 25 gp each, and her cargo includes one crate she'll open for them: one roll on the Random magic table.

### 10. The girl with the jar
> **SAY:** "A girl of about nine is sitting on the milestone with a bottle in her lap. It glows faintly. 'Five gold,' she says, holding it up. 'Da says I'm not to come home with it.'"
- **What's going on:** it's her father's memory of her mother, who died. He bottled it because he couldn't bear it, and now he can't bear to keep it.
- **What to do:** buy it for 5 gp. Walk her home and talk to her father, Aldo Brack, a cooper (Influence DC 13; Advantage if they show they understand). Or give her the money and the jar both.
- **Reward:** if the jar goes home and he drinks it back, he weeps, and the whole family will hide the party, feed them or lie for them for the rest of the campaign. Each character who helped gains Heroic Inspiration. Sold on, it fetches 15 gp from Venn.

### 11. The chapel at low tide
> **SAY:** "The tide is out further than you've ever seen it. Half a mile across the wet sand stands a chapel, its roof gone, its door still on its hinges, the water still draining out of its windows."
- **What's going on:** a chapel of Old Pellmoor that drowned in 14 SS. The tide gives them an hour.
- **What to do:** walk out (Survival DC 12 to keep out of the soft sand), and search before the water comes back. The reliquary behind the altar is hidden (Investigation DC 13). Track time: after 50 minutes the sea comes in fast, and getting back is a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check each, or swim the last stretch.
- **Reward:** 2d6 × 5 gp in Old Pellmoor coin (collectors in Hallowmere pay half as much again), a silver chalice worth 50 gp, and one roll on the Random magic table. On the altar, under the weed, the chapel's bell-hymn; the Dawn Mission will pay 25 gp to copy it.

### 12. The crier at the crossroads
> **SAY:** "A Court crier stands on a cart at the crossroads, ringing a handbell, with a little crowd round him. 'Hear the Chancellor's word!' he shouts, and unrolls a paper."
- **What's going on:** the world moving on. Pick one, or roll a d4:
  1. A new curfew in Pellmoor, from sunset to the dawn bell.
  2. A reward of 100 gp for news of "persons interfering with the Tithe", with a rough sketch. If the party has been noticed, the sketch is one of them, badly drawn.
  3. The price of a heartkeep has gone up; the Tithe-house is buying.
  4. A pardon for any debtor who tithes this month. People in the crowd look at each other.
- **Reward:** news. A Persuasion DC 12 afterwards gets a rumor about the next place they're going.

page.title: HALLOWMERE'S STREETS
page.aliases: Hallowmere streets, Grey City streets, Tallow Lane, Tallow Boys, night in Hallowmere
page.body:
**Hallowmere's streets (7.22): the Grey City, its canals and lanes, and the country round it.** For Act II, levels 3 to 5. Roll a d12 when they cross the city, or once a day on the roads outside, or pick. See On the road.

| d12 | What | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A Blank on the bridge | People |
| 2 | The silent procession | People |
| 3 | The book-burning | People |
| 4 | Knives in Tallow Lane | Fight |
| 5 | A wall-shrine | Find |
| 6 | Gammer Tansy | People |
| 7 | The girl on the roofs | People |
| 8 | The Tithe-house cart | Find |
| 9 | Madame Orsini | Oddity |
| 10 | Pistols at dawn | People |
| 11 | The speaking skull | Oddity |
| 12 | Papers, please | News |

### 1. A Blank on the bridge
> **SAY:** "A man in a good coat is standing in the middle of a canal bridge, turning a key over and over in his hands. People walk round him. Across the square, two Hushmen have noticed him too, and they're coming."
- **What's going on:** Tomas Wedd tithed one memory too many this morning and has forgotten where he lives. If the Hushmen get him, he goes to the Tithe-house as a Blank.
- **What to do:** turn out his pockets. The key has a tag, *Pin Lane, 4*, and Investigation DC 12 finds the rest (a letter to his wife). Or stall the Hushmen (Deception or Persuasion DC 14: "He's our uncle, he's drunk"), or walk him away fast (DC 12 group Stealth check).
- **Reward:** his wife, Hanne, hides them in the attic any night in Act II. Tomas was a locksmith, and even now his hands remember: once, he'll open any lock in Hallowmere for them, no roll.

### 2. The silent procession
> **SAY:** "A bell rings once, and the whole street stops. Carts. Children. A woman with her mouth open in the middle of a word. Down the middle of the road comes a line of grey-robed clerks, and nobody makes a sound."
- **What's going on:** a Procession of the Quiet. By law the street is silent until it has passed, about five minutes. A pickpocket is working the frozen crowd, and he's heading for the party.
- **What to do:** stay silent (anyone loud, nervous or with an animal makes a DC 12 Constitution or Performance check). Notice the pickpocket (Perception DC 14) and catch him without a sound (Sleight of Hand or Athletics DC 13). Anyone who speaks is taken aside by a Hushman and fined 5 gp, or a memory.
- **Reward:** the pickpocket, a boy called Wick, is grateful to be let go. He becomes their eyes on the street: once per session, a rumor or a warning.

### 3. The book-burning
> **SAY:** "In the square, clerks are feeding books into a brazier, one at a time, reading out each title before it burns. An old man in ink-stained sleeves stands beside the cart with his hands over his mouth."
- **What's going on:** the Court is burning unlicensed histories of the bells. The bookseller is Absalom Dray (see Shops of Hallowmere).
- **What to do:** swipe a box from the cart (Sleight of Hand DC 13, with a distraction), pose as clerks come to collect "evidence" (Deception DC 14), or buy them out of the fire (a bribe of 20 gp to the senior clerk, Influence DC 12).
- **Reward:** a box of six books. Among them a Spell Scroll (level 1) of the DM's choice, and *A True History of the Concord*: anyone who reads it (an hour) has Advantage on one History or Religion check about the bells. Absalom gives them a discount for life.

### 4. Knives in Tallow Lane
> **SAY:** "Tallow Lane is narrow and dark, and the lamps have been put out. Halfway down, someone steps out of a doorway ahead. Behind you, somebody else does the same."
- **What's going on:** a gang of cutpurses, the Tallow Boys, who think the party looks rich and lost.
- **What to do:** fight (*Knives in Tallow Lane* in the Combat tab for Session 5): four Bandits, the two Tallow brothers (Toughs) and their leader, Silk Annie (Spy), a little under Low for four level 3 characters. A show of strength or magic (Intimidation DC 13) sends them running before it starts. They run when Annie drops or two of them do.
- **Reward:** 15 gp between them, a set of thieves' tools, and Annie's map of the city's back ways: with it, the party never needs a check to get across Hallowmere unseen at night.

### 5. A wall-shrine
> **SAY:** "Set into a wall at the corner of the lane is a niche no bigger than a bread oven, with a little bronze bell hung in it, green with age. Somebody has left something in the dish beneath."
- Roll on Wayshrines in Random magic and wonders.

### 6. Gammer Tansy
> **SAY:** "In the middle of the Grey City, in a street where nobody sells anything without a licence, a mule is eating a window box. Its owner, a tiny old woman with a clay pipe, looks up. 'Oh, it's you. Buying or selling?'"
- See Gammer Tansy in Random magic and wonders. She has never had a licence in her life.

### 7. The girl on the roofs
> **SAY:** "Slates clatter overhead. A girl comes over the gutter and drops into the lane right in front of you, with a leather satchel under her arm and Hushmen shouting on the roof behind her. She looks at you, shoves the satchel into somebody's hands and is gone."
- **What's going on:** Lark is a Harper runner. The satchel holds Court arrest warrants for tomorrow night, twelve names. One is someone they know.
- **What to do:** hide it (Sleight of Hand DC 12 before the Hushmen drop down), hand it over, or run. Two Hushmen arrive in a round; they want the girl, not the party, unless the party gives them a reason.
- **Reward:** the warrants. Warning the twelve saves them, and everybody in their street hears who did it. Lark finds them that night. The Harpers owe them a favor, and Lark will carry one message anywhere in Hallowmere for them, no questions asked.

### 8. The Tithe-house cart
> **SAY:** "A covered cart goes by, heaped with the belongings of people who no longer remember owning them. Shoes. Toys. A clock. It hits a rut, a box falls off the back, and something inside it is glowing."
- **What's going on:** Blanks' belongings, on their way to be sold at the Tithe market. The driver doesn't care what falls off.
- **What to do:** pick it up. The driver shrugs. Or follow the cart to the market (see Shops of Hallowmere).
- **Reward:** one roll on the Random magic table, and a name scratched inside the box lid: Elsa Marrow. If they find her (she's a Blank in the Lamplighters' cistern, or at the Dawn Mission), she won't remember it, but she'll smile at it.

### 9. Madame Orsini
> **SAY:** "A booth in an archway, hung with bead curtains. 'Madame Orsini Reads Keeps,' says the sign. A hand with a great many rings beckons. 'Come, come. One copper. I see the past, the future, and sometimes your mother.'"
- **What's going on:** she's mostly a fraud, but she has a touch of real sight.
- **What to do:** let her read one character. Give the player one line that will be true, from what's coming in your campaign. For example: "You will be asked to choose between a bell and a friend"; "Someone you saved will save you, but not in the way you think"; "You will meet your own face in the snow." Insight DC 15 catches her guessing the rest from their clothes.
- **Reward:** when the prophecy comes true, that character gains Heroic Inspiration.

### 10. Pistols at dawn
> **SAY:** "In a little park by the canal, two young men in good coats are taking off their gloves, very slowly. A third holds a pair of swords and looks as if he might be sick. One of the duellists is very good. The other is fifteen."
- **What's going on:** young Lord Perrin Ashby insulted the Chancellor's nephew, Ser Osric Vale, and Osric means to kill him.
- **What to do:** talk them out of it (Persuasion DC 14, or DC 10 with a good joke that lets Osric keep his pride), take Perrin's place (Osric fights to first blood against an adult: a Knight, and he stops when he's hit), or trick them.
- **Reward:** the Ashby family send a gift of 50 gp and an invitation to supper, and Perrin's older sister, a Court clerk, will tell them one thing from the Chancellor's office. Osric remembers them too.

### 11. The speaking skull
> **SAY:** "The Bone Archive's cart is stopped outside a tavern while the driver drinks. It's full of skulls, each with a paper label tied to it. As you pass, one of them says your name, very quietly."
- **What's going on:** an old Archive skull with a scrap of the bells' magic in it. It belonged to Brother Calloway, a bell-keeper, and it knows things.
- **What to do:** ask it three questions before the driver comes back; it answers like *Speak with Dead*, about the bells and the Concord. Take it (Sleight of Hand DC 12), and it talks at night, which is annoying, and helpful once more.
- **Reward:** three true answers. Taken, it gives one more answer in each later act, then is quiet.

### 12. Papers, please
> **SAY:** "A Hushman checkpoint has been set up overnight across the end of the street, with a table, a clerk and a lamp. 'Papers,' says the clerk, not looking up."
- **What's going on:** the Court tightening its grip. Everyone in Hallowmere is asked for papers now.
- **What to do:** show papers (a forged writ from the Inkwell passes without a roll), bluff (Deception DC 14), turn round (a Hushman notices: DC 13 group Stealth check), or go over the roofs.
- **Reward:** none but getting past. If they're caught, they're fined 10 gp each and their names go on a list, which matters in Session 9.

page.title: THE NORTH ROAD
page.aliases: North Road, ash plain road, bounty-riders, Kettle Marr
page.body:
**The North Road (7.22): the ash plain, Kell's Crossing and the edge of the glass.** For Act III, levels 5 to 6. Roll a d12 once a day, or pick. See On the road.

| d12 | What | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The families going north | People |
| 2 | Ash-storm | Find |
| 3 | The bounty-riders | Fight |
| 4 | The scarecrow field | People |
| 5 | A wayshrine | Find |
| 6 | Gammer Tansy | People |
| 7 | The frozen wagon | Find |
| 8 | The wolf with the splinter | People |
| 9 | The singing ice | Oddity |
| 10 | The burned waystation | People |
| 11 | The falling star | Find |
| 12 | The pigeon | News |

### 1. The families going north
> **SAY:** "Ahead, a line of carts has stopped on the road. Children sit on bundles. A man is lying under the last cart, cursing at a wheel. A woman runs back to you and grabs your arm. 'Riders,' she says. 'An hour behind us. Maybe less.'"
- **What's going on:** six families running from the Tithe toward Kell's Crossing, with Court riders on their trail.
- **What to do:** fix the wheel (a DC 12 check with tools, or a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check to hold the axle while somebody else does), carry the children, or lay a false trail for the riders (Survival DC 14). If they fail, the riders catch up: run *The bounty-riders* (entry 3), or let them talk the riders off.
- **Reward:** the families reach the Crossing and tell everyone. The party eat and sleep free there, and one mother gives them a carved wooden bell on a cord: hold it and pray, once, and gain Heroic Inspiration.

### 2. Ash-storm
> **SAY:** "The sky turns the color of a dirty sheet. Then the wind comes, full of grey ash, and the world shrinks to the length of your arm."
- **What's going on:** a storm off the old burn-scars. It lasts 1d4 hours.
- **What to do:** press on (a DC 12 Constitution saving throw each hour, or 1 level of Exhaustion), or shelter. Survival DC 13 finds a half-buried coach. Inside it is a dead Court courier and his satchel.
- **Reward:** the satchel holds a sealed letter (the Court's orders for the road north: where its patrols will be for the next three days, so the party can avoid them) and one roll on the Random magic table. The courier's horse is still alive, tied to the coach and terrified: Animal Handling DC 12 and it's theirs (a riding horse, worth 75 gp).

### 3. The bounty-riders
> **SAY:** "Riders on the ridge: eight of them, in grey coats, with a man in a wide hat at the front. He takes a paper out of his coat, looks at it, looks at you, and folds it away. 'Afternoon,' he calls. 'I think you're worth a good deal of money.'"
- **What's going on:** Kettle Marr is a bounty-rider with a Court warrant and the party's descriptions. Five of his riders are Hushmen (one a sergeant), and two are trackers.
- **What to do:** fight (*The bounty-riders* in the Combat tab), talk (Marr's paid by the head, so a better offer works: Influence DC 15, or DC 12 with 100 gp), or outrun them (a DC 14 group Survival check to lose them in the ash).
- **Reward:** Marr's purse (40 gp), the warrant (it lists what the Court knows about each of them, which is worth reading), and eight horses. Let Marr go, and he turns up in Act IV with a new warrant, or with a job.

### 4. The scarecrow field
> **SAY:** "A field of scarecrows, a hundred of them, standing in rows on the ash where a crop used to be. Each one wears real clothes: a farmer's smock, a girl's dress, a soldier's coat. As you pass, one of them turns its head."
- **What's going on:** the villagers dressed the scarecrows in the clothes of people who were taken. The one that moved is Pell Hartigan, a farmer, hiding from the Court in his own scarecrow coat.
- **What to do:** Perception DC 12 notices he's breathing. Talk him down (Influence DC 12); he's terrified.
- **Reward:** Pell tells them about the kilns on the plain where the Grey Coats keep what they steal (The kilns at Kell's Crossing), and the back way into the store kiln. He gives them a sack of apples and the best directions on the plain.

### 5. A wayshrine
> **SAY:** "A cairn of grey stones by the road, with a little iron bell hung from a stake on top, frosted white. At its foot, a flat stone with something on it."
- Roll on Wayshrines in Random magic and wonders.

### 6. Gammer Tansy
> **SAY:** "Out of the ash, of all the places in the world, comes a mule with a birdcage on its back and a tiny old woman leading it, smoking a clay pipe. 'You do get about,' she says. 'Buying or selling?'"
- See Gammer Tansy in Random magic and wonders. Ask her how she got here and she says, "Walked."

### 7. The frozen wagon
> **SAY:** "At the edge of the glass a merchant's wagon has stopped in the middle of the road, its two horses frozen mid-stride and its driver frozen with the whip raised. Glass has grown over all of them like frost. The back of the wagon has not been touched."
- **What's going on:** they were caught when Glassreach froze. The driver, Jem Sorrel, is Stilled, not dead.
- **What to do:** reach the cargo (no check) or cut the cargo free of the glass (glass-cutting tools, or a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check; failure is loud, and a Glass-Wolf comes to look in 1d4 rounds; it goes away if it's hit once).
- **Reward:** Jem's strongbox: 3d10 gp, four warm cloaks (worth 10 gp each, and they matter on the glass), a cask of brandy, and one roll on the Random magic table. If the thaw comes, Jem wakes, and he remembers the faces of whoever left his strongbox alone, or didn't.

### 8. The wolf with the splinter
> **SAY:** "Tracks round your camp in the morning, big ones, circling and circling. Then you see it: a Glass-Wolf lying in the snow fifty feet away, watching you. It's holding one forepaw off the ground, and it's whining."
- **What's going on:** a young Glass-Wolf with a shard of the glass in its paw. It's alone and in pain.
- **What to do:** approach (Animal Handling DC 15; Advantage with food) and pull the shard (Medicine DC 12). Attacked, it runs.
- **Reward:** it follows the party at a distance for the rest of Act III. Once, it howls before an ambush: the party can't be Surprised, and they have Advantage on Initiative. In the Frost Spire, the echo-stair wolves hesitate one round when they smell it on the party.

### 9. The singing ice
> **SAY:** "At dusk the ice in a frozen stream begins to sing: not wind, a tune, high and slow, with words you almost catch. It stops when the sun goes."
- **What's going on:** it's the old hymn of Hieme, the same one the choir sang in the Frost Spire, frozen into the stream when the glass came.
- **What to do:** listen and learn it (a DC 12 Performance or Intelligence check, or write it down). It sings again tomorrow at dusk.
- **Reward:** anyone who learned it has Advantage on the Performance check to sing the hymn in the Frost Spire's choir loft, and a bard can use it as a song that gives Heroic Inspiration to one listener, once.

### 10. The burned waystation
> **SAY:** "The waystation on Yara's map is a black shell, burned out weeks ago. But there's smoke from somewhere under it, and when you come close, the smoke stops."
- **What's going on:** a deserter from the Court, Hushman Brannoc, is hiding in the cellar. He set the fire to make people think it was empty.
- **What to do:** talk him out (Influence DC 12; he's starving and ashamed), or force it (he's a Hushman, and he gives up when hit).
- **Reward:** the cellar is full of the waystation's stores: rations for a week, oil, a tent, rope, 2 Potions of Healing. Brannoc tells them the Court's patrol routes and its signal-horns. If they let him go home, he does. If they take him along, he's useful and nervous.

### 11. The falling star
> **SAY:** "A light falls out of the sky, bright enough to throw shadows, and hits the plain a mile off the road with a sound like a door slamming. When you get there, there's a crater, still steaming, and in it something black that ticks as it cools."
- **What's going on:** a lump of star-iron, the size of a loaf.
- **What to do:** dig it out (a DC 12 Strength (Athletics) check; without gloves, 1d6 Fire damage) before the villagers from the Crossing come to look.
- **Reward:** star-iron is worth 100 gp to any smith, 150 gp to the Ironhorn. Bruna Hardshale or a Brassfall smith will make a weapon from it for nothing, just to have done it: a Moon-Touched Sword that also shines like a star in moonlight.

### 12. The pigeon
> **SAY:** "A pigeon drops out of the sky and lands on someone's shoulder, exhausted, with a tiny case on its leg. Then it goes to sleep."
- **What's going on:** a message from somebody to somebody else. Pick one, or roll a d4:
  1. A Court officer to Isolde Drave: the party's route, wrong in an important way.
  2. A farmer to his son in Hallowmere: "Come home. The Tithe-man's gone."
  3. Yara to a buyer in Hallowmere: what she's selling, and her prices, higher than she charges the party.
  4. Written in a hand nobody knows: "Don't go up the Spire by the front."
- **Reward:** news. Send the pigeon on, and it finds its way home.

page.title: THE BRASS ROAD AND THE STEPPE
page.aliases: Brass Road travel, steppe road, storm country, lightning tree, deserters
page.body:
**The Brass Road and the steppe (7.22): bronze mountains, the storm country, the Ironhorn grass and the roads to the Tor.** For Acts IV and V, levels 7 to 11. Roll a d12 once a day, or pick. See On the road.

| d12 | What | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The lightning tree | Find |
| 2 | The bronze carts | People |
| 3 | The salvage riders | Fight |
| 4 | The sleeping village | Oddity |
| 5 | A wayshrine | Find |
| 6 | Gammer Tansy | People |
| 7 | The dead courier | News |
| 8 | The giant's cairn | Find |
| 9 | The dreamer at the well | People |
| 10 | The deserters | Fight |
| 11 | The horse-fair | People |
| 12 | The weather | News |

### 1. The lightning tree
> **SAY:** "A lone oak stands on the hillside, split down the middle by lightning, years ago. It's still crackling. Blue light crawls up and down the wound, and every hair on your arms stands up when you come near."
- **What's going on:** a storm-stone has grown in the heart of the tree, fed by lightning that had nowhere else to go.
- **What to do:** cut it out (a DC 14 Strength check with an axe or a pick). Each attempt, the cutter makes a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw: 2d10 Lightning damage, half on a success. Gloves of anything but metal give Advantage.
- **Reward:** a storm-stone, worth 100 gp in Brassfall or to the Ironhorn. Or take it to a Brassfall storm-smith, who binds it into a Javelin of Lightning (uncommon) for 100 gp and the stone.

### 2. The bronze carts
> **SAY:** "A line of bronze carts comes down the road toward you, a dozen of them, each pulled by two oxen. Every wheel is humming. The carters keep looking at the sky."
- **What's going on:** a Brassfall cart-train, carrying bronze to the steppe. A storm is coming, and if lightning hits a cart, it hits them all. Their quartermaster is Sallow Kett (see Shops of the Brass Road).
- **What to do:** help them earth the carts with chains into wet ground before the storm (a DC 13 Arcana check, or tinker's or smith's tools, or three DC 12 Strength checks in a row), or shelter with them under the rocks.
- **Reward:** the carters pay 50 gp and let the party buy from Kett's cart at a tenth off. If a cart is hit, it's a terrible noise, and everyone has seen it.

### 3. The salvage riders
> **SAY:** "Four riders come over the grass at a canter, with axes on their saddles and horns on their helmets, and they rein in in a circle round you. The leader leans down from her saddle. 'That's a lot of iron,' she says. 'You don't need all of it.'"
- **What's going on:** Ironhorn salvagers, led by Hask Torvi (if you ran *Four riders* in Session 16A, these are the same four, and they remember the party), who take metal from travellers to melt in the Heart-Hall. They're not killers. They're hungry for iron, and they respect nerve.
- **What to do:** fight (four Ironhorn Riders, using the Warrior Veteran, a Low encounter for four level 7 characters; they stop when two are down), give them something metal they'd value (a weapon or armor worth 25 gp or more), or win it off them: a challenge (an arm-wrestle, a horse race, a drinking match) at DC 15. They respect a good loser almost as much.
- **Reward:** a win or a fair gift makes Hask a friend: she rides to the Thane's camp ahead of them and tells him they're worth meeting (Advantage on the first check of the steppe contest, Session 17A). A fight won gets their horses and 60 gp in hack-silver, and the Ironhorn hear about it.

### 4. The sleeping village
> **SAY:** "The village is quiet. Smoke from the chimneys, a cart in the lane, chickens in the road, and nobody moving. Through a window, you see a family at their table, asleep in their chairs, smiling."
- **What's going on:** it's near the Tor. The Hush has reached out a little further than it used to, and the village fell asleep at supper two days ago. They're dreaming the same dream: a room full of beds.
- **What to do:** wake one (anything loud works for a minute; a *Lesser Restoration* wakes one person for good). The child Tam wakes first and is very cross.
- **Reward:** Tam says what everyone in the village was dreaming, which is the Sleeping Hall, exactly. Anyone who listens has Advantage on the first check to find their way inside, Session 16B. If the party wakes everyone, the village will take them in for as long as they need.

### 5. A wayshrine
> **SAY:** "A wayshrine of bronze, green with age, stands beside the road with a little bell in its roof. The bell is humming. In the dish beneath it, something's been left."
- Roll on Wayshrines in Random magic and wonders.

### 6. Gammer Tansy
> **SAY:** "On a mountain road a long way from anywhere, there's the mule, and the pots, and the old woman with her pipe. 'You look older,' she says. 'Buying or selling?'"
- See Gammer Tansy in Random magic and wonders. By now she has a few things she didn't have before.

### 7. The dead courier
> **SAY:** "A horse grazes by the road with an empty saddle. Fifty feet away, in the grass, lies its rider, in Court grey, an arrow in his back and a satchel still under his arm."
- **What's going on:** a Court courier killed by somebody who didn't know what he was carrying. Two days dead.
- **What to do:** search him. Investigation DC 13 on the arrow: it's Hush Cult fletching. Medicine DC 12: he was running, not fighting.
- **Reward:** the satchel holds orders for the Court's strike force: its route, its numbers, its date (useful in Session 19A). His purse holds 30 gp, his horse is a Court warhorse (worth 400 gp; branded).

### 8. The giant's cairn
> **SAY:** "At the top of the pass stands a cairn as tall as a house, built of stones no human could lift. A door of bronze is set into its side, green and shut, and above it a face is carved, with its mouth open."
- **What's going on:** a storm giant's grave from before the Concord. The door is a puzzle: The echo door, in Puzzles.
- **What to do:** solve the door, or break it (a DC 22 Strength check, or 60 damage to AC 19 bronze). Breaking it brings the thunder: everyone within 60 feet makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or takes 3d8 Thunder damage and is Deafened for an hour.
- **Reward:** the giant's grave goods: 200 gp in ancient bronze rings (collectors in Brassfall pay double), a drinking horn as big as a man, and two rolls on the Random magic table. On the giant's chest, a carved stone plate that shows Thrane, ringing.

### 9. The dreamer at the well
> **SAY:** "An old man sits by a well at the roadside with a bucket beside him and a cup in his hand. 'You'll want water,' he says. 'And I'll want a story. I dreamed one last night that I can't finish. Perhaps you know the end.'"
- **What's going on:** Hob Ellery dreams other people's memories, the ones that were tithed, as if they float up from somewhere. Last night he dreamed one of the party's.
- **What to do:** ask him to tell it. Ask the player what memory it was: something they gave up, or lost, or never told the table. Tell it back to them in Hob's words. They can finish it for him.
- **Reward:** water and a night's rest by the well. The character gains Heroic Inspiration, and the player gets a scene about their character that nobody else could have planned.

### 10. The deserters
> **SAY:** "Ten soldiers in Court grey are sitting round a fire that's mostly smoke. Their banner is wrapped round a stick, and one of them is cooking a crow. When they see you, the sergeant gets up slowly and puts his hand on his sword."
- **What's going on:** Court soldiers who've had enough. Their warden, Corran Holloway, wants to get his people home, and he'll fight if he thinks the party are sent to bring them back.
- **What to do:** talk (Influence DC 13; show them food or the party's own trouble with the Court, and it's DC 10), fight (*The deserters* in the Combat tab), or slip by (DC 14 group Stealth check).
- **Reward:** fed and pointed home, they give up everything they won't need: 50 gp, two Potions of Greater Healing, and the Court's camp passwords for the month. In Session 22, if the party need people, Holloway brings six of them back.

### 11. The horse-fair
> **SAY:** "There's a town of tents in the grass, and a thousand horses, and a noise like a storm: hooves, shouting, bells, somebody singing in a language you don't know. An Ironhorn horse-fair, and everyone is welcome who doesn't steal."
- **What's going on:** an Ironhorn fair, where horses, iron and gossip change hands.
- **What to do:** buy horses (see Shops of the Brass Road), enter the race (a DC 15 Wisdom (Animal Handling) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, three in a row, against the best rider of the fair), or listen (Persuasion DC 12: news of the Thane, of the Court, and of the Cult).
- **Reward:** the race's prize is a warhorse (worth 400 gp) and the right to sit at the Thane's table. Losing gets cheered almost as loudly.

### 12. The weather
> **SAY:** "The sky changes. You'd swear it was listening."
- **What's going on:** the weather follows the bells. Say what's true in your campaign:
  - If Thrane has rung: a proper rain, the first in a hundred years. Children are dancing in it.
  - If Thrane hasn't: dry thunder, and lightning that crawls along the ground.
  - If Mirel has rung: people stop on the road, smiling, as if they've remembered something nice.
  - If neither: a grey stillness, and everyone talking quietly.
- **Reward:** none, except that the players see what they've done.

page.title: RANDOM MAGIC AND WONDERS
page.aliases: random magic item, random magic, magic item table, wonders, wayshrine, wayshrines, Gammer Tansy, Patience, peddler, oddities, trinkets
page.body:
**Random magic and wonders (7.22): what turns up in a dish, a wreck, a pawnshop box or a dead man's satchel.** Use it whenever a page says "one roll on the Random magic table", or whenever the party searches somewhere that deserves a surprise.

**Random magic (d20).** Every result has a "where it came from" line; read it out, and the item has a past.
1. **Potion of Healing,** in a little stoppered bottle with a Dawn Mission sun pressed into the wax.
2. **Spell Scroll** (level 1) of your choice, rolled round a candle stub and tied with a hair-ribbon.
3. **Potion of Climbing,** brown and gritty. The label says *For the Spire roof. Don't look down.*
4. **Moon-Touched Sword,** a plain shortsword that sheds moonlight in the dark. The hilt is wrapped in a woman's scarf.
5. **Clockwork Amulet,** ticking quietly, engraved *O.F.* (Osgood Fennick's work; he'll be delighted to see it again).
6. **Cloak of Many Fashions,** grey until somebody wishes it were otherwise.
7. **Orb of Direction,** a glass marble with a needle of light that always points north. It was a sailor's.
8. **Horn of Silent Alarm,** a ram's horn with a Hushman's number burned into it.
9. **Candle of the Deep,** fat and green, smelling of the sea. It burns under water.
10. **Pole of Collapsing,** a walking stick that folds down to a foot long, with a fisherman's initials.
11. **Rope of Mending,** 50 feet of hemp that knits itself back together. Somebody has tied a bell to one end.
12. **Tankard of Sobriety,** pewter, dented, with *NOT TONIGHT* scratched on the bottom.
13. **Mystery Key,** brass, warm, on a string. It opens one lock, once, and nobody knows which.
14. **Talking Doll,** a rag doll that says six things in a child's voice. You choose them; one should be heartbreaking.
15. **Bead of Nourishment,** in a twist of paper, with a note: *For the road north.*
16. **Potion of Water Breathing,** green, with a tiny fish drawn on the label.
17. **Potion of Resistance,** of whichever damage the party will need next; its color says which.
18. **Potion of Greater Healing,** in a heavy blue bottle, very old and still good.
19. **Driftglobe,** a glass ball that glows when its word is spoken. The word is scratched on it, very small, in Old Pellmoor.
20. **Something wonderful (d6):** 1 Immovable Rod; 2 Sending Stones (the other is somewhere you'll want to go); 3 Goggles of Night; 4 Wand of Secrets; 5 Gloves of Swimming and Climbing; 6 Sentinel Shield. At most one of these an act; after that, roll again.

**Wayshrines.** Little bell-shrines older than the Ninefold Church stand at crossroads and fords all over Corvane, from the days when each of the seven bells had its own wayside saint. Folk still leave things in them: what you leave, the next traveler takes. Leave something and take something; that's the whole rule.
- **What's in the dish (d8):**
  1. A clay cup of good wine, still full. Drink it, and gain Heroic Inspiration.
  2. A child's drawing of a bell, very carefully colored, and 3 gp.
  3. One roll on the Random magic table, wrapped in a handkerchief.
  4. A letter addressed *To whoever needs this*. It's a kind letter. Whoever reads it gains 1d6 Temporary Hit Points each morning for a week.
  5. A heartkeep, and a note: *I don't want it. Maybe you do.* The memory is sweet and not the reader's.
  6. A silver bell-charm worth 10 gp. Worn, it rings when someone lies to the wearer. Once.
  7. Nothing, but somebody has written on the shrine: *Sorry. Back soon.* in a hand one of the party knows.
  8. A Potion of Healing and a sprig of rosemary.
- **Leave something you'll miss** (a keepsake, a letter, a weapon you love), and the character who left it gains Heroic Inspiration. Once per act, per character. What they left turns up later, in somebody else's hands, when it matters.
- **Rob a shrine without leaving anything** and nothing happens, except that the next shrine they come to is empty.

**Gammer Tansy and her mule, Patience.** A tiny old woman with a clay pipe and a mule under a load of pots, birdcages, lanterns, a mirror and a rocking horse. She turns up on every road in Corvane, often before the party gets there, and she won't say how. She buys anything, sells anything, and talks to Patience as an equal.
- **She says:** "Buying or selling?" / "Patience doesn't like you. That's a compliment; she doesn't like anybody." / "I've walked further than that for less."
- **She sells** ordinary gear at the usual price, but only what's on the mule, and always one thing they'll need in the next session (a rope, a warm coat, a crowbar). She buys anything at half its price, and keeps at their value.
- **What else is on the mule (d20).** Each costs 1d10 gp, or a good trade.
  1. A brass spyglass that shows tomorrow's weather.
  2. A jar of fireflies that never die.
  3. A boot with a mouse living in it. The mouse is very well mannered.
  4. A map of a town that doesn't exist. Yet.
  5. A tin soldier with a Hushman's face.
  6. A handbell that rings a note that makes dogs sit.
  7. Seven keys on a ring, all the same.
  8. A pipe that blows smoke in the shape of whatever the smoker is thinking about.
  9. A glass eye that blinks.
  10. A book of blank pages that are always warm.
  11. A music box that plays a song nobody at the table has heard, and everyone can hum afterwards.
  12. A tiny portrait of one of the party, painted years ago.
  13. A walking stick with a compass in the knob.
  14. A Potion of Healing, a little cloudy. It works.
  15. A pair of red shoes that are a size too big for everybody.
  16. A stoppered bottle of sea-fog.
  17. A deck of cards with one card missing: the one they draw.
  18. A wooden bird that sings at dawn.
  19. A bottled memory of a perfect summer's day. Nobody's; she made it, she says.
  20. One roll on the Random magic table. "Oh, that. I'd forgotten I had that."
- **One true thing.** Every time they meet her, she tells them one rumor about the next place they're going, and it's always true.
- **The bell on Patience's collar.** Ask about it, and she says, "Spoken for." At the last meeting of the campaign she unhooks it and gives it to whoever has been kindest to Patience. It isn't magic. It rings a note nobody can name, and whoever carries it gains Heroic Inspiration at the start of the last session.

**Places of wonder (d10).** For a long road, a lost party, or a session that needs one strange good thing. Most hold a find.
1. **The drowned belfry.** A church tower stands up out of a lake, its bell still hanging. Swim out and ring it, and every fish in the lake comes to the surface to listen. Under the bell, on a ledge: one roll on the Random magic table.
2. **The tree of keys.** An oak hung with hundreds of keys on ribbons, left by people who'd lost a home. One key is still warm (a Mystery Key).
3. **The giant's chair.** A stone throne a hundred feet tall on a hilltop. Climb it (DC 13 Athletics), and from the seat they can see two days of road in every direction: Advantage on Survival checks to navigate for the rest of the journey.
4. **The upside-down waterfall.** A stream falls up a cliff into the clouds. A coin thrown in comes back down an hour later as a different coin, from a country nobody knows (worth 10 gp to a collector).
5. **The ghost market.** On the first night of the new moon, a market of lantern-lit stalls appears in a ruined square, kept by smiling, silent people from three hundred years ago. They take old coin and memories, and they sell one roll on the Random magic table for a memory of a meal. At dawn it's gone, and so is anything they didn't pay for.
6. **The library in the hill.** A door in a grassy mound opens on a dry room of shelves: a bell-keeper's library, sealed before the Concord. One book is a Spell Scroll (level 2) of your choice, and one is a history that gives Advantage on a History check about the bells.
7. **The statue that moved.** A stone knight by the road, pointing. Every time they pass, it's pointing somewhere else. Follow where it points, and in a mile there's a cairn, and in the cairn 3d10 gp and a Potion of Healing.
8. **The singing stones.** A ring of standing stones that hum when the wind blows. Stand in the middle and sing, and they sing it back in harmony. A bard who does it learns a song that grants Heroic Inspiration to one listener, once.
9. **The wreck in the trees.** A ship, a whole ship, wedged in the branches of a forest, forty feet up, a hundred miles from the sea. In the captain's cabin: a log that ends mid-sentence, 2d10 gp, and one roll on the Random magic table.
10. **The well that answers.** Drop a coin in and ask a question; the well answers yes or no, in your own voice, and it's right. It takes one coin a question, and three questions a lifetime.

page.title: PUZZLES
page.aliases: puzzle, puzzles, riddle, riddles, puzzle door, puzzle lock, hint ladder
page.body:
**Puzzles (7.22): how to run them, and six to drop in anywhere.** The side dungeons each have one puzzle of their own now (marked 7.22 on their pages). These six are for a door, a vault or a tomb you want to make memorable.

**How to run a puzzle.**
- **Never block the main road.** A puzzle guards a treasure, a shortcut or a secret, never the only way on.
- **Give the clue freely.** Anyone who looks at the room sees the clue without a roll. The roll is for understanding it, not finding it.
- **The hint ladder.** Stuck for five minutes of real time? A character with a good Intelligence, Wisdom or a matching skill makes a DC 12 check and you give a nudge. Stuck for ten? Give the answer through the world: a ghost, a carved line, an NPC, a Talking Doll. No puzzle should take more than fifteen minutes.
- **Brute force always works, at a cost:** a noise, a hurt, a lost treasure, an alarm. Say what the cost is before they try.
- **Reward the solve.** A clever answer gets Heroic Inspiration for whoever said it, and the best treasure in the room.

### 1. The seven-bells door
> **SAY:** "A round bronze door, and set into it seven small bells in a ring, each with a different mark: a sun, an eye, a snowflake, a sheaf of wheat, a lightning bolt, a crescent moon, and one with no mark at all. Above them, a line is carved: SIX TO WAKE THE WORLD, AND ONE TO LET IT SLEEP."
- **The answer:** ring the six in the order of the Concord (Vaer the Dawn, Ossa the Memory, Hieme the Winter, Calla the Harvest, Thrane the Storms, Mirel the Dreams), and leave the seventh, Ysh, silent.
- **Clues:** the order is in the Concord hymn, which any cleric, bard, or anybody raised in Corvane knows (Religion DC 10). Ringing the unmarked bell makes every other bell go quiet: the door is resetting.
- **Brute force:** the door is AC 19 with 50 Hit Points, or a DC 20 Strength check. Every blow rings all seven at once: everyone within 30 feet makes a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or is Deafened for an hour.
- **Reward:** behind it, a bell-keeper's cell: 4d10 gp in old coin and one roll on the Random magic table. Whoever rang the last bell gains Heroic Inspiration.

### 2. The two heads
> **SAY:** "Two stone heads are set into the wall between two doors, one smiling, one frowning. 'One of us always tells the truth,' says the smiling head. 'And one of us always lies,' says the frowning one. 'One door goes on. One door goes down. Ask one of us one question.'"
- **The answer:** ask either head, "Which door would the other head say goes on?" and take the other door. (Both heads point at the wrong door.)
- **Clues:** the heads bicker. Get them talking (they're bored; Persuasion DC 10) and each says something about the other that the players can check.
- **Brute force:** pick a door and open it. The wrong one is a 20-foot drop into water (2d6 Bludgeoning damage, DC 13 Dexterity saving throw for half), and the heads laugh for a full minute.
- **Reward:** the right door leads on. Under the smiling head's chin, a coin-slot holds what the last visitors paid: 2d10 gp and a Potion of Healing.

### 3. The weighing scales
> **SAY:** "A pair of great bronze scales stand on a dais. In one pan, a heavy stone. The other pan is empty, and on its rim are the words: WHAT WEIGHS MORE THAN GOLD?"
- **The answer:** a memory. Somebody stands in the empty pan and tells a true happy memory aloud, to the whole table, and the pan sinks.
- **Clues:** gold, weapons and stones don't move it. Lies don't either: the pan rises a little, as if amused (Insight DC 10 notices).
- **Brute force:** pull the pan down by hand (a DC 18 Strength check), and the scales take a memory anyway. The player chooses something their character forgets, and writes it in the Memory ledger.
- **Reward:** the stone pan rises and opens. In it: a heartkeep worth 50 gp, and one roll on the Random magic table. The player who told the memory gains Heroic Inspiration.

### 4. The sun-floor
> **SAY:** "The floor is a great bronze sundial, its hours marked in a ring of tiles. In the middle stands the pointer. Hanging from the ceiling on a chain is an iron lantern, cold. Over the far door is carved: OPEN AT THE HOUR OF THE DAWN BELL."
- **The answer:** light the lantern and swing it on its chain until the pointer's shadow falls on the sixth hour (the dawn bell rings at six). Hold it there, and the door opens.
- **Clues:** the lantern chain can be hooked at different points along a rail on the ceiling (Investigation DC 10). The tile of the sixth hour is worn by old feet.
- **Brute force:** pry the door with a crowbar (DC 15 Strength). The floor tilts, and everyone on it makes a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw or slides into the pit in the middle: 10 feet, 1d6 Bludgeoning damage.
- **Reward:** behind the door, an old vestry: two Potions of Healing, a Spell Scroll (level 1) of your choice, and a bronze sun worth 25 gp.

### 5. The echo door
> **SAY:** "A face is carved over the door, its mouth wide open. When you speak, it says your words back to you, a moment later, from somewhere deep inside the stone. Carved under its chin: SPEAK MY NAME AND I WILL ANSWER. NOBODY HAS EVER SEEN ME. YOU HAVE HEARD ME ALL YOUR LIFE."
- **The answer:** "Echo." Say it, and the face says it back, louder each time, until the door opens.
- **Clues:** the face repeats everything except questions. Asked one, it's silent. (It's an echo; it can only give back.)
- **Brute force:** break it (scale the door to the place: at the giant's cairn on the Brass Road it's a DC 22 Strength check). Breaking it lets the stored sound out: everyone within 60 feet makes a Constitution saving throw (DC 13, or DC 15 above level 6), taking 3d8 Thunder damage and Deafened for an hour on a failure.
- **Reward:** whatever the place holds. Whoever said "Echo" gains Heroic Inspiration.

### 6. The three caskets
> **SAY:** "Three caskets on a table: gold, silver and lead. On each lid, a line. Gold: THE KEY IS IN THIS CASKET. Silver: THE KEY IS NOT IN THIS CASKET. Lead: THE KEY IS NOT IN THE GOLD CASKET. Under them, on the table: ONLY ONE OF US TELLS THE TRUTH."
- **The answer:** silver. (If the key were in gold, gold and silver would both be true. If it were in lead, silver and lead would both be true. Only with the key in silver is exactly one line true: lead's.)
- **Clues:** let them reason it out. A DC 13 Intelligence check gives the first step: "If the key were in the gold casket, what else would be true?"
- **Brute force:** open the wrong casket, or smash them. Each wrong casket puffs sleeping dust: DC 13 Constitution saving throw or Unconscious for 1 minute (another creature can wake them with an action). Smashing the silver casket breaks the key's glass vial, and whatever it opens stays locked unless they break that too.
- **Reward:** the key opens whatever you like: a strongbox, a cell, a secret door. In the silver casket with it: a Potion of Greater Healing, wrapped in velvet.

page.title: SHOPS OF PELLMOOR
page.aliases: shop, shops, shopkeeper, shopkeepers, merchant, trader, buy, sell, haggle, Pellmoor shops
page.body:
**Shops of Pellmoor (7.22): Strangers' Row, the Quays and the Old Shore.** Everyone in Pellmoor who'll trade with the party, what they have, and what they might have today. Uncommon items can also be ordered through the Vennmark Coster or Smiling Dace, and take a week.

**How shops work (7.22).**
- **Prices** are the 2024 rules prices. Common magic items cost 100 gp and uncommon ones 400 gp; potions and scrolls cost half that. Rare items are never for sale: they're found.
- **Something special.** Each time the party visits a trader, roll a d6. On a 1 to 4, it's the usual stock. On a 5, the trader has their **good find**. On a 6, they have **something that shouldn't be here**. Once a special item is sold, it's gone.
- **Selling.** Traders buy ordinary gear at half its price, if they want it at all. Magic items sell for half their price, and only to the traders who say they buy them.
- **Keeps.** Traders who take keeps (heartkeeps) value one at 25 to 100 gp, depending on the memory. The player chooses which memory, and writes it in the Memory ledger.
- **Haggling.** Persuasion DC 15 takes a tenth off; DC 20 takes a fifth. Fail by 5 or more and the price goes up a tenth, and that trader won't haggle again this visit. Some traders say what works better than Persuasion.

### Bruna Hardshale, the smithy on Strangers' Row
> **SAY:** "Heat, and a hammer going like a heartbeat. The smith is a dwarf with arms like hawsers and her beard tied up out of the sparks. She looks at your weapons before she looks at your faces."
- **Says:** "Gold or keeps, I don't care which. Bronze, I care about." / "Who sharpened this? Never let them near it again."
- **Stock:** longsword 15 gp, shortsword 10 gp, rapier 25 gp, battleaxe 10 gp, warhammer 15 gp, handaxe 5 gp, spear 1 gp, crossbow bolts (20) 1 gp, chain shirt 50 gp, scale mail 50 gp, chain mail 75 gp, shield 10 gp. Breastplate (400 gp) and half plate (750 gp) to order, in a week. Repairs for nothing if she likes you. Silvering a weapon or ten bolts: 100 gp, a day.
- **Good find (5):** a **Moon-Touched Sword** (common, 100 gp), a longsword she made "for practice".
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Mithral Chain Shirt** (uncommon, 400 gp), from Mirabar. A cousin owed her; she'll sell it only to someone she thinks will get it scratched properly.
- **Buys:** any bronze at twice its weight in silver, and good weapons at half price. She doesn't buy magic. "Not my trade."
- **Haggling:** she doesn't. Bring her bronze, or a story about a fight that's actually true (Insight DC 10 says she can tell), and she takes a fifth off.

### Ulm Teasel, chandler
> **SAY:** "A shop like the inside of a ship's hold: rope in coils to the ceiling, lanterns hanging like fruit, barrels, sacks, nets. The chandler is a small, sad man with very clean hands."
- **Says:** "Everything for the road, and nothing for the heart." / "You'll want more rope than that. Everyone always wants more rope than that."
- **Stock:** rope (50 feet) 1 gp, hooded lantern 5 gp, oil 1 sp a flask, rations 5 sp a day, tent 2 gp, bedroll 1 gp, blanket 5 sp, climber's kit 25 gp, healer's kit 5 gp, crowbar 2 gp, grappling hook 2 gp, chain (10 feet) 5 gp, caltrops 1 gp, ball bearings 1 gp, waterskin 2 sp, shovel 2 gp, manacles 2 gp, torches 1 cp each, candles 1 cp each.
- **Good find (5):** a **Candle of the Deep** (common, 50 gp), "for divers".
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a coil of **Rope of Climbing** (uncommon) on the shelf with the rest, priced as rope, 1 gp. Ulm doesn't know. *Detect Magic*, or Arcana DC 15 from anyone who handles it, notices it's knotting itself. If they tell him, he looks at it a long time and then says, "Still 1 gp. Honesty's worth something."
- **Buys:** ordinary gear at half price. No magic, no keeps.

### Pim Coyle, the Quays chandlery
> **SAY:** "A bow-fronted shop on the Quays, hung with oilskins and fishing gear. The man behind the counter is all smile and no eyes."
- **Says:** "Boat hire by the day. No questions by the hour." / "Whatever you heard about the cellar, you heard it from somebody else."
- **Stock:** oilskin coat 5 gp, net 1 gp, fishing gear 1 gp, pitch, sailcloth, hooded lantern 5 gp, rope 1 gp, rowboat hire 2 gp a day (or 50 gp to buy).
- **Good find (5):** a **Potion of Water Breathing** (uncommon, 200 gp). "Off a diver. He won't need it."
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a set of **Mariner's Armor** (uncommon, scale mail, 400 gp), taken off a drowned man and sold as a curiosity.
- **Buys:** anything off a boat. If the Undertow are still in business below him, he buys stolen bottles too, at 3 gp each.

### Smiling Dace, the fence on Strangers' Row
> **SAY:** "A back room behind a pawn-shop, warm and smelling of oranges. A thin man in a very good coat smiles at you, and keeps smiling, all the time you're there."
- **Says:** "I don't know you. That's the arrangement." / "Everything has a price. I'm just the one who knows it."
- **Stock:** thieves' tools 25 gp, disguise kit 25 gp, forgery kit 15 gp, poisoner's kit 50 gp, a vial of basic poison 100 gp. Uncommon magic to order: 400 gp plus a tenth, a week, no questions.
- **Good find (5):** a **Potion of Climbing** (common, 50 gp), "for windows".
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** **Dust of Disappearance** (uncommon, 200 gp), in a twist of paper. He doesn't say where it came from, and if they ask, his smile gets a little wider.
- **Buys:** anything stolen, at a third of its price; magic at half; keeps at full value. He's the Zhentarim's man, and the Zhentarim write everything down.
- **Haggling:** never with Persuasion. A secret he can sell takes a fifth off.

### The Vennmark Coster: Tesra Velarion and Ilario Brask
> **SAY:** "A counting-house on the Quays with glass in its windows and a guard at its door. Inside, two clerks in Amnian plum, one older and very calm, one young and very eager, sit at desks under a portrait of Master Venn."
- **Says (Tesra):** "The Coster buys what Corvane has. Corvane has memories." / **(Ilario):** "And we sell everything else! Have you tried the perfume?"
- **Stock:** Amnian wine 10 gp a bottle, perfume 5 gp, fine clothes 15 gp, spices, silk, glass. Magic to order from Amn: any uncommon item, 400 gp, a week.
- **Good find (5):** **Perfume of Bewitching** (common, 50 gp), in a plum bottle.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Lantern of Revealing** (uncommon, 400 gp). "From an estate. The family thought it was haunted."
- **Buys:** keeps at full value, always, and they don't ask whose. Magic at half price.
- **Remember:** buying from the Coster feeds Venn's trade, and Venn is watching who buys.

### The Corvane Venture: Aubric Delamere and Marigold Teague
> **SAY:** "A Waterdhavian trading-house in a borrowed hall. Bolts of cloth on trestles, a map of the Sword Coast on the wall, and two merchants who look as if they've been in Pellmoor for a week and would like to leave tomorrow."
- **Says (Aubric):** "We're here for the long road, not the quick coin." / **(Marigold):** "You'll want wool for the north. Real wool. Not that Corvanese stuff."
- **Stock:** fine clothes 15 gp, traveler's clothes 2 gp, costume 5 gp, a fur-lined cloak 10 gp (worth it for Act III), boots, gloves, maps of the Sword Coast 1 gp. Letters of credit, honored in Hallowmere.
- **Good find (5):** a **Cloak of Many Fashions** (common, 100 gp). Marigold wears it to the counter.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Cloak of Elvenkind** (uncommon, 400 gp), bought from a half-elf who needed passage home.
- **Buys:** Corvanese cloth, carvings and old coin (half again its value). No keeps: "We're from Waterdeep. We like our memories where they are."

### Osgood Fennick, clockmaker
> **SAY:** "A shop full of ticking. Clocks on the walls, clocks on the floor, clocks in pieces on every surface. A gnome with three pairs of spectacles pushed up his forehead doesn't look up. 'One moment. One moment. There.'"
- **Says:** "Everything works if you love it enough and take it apart often." / "Venn's clocks don't tick, you know. I made them that way. He asked."
- **Stock:** tinker's tools 50 gp, a pocket clock 25 gp, locks 10 gp, clockwork toys 5 gp, lock and clock repairs. Magnifying glass 100 gp.
- **Good find (5):** an **Orb of Time** (common, 100 gp), a brass ball that tells the time of day when you ask it.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Decanter of Endless Water** (uncommon) in pieces on his bench. He took it apart to see how it works and can't put it back together. Help him (Arcana or tinker's tools DC 13) and he sells it for 300 gp, or gives it to them for a week's work.
- **Buys:** clockwork of any kind, and Clockwork Amulets at full price ("Mine. I made those.").

### Sister Aurelie Dawnmantle, the Dawn Mission
> **SAY:** "A whitewashed hall with a sun painted over the door, cots along the walls, and the smell of soap and barley soup. A priestess in white with her sleeves rolled up nods to a cot without asking what you need."
- **Says:** "Sit. You can tell me after." / "We don't charge. We do accept."
- **Stock:** Potions of Healing (50 gp; she has 1d4 a week), healer's kit 5 gp, holy water 25 gp, antitoxin 50 gp. Spells cast for a donation: a cantrip 30 gp, a level 1 spell 50 gp, *Lesser Restoration* 200 gp, *Remove Curse* or *Revivify* 300 gp (plus the diamond).
- **Good find (5):** a **Potion of Healing** for nothing, pressed into the hand of whoever's worst hurt.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Periapt of Wound Closure** (uncommon). It isn't for sale. It belonged to a knight who died in her care, and she gives it to whichever of them has done the Mission a kindness.
- **Buys:** nothing. Gifts of food or coin to the Mission, of 25 gp or more, earn a bed for life.

### Dorra Pell, the Shuttered Bell
> **SAY:** "A low inn with shutters painted the blue of old bells. The landlady has a bun of iron-grey hair and an apron she's never once taken off in front of a customer."
- **Says:** "Rooms are upstairs. Rumors are extra." / "Writs have a way of arriving for interesting people."
- **Stock:** a modest room 5 sp a night, a comfortable one 8 sp, a meal 3 sp, ale 4 cp, wine 2 sp a jug, stabling 5 sp a night. Packed rations 5 sp a day.
- **Good find (5):** **Heward's Handy Spice Pouch** (common, 100 gp), left by a cook who went to sea.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Bag of Tricks** (grey, uncommon, 400 gp), left by a lodger who never came back for it. She'd take it off the bill.
- **Buys:** news. A good rumor pays for a night's room.

### The Old Shore: Mother Sallow and the ferry-folk
> **SAY:** "Net-racks, smoke-houses and boats drawn up on the shingle. Nobody here sells anything, exactly. But everybody trades."
- **Trades:** smoked fish for a week's rations (1 gp of anything), boat passage anywhere on the Mere (a favor, or 1 gp), net-mending, oilskins (5 gp, or a good knife).
- **Good find (5):** a **Potion of Water Breathing** (uncommon), traded for a real kindness to the ferry-folk.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Driftglobe** (uncommon) found in a net. Mother Sallow's grandson thinks it's a fish egg. He'll trade it for something that makes him laugh.
- **Doesn't trade in:** keeps. Offer one and the whole beach goes quiet.

page.title: SHOPS OF HALLOWMERE
page.aliases: Hallowmere shops, Grey City shops, Tithe market, Grael and Sons, Pale Ledger
page.body:
**Shops of Hallowmere (7.22): the Grey City's licensed shops, and the ones that aren't.** In Hallowmere every trader needs a Court licence. Most have one. See Shops of Pellmoor for how shops work (the d6 special roll, selling, keeps and haggling).

### Oswin Crake, the Pale Ledger (pawnbroker)
> **SAY:** "A pawnshop on a canal corner, its window so crowded you can't see in: lutes, swords, wedding dresses, spectacles, a stuffed owl. A pale man with ink on his cuffs writes something in a ledger before he says hello."
- **Says:** "Everything here belonged to somebody once. Now it belongs to the Ledger." / "I don't ask. I write it down."
- **Stock:** a little of everything at the usual price: weapons, instruments (lute 35 gp, flute 2 gp), tools, clothes, books. Roll a d6 for an odd item on every visit, too.
- **Good find (5):** a **Mystery Key** (common, 100 gp), pawned by a woman who said it "opens the door I'm not brave enough for".
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Stone of Good Luck** (uncommon, 400 gp), pawned by a gambler who never came back.
- **Buys:** anything at a third of its price, magic at half, keeps at half value, and he writes your name in the Ledger. The Court reads it every week.

### Widow Hesp, apothecary
> **SAY:** "A green shop down three steps, hung with herbs, dark and cool. An old woman with a mortar in her lap says, 'Mind the cat,' and there isn't a cat."
- **Says:** "Bring me willow bark and I'll bring you back from the dead. Nearly." / "Remembering tea? One copper. Works one time in six. That's better than the Tithe."
- **Stock:** Potions of Healing (she brews them, 50 gp; 1d6 on the shelf), antitoxin 50 gp, healer's kit 5 gp, herbalism kit 5 gp, alchemist's fire 50 gp, acid 25 gp. *Remembering tea* (1 cp): a Blank who drinks it remembers their own name, on a 6 on a d6.
- **Good find (5):** a **Potion of Resistance** (uncommon, 200 gp), against whatever the next danger is.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** **Oil of Slipperiness** (uncommon, 200 gp). She made it by mistake.
- **Buys:** herbs, roots, rare plants, monster parts (a Glass-Wolf's eye is worth 25 gp to her). Not keeps: "Poor things."
- **Haggling:** Medicine DC 13 instead of Persuasion, if they talk herbs with her.

### Grael and Sons, Court armourers
> **SAY:** "A grand shop on the Hall of Tithes square, with a Court licence framed beside the door and two Hushmen leaning in the doorway. Inside, three identical brothers in leather aprons look up together."
- **Says:** "Licence?" / "No licence, no blades. That's the law." / (Quietly) "...But the law's expensive to keep, isn't it?"
- **Stock:** every weapon and armor in the rules, at a tenth above the usual price: half plate 825 gp, breastplate 440 gp, plate 1,650 gp to order (two weeks), longsword 17 gp, longbow 55 gp. To buy a weapon or armor, you need a Court licence, or a bribe of 20 gp to the youngest brother (Influence DC 12 to find out which one).
- **Good find (5):** **Armor of Gleaming** (common, 100 gp plus the armor), a breastplate that never needs polishing.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** an **Adamantine Breastplate** (uncommon, 400 gp plus the armor), made for a Court captain who died before he collected it.
- **Buys:** good weapons at half price, and asks where they came from.

### Absalom Dray, bookseller on Vellum Lane
> **SAY:** "A shop so full of books you have to turn sideways to get in. A bent old man with ink-stained sleeves comes out of the stacks, holding a candle well away from everything."
- **Says:** "Licensed books are at the front. History is at the back." / "They burned forty of mine last month. I remembered them. I'm writing them out again."
- **Stock:** books 25 gp, maps 1 gp, ink 10 gp, paper 2 sp a sheet, a calligrapher's kit 25 gp. Spell scrolls he copies himself: a cantrip 30 gp, a level 1 spell 50 gp, a level 2 spell 200 gp (one of each a week).
- **Good find (5):** an **Enduring Spellbook** (common, 100 gp).
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Spell Scroll of Remove Curse** (uncommon, 200 gp), from a dead priest's library.
- **Buys:** old books at half price, unlicensed histories for more than they're worth.
- **Note:** after the book-burning (Hallowmere's streets, entry 3), he gives the party a fifth off for life.

### The Tithe market
> **SAY:** "In the yard behind the Tithe-house, clerks sell the belongings of the Blanks off trestle tables, by the box. Shoes. Toys. A clock still ticking. A crowd is picking through it quietly, not meeting each other's eyes."
- **Stock:** boxes of whatever a Blank was carrying, 5 gp a box, sight unseen. Roll a d6 for each box: on a 6, there's one roll on the Random magic table in it.
- **Something special:** once in Act II, a box with a name inside the lid that one of the party knows.
- **Remember:** the coin goes to the Court. Buying here feels terrible, and it should. Taking a box back to the person it belonged to is worth Heroic Inspiration.

### The Tithe-house counter
> **SAY:** "A long counter of black wood with brass grilles, and behind each grille a clerk with a little silver bowl and a pen. Over it: THE COURT IS GRATEFUL."
- **Buys:** keeps at full value (25 to 100 gp), and memories straight from the head: a clerk takes one with a touch, and pays 10 to 50 gp. The player chooses the memory, and writes it in the Memory ledger. Every sale is recorded, with a name.
- **Sells:** nothing. Ever.

page.title: SHOPS OF THE NORTH ROAD
page.aliases: North Road shops, Empty Sheaf, Haddy Corn, waystation shop
page.body:
**Shops of the North Road (7.22): the waystation, Kell's Crossing and the edge of the glass.** There are fewer shops up here, and they sell what keeps people alive. See Shops of Pellmoor for how shops work (the d6 special roll, selling, keeps and haggling).

### Orrin Lisk, the waystation
> **SAY:** "A stone waystation with a turf roof and a stable, the last lit window for twenty miles. The keeper, a big slow man with a shepherd's crook, has a dog on each side of him."
- **Says:** "Pay for the bed, the fire's free." / "Riders came through yesterday. Grey coats. They paid. You don't have to."
- **Stock:** a bed 5 sp, a meal 3 sp, stabling 5 sp, rations 5 sp a day, oil, rope, blankets, a riding horse 75 gp (he has one), a mule 8 gp, feed.
- **Good find (5):** a **Bead of Nourishment** (common, 50 gp), "found in a ditch".
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** **Boots of Elvenkind** (uncommon, 400 gp), left by a traveler who walked out one night and never came back. Orrin keeps them by the door, in case.
- **Buys:** horses, news, and nothing else. He'd rather have the news.

### Haddy Corn, the Empty Sheaf
> **SAY:** "The inn at Kell's Crossing is crowded with people who've run from somewhere. The innkeeper has six children under her feet and one coat on her back, and she still makes room."
- **Says:** "Sit where there's a gap." / "Pay what you can. If you can pay more, pay for somebody who can't."
- **Stock:** a bed 5 sp (or a share of the hayloft, free), a meal 3 sp, ale 4 cp, rations, warm cloaks 10 gp (patched, and they matter on the glass).
- **Good find (5):** a **Potion of Healing**, from the Dawn Mission's last cart north.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Ring of Warmth** (uncommon). Not for sale: a runaway left it as payment. She'll give it to whoever helps the Crossing most.
- **Buys:** food at full price, and seed-corn at twice that.

### Dob Sallis, carter
> **SAY:** "A carter with a cart full of everything, and a pony called Radish who's seen it all."
- **Says:** "I go north with goods and south with people. Both pay." / "Radish knows the road better than I do."
- **Stock:** cart hire with Dob driving, 2 gp a day; ordinary gear at a quarter above the price; lamp oil, rope, nails, a tent, a saddle.
- **Good find (5):** a **Rope of Mending** (common, 100 gp).
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** **Slippers of Spider Climbing** (uncommon, 400 gp), in a crate marked *Hallowmere, the Chancellor's household*. Dob has no idea, and doesn't want one.
- **Buys:** anything he can sell further down the road, at half price.

### Finch, the pedlar
> **SAY:** "A young pedlar with a pack taller than she is, pots clanking. 'Ribbons, needles, news!'"
- **Stock:** needles, thread, ribbons, soap, a mirror 5 gp, a whistle 2 cp, playing cards 5 sp, a lute string, dried apples.
- **Good find (5):** a **Talking Doll** (common, 100 gp). It says, "Where's Mama?", which is creepy.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** **Sending Stones** (uncommon, 400 gp), one stone. The other is with her brother in Hallowmere. She won't sell it unless they promise to give it to him.
- **Buys:** small things. She trades better than she sells: Persuasion DC 12 to trade an item for one of equal value.

### Yara's camp, at the edge of the glass
> **SAY:** "A tent of hides at the edge of the glass, with a fire inside it that's kept going day and night. The woman who keeps it has frost in her eyebrows and a map she won't let you touch."
- **Says:** "Everything for the glass is for sale. The map isn't." / "Gold or a keep. Keeps are lighter."
- **Stock:** a warm cloak 10 gp or a keep, glass-cutting tools 5 gp, a bed 5 gp or a keep, crampons 2 gp, snow goggles 1 gp, fuel for a night 5 sp, rations 1 gp a day.
- **Good find (5):** a **Potion of Resistance (Cold)** (uncommon, 200 gp).
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Necklace of Adaptation** (uncommon, 400 gp), taken off a Stilled diver at the edge of the glass. She'll say so.
- **Buys:** keeps, at full value, and Glass-Wolf pelts at 25 gp.

page.title: SHOPS OF THE BRASS ROAD
page.aliases: Brass Road shops, Dry Thunder, Mother Ash, storm-smith, Tavi Ondrel, horse-traders
page.body:
**Shops of the Brass Road (7.22): the Dry Thunder, Brassfall and the steppe.** Acts IV and V. Coin is still good here, but the Ironhorn would rather have metal. See Shops of Pellmoor for how shops work (the d6 special roll, selling, keeps and haggling).

### Mother Ash, the Dry Thunder
> **SAY:** "The last tavern before the Shafts. Low, stone, and dark inside, and on every table the cups hum, very faintly, as if there's a song in them."
- **Says:** "Sit. Eat. Don't touch the cups." / "I've heard everything once. Say it slower."
- **Stock:** a bed 8 sp, a meal 3 sp, beer 4 cp, rations 5 sp a day, lamp oil, rope, a mule 8 gp.
- **Good find (5):** a **Tankard of Sobriety** (common, 100 gp). "Somebody needed it more than you."
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Potion of Greater Healing** (uncommon, 200 gp), behind the bar. She says it was her husband's, and she doesn't need it now.
- **Buys:** food and news. She knows what the party are. She'll ask who they are.

### Tavi Ondrel, storm-smith of Brassfall
> **SAY:** "A forge with copper rods on its roof, and blue fire in the hearth instead of red. A young woman in a leather apron, her hair standing straight up, is hammering something that crackles."
- **Says:** "Storms aren't dangerous. They're just impatient." / "Bring me a storm-stone and I'll make you something that'll make the sky jealous."
- **Stock:** bronze weapons and armor at the usual price (they don't rust), lightning rods 5 gp, smith's tools 20 gp, insulated gloves 2 gp.
- **Good find (5):** a **Wand of Conducting** (common, 100 gp), with a spark at its tip.
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Javelin of Lightning** (uncommon, 400 gp), finished, hanging on the wall. Or bring her a storm-stone and 100 gp, and she binds one in a week.
- **Buys:** storm-stones (100 gp), star-iron (150 gp), bronze at its weight in silver.

### The Ironhorn horse-traders
> **SAY:** "Corrals of rope on the steppe, and horses everywhere, more than you've ever seen. The traders are tall and loud and very cheerful, and every one of them is wearing more iron than a knight."
- **Says:** "Coin? Coin is flat iron. Show me real metal." / "That horse? That horse is a poem."
- **Stock:** a riding horse 75 gp, a warhorse 400 gp, a pony 30 gp, a riding saddle 10 gp, a military saddle 20 gp, a felt tent 5 gp, mare's milk 1 sp a skin.
- **Paying:** they take metal by weight, not coin. A weapon or armor counts for its full price, if it's iron or steel. Coin counts too, but they sniff at it.
- **Good find (5):** a quiver of **Walloping Ammunition** (common, 10 arrows, 50 gp).
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** **Bracers of Archery** (uncommon, 400 gp of metal), won in a race by a rider who can't draw a bow.
- **Haggling:** never with Persuasion. Win a contest (a race, a wrestle or a drinking match, DC 15) and they take a fifth off.

### Sallow Kett, the bronze carts' quartermaster
> **SAY:** "A bronze cart parked off the road, and a woman sitting on its tail with a slate and a pencil. 'You've the look of people who need things,' she says. 'Good. I've got things.'"
- **Says:** "Everything on this cart's counted twice." / "Storms coming? Then we're not standing next to the bronze."
- **Stock:** road stores at a tenth above the usual price: rations, rope, tents, oil, cold-weather gear, waterskins, a cart wheel, oxen 15 gp each. Healer's kits 5 gp. Potions of Healing 50 gp (two).
- **Good find (5):** a **Bead of Refreshment** (common, 50 gp).
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Wind Fan** (uncommon, 400 gp), which the carters use to keep the dust off the oxen, not knowing what it is.
- **Buys:** anything that fits on the cart, at half price. If the party helped earth the carts in a storm (The Brass Road and the steppe, entry 2), she takes a tenth off everything.

### The Heart-Hall's fires
> **SAY:** "Round the Heart-Hall forty fires burn, and at every fire someone is mending, smithing, carving or cooking, and all of them will trade."
- **Trades:** horn cups, bone-handled knives (5 gp), felt cloaks (5 gp), dried meat, saddlebags. Metal by weight.
- **Good find (5):** a **Horn of Silent Alarm** (common, 100 gp).
- **Shouldn't be here (6):** a **Gem of Brightness** (uncommon, 400 gp), set into an old chieftain's belt-buckle, offered by her grandson for a good iron sword.

page.title: SHAPES OF THE CAMPAIGN
page.aliases: campaign length, short campaign, shorter campaign, skip, skipping, cut, pacing, one evening, merge sessions, shapes
page.body:
**The Seventh Bell is 28 sessions as written, but it doesn't have to be (7.23).** Every cut below is a card in its session. Waypoint tracks the flags, so the Forecast and the endings keep up, and nothing later breaks.

| Shape | Evenings | How |
|---|---|---|
| The whole road | 28 | Every session as written, with the second Act IV road compressed into Sessions 20 and 21. |
| Brisk Glassreach | 26 | Run Sessions 10 and 11 as one evening (s10-one-evening), and 12 and 13 (s12-one-evening). |
| One road | 26 | Skip the second Act IV road and march on the Tor short-handed (s20-march-short-handed). |
| Both | 24 | Brisk Glassreach and one road. |
| The south road | 22 | Turn south before Glassreach (s10-leave-the-north): no Act III, and the Court holds the Frost Heart and the Sexton. |
| The short campaign | 20 | The south road and one road. Two bells unrung; the Concord needs both back. |

**What each cut costs.**
- **Only the Concord needs every bell.** The other five endings survive every cut. A bell left behind can still be rung: Session 22's detour (s22-detour-for-a-missed-bell) or, for Hieme, going back north (any-go-back-north).
- **The world notices.** Skip Glassreach and the Long Cold creeps south (any-the-cold-comes-south). March short-handed and the Court isn't ready (s22-short-handed-strike).
- **Levels catch up.** Each card says when to level, so the party arrives at the next act at the level it was written for.

**Choosing.**
- **Cut travel and talk before dungeons.** The big dungeons (the Tithe-works, the Frost Spire, the Quiet Quarry) are where the campaign is most a game. Keep them if you can.
- **Ask the table.** "Do we go into the glass?" is a real choice, not a DM's shortcut. Put it to them in the fiction and let them pick.
- **Plan the shape at session zero** if you know how many evenings you have, and decide again at the end of each act.

page.title: THE TITHE-WORKS, AREA BY AREA
page.aliases: Tithe-works, tithe works, service passage, back shelves, First Tallyman, Nell Quell
page.body:
**The Tithe-works as a dungeon (7.23): under the palace's service wing.** Before the Hall of Tithes had its vault, tithes were drawn and bottled down here, and the vault's service passage still runs through the old works to its back shelves. **This is Session 8's big dungeon:** the way to bring the jars out before the party leaves Hallowmere. Run it at dusk, between Scene 2 and the goodbyes, so the jars can be handed over in Scene 3. The play is *The Tithe-works: the dungeon under the palace*.
