anytime.title: They use Hold Person, Suggestion, Charm Person or Sleep on an NPC
anytime.why: Four characters with subclasses and 2nd-level spells can solve a scene in one action.
anytime.response: They work as written, with a Corvane cost. Every spell hums within 30 feet, so any Hushman nearby hears the cast, and a held or charmed NPC knows afterward that something was done to them and who stood near. Hold Person and Sleep need a Humanoid and a failed save; a Hushman's silence-stone glove does not protect the wearer. Suggestion cannot make an NPC reveal a secret that would harm them seriously (the DM may judge the request unreasonable), and it cannot undo a Tithe or a memory. Charm Person makes the target Friendly, not obedient. The NPC's next report names the caster: raise clock_court by 1 if a Court officer is the target.
anytime.consequence: The scene is solved fast and the Court has a name.
anytime.fallback: If the save succeeds, the NPC shouts, and the encounter begins.
anytime.tells: A caster asks whether Quill, Cole, Venn, Eld or a Hushman can be held, charmed or put to sleep.
anytime.rules: Hold Person: Wisdom save each turn, ends on success. Suggestion: Wisdom save, up to 8 hours, reasonable request only. Charm Person: Wisdom save, advantage if fighting, target knows afterward. Sleep: HP pool. Blanks and the Drowned are not valid targets for Charm.
anytime.later: The target's next report puts the caster on the Court's list (court_eye). Repeated use makes the Gate Clerk and the Landing House expect it.
anytime.keywords: hold person, suggestion, charm person, sleep, command, enchant, control npc, quill, venn

anytime.title: They cast Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth or Calm Emotions on someone
anytime.why: The campaign is built on secrets; a level-3 to 6 party has the spells to ask.
anytime.response: The firm rulings: the spell hums, so the target usually hears it. At the oath-duel (S6) the knights stand in herald fields (10-foot silence-stone), so both spells fail there and casting at them costs the caster's side a question. At Maudrin's dais (S4) the plinth stones kill Zone of Truth; Detect Thoughts on her surface mind gives 'Four of them. Ossa's. Not yet.' and a probe saves at +4. Haldric's shield negates the first spell targeting only him each day. Elsewhere Zone of Truth works as written (Charisma save; creatures may refuse to answer, which is itself telling). Detect Thoughts on a Tithed person finds blank patches; on a Blank it finds only a looping 'who was I?'. Calm Emotions suppresses Charmed or Frightened (including the Sermon in a fight) but does not undo a Toll, a Tithe or a Blank.
anytime.consequence: Truth magic is a tool with edges, not a skeleton key.
anytime.fallback: If the table argues, rule it by the stones: a field stops the spell, no field means it works.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Zone of Truth before a hearing, or names Detect Thoughts at a table with Maudrin, Venn or Isolde.
anytime.rules: Zone of Truth (2nd): Charisma save, 10-minute zone. Detect Thoughts (2nd): Wisdom save to probe, concentration. Calm Emotions (2nd): Charisma save, suppresses Charmed or Frightened. Silence-stone fields stop all three.
anytime.later: S4: read-maudrin. S6: spells-on-the-steps. S13: the Sexton says he has told no lie since 32 SS.
anytime.keywords: zone of truth, detect thoughts, calm emotions, read mind, interrogate, lie, truth magic

anytime.title: They use Locate Object, Find Familiar, Clairvoyance or Detect Magic to find a Heart
anytime.why: Five Hearts are scattered across Corvane, and a caster wants to know where.
anytime.response: Locate Object (2nd level) on a Heart the caster has seen works: the hum gives a direction within 1,000 feet. It fails if the Heart is in a silence-stone box, the Tithe-Ledger Room or the Hallowmere vault; a lined box shows nothing. Locate Object on 'the page', 'the diary' or 'the Key' works only if the caster has seen it. Find Familiar (ritual) can watch the Heron, Quill's office or a Hushman's door; Detect Magic shows the faint aura of a Heart, and a Bell-Touched character senses it without magic. Clairvoyance (3rd, level 5+) fails inside silence-stone and in any Court city under a raised Silence. Scrying on the Sexton fails: Hieme's silence blocks it.
anytime.consequence: They can find a Heart or watch a place, but the Court's stones block the hard places.
anytime.fallback: If the spell fails, the hum fades and Bell-Touched characters still feel a direction.
anytime.tells: A player asks whether a Heart can be tracked, or sends an owl to watch a ship.
anytime.rules: Locate Object: 1,000-foot range, concentration, blocked by lead; here also by silence-stone. Detect Magic: ritual. Find Familiar: ritual, 1 hour.
anytime.later: Hallowmere: the vault (S5) and the armory (S9) are lined and show nothing. The Heron (S3) is findable until she clears the Seam.
anytime.keywords: locate object, find familiar, clairvoyance, scry, track heart, detect magic, divination

anytime.title: They use Misty Step, Invisibility, Pass without Trace, Spider Climb or Knock
anytime.why: Heist scenes meet 2nd-level spells at level 3, and the silence-stone rule needs a clear answer.
anytime.response: They work as written outside a silence-stone field. Inside a field (the Tithe-Ledger vault, a dais, a herald's rod) no spell can be cast or produce an effect: Knock fails, Invisibility and Pass without Trace are suppressed, Disguise Self drops, and Misty Step cast from outside lands at the edge of the field, not inside. Pass without Trace gives +10 to Stealth for the group; the spell still hums when it is cast, so anyone within 30 feet hears the cast. Invisibility ends when the target attacks or casts. Spider Climb skips the chain-room climb (S9) but not the chains. On a ship (the Heron) a shimmer on the water gives the mate Passive Perception 14 a chance.
anytime.consequence: Mobility spells open the plan but not the stone.
anytime.fallback: If the player's plan needs a spell the field blocks, the Hushman passing every ten minutes gives them a mundane way through.
anytime.tells: A caster asks whether a blink, a shimmer or a lockpick spell works at the vault, the armory or the Heron.
anytime.rules: Silence-stone field: Part 2.6 house rule. Pass without Trace: +10 Stealth, concentration. Misty Step: 30 feet, bonus action, blocked into a field.
anytime.later: S5: the vault. S9: the armory and the chain-room. S3: boarding the Heron.
anytime.keywords: misty step, invisibility, pass without trace, spider climb, knock, silence-stone, heist

anytime.title: They use a level-3 class feature in a Corvane scene
anytime.why: Subclasses mean Cunning Action, Wild Shape, Turn Undead, Smite, Portent, Cutting Words and Subtle Spell all arrive at once.
anytime.response: Cunning Action and Fast Hands work in S1's theft and raid; a ferry-folk witness makes it risky. A druid's swimming Wild Shape removes the breath clock in the Mere (S2) but the Cantor reads an animal shape as a lie unless it is named. Turn Undead and Divine Smite work on the Drowned Singers; the Cantor is immune to Frightened and Charmed and is offended. Wizard Portent and Bard Cutting Words work on Stealth and Influence rolls. Sorcerer Subtle Spell hides the verbal and somatic components, so the Tonework hum is still heard within 30 feet, and Hushmen can still hear a cast. Warlock Devil's Sight sees through the Mere's dark but not through silence-stone. A Monk's Stunning Strike works on Hushmen but not on Stilled (Gargoyle) or Singers.
anytime.consequence: Class features speed the plan but do not skip the telegraph.
anytime.fallback: If a feature seems to break a scene, tell the player what the scene's real obstacle is and let them solve that.
anytime.tells: A rogue asks about Fast Hands, a druid asks about a swimming Wild Shape, a cleric about Turn Undead.
anytime.rules: Turn Undead: Wisdom save vs your spell save DC, Frightened for 1 minute. Wild Shape: swimming beasts ignore Suffocation but not eel bites. Portent: replace a roll before it is made.
anytime.later: Features that touch bells or Tolls follow the bell: nothing a class does rings a bell without its Heart and Toll.
anytime.keywords: cunning action, wild shape, turn undead, divine smite, portent, cutting words, subtle spell, class feature

anytime.title: Level 5 to 6: Dispel Magic, Counterspell, Hearts, Sending, Speak with Dead, Water Breathing
anytime.why: Third-level slots arrive at level 5 (S10). Before then these are NPC-only; after, they touch bells, silence and memory.
anytime.response: Dispel Magic ends a spell effect on a creature or object, but not a Toll, a Tithe, a Blank's state, a winter-moment (Hieme's silence), a bell's ringing, or Oum. It cannot target a silence-stone because a stone is not a spell. Counterspell stops an NPC's spell (Maudrin, Aurelie, Brother Eld's Silence) but not a bell, the Sexton's Sermon or a Hushman's glove. Hearts lets the caster understand and speak any language: it makes the old Stilled dialect and Hesk accessible but cannot read bell-script. Sending reaches anyone inside Corvane who is not in a silence-stone field; across the Stormwall it fails (the weather is in the way) unless the Seam is wide. Speak with Dead works on any corpse with a mouth for 10 days: five questions, and the corpse knows only what it knew in life (see any-speak-with-dead). Water Breathing lets a party reach the Ossa Belfry without the Tidewarden's pocket and works on the Mere's drowned streets; the Cantor treats it as a courtesy.
anytime.consequence: The party has tools for NPC casters and for the Mere, but the world's big magic stays out of their hands.
anytime.fallback: If a player is disappointed, offer the narrower thing the spell does well.
anytime.tells: A level-5 caster asks what Dispel Magic or Counterspell can do against the Court's tools.
anytime.rules: Dispel Magic (3rd): ability check DC 10 + spell level for a higher-level spell. Counterspell: reaction, 60 feet. Hearts: 1 hour. Sending: 25 words. Speak with Dead: 10 days, five questions. Water Breathing: ritual, 24 hours.
anytime.later: S10 onward: Hearts unlocks the Stilled; S11: Speak with Dead on a shattered Stilled; S13: the Sexton's Sermon cannot be countered.
anytime.keywords: dispel magic, counterspell, hearts, sending, speak with dead, water breathing, third level, fireball

anytime.title: They kill a named NPC
anytime.why: A table that has been hunted by Hushmen for ten sessions will eventually go for someone with a name.
anytime.response: Ask once: 'You mean to kill them?' A creature at 0 HP can be knocked out instead (2024), and a Hold Person'd target is a murder, not a fight. If they do it, the NPC is dead; no resurrection. Record the flag if one exists (quill, eld, haldric, ilam, rook, ansel, corin, kessa, sexton, maudrin) and note the rest in the Bargain Log (Brannagh, Sela, Venn, Sallow, Lysse, Bet, Aurelie, Hadrik, Wren, Isolde, Edrin). Then show the ripple: a Court officer's death raises the Court clock and names the killers; a ferry-folk or Bellwright ally's death costs trust and a door. Never a child. If a death would end a thread the story needs (Rook dead, no Vaer loan), let another door open: Haldric, Aurelie, a theft, or the Bellwrights.
anytime.consequence: The NPC is gone and the table sees the cost.
anytime.fallback: If the table regrets it at once, it still stands: a gentle reminder that the story goes on.
anytime.tells: A player says 'finish him', ambushes a named NPC alone, or waits at their door.
anytime.rules: No check. Record the death. Court officers: clock_court +1 to +2; the Dawn Order: clock_dawn +2; ferry-folk: clock_ferry +1.
anytime.later: The NPC's later promises lapse. Their allies hold a grudge; their enemies are surprised. S28 and the endings read the death honestly.
anytime.keywords: kill npc, murder, assassinate, execute, kill quill, kill rook, kill venn, named character

anytime.title: They split the party
anytime.why: Four players, four plans: a rogue at the vault and a cleric at the Mission is how every table plays.
anytime.response: Cut between the groups in short scenes (about five minutes each) and let a timer run: Quill reaches the Old Shore on the second evening; the Tithe Clock ticks per night; Hushmen pass every ten minutes. Give each half a clear danger and a clear exit. Keep players who are not in the current scene engaged by asking them to play the NPCs. Regroup at a natural meeting point (a bakery, a chapel, a camp). Tolls, Tithes and bells need the consenting character present; an absent player's character is never charged (any-absent-player).
anytime.consequence: Parallel scenes shorten the session and raise tension.
anytime.fallback: If a split drags, call a cut and bring one group to the other.
anytime.tells: A player says 'I'll go and' while the others plan something else.
anytime.rules: No check. Each group gets its own encounter budget; do not stack difficulty on one half.
anytime.later: Splits matter at S4 (masque vs barracks), S5 (vault vs Archive), S12 (Hobb vs the Sexton), S16A onward (Branches A and B).
anytime.keywords: split party, divide, separate, two groups, scout, stealth team

anytime.title: When the party levels up
anytime.why: The table is four players starting at level 3, so Act I is no longer a level 1 climb.
anytime.response: Milestone levels follow the session schedule: sessions 1 to 5 are level 3 (Pellmoor and Hallowmere's first week); level 4 after S6 (the oath-duel); level 5 at S10 (Glassreach); level 6 at S14 (the Frost Spire); level 7 at S16A. Do not hand levels out in the Mere. 3rd-level spells arrive at level 5, which is why Fireball, Speak with Dead and Hearts appear in Glassreach. If a table is ahead or behind, adjust encounters with Waypoint's difficulty readout, not the story.
anytime.consequence: The party's tools match the scene.
anytime.tells: A player asks when they level, or what level they should be.
anytime.rules: No check.
anytime.later: Act IV: levels 7 and up. Act V: levels 10 to 11.
anytime.keywords: level up, milestone, experience, level schedule, when do we level

anytime.title: They hide a Heart somewhere Quill's warrant does not reach
anytime.why: A party that knows Quill will search the Old Shore hides the Heart elsewhere.
anytime.response: Quill's warrant covers the Old Shore. A foreign ship, the Pilots' Hall loft, the Dawn Mission or a Quays warehouse is outside it. A Heart in a silence-stone-lined box does not hum, but the box itself is contraband; a lead-lined sailor's chest hides the hum from Locate Object. The ferry-folk keep it without being asked if Ila vouches. A ship's captain wants a fee, and Venn's friends notice.
anytime.consequence: The Heart is hidden and the party has bought time.
anytime.fallback: If the hiding place is bad, Quill's guard finds it and the scene becomes a raid.
anytime.tells: A player asks about a Baldurian ship, the Pilots' Hall loft, a Quays warehouse or a silence-stone-lined box.
anytime.rules: Stealth DC 15 to carry it unseen; Locate Object fails on a lined box.
anytime.later: S1: Quill's search finds nothing and he is suspicious. S3: the hiding place is the party's, not the Court's.
anytime.keywords: hide heart, stash, lined box, pilots hall, baldurian ship, conceal

anytime.title: The Gilded Heron wrecks in the Wall and the Mere returns the Heart
anytime.why: The sale was the campaign's hardest consequence. This is the canon's safety valve, if the table wants it.
anytime.readAloud: On a still morning, a Pilots' Hall skiff comes in with a plum-coloured sail across its bows. Brannagh Wick stands in the bow, holding a wet oilskin bundle. 'The Mere remembers what is taken from it,' she says.
anytime.response: The Heron wrecks in the Wall; the Heart washes back up the Pell and into the Mere weeks later. The Mere places it at the foot of the Ossa Belfry: the Tidewarden finds it. Tell the table honestly that this is a gift, not a reward, and that Venn is ruined and furious. Mother Sallow takes the bundle to the shore. Ila holds it first.
anytime.consequence: Ossa's Heart is at the belfry. The Concord is open again.
anytime.fallback: If the table prefers a harder road, play any-ossa-written-off.
anytime.tells: The Heron has sailed with Ossa's Heart and the table is stuck, or a player asks whether it can come back.
anytime.rules: No check. Weeks pass: advance clock_court and clock_landing by 1.
anytime.later: Any time: ring Ossa (any-ring-ossa-later). Venn is ruined and furious when the party returns.
anytime.keywords: heron wreck, heart returns, safety valve, stormwall, washed back, recover ossa

anytime.title: They write off Ossa's Heart
anytime.why: A table that refuses the safety valve, or has decided the Concord is closed.
anytime.readAloud: 'Then the Mere is quiet,' says the Tidewarden, 'and will stay quiet.' He turns his oar and does not look at you.
anytime.response: Ossa's Heart is lost beyond the Seam. The Concord requires all six bells and is closed unless a later voyage brings it back (Situation 17: leaving Corvane for six weeks). The Second Dawn stays open with fewer domains. Ila grieves. The Choir stays hunting; the ferry-folk blame the party quietly.
anytime.consequence: Ossa's Heart is gone; the Concord is closed for now.
anytime.fallback: The safety valve is always available (any-heron-wrecks).
anytime.tells: A player says 'it's gone' or 'let it go'.
anytime.rules: No check. Voyage: about six weeks each way, advancing every faction clock by two for each month away.
anytime.later: S28: Ila never forgives it. Any time: any-heron-wrecks returns the Heart if the table changes its mind.
anytime.keywords: give up ossa, lost heart, concord closed, write off

anytime.title: They ring Ossa after Session 3
anytime.why: They recovered the Heart from the armory, the Court's vault, Venn or the sea, and the bell is waiting.
anytime.readAloud: The Tidewarden's ferry waits at the end of the old dock, oar dripping. The water is very still.
anytime.response: Warn and wait for a yes: 'Ossa will take a memory of the dead from you, and it will be [weight].' You choose which after it rings (Part 2.7). If they decline, the bell does not ring and no Toll is taken. Ila may not be the Ringer; offer it to an adult and let her stand beside them. The Tidewarden ferries the Ringer and holds an air pocket. If they ring it, the Choir rests, Mother Sallow remembers Davin, and the Cantor can be released with the verse.
anytime.consequence: Ossa is rung. The Choir rests.
anytime.fallback: If the Ringer hesitates, the Cantor waits a night.
anytime.tells: A player says 'we have it back, let's ring it', or asks the Tidewarden for passage.
anytime.rules: Record the Toll (Toll, Ossa). Ringer at the bell with the Heart.
anytime.later: Concord: 1 of 6. S27: the released Choir can sing at the summit.
anytime.keywords: ring ossa later, toll, belfry, tidewarden, choir rests

anytime.title: Captain Rook dies
anytime.why: Rook stands in the open at the oath-duel, the gate and the Strike; a table that fights the Dawn Order, or loses a protector, can lose her.
anytime.response: Play it only if it happened at the table: no NPC dies off-screen to suit the plot. The Dawn Order goes to Haldric if he is still a knight, and Vaer's Heart stays wherever it was. Her knights hold the party responsible if the party caused it, and mourn with them if not. If Rook had loaned Vaer's Heart, Haldric demands it back.
anytime.consequence: The Dawn Order loses its honest captain; Haldric commands it.
anytime.fallback: If the table is upset, give them her last words: a name, and the place of a hidden key.
anytime.tells: A fight breaks out around Rook, or the party sends her somewhere dangerous alone.
anytime.later: S22: the Dawn Order will not stand with the party unless Haldric has turned. S23: if Haldric commands, Dawn Order Knights are at the Strike.
anytime.keywords: rook, captain, dies, killed, dawn order, death

anytime.title: They kill the Quiet Chancellor
anytime.why: She is the obvious villain, and some tables go straight for the throat (Situation 1).
anytime.readAloud: "You could try. She's surrounded by Hushmen and Dawn Order knights, and every glove on her hands is silence-stone. Are you sure?"
anytime.response: Let them plan; good plans get a real chance. Use the Strike (S23) or summit (S24) forces scaled to where she is. She has allies, a favor she may be owed, and a retreat, but she can die. Foreshadow her successor with a rumour: her cousin Tristan Vesk has been writing quietly to the Court's council.
anytime.consequence: She is dead. The Court splinters and Hallowmere's factions fight each other; the party is hunted by both sides. Tristan Vesk takes the chair and the Key.
anytime.fallback: If the attempt stalls, Haldric's knights arrive and offer the party a clean surrender instead of a death.
anytime.tells: Players ask where Maudrin sleeps, who guards her, or whether a crossbow reaches the palace balcony.
anytime.rules: Use the Maudrin Vesk stat block (CR 8) plus her guards; calculate the 2024 budget in Foresight. Her Silence-Stone Gloves impose Disadvantage on one spell attack within 10 feet each round.
anytime.later: S22: Tristan marches in her place (s22-tristan-takes-the-march). S23: the Strike with Tristan (enc-s23-strike-tristan). Anytime: he offers a deal for the Key (any-tristan-chancellor).
anytime.keywords: kill, assassinate, murder, maudrin, chancellor, attack her, poison, crossbow

anytime.title: They want to ring every bell right now
anytime.why: Once players learn what the bells do, the obvious plan is all of them, immediately (Situation 2).
anytime.readAloud: "You can't. The Hearts are scattered across Corvane, and each bell is guarded. What do you want to ring first?"
anytime.response: Show them the Forecast tab's Concord list: each bell and where its Heart is now. Make them earn each Heart. Each bell rung makes the Court more aggressive: use the Court as that session's faction tick.
anytime.consequence: The party has a route plan, and the Court takes notice of it.
anytime.fallback: If they freeze at the size of it, Mother Sallow, Rook or Corin names the nearest Heart.
anytime.tells: Players list the bells and ask how fast they can travel.
anytime.later: Every ringing advances the Court's clock. Thrane's ringing loosens the Stormwall (Act IV).
anytime.keywords: ring all bells, every bell, all at once, fast, plan, route

anytime.title: They go straight for the Seventh Bell
anytime.why: Some parties skip to the end the moment they hear of Ysh (Situation 3).
anytime.readAloud: "What do you know about the shrine and where the Key is now? What is your plan for reaching them?"
anytime.response: Allow the expedition. Ysh is at the bottom of a hundred steps and needs the Key to ring. Apply the stairs price only to steps actually walked: nineteen free steps, then one memory per twenty, one DC 13 Wisdom save at step 20 (campaign cap five on a failure, two on a success). A workable alternative route avoids that cost (the foundry chute, s25-foundry-chute). The Hush Cult notices them only if they are seen.
anytime.consequence: They learn the shrine is real and that the Key is the only way to ring it.
anytime.fallback: If they have no plan for the Key, the Hush speaks to them in their own sleeping voice and tells them who holds it.
anytime.tells: Players ask where the Hush Shrine is and how far Vael Tor is.
anytime.rules: Stairs: see any-stairs-price.
anytime.later: Without the Key they can't ring or seal Ysh. A visit spends part of their stairs cost early (record it as Stairs in the ledger).
anytime.keywords: seventh bell, ysh, hush shrine, vael tor, skip, go straight, ending, stairs

anytime.title: They try to steal the Key from Maudrin's palace vault
anytime.why: Heist-minded parties go for the most important object in the campaign (Situation 4).
anytime.readAloud: "Before her departure, the Key is in Maudrin's separate palace vault. Once she leaves for the Tor, she carries its case on a chain. Which are you scouting?"
anytime.response: Good plans should work. Ansel knows the vault schedule and can get them an audience or the service entrance. The Key vault has two Hushman guards, a mechanical lock, and a case tether that rings a mundane alarm when lifted; looking at it reveals the tether without a roll. A successful plan may bypass the checks.
anytime.consequence: If they succeed, they hold the Key, and Maudrin knows within a day.
anytime.fallback: If caught, a DC 15 Wisdom (Insight) check shows Maudrin is not bluffing about the price.
anytime.tells: Players ask Ansel Quay about the vault schedule, or scout the palace.
anytime.rules: Lock: DC 16 Dexterity (Thieves' Tools). Tether: DC 14 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand); failure alerts the guards but doesn't move the Key. Two Hushmen (CR 1/2).
anytime.later: With the Key: each night it hums louder and a holder begins to dream the lullaby; the Strike (S23) becomes a pursuit, and Concord and Second Dawn become possible. On failure, Maudrin demands a Heart, evidence or a service they actually have, never the Key she still holds.
anytime.keywords: steal key, tuning key, vault, palace, heist, ansel, break in

anytime.title: They try to take the Key from Maudrin's chain
anytime.why: Once she leaves Hallowmere, the Key travels on her chain in a silence-stone case.
anytime.readAloud: The case at Maudrin's throat is grey and dull and swallows the light. Under it, very faintly, something hums.
anytime.response: Taking the case needs a character to reach her after she has been struck once. On a failure she keeps it and notices the attempt; she escapes only by normal movement and actions. On a success, Haldric (if present) sees the Key in the party's hands and hesitates, which breaks the Court's line.
anytime.consequence: The party holds the Key, or Maudrin knows exactly what they want.
anytime.fallback: If the attempt fails, a Stilled ally or Ilam Bray can create a second opening.
anytime.tells: Players ask how the case is fastened, or plan to grapple her.
anytime.rules: DC 17 at the summit (Keeper), DC 16 at the Strike (Maudrin): Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) once she has taken damage this encounter. Grapple and disarm by 2024 rules work too. Haldric's hesitation costs him his next turn.
anytime.later: With the Key: Concord, Second Dawn and the Unbound all open (Forecast). Without it: S24 she seals or threatens a strike at the shrine.
anytime.keywords: key, chain, case, take the key, grab, sleight of hand, strike, maudrin

anytime.title: They make a deal with Maudrin
anytime.why: She always offers a bargain before a threat (Situation 5).
anytime.readAloud: "I'm listening. What do you want, and what are you willing to give?"
anytime.response: Her bargains are always real and always incomplete: she keeps her word about the thing bargained for and breaks every other promise. Typical deals: safe passage for a Heart; a memory restored for another given to the Tithe; a prisoner freed for a secret; a Court pension for silence about the Quiet Night.
anytime.consequence: A deal exists with the main antagonist, with teeth.
anytime.tells: Players ask what she wants, or offer something.
anytime.rules: Record every deal in the Bargain log (Campaign → Party & preferences).
anytime.later: She calls in favors at the worst moment: S23 at the latest (s23-favor-called). A broken deal makes her personal (s23-favor-broken).
anytime.keywords: deal, bargain, negotiate, maudrin, offer, trade, favor

anytime.title: They try to ring a bell without paying the Toll
anytime.why: Players hate costs, and will look for a loophole (Situation 6).
anytime.readAloud: "The Toll is part of the bell. You can't ring it without giving something up. What do you want to give?"
anytime.response: Warn of the bell's Toll kind and its weight; you choose the exact loss after it rings, from what the table knows of the character, never from anything Off-limits. If they decline, the bell doesn't ring. Another willing Ringer may pay instead. No unnoticed cost or involuntary loss ever substitutes for an agreed Toll. Corin can defer a Toll for an hour, not cancel it.
anytime.consequence: The table understands the price is real and always chosen.
anytime.fallback: If no one will pay, the bell waits. The Forecast shows what that costs the Concord.
anytime.tells: Players ask whether an animal, an NPC, or magic could pay instead.
anytime.rules: Tolls by bell: Vaer a memory of a beginning; Ossa a memory of the dead; Calla a gift; Hieme a memory; Thrane a sense; Mirel a fear. Weight (Heavy for the first two bells the party rings, Grievous for the third and fourth, Ruinous after; the card shows it).
anytime.keywords: toll, pay, avoid, loophole, free, cost, ring without paying, someone else pays

anytime.title: Someone wants to hurt Ila, Jonah or another child
anytime.why: It happens, and it needs a firm table answer (Situation 7).
anytime.readAloud: "They're children. Why would you want to hurt them?"
anytime.response: Stop and use your session-zero agreements. If harm to children is a Line, rewind: don't enact it and then punish it in the fiction. Replace threatened-child scenes with agreed alternatives. If a child is in danger in the fiction, an adult steps in: Mother Sallow, Ilam Bray, Bet Ostrow or Brannagh Wick.
anytime.consequence: The table's boundaries hold.
anytime.fallback: Take a break and talk out of character.
anytime.tells: A player threatens a child in character.
anytime.keywords: child, kill ila, hurt jonah, children, threaten child, lines and veils

anytime.title: They ignore the plot to explore, trade or take side jobs
anytime.why: A port full of ships and money invites it (Situation 8).
anytime.readAloud: "That's fine. Corvane is big, and Pellmoor is busy. What do you do first?"
anytime.response: Let them. Use v5's side quests (11.6) and the Landing: a pilot's job through the Seam, a Coster cargo with something illegal in it, a Reckoner's forgery problem. The main plot keeps moving: advance one faction clock each session and send news of threatened moves. Absence alone never destroys Pellmoor.
anytime.consequence: The party earns money and contacts; the world advances without them.
anytime.fallback: If they drift too long, an NPC brings a direct request: Mother Sallow, Rook, Kessa, Corin or Lysse.
anytime.tells: Players ask about work on the Quays, cargoes, or what sells abroad.
anytime.later: Clocks near their thresholds show in Foresight's Pressure ahead. Faerûnian contacts made here can become Act IV allies (the Stormborn).
anytime.keywords: side quest, explore, money, trade, job, merchant, cargo, ignore plot, wander

anytime.title: They join the Quiet Court
anytime.why: Order, safety and access are tempting (Situation 9).
anytime.readAloud: "That's an unusual choice. The Court values order above all things. What do you bring to the table?"
anytime.response: Let them; it's a strong route. They gain power, safety and access to the Tithe-Ledger. They will be asked to Tithe people, including friends. Each session, ask for one name they record. Ask: "Will you still believe in Order when it is asked of someone you love?"
anytime.consequence: The party works for the Court, with the Court's protection.
anytime.tells: Players ask what the Court pays, or what Hushmen get.
anytime.later: Endings shift: the Empty Choir becomes their victory unless they turn. The Bellwrights and the Choir become enemies. S23: s23-march-with-maudrin. S24: s24-deal-with-maudrin. S26: s26-help-seal. S27: s27-empty-choir.
anytime.keywords: join court, quiet court, hushman, become hushmen, serve maudrin, work for the court

anytime.title: They become Bellwrights
anytime.why: The underground bell-makers are sympathetic and hunted (Situation 10).
anytime.readAloud: "The Bellwrights are hunted, and they have few resources. They'll need proof of your skill. Can you make a bell?"
anytime.response: Let them learn the Bellwright story talent (v5 2.6). Give them an apprentice: Wren, Ila or Bet. Their test is ringing a small, ordinary bell, with a small, chosen price. In Pellmoor, Lantanese tinkers are eager collaborators and terrible at keeping secrets.
anytime.consequence: The party has an underground network, and the Court's hatred.
anytime.tells: Players ask how bells are made or who teaches Tonework.
anytime.rules: Tool proficiency with Smith's Tools or Tinker's Tools helps; use 2024 crafting rules for ordinary bells.
anytime.later: Corin treats them as kin when they meet (S18A or S20). Wren's betrayals now endanger them directly (S6).
anytime.keywords: bellwright, join, bell-making, craft bell, tonework, apprentice

anytime.title: They negotiate with the Choir, the Stilled, the Sleepless or the Hush
anytime.why: Talking to the strange is a Seventh Bell signature (Situation 11).
anytime.readAloud: "They're not like the living. They don't negotiate the way you do. What do you want to ask them?"
anytime.response: They can bargain, but they ask strange things. The Drowned Choir wants a true memory of the dead. The Stilled want to move. The Sleepless want a dream of their own. The Hush wants rest.
anytime.consequence: A strange ally, or a strange debt.
anytime.tells: Players address the dead, the frozen or the dream directly.
anytime.rules: Influence works if they can understand you; their attitude is set by what they want, not by charm.
anytime.later: Record the bargain; these debts come due in Act V.
anytime.keywords: talk, negotiate, choir, stilled, sleepless, hush, bargain, dead, dream

anytime.title: They burn the Bone Archive, the Hall of Tithes, or the city
anytime.why: Rage at the Tithe can boil over (Situation 12).
anytime.readAloud: "That's a lot of books. And a lot of people. Are you sure?"
anytime.response: If they clearly mean it, let them. The city answers with a massive Hushmen sweep and a Dawn Order response. Smashing Tithe jars scatters those memories; it doesn't return them. The Blanks are freed, and some are permanently changed by the fire. The party is hunted across the Ninefold Shore.
anytime.consequence: Hallowmere burns; the Tithe Clock jumps to 12.
anytime.tells: Players ask for oil, or where the jars are stored.
anytime.later: Acts IV and V become more dangerous and the ending darker. The Court raises the Silence in every street. S28: the jars are gone; only a Remake mends them (s28-jars-destroyed).
anytime.keywords: burn, fire, archive, hall of tithes, destroy, arson, smash jars

anytime.title: The characters turn on each other
anytime.why: Secrets and Tolls create tension (Situation 13).
anytime.readAloud: "Corvane is full of people who want things from you. Your friends may want something too. Who is hiding something?"
anytime.response: Use the secrets: each character's secret is known only to them and the DM. Play betrayal only when the affected players have agreed out of character; otherwise resolve the disagreement without player-versus-player coercion. Never take away a player's character.
anytime.consequence: The conflict is settled by agreement, at the table or in the fiction.
anytime.tells: A player hides a Heart, or wants to sell another character's secret.
anytime.keywords: betray, pvp, each other, steal from party, secret, conflict

anytime.title: They rest for a long time in a Court city
anytime.why: Healing up and shopping take days (Situation 14).
anytime.readAloud: "You can rest, but the Long Dusk doesn't wait. Every night you rest in a Court city, the Tithe-quota grows, and the Hush gets a little louder."
anytime.response: Let them rest, and tick the Tithe Clock once per night in a Court city. At 6: a Hushmen sweep and checkpoints. At 12: silence-stones in every street. Pellmoor is not a Court city; resting there costs nothing.
anytime.consequence: Time passes; the Court tightens.
anytime.tells: Players plan downtime in Hallowmere or another Court city.
anytime.rules: World state: Tithe Clock +1 per night (use the stepper).
anytime.later: Thresholds trigger once per cycle; a week outside Court cities resets the clock but deployed checkpoints stay.
anytime.keywords: rest, downtime, long rest, wait, days, shop, heal, hallowmere

anytime.title: They try to talk to the bells, the Silence or a god
anytime.why: Clerics and curious players ask the biggest questions (Situation 15).
anytime.readAloud: "The bells can't speak. But the Hush can, and so can the Librarian. And the Dreamer, if you're brave enough to ask."
anytime.response: Use the Librarian (Act II) and the Hush (Act IV). Both answer one question for each true memory or true sacrifice: true but partial. Faerûnian divination works normally, but the gods are guarded about Corvane: Commune answers about Oum come back "unclear" unless the question is very precise. If they learn the truth early, let it change their plans.
anytime.consequence: A true, partial answer, paid for with a memory or a sacrifice.
anytime.tells: A cleric casts Commune or Augury, or someone prays at a bell.
anytime.rules: Commune, Augury and Divination work by 2024 rules; Oum is not a god the Faerûnian powers will speak for.
anytime.keywords: talk to bell, pray, god, commune, augury, divination, oum, dreamer, silence, question

anytime.title: They want to pay a Toll for something other than a bell
anytime.why: Once memory is money, players spend it creatively (Situation 16).
anytime.readAloud: "The Toll is always personal. It's what you give. What do you want to buy with it?"
anytime.response: Let them, with a real cost. A memory can buy protection, a favor, a ritual or a key. In v6 most of this is ordinary memory money (a keep or heartkeep) rather than a bell Toll; record it as Trade or Gift. Make the price visible.
anytime.consequence: Something real is bought with something personal, and recorded.
anytime.tells: Players offer a memory to an NPC, a spirit or a door.
anytime.rules: Memory money table rules apply (Campaign → Party & preferences, under the Memory ledger).
anytime.keywords: memory as payment, toll for, spend memory, buy with memory, offer a memory

anytime.title: They want to leave Corvane
anytime.why: In v6 there is a whole world beyond the Stormwall, and ships leave every week in season (Situation 17).
anytime.readAloud: "There is a world beyond the Stormwall, and ships sail to it from Pellmoor every week in season. Six weeks to the Sword Coast. Is that where you want to go?"
anytime.response: Let them if they insist. Leaving pauses the plot: advance the Court clock by two and the Ferry clock by one for each month away, and send news of what the Court did. A writ of departure is needed to board legally; Brannagh's pilots can arrange otherwise. They may bring Faerunian help back (Harpers, a Lords' Alliance envoy, a Dawn Mission delegation); it arrives as an Act IV ally (s22-ally-stormborn). Once the Seam is wide (Thrane rung), leaving for good with whoever will come is the Far Shore ending: run any-sail-out.
anytime.consequence: The campaign pauses for weeks of travel.
anytime.fallback: If they only want to see the edge, use the Edge of the Dream (11.7), now inside the Stormwall.
anytime.tells: Players ask about ships home, the Seam, or Faerûnian help.
anytime.later: Faerûnian allies join the S22 ally roster as the Stormborn. The Court's clocks will have moved.
anytime.keywords: leave, sail home, faerun, sword coast, ship, seam, stormwall, go home, other world

anytime.title: They want to fight a dragon, a god, or something unplanned
anytime.why: Big-game hunters exist at every table (Situation 18).
anytime.readAloud: "There's no dragon in Corvane. Sailors swear one tried the Stormwall in 1479 DR and fell burning into the sea. But there's the Dreamer, and it's enormous."
anytime.response: Oum's visible form is a dream-image of sleeping bells and mountains; ordinary attacks pass through it. Say so before they spend big resources. Only a strike of Ysh with the Key opens the Hush; after that, use conversation with Oum.
anytime.consequence: The party learns Oum cannot be fought, only answered.
anytime.tells: Players ask where the dragons are.
anytime.keywords: dragon, fight god, oum, monster, boss, kill the dreamer

anytime.title: A player is absent, leaves, or loses a character
anytime.why: Every campaign deals with it (Situation 19).
anytime.response: Follow the table's agreed rules. A new character arrives in Pellmoor on the next ship, or in Hallowmere, with a personal hook (v5 7.7). An absent player's character is a loyal companion who doesn't spend their resources, accept bargains or take personal losses, or stays safely off-screen by agreement.
anytime.consequence: Every player keeps their character and their choices.
anytime.rules: No Toll, stairs cost or memory payment is ever taken from an absent player's character.
anytime.keywords: absent, missing player, character death, new character, leave game

anytime.title: The party doesn't know where to go next
anytime.why: Mysteries stall (Situation 20).
anytime.readAloud: "Let's look at what you know. Who do you trust most, and where do you want to go?"
anytime.response: Use the Clue Ladder: a rumour pointing at the next place, then an NPC's direct hint, then a document or person who names it outright. If still stuck, an NPC approaches with a direct request: Mother Sallow, Rook, Kessa, Corin or Lysse. Foresight's Forecast lists the routes still open.
anytime.consequence: A clear next step, earned through clues rather than handed out.
anytime.tells: Long silence, or "what are we supposed to do?"
anytime.keywords: lost, stuck, confused, what next, where to go, no idea

anytime.title: They send Bet's carts for Calla's Heart
anytime.why: They left the capital and the Heart is still in the vault (Situation 21).
anytime.readAloud: "The Calla Heart is in the Court's vault, in Hallowmere. That hasn't changed."
anytime.response: Bet Ostrow knows which carts leave the city unsearched. The Heart comes out among the grain sacks over four days, at a cost: the Tithe Clock ticks once for the night Bet's people spend in the city. In v6 a Harper on Strangers' Row can forge a writ that gets one person in.
anytime.consequence: The party holds Calla's Heart.
anytime.tells: Players look at the Forecast and see Calla missing.
anytime.later: Calla is one of the six for the Concord.
anytime.keywords: calla, heart, vault, hallowmere, go back, return, harvest

anytime.title: They cast Modify Memory to restore or remove a memory
anytime.why: In a campaign about memory, the spell will come up once a bard or cleric reaches it.
anytime.readAloud: The spell finds the shape of the forgetting, a clean hollow where something was, and there is nothing in it to move.
anytime.response: Modify Memory works as written on ordinary memories (forgetting the party's faces, changing how a recent conversation went). It cannot restore a Tithed memory (that memory is in a jar in Hallowmere; only opening the jar returns it), a sold keep (it's in someone's vial), or a Toll (the bell took it). It can plant a false memory in a Blank, but not recognition of a real person. Make the limit clear before the slot is spent.
anytime.consequence: Ordinary memories bend; the Tithe, the trade and the Tolls do not.
anytime.tells: A caster asks whether magic can give Mother Sallow back her husband, or make a Hushman forget them.
anytime.rules: Modify Memory (2024): Wisdom save; the target has the Charmed condition while you work; the time window depends on spell level.
anytime.later: Planting false memories in Blanks is exactly what the Court would do. If the party does it, the Choir and the Bellwrights notice.
anytime.keywords: modify memory, restore memory, erase memory, spell, bard, cleric, wizard, forget

anytime.title: They use healing magic on a Blank, a Toll or an eel-bite
anytime.why: Players reach for Greater Restoration, Remove Curse or Heal on memory loss.
anytime.response: Rulings: Greater Restoration, Heal and Remove Curse don't restore Tithed or traded memories (those are elsewhere, in glass). A Toll can't be ended early by any magic: the bell holds it until it ends. Remove Curse or Greater Restoration does return an eel-stolen memory at once. Lesser Restoration ends Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed or Poisoned (and a disease); it does not end Frightened. Use Calm Emotions for a fear in the moment, Heroes' Feast against fear for a day. A dream lost to the Hush Cult returns only when the Hush is struck, sealed or tuned.
anytime.consequence: The table learns which losses magic can mend and which only a jar, a vial or the Remake can.
anytime.tells: A cleric offers to cure a Blank, or end a Sense Toll early.
anytime.rules: Lesser and Greater Restoration, Remove Curse and Heal work by 2024 rules except as ruled here.
anytime.later: The cure for a Blank is finding their jars, or the Remake.
anytime.keywords: greater restoration, remove curse, heal, cure, blank, toll, eel, restore, lesser restoration

anytime.title: They cast Speak with Dead on Tam Harrow
anytime.why: A level-5 cleric or bard with a drowned father's body nearby will try it.
anytime.readAloud: Tam's lips move slowly, as if the water were still in them. "Grey gloves. They took the way. I couldn't find the way home."
anytime.response: Mere-drowned bodies don't decay; the ferry-folk keep Tam in the cold-house until his name is written in the ledger. Speak with Dead works: he answers five questions from what he knew. He remembers grey gloves, a patrol, being asked about a route, and then nothing about the route at all, because it was taken from him. He wanted to return the Heart to the Choir and keep Ila safe.
anytime.consequence: A clear source on Tam's death.
anytime.tells: Players ask where Tam is buried.
anytime.rules: Speak with Dead (2024): five questions; the corpse knows only what it knew in life. Ask Ila or Mother Sallow first; doing it without asking angers the ferry-folk.
anytime.later: Counts as one of the sources on Tam's death; any two establish the Court's responsibility.
anytime.keywords: speak with dead, tam, corpse, body, cleric, question the dead, father

anytime.title: They cast Zone of Truth or Detect Thoughts on someone
anytime.why: Investigative parties reach for truth magic in a story built on lies.
anytime.response: The firm rulings for levels 3 to 6 are in the early play on truth and minds (the oath-duel's herald fields, Maudrin's dais, Haldric's shield). Later in the campaign the same rules hold: Zone of Truth works as written (Charisma save; a creature may refuse to answer, which is itself telling), and Haldric and Maudrin, who know the spell, refuse. Detect Thoughts on a Tithed person finds blank patches where things were taken; on Maudrin with the Key it finds one repeating thought: “keep it as it is.”
anytime.consequence: Truth magic gets answers outside the hearing, and pointed refusals from the people who know the spell.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Zone of Truth before the oath-duel or an interrogation.
anytime.rules: Zone of Truth: Charisma save; creatures can evade or refuse to answer. Detect Thoughts: Wisdom save to probe deeper.
anytime.keywords: zone of truth, detect thoughts, lie, truth, read mind, interrogate, spell

anytime.title: They use Silence, Dispel Magic or Counterspell against silence-stones
anytime.why: Casters want to know how their magic interacts with the Court's stones.
anytime.response: Silence-stones aren't spells. Dispel Magic and Counterspell don't affect them; break one (AC 12, 10 HP) or carry it off. The spell Silence is a different thing: Corvanese find it eerie and holy, and Hushmen are amused. A bell rung inside a Silence spell still rings and still takes its Toll; its tone travels through the world, not the air. Silence does stop a Heart-Hound's ring.
anytime.consequence: Casters know stones must be broken or carried, not dispelled.
anytime.tells: A caster tries to dispel a checkpoint stone, or casts Silence around a Hushman.
anytime.rules: House rule (v5 2.6): a fixed stone suppresses spells in a 10-foot radius; a glove suppresses only its own strike.
anytime.keywords: silence, silence-stone, dispel magic, counterspell, stone, checkpoint, suppress, antimagic

anytime.title: They send a message across the Stormwall
anytime.why: A Stormborn caster with Sending can reach home.
anytime.response: It works: Corvane is on the same plane as the Sword Coast. The recipient hears a faint ringing under the words. Help sent in reply takes weeks to arrive by sea; magical travel needs a destination the caster knows, and Corvane has no permanent teleportation circles.
anytime.consequence: Faerûn knows what the party knows.
anytime.tells: A player asks whether Sending works from Corvane.
anytime.rules: Sending (2024): 25 words each way.
anytime.later: A reply can become a Stormborn ally for S22, or a complication if the Lords' Alliance decides the Seam is worth controlling.
anytime.keywords: sending, message, home, faerun, contact, harpers, teleport, scroll

anytime.title: They use Water Breathing or similar to reach Old Pellmoor
anytime.why: Diving magic makes the drowned town an explorable dungeon.
anytime.readAloud: The drowned streets of Old Pellmoor open in front of you, doors hanging, a chandelier swaying with no current.
anytime.response: It works (v5 allows diving magic). The Choir notices anyone who lingers; the response hymn keeps them calm. The drowned houses can collapse, and memory-eels nest in chimneys. Treasure: memory-pearls (v5 11.5).
anytime.consequence: Old Pellmoor becomes a place the party can explore.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Water Breathing before visiting the belfry.
anytime.rules: Underwater combat (2024): melee attackers without a Swim Speed have Disadvantage unless using a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear or trident.
anytime.keywords: water breathing, dive, underwater, old pellmoor, drowned town, swim, explore

anytime.title: They pay with a memory instead of coin
anytime.why: It's the everyday currency of Corvane, and players love trying it.
anytime.readAloud: The Reckoner touches a cold fork to your temple. For a moment you know exactly what you're about to lose. Then you don't, and you don't mind.
anytime.response: The player chooses the memory and its weight (mote, keep, heartkeep or knowing) and writes one line in the Memory ledger. Price it from the Reckoning House slate. Motes and keeps change nothing on the sheet. Ask the player what the character no longer remembers, and let that be a small moment.
anytime.consequence: The character has paid in the local way.
anytime.tells: A player asks what a memory is worth, or offers one at a stall.
anytime.rules: Rates at Pellmoor: mote about 1 sp; keep about 1 gp 2 sp; heartkeep 25–100 gp by appraisal. A Reckoner buying memories for gold takes a 10 percent fee.
anytime.later: Patterns of what a character sells say a lot about them; use the ledger as a spotlight prompt.
anytime.keywords: pay with memory, memory money, keep, mote, buy, sell memory, reckoner, price, coin

anytime.title: They sell a heartkeep
anytime.why: Heartkeeps pay well, and desperate characters sell them.
anytime.readAloud: Sela Maunt holds the red-waxed vial up to the light and doesn't say anything for a long moment. "Are you sure, love? This one's heavy."
anytime.response: Appraise it at 25 to 100 gp or more. Before the sale, the player names the memory and what it held up in the character (a belief, a bond, a fear); after, they rewrite that one thing. Sela will quietly offer to keep it on her Lost Shelf so they can buy it back at cost.
anytime.consequence: Real money, and a real change in the character.
anytime.tells: A player asks what a big memory is worth.
anytime.rules: No mechanical penalty. The DM may award Heroic Inspiration if the money is used for someone in need.
anytime.later: Venn's Coster pays more and ships it abroad, and then it is gone for good. A heartkeep on Sela's shelf can be bought back.
anytime.keywords: heartkeep, sell big memory, defining memory, desperate, money, sela, lost shelf

anytime.title: They try to buy back a memory
anytime.why: Someone (a PC, Mother Sallow, Lysse, a Blank) wants something back.
anytime.response: Traded keeps: find who holds the vial (Sela's Lost Shelf, a collector, a Coster crate) and buy it; the owner opens it and the memory returns whole. Tithed memories: they're jars in the Tithe-Ledger Room in Hallowmere; only theft or a Court bargain gets them. Tolls: never.
anytime.consequence: The party knows where each kind of lost memory went and what getting it back would take.
anytime.tells: A player asks where sold or Tithed memories go.
anytime.rules: Finding a sold keep: a Reckoner's records (DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation), or Sela's help) say who bought it.
anytime.later: Mother Sallow's wedding memory is a Tithe jar in the Hallowmere vault (S5). Lysse's missing memories are filed under other names there.
anytime.keywords: buy back, recover memory, get memory back, jar, tithe jar, lost shelf, restore

anytime.title: They open a stranger's keep
anytime.why: Curiosity, a clue, or an investigation can be inside a vial.
anytime.readAloud: For a moment you are someone else, on a different shore, laughing at something you'll never understand. Then the vial is a little greyer.
anytime.response: They witness the memory as a guest, without becoming its owner. Each stranger's opening fades it; after three it's spent. A Knowing gives them its knowledge for one use. Opening a keep is how investigations in Corvane find evidence: a route, a face, a password.
anytime.consequence: A stranger’s memory, and possibly a clue, at the cost of fading it.
anytime.tells: A player asks what is in a keep, or buys one to open.
anytime.rules: Once, a character who witnesses a Knowing has Advantage on one ability check that knowledge plainly helps.
anytime.keywords: open keep, witness, stranger's memory, knowing, vial, clue, evidence

anytime.title: They pay a local's Tithe in gold (gilding)
anytime.why: Faerûnian characters with gold want to spare friends their memories.
anytime.readAloud: Quill looks at the coins, then at you, then very carefully at nothing at all. "I didn't see that."
anytime.response: It is illegal and common. A bribed or tired officer looks away; an ambitious one writes it down. Quill accepts gilding once if bribed or befriended; any Hushman Sergeant reports it. Getting caught makes the payer a Tithe-case and the local pays double.
anytime.consequence: A neighbour keeps their memory; the party owes or is owed.
anytime.tells: A player offers to cover someone's Tithe with coin.
anytime.rules: Influence (Persuasion or Deception) DC 15 to get an officer to look away; automatic with Quill if he's bribed.
anytime.later: Repeated gilding advances the Court clock and raises Pellmoor's quota. The ferry-folk remember who paid.
anytime.keywords: gild, gilding, pay tithe in gold, gold for tithe, cover tithe, bribe officer

anytime.title: They make or pass a forged keep
anytime.why: Rogues will try to counterfeit the local money.
anytime.response: A forged keep is a real vial with a false or empty memory and a copied wax stamp. It passes in a busy market and fails in front of a Reckoner, whose fork rings in the wrong note. Forgery is a Court crime; the Landing's merchants take it personally.
anytime.consequence: Easy money, and enemies in the Tally.
anytime.tells: A player asks how keeps are stamped, or whether you can fake a memory.
anytime.rules: Making one: DC 15 Dexterity (Forgery Kit). Passing it: Charisma (Deception) against a merchant's Passive Insight; a Reckoner detects it automatically unless bribed.
anytime.later: Venn's Coster hires investigators; the Landing clock advances.
anytime.keywords: forge, forgery, fake keep, counterfeit, fake memory, scam

anytime.title: Someone tries to take a memory without consent
anytime.why: A player wonders if they could rip a secret out of an NPC.
anytime.response: Drawing needs a Reckoner's fork, a Mere-glass vial, training and consent; without consent the memory won't seal. Only Court Tithe-collectors and leeches force it, using tools and methods that are the Court's darkest secret. A PC cannot do it on the fly. If the table wants this thread, it is a villain's method, not a player tool.
anytime.consequence: The table knows forced drawing is the Court’s secret, not a player tool.
anytime.tells: A player asks how drawing works, intending to use it on a prisoner.
anytime.keywords: leech, steal memory, force, take memory, interrogate, without consent

anytime.title: They confront Master Venn about the memory trade
anytime.why: Once they know the Coster buys Tithed memories, Venn becomes a target.
anytime.readAloud: Venn closes his ledger gently, as if it might bruise. "Friend. Everyone in Corvane sells memories. I only pay better."
anytime.response: Venn denies nothing he can't be forced to. Evidence (the Tithe-Ledger column, a crate manifest, a bribed Quill) makes him bargain: he'll give up a crate bound for Athkatla, or betray Quill, to keep his licence hopes. Exposing him publicly turns the Old Shore against the Coster.
anytime.consequence: Venn becomes an enemy or an unwilling source.
anytime.tells: The party has seen the EXPORT — VENNMARK column, or follows a Coster crate.
anytime.rules: Influence: Venn is Indifferent; Hostile once humiliated in public. Evidence grants Advantage.
anytime.later: A recovered crate holds Blanks' memories. Return them and the Blanks can join the S22 allies (s22-ally-blanks). The Landing clock moves.
anytime.keywords: venn, confront, coster, export, memory trade, crates, athkatla, merchant

anytime.title: They seek out the Harpers or other Faerûnian help
anytime.why: Faerûnian characters know there are people in Pellmoor who distrust the Court.
anytime.readAloud: The Harper's lute has one string tuned wrong, on purpose. "You're asking the right questions. Ask them quieter."
anytime.response: Two Harper agents work Strangers' Row. They distrust the Tithe and sympathise with the Bellwrights. They can forge one writ of passage, carry a message home, or introduce the party to a Bellwright contact. In return they want the truth about the Tithe-Ledger. The Zhentarim offer the same services for money and a cut of the memory trade.
anytime.consequence: A Faerûnian contact network.
anytime.tells: A Stormborn character mentions the Harpers, the Lords' Alliance or the Zhentarim.
anytime.later: Harper help can become the Stormborn ally at S22. A Zhentarim debt comes due in Act III.
anytime.keywords: harpers, zhentarim, lords alliance, faerunian help, spies, writ forgery, contact

anytime.title: The attempt on Maudrin fails
anytime.why: Plans against her fail more often than they work.
anytime.readAloud: The balcony door is already open. “Do come in,” says a voice in the dark.
anytime.response: The party escapes, is captured, or is allowed to leave. The Court knows their faces. Do not force a merciful Maudrin; play what the dice and the plan give. She never forgives a second attempt.
anytime.consequence: The Court hunts the party.
anytime.tells: The assassination goes wrong.
anytime.later: S23: the Strike is harder.
anytime.keywords: kill maudrin, fail, assassination

anytime.title: They bargain with Chancellor Tristan
anytime.why: With Maudrin dead, Tristan holds the Key and wants allies.
anytime.readAloud: Tristan Vesk folds his hands. “My cousin made a great many enemies. I would like to make fewer.”
anytime.response: Tristan offers the Key's whereabouts for the Hearts the party holds, or a pension for silence about the Quiet Night. He is cautious and afraid of the Hush. He cannot be forced.
anytime.consequence: A deal with a new Court head.
anytime.tells: Players ask what Tristan wants.
anytime.later: S22: s22-tristan-takes-the-march.
anytime.keywords: tristan, chancellor, deal, key

anytime.title: They Scry on Maudrin, the Key or the shrine
anytime.why: A fifth-level spell for a campaign about secrets.
anytime.readAloud: In the water a figure turns away, and the scene dims as if under a cloth.
anytime.response: Scrying works but is hampered: Maudrin's gloves and the Key's silence-stone case give her Advantage on the save if she knows she is watched; the Key itself cannot be seen. The shrine can be scried only by someone who has stood at the bottom (it also becomes a Teleport destination, Viewed Once). The Hush notices a scryer and speaks to them.
anytime.consequence: A view of the column, a face, a place.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Scrying.
anytime.rules: Scrying (5th): Wisdom save modified by familiarity. A silence-stone cloth blocks it entirely.
anytime.later: S22: the column (s22-scry-the-column).
anytime.keywords: scrying, spy, watch, divination

anytime.title: They Teleport, Dimension Door or Gate
anytime.why: High-level casters will try to skip the road.
anytime.readAloud: The air folds, and for a moment you smell tide and bronze.
anytime.response: Corvane has no permanent teleportation circles. Teleport works within the Ninefold Shore to places the caster knows; Hallowmere's silence-stones block arrival within 10 feet of a stone. Teleport or Gate across the Stormwall misfires: you arrive at Pellmouth in the Seam, taking 3d10 Lightning damage. Teleport or Dimension Door to the Hush chamber avoids the stairs if you have seen it (s25-teleport-to-the-shrine).
anytime.consequence: Travel has rules.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Teleport or Gate.
anytime.rules: Teleport (7th), Dimension Door (4th), Gate (9th).
anytime.later: S25: the stairs.
anytime.keywords: teleport, gate, dimension door, travel

anytime.title: They Plane Shift or leave the plane
anytime.why: A high-level escape hatch.
anytime.readAloud: The tuning fork hums, and the grey world slips away.
anytime.response: Plane Shift works (Corvane is on the Material Plane); it does not cross to Faerun because that is the same plane. Leaving Corvane's plane strands the party outside the Hush's reach: Tolls, stairs memories and the Great Toll stay with them; bells cannot be rung from another plane. Advance the Court clock by two for each month away. The Court does not follow.
anytime.consequence: The party leaves and returns later.
anytime.tells: A caster prepares Plane Shift.
anytime.rules: Plane Shift (7th), Banishment (4th).
anytime.later: Anytime: the Court's clocks have moved.
anytime.keywords: plane shift, astral, leave, escape

anytime.title: They cast Wish
anytime.why: A ninth-level caster will try.
anytime.readAloud: The word is out before you finish it. The bells do not answer.
anytime.response: Wish can duplicate a spell of 8th level or lower (including Resurrection, Heal and Greater Restoration), obey the usual stress rule, and teleport a Tithe jar to its owner. It cannot pay a Toll, ring a bell, strike Ysh, undo Oum, restore a Tithed memory as if it had never been taken, or change an ending flag. The lullaby ignores wishes.
anytime.consequence: A wish is a spell.
anytime.tells: A caster has Wish and a long list.
anytime.rules: Wish (9th). Stress: Strength drops, 33% to lose the spell forever (2024).
anytime.keywords: wish, limited, jar, toll

anytime.title: They cast Revivify, Raise Dead or Resurrection
anytime.why: Parties die in Act IV and V.
anytime.readAloud: The dead are listened to in Corvane, and they take a long time to answer.
anytime.response: Player characters: Revivify (within 1 minute, 300 gp diamond), Raise Dead (within 10 days, 500 gp diamond; -4 penalty to D20 Tests that fades one per Long Rest), Resurrection (within 100 years) work. Sister Aurelie's Dawn Mission can provide Raise Dead. Bell Tolls, stairs memories and lost dreams are not restored. NPCs whose death advances the plot (Tam, Imber, Kessa, Maudrin, Corin) are not restored; offer a Mere Memory instead. A Ringer who became the Seventh's voice cannot be raised.
anytime.consequence: The party's dead have a way back.
anytime.tells: A character drops or an NPC dies.
anytime.rules: Revivify (3rd), Raise Dead (5th), Resurrection (7th).
anytime.later: See any-pc-dies.
anytime.keywords: revivify, raise dead, resurrection, death, revive

anytime.title: A player character dies
anytime.why: Acts IV and V are dangerous.
anytime.readAloud: Your friend lies still, and the bells ring from a long way off.
anytime.response: The dead pay no Toll, stairs memory or ledger entry. Allies drag them out. Revivify within 1 minute; Raise Dead via Sister Aurelie's mission or a Tithe-free temple. A new character arrives by the next ship or road (any-absent-player). Nothing is taken from an absent player's character.

Each reform won ticks the Reform clock. Show it in the world next session: a family with its memories back, a bell-house with its doors open.

The Ninefold Church: its charity-houses left alone. The Drowned Choir: the names sung at the shore. The Landing: the Charter kept. The Blanks: a seat. The Stilled: someone looking for a cure. The Court's clerks: their jobs. Each backer won ticks the Claim clock. A promise made must be kept later; breaking it loses the backer and ticks that faction's clock.

anytime.why: Thrane's storms have gone home. The Wall is thinner, and the world on the far side can see in.

anytime.response: The Seam is wide now, and the fleets of the Sword Coast are coming: a Waterdhavian merchant fleet, a Lords' Alliance squadron and a ring of Amnian traders, all within a month or two. Pellmoor's Landing (Brannagh's pilots, Sela Maunt's Reckoning House, Venn's Coster) will fight over who lets them in. From now on Pellmoor is a front of its own.
anytime.consequence: The Seam is wide, and the Seam clock starts. The Far Shore ending can open.
anytime.fallback: If the party is far from the coast, a Faerunian sailor in a tavern tells them, delighted.

anytime.title: A Sword Coast fleet reaches Pellmoor
anytime.why: Each fleet brings trade, soldiers and questions, and nobody has agreed the terms.
anytime.readAloud: Forty ships in the roads, and the Quays sinking under barrels. A captain in a plumed hat asks, loudly, who is in charge here.
anytime.response: Pick a fleet. The Waterdhavian merchants want trade and storm-stones. The Lords' Alliance squadron wants a treaty and a fort. The Amnian traders want memory money, which they think is a joke until they see a Reckoner pay it. Each wants something from the party and offers something back: marines, coin, a ship. Every fleet that lands without a Charter ticks the Seam clock.
anytime.consequence: Another fleet in the roads. Pellmoor is more crowded and more dangerous.
anytime.fallback: If the party isn't in Pellmoor, Sela Maunt writes: "Come quickly, or come to an occupied port."
anytime.tells: The Seam is wide and a session passes without a Charter.

anytime.title: They write the Pellmoor Charter with the Landing
anytime.why: Whoever sets the terms at the Landing decides what the world beyond the Wall means for Corvane.
anytime.readAloud: Brannagh wants pilots' rights. Sela wants a Reckoning on every barrel. Venn wants everything else. "Well," Brannagh says. "Somebody start."
anytime.response: Run a three-way negotiation. Each Landing faction wants one thing in the Charter and gives one thing for it. Brannagh's pilots: the right to refuse any ship (they give the party ships). Sela Maunt: memory money taxed like gold (she gives coin and records). Venn: a monopoly on storm-stones (he gives the marines he has already hired, and he will cheat). Under a Charter the fleets land under the Landing's law, not the Court's.
anytime.consequence: The Landing and the party hold the Seam. The Seam clock stops mattering.
anytime.fallback: If the talks fail, try again next session; each failure ticks the Seam clock.
anytime.tells: The Seam is wide and the party brings Brannagh, Sela and Venn to one table.
anytime.rules: One Charisma (Persuasion) check for each faction, DC 15; two successes make the Charter. If Venn is exposed, Brannagh and Sela are enough.

anytime.title: Corin gives a Ringer a bell-charm
anytime.why: Corin has spent three generations learning how to make a Toll wait. He can't make it smaller, but he shares the trick with people he trusts.
anytime.readAloud: Corin turns a bronze bell no bigger than a thimble over in his fingers. It has no clapper. "It won't make it cheaper," he says. "Nothing does. It only lets you choose the hour."
anytime.response: He gives one Ringer a bronze bell no bigger than a thimble, with no clapper: his Deferred Toll in a thing you can carry. Be clear about what it doesn't do: the Toll is never smaller and never avoided. If they refused Corin, the Bellwrights' apprentices make one in a week for a party the Bellwrights hold Trusted (faction standing).
anytime.consequence: One Ringer carries the charm.
anytime.tells: Corin is their ally and they meet him, or a Ringer is about to ring a bell with him there.
anytime.rules: **Bellwright's Charm** (rare, requires attunement): Resistance to Thunder damage. Once per dawn, when a bell you ring takes its Toll, you can let the Toll come an hour later, at a moment you choose within that hour; it is never less. As a Bonus Action, ring it to end the Charmed or Frightened condition on yourself or a creature within 30 feet; then not again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

anytime.title: A personal beat from session zero (once per character per act)
anytime.why: Every character came to Pellmoor with a road behind them, a thing lost and a person they knew. Once an act, the story should be about one of those.
anytime.readAloud: Someone at the edge of the firelight says your name. Not the one you use now: the one from before Pellmoor.
anytime.response: Look up the character's session-zero answers in the Roster notes and pick one: the road they came by (someone from it turns up), the thing they lost (a lead to it), or the person they know in Pellmoor (that person needs them, or writes). Give it one scene of ten minutes and let the player steer, then add it as a beat under Party & preferences → Roster → Personal threads (write what they want there too); Prep names anyone five played sessions without one. Each act from II on has a ready version: Session 8, Session 11, Session 20 and Session 24. In Act I, use this play.
anytime.consequence: One character's story moved, and it's theirs.
anytime.fallback: If a player has no answers, ask the three questions now, at the table, in a minute.
anytime.tells: A character hasn't had a scene of their own this act, Prep shows them under Their own story, or a player mentions their past.
anytime.rules: When the beat lands, that character gains Heroic Inspiration.
anytime.later: Five beats per character across the campaign. The last pays off in the epilogue.

anytime.title: The Long Cold comes south (they skipped Glassreach)
anytime.why: Nobody rang Hieme. The glass doesn't wait for the party to change its mind.
anytime.readAloud: Frost on the grass at midsummer, in the shape of ferns that never grew here. In the ditch by the road a fox stands perfectly still, in a coat of glass.
anytime.response: Once an act, let the cold turn up where it shouldn't: a village well frozen solid (the folk pay 10 gp to have it thawed), a Stilled traveler at a crossroads who wakes if spoken to kindly (DC 13 Persuasion; they know a true rumor about the road ahead), or one night on the road that is Extreme Cold. It's a reminder, not a punishment: the bell is still there to ring (any-go-back-north).
anytime.consequence: The world shows them what skipping Glassreach cost.
anytime.fallback: If it falls flat, skip it. The Forecast still shows Hieme as unrung.
anytime.tells: They turned south at Session 10 (s10-leave-the-north) and are on the road, above all in the high passes or north of Hallowmere.
anytime.rules: Extreme Cold: for each hour without a warm cloak, a fire or Resistance to Cold damage, a creature makes a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gains 1 Exhaustion level.
anytime.later: If they go back north, the glass has grown: the Glassreach clock starts at 1.

anytime.title: They go back north to ring Hieme after all
anytime.why: They skipped Glassreach, and now they want the Concord, or just want to finish what they left.
anytime.readAloud: The North Road is quieter than you remember. The glass has come further down it, and the trees are taller. On the last waystation somebody has painted, in red: THE SPIRE IS STILL THERE.
anytime.response: Glassreach is about two weeks from Hallowmere. Skip Sessions 10 to 13: Yara meets them at the edge of the glass and leads them straight to the Frost Spire. Run Session 14 as one evening (the climb, the inner stair, the Bell-Warden) and ring Hieme with s14-ring-hieme. They need the Frost Heart first: Isolde keeps it in Hallowmere until the Strike, then it travels with the Court's column (s23-recover-hieme). The Sexton is the Court's prisoner, so the Spire has nobody to stop them but its guards.
anytime.consequence: Hieme rings late. The thaw comes to Glassreach, and the Concord is open again.

anytime.tells: They hold the Frost Heart again, or talk about the Frost Spire.
anytime.rules: Session 14 is written for level 6. At level 7 or more, add one Glass-Wolf to each fight and give the Bell-Warden 20 more Hit Points for each level above 6. Add 2 to the Court Clock for the time away, as Session 22's detour does.

anytime.title: They go after the thing they lost
anytime.why: Session zero asked what each character had lost. A campaign that only takes more is missing half the story: let them win one thing back.
anytime.readAloud: It's there, after all this time. Not far, and not safe, but close enough to reach, if you're willing to go and get it.
anytime.response: Run it as a small quest over a session or two, with three leads; any one is enough. **A Tithe jar:** if it's a memory, the Tithe-Ledger names its jar. While the jars are intact they can buy it, argue for it or steal it; if the jars went home, it comes back in a dream. **The Hush's dreams:** anything lost in sleep is somewhere in the Hush, and the Sleeping Hall's keepers can send them to look for one night; they come back with it, and the Hush learns their name. **A person:** lost people are alive somewhere on the Ninefold Shore more often than not, and a personal beat says where. Once it's back, it's theirs.
anytime.consequence: One character has won back what they lost, and grown.
anytime.fallback: If the quest would take over a session, make it one scene: the jar on a shelf, the face in a crowd.
anytime.tells: A character has a lead to their lost thing, or a player says they want to look for it.
anytime.rules: Give the character an Origin feat that fits what came back (Skilled for a skill, Healer for a mentor's craft, Lucky for a person, Alert for a memory), or the person as a named ally. Tolls are permanent, and nothing here undoes one: if a Toll took it, it stays gone. Give a Toll-mark instead (any-toll-mark).
anytime.later: S24: Maudrin can offer any lost thing still unfound.

anytime.title: The Toll leaves a mark
anytime.why: The Toll is permanent, and it should be. But something grows in the space a Toll leaves, and the players should see it.
anytime.readAloud: The Toll is paid, and it stays paid. But when you look into the water afterwards, there is something in your face that wasn't there before.
anytime.response: The Toll stays paid. The Ringer also gets a Toll-mark, chosen with the player: a fleck of bronze in one eye, a note under the voice, a cold palm. The mark comes with one small boon that grows out of what was taken. A memory of someone: proficiency in Insight, because they read faces harder now. A Gift (Calla): one cantrip from any class's list. A dawn (Vaer): they always know the time and which way is east, and can't be Surprised at dawn. After Thrane: Resistance to Thunder damage. After Mirel: Advantage on saves against being Frightened. Or any skill or tool proficiency that fits.
anytime.consequence: The Ringer is changed, not only diminished. Read the marks with the Tolls in the epilogue.
anytime.tells: A Ringer has just paid a Toll, at the end of the ringing scene.
anytime.rules: One Toll-mark per Toll. A mark never gives back what was taken.

anytime.title: Faction standing: what each tier gets them
anytime.why: The party makes friends and enemies all campaign. Standing makes that pay a little, every session.
anytime.readAloud: "Word gets around," the innkeeper says, and sets down a second cup nobody ordered. "Some people round here think well of you. Some don't."
anytime.response: Each faction's standing is set in Waypoint (Faction standing, in the Campaign hub), from Enemies to Allied. Move it one step for a real favour or a real betrayal, never for a roll. **Enemies, Hostile:** they hunt or inform on the party; doors shut, prices double. **Wary:** no favours until they see proof. **Neutral:** business as usual. **Friendly:** one favour per act (a safe house, a guide, a message carried) and fair prices. **Trusted:** they lend a person for a session, sell uncommon items at book price, and share what they know, plus the faction's own perk (see Faction standing in the wiki). **Allied:** they stand with the party at the Strike.
anytime.consequence: Standing is visible, and it pays.
anytime.tells: The party does a faction a real favour or crosses it, or asks a faction for help.
anytime.rules: Standing and the faction clocks are separate: the clock is what the faction does next; standing is how it feels about the party.
anytime.later: S22: each Allied faction is a company that comes up the road; tick the Allies clock for it.
anytime.keywords: faction, standing, reputation, allies, friendly, hostile, trusted, renown, favour, waypoint
